n.10: Literally "my prayer returned to my bosom". Or "may my prayer return to me", that is, unanswered.
n.11: Or "in dark clothes", the clothing of mourning.
n.12: Hebrew *nekhim*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "attackers", "slanderers" or "outcasts".
n.13: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "with the godless of the mockers of a cake".
n.14: Hebrew *nephesh*.
n.15: Literally "my only one", that is, my precious life (compare 22:21; 22:20 in most English Bibles).
n.16: John 15:25 quotes "They hated me without cause", from this verse or from 69:5 (69:4 in most English Bibles).
n.17: Or "Vindicate me".
n.18: Literally "Aha, our soul (*nephesh*)!", that is, our desire.

v: For the director. Of the servant of the LORD,[^1] of David.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ ׀ לְעֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֬ה לְדָוִֽד׃
Rebellion speaks to the wicked deep in my heart:[^3] there is no fear of God before his eyes.[^4]
נְאֻֽם־פֶּ֣שַׁע לָ֭רָשָׁע בְּקֶ֣רֶב לִבִּ֑י אֵֽין־פַּ֥חַד אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָֽיו׃
For it flatters him in his own eyes, that his guilt will not be found out and hated.[^5]
כִּֽי־הֶחֱלִ֣יק אֵלָ֣יו בְּעֵינָ֑יו לִמְצֹ֖א עֲוֺנ֣וֹ לִשְׂנֹֽא׃
The words of his mouth are wickedness and deceit; he has stopped acting wisely and doing good.
דִּבְרֵי־פִ֭יו אָ֣וֶן וּמִרְמָ֑ה חָדַ֖ל לְהַשְׂכִּ֣יל לְהֵיטִֽיב׃
He plans wickedness on his bed; he sets himself on a path that is not good; he does not reject evil.
אָ֤וֶן ׀ יַחְשֹׁ֗ב עַֽל־מִשְׁכָּ֫ב֥וֹ יִ֭תְיַצֵּב עַל־דֶּ֣רֶךְ לֹא־ט֑וֹב רָ֝֗ע לֹ֣א יִמְאָֽס׃
LORD, your faithful love[^6] reaches to the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds.
יְ֭הוָה בְּהַשָּׁמַ֣יִם חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ עַד־שְׁחָקִֽים׃
Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains,[^7] your judgments like the great deep. LORD, you save humans and animals alike.
צִדְקָֽתְךָ֨ ׀ כְּֽהַרְרֵי־אֵ֗ל מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶךָ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֑ה אָ֤דָֽם־וּבְהֵמָ֖ה תוֹשִׁ֣יעַ יְהוָֽה׃
How precious is your faithful love, God! Human beings take refuge in the shadow of your wings.
מַה־יָּקָ֥ר חַסְדְּךָ֗ אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים וּבְנֵ֥י אָדָ֑ם בְּצֵ֥ל כְּ֝נָפֶ֗יךָ יֶחֱסָיֽוּן׃
They feast on the abundance of your house, and you give them drink from your river of delights.[^8]
יִ֭רְוִיֻן מִדֶּ֣שֶׁן בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ וְנַ֖חַל עֲדָנֶ֣יךָ תַשְׁקֵֽם׃
For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.
כִּֽי־עִ֭מְּךָ מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים בְּ֝אוֹרְךָ֗ נִרְאֶה־אֽוֹר׃
Continue your faithful love to those who know you, and your righteousness to the upright in heart.
מְשֹׁ֣ךְ חַ֭סְדְּךָ לְיֹדְעֶ֑יךָ וְ֝צִדְקָֽתְךָ֗ לְיִשְׁרֵי־לֵֽב׃
Do not let the foot of the proud come against me, or the hand of the wicked drive me away.
אַל־תְּ֭בוֹאֵנִי רֶ֣גֶל גַּאֲוָ֑ה וְיַד־רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים אַל־תְּנִדֵֽנִי׃
There the evildoers lie fallen; they are thrust down and cannot rise.
שָׁ֣ם נָ֭פְלוּ פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן דֹּ֝ח֗וּ וְלֹא־יָ֥כְלוּ קֽוּם׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–13 are 36:1–12 in most English Bibles.
n.3: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "An oracle of rebellion to the wicked in the middle of my heart". *Oracle* (*ne'um*) is the word used in "says the LORD". Or "I know deep in my heart what rebellion says to the wicked". The Septuagint reads "The lawless one says in himself that he will sin".
n.4: Romans 3:18 quotes the second line of this verse.
n.5: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "For he makes it smooth to him in his eyes, to find his guilt, to hate".
n.6: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.7: Literally "the mountains of God".
n.8: The word for "delights" (*adanim*) is related to the name *Eden*.

v: Of David.[^1] Do not fret because of evildoers; do not envy those who do wrong.[^2]
לְדָוִ֨ד ׀ אַל־תִּתְחַ֥ר בַּמְּרֵעִ֑ים אַל־תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א בְּעֹשֵׂ֥י עַוְלָֽה׃
For like grass they will soon wither, and like green plants they will fade.
כִּ֣י כֶ֭חָצִיר מְהֵרָ֣ה יִמָּ֑לוּ וּכְיֶ֥רֶק דֶּ֝֗שֶׁא יִבּוֹלֽוּן׃
Trust in the LORD[^3] and do good; live in the land and cultivate faithfulness.[^4]
בְּטַ֣ח בַּֽ֭יהוָה וַעֲשֵׂה־ט֑וֹב שְׁכָן־אֶ֝֗רֶץ וּרְעֵ֥ה אֱמוּנָֽה׃
Delight yourself in the LORD, and he will give you the desires of your heart.
וְהִתְעַנַּ֥ג עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וְיִֽתֶּן־לְ֝ךָ֗ מִשְׁאֲלֹ֥ת לִבֶּֽךָ׃
Commit your way to the LORD;[^5] trust in him, and he will act.
גּ֣וֹל עַל־יְהוָ֣ה דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ וּבְטַ֥ח עָ֝לָ֗יו וְה֣וּא יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
He will make your righteousness shine like the light, and your justice like the noonday sun.
וְהוֹצִ֣יא כָא֣וֹר צִדְקֶ֑ךָ וּ֝מִשְׁפָּטֶ֗ךָ כַּֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃
Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for him. Do not fret because of the one who prospers in his way, the one who carries out evil schemes.
דּ֤וֹם ׀ לַיהוָה֮ וְהִתְח֢וֹלֵ֫ל ל֥וֹ אַל־תִּ֭תְחַר בְּמַצְלִ֣יחַ דַּרְכּ֑וֹ בְּ֝אִ֗ישׁ עֹשֶׂ֥ה מְזִמּֽוֹת׃
Stop being angry and abandon your rage; do not fret: it leads only to evil.
הֶ֣רֶף מֵ֭אַף וַעֲזֹ֣ב חֵמָ֑ה אַל־תִּ֝תְחַ֗ר אַךְ־לְהָרֵֽעַ׃
For evildoers will be cut off, but those who wait for the LORD, they will inherit the land.
כִּֽי־מְ֭רֵעִים יִכָּרֵת֑וּן וְקֹוֵ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה הֵ֣מָּה יִֽירְשׁוּ־אָֽרֶץ׃
Yet a little while and the wicked will be no more; you will look closely at his place, and he will not be there.
וְע֣וֹד מְ֭עַט וְאֵ֣ין רָשָׁ֑ע וְהִתְבּוֹנַ֖נְתָּ עַל־מְקוֹמ֣וֹ וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
But the humble will inherit the land[^6] and delight in abundant peace.
וַעֲנָוִ֥ים יִֽירְשׁוּ־אָ֑רֶץ וְ֝הִתְעַנְּג֗וּ עַל־רֹ֥ב שָׁלֽוֹם׃
The wicked plots against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him.
זֹמֵ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע לַצַּדִּ֑יק וְחֹרֵ֖ק עָלָ֣יו שִׁנָּֽיו׃
The Lord laughs at him, for he sees that his day is coming.
אֲדֹנָ֥י יִשְׂחַק־ל֑וֹ כִּֽי־רָ֝אָ֗ה כִּֽי־יָבֹ֥א יוֹמֽוֹ׃
The wicked draw the sword and bend their bow to bring down the afflicted and the needy, to slaughter those whose way is upright.
חֶ֤רֶב ׀ פָּֽתְח֣וּ רְשָׁעִים֮ וְדָרְכ֢וּ קַ֫שְׁתָּ֥ם לְ֭הַפִּיל עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְי֑וֹן לִ֝טְב֗וֹחַ יִשְׁרֵי־דָֽרֶךְ׃
Their sword will enter their own heart, and their bows will be broken.
חַ֭רְבָּם תָּב֣וֹא בְלִבָּ֑ם וְ֝קַשְּׁתוֹתָ֗ם תִּשָּׁבַֽרְנָה׃
Better is the little that the righteous has than the wealth of many wicked.
טוֹב־מְ֭עַט לַצַּדִּ֑יק מֵ֝הֲמ֗וֹן רְשָׁעִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃
For the arms of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD upholds the righteous.
כִּ֤י זְרוֹע֣וֹת רְ֭שָׁעִים תִּשָּׁבַ֑רְנָה וְסוֹמֵ֖ךְ צַדִּיקִ֣ים יְהוָֽה׃
The LORD knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance will last forever.
יוֹדֵ֣עַ יְ֭הוָה יְמֵ֣י תְמִימִ֑ם וְ֝נַחֲלָתָ֗ם לְעוֹלָ֥ם תִּהְיֶֽה׃
They will not be put to shame in evil times; in days of famine they will have plenty.
לֹֽא־יֵ֭בֹשׁוּ בְּעֵ֣ת רָעָ֑ה וּבִימֵ֖י רְעָב֣וֹן יִשְׂבָּֽעוּ׃
But the wicked will perish; the enemies of the LORD are like the glory of the pastures:[^7] they vanish; like smoke they vanish.
כִּ֤י רְשָׁעִ֨ים ׀ יֹאבֵ֗דוּ וְאֹיְבֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה כִּיקַ֣ר כָּרִ֑ים כָּל֖וּ בֶעָשָׁ֣ן כָּֽלוּ׃
The wicked borrows and does not repay, but the righteous is generous and gives.
לֹוֶ֣ה רָ֭שָׁע וְלֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑ם וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק חוֹנֵ֥ן וְנוֹתֵֽן׃
For those whom he blesses will inherit the land, but those whom he curses will be cut off.
כִּ֣י מְ֭בֹרָכָיו יִ֣ירְשׁוּ אָ֑רֶץ וּ֝מְקֻלָּלָ֗יו יִכָּרֵֽתוּ׃
A man's steps are made firm by the LORD, and he delights in his way.[^8]
מֵ֭יְהוָה מִֽצְעֲדֵי־גֶ֥בֶר כּוֹנָ֗נוּ וְדַרְכּ֥וֹ יֶחְפָּֽץ׃
Though he falls, he will not be thrown down, for the LORD holds his hand.
כִּֽי־יִפֹּ֥ל לֹֽא־יוּטָ֑ל כִּֽי־יְ֝הוָ֗ה סוֹמֵ֥ךְ יָדֽוֹ׃
I have been young and now I am old, yet I have not seen the righteous abandoned, or his children begging for bread.
נַ֤עַר ׀ הָיִ֗יתִי גַּם־זָ֫קַ֥נְתִּי וְֽלֹא־רָ֭אִיתִי צַדִּ֣יק נֶעֱזָ֑ב וְ֝זַרְע֗וֹ מְבַקֶּשׁ־לָֽחֶם׃
He is always generous and lends, and his children become a blessing.
כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם חוֹנֵ֣ן וּמַלְוֶ֑ה וְ֝זַרְע֗וֹ לִבְרָכָֽה׃
Turn away from evil and do good, and you will live in the land forever.
ס֣וּר מֵ֭רָע וַעֲשֵׂה־ט֗וֹב וּשְׁכֹ֥ן לְעוֹלָֽם׃
For the LORD loves justice and will not abandon his faithful ones.[^9] They will be kept safe forever, but the children of the wicked will be cut off.
כִּ֤י יְהוָ֨ה ׀ אֹ֘הֵ֤ב מִשְׁפָּ֗ט וְלֹא־יַעֲזֹ֣ב אֶת־חֲ֭סִידָיו לְעוֹלָ֣ם נִשְׁמָ֑רוּ וְזֶ֖רַע רְשָׁעִ֣ים נִכְרָֽת׃
The righteous will inherit the land and live in it forever.
צַדִּיקִ֥ים יִֽירְשׁוּ־אָ֑רֶץ וְיִשְׁכְּנ֖וּ לָעַ֣ד עָלֶֽיהָ׃
The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.
פִּֽי־צַ֭דִּיק יֶהְגֶּ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנ֗וֹ תְּדַבֵּ֥ר מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
The law[^10] of his God is in his heart; his steps do not slip.
תּוֹרַ֣ת אֱלֹהָ֣יו בְּלִבּ֑וֹ לֹ֖א תִמְעַ֣ד אֲשֻׁרָיו׃[c]
The wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to kill him.
צוֹפֶ֣ה רָ֭שָׁע לַצַּדִּ֑יק וּ֝מְבַקֵּ֗שׁ לַהֲמִיתוֹ׃
The LORD will not abandon him to his power, or let him be condemned when he is brought to trial.
יְ֭הוָה לֹא־יַעַזְבֶ֣נּוּ בְיָד֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יַ֝רְשִׁיעֶ֗נּוּ בְּהִשָּׁפְטֽוֹ׃
Wait for the LORD and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land; you will see it when the wicked are cut off.
קַוֵּ֤ה אֶל־יְהוָ֨ה ׀ וּשְׁמֹ֬ר דַּרְכּ֗וֹ וִֽ֭ירוֹמִמְךָ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אָ֑רֶץ בְּהִכָּרֵ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים תִּרְאֶֽה׃
I have seen a wicked and ruthless man, spreading himself like a luxuriant tree in its native soil.[^11]
רָ֭אִיתִי רָשָׁ֣ע עָרִ֑יץ וּ֝מִתְעָרֶ֗ה כְּאֶזְרָ֥ח רַעֲנָֽן׃
But he passed away,[^12] and look, he was gone; I searched for him, but he could not be found.
וַ֭יּֽ͏ַעֲבֹר וְהִנֵּ֣ה אֵינֶ֑נּוּ וָֽ֝אֲבַקְשֵׁ֗הוּ וְלֹ֣א נִמְצָֽא׃
Watch the blameless and observe the upright, for there is a future[^13] for the person of peace.
שְׁמָר־תָּ֭ם וּרְאֵ֣ה יָשָׁ֑ר כִּֽי־אַחֲרִ֖ית לְאִ֣ישׁ שָׁלֽוֹם׃
But rebels will be destroyed altogether; the future of the wicked will be cut off.
וּֽ֭פֹשְׁעִים נִשְׁמְד֣וּ יַחְדָּ֑ו אַחֲרִ֖ית רְשָׁעִ֣ים נִכְרָֽתָה׃
The salvation of the righteous comes from the LORD; he is their stronghold in time of trouble.
וּתְשׁוּעַ֣ת צַ֭דִּיקִים מֵיְהוָ֑ה מָֽ֝עוּזָּ֗ם בְּעֵ֣ת צָרָֽה׃
The LORD helps them and rescues them; he rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they take refuge in him.
וַ֥יַּעְזְרֵ֥ם יְהוָ֗ה וַֽיְפַלְּ֫טֵ֥ם יְפַלְּטֵ֣ם מֵ֭רְשָׁעִים וְיוֹשִׁיעֵ֑ם כִּי־חָ֥סוּ בֽוֹ׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Psalm 37 is an acrostic: in the Hebrew, each letter of the alphabet in turn begins a section, usually of two verses (*aleph* at verse 1, *bet* at verse 3, and so on, to *tav* at verse 39). The *ayin* section begins in the middle of verse 28, with *le'olam*, "forever".
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Or "and graze in safety", "and feed on faithfulness".
n.5: Literally "Roll your way on the LORD".
n.6: Or "the earth". Jesus echoes this line in Matthew 5:5.
n.7: Or "like the fat of lambs", which is burned up in sacrifice.
n.8: It is not clear whether the LORD delights in the man's way, or the man in the LORD's.
n.9: Hebrew *chasidim*, "faithful, loyal ones", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.10: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching".
n.11: Literally "like a green native". The Septuagint reads "like the cedars of Lebanon".
n.12: The Septuagint reads "I passed by".
n.13: Or "descendants". Also in verse 38.

v: A psalm of David.[^1] To bring to remembrance.[^2]
מִזְמ֖וֹר לְדָוִ֣ד לְהַזְכִּֽיר׃
LORD,[^3] do not rebuke me in your anger, or discipline me in your wrath.[^4]
יְֽהוָ֗ה אַל־בְּקֶצְפְּךָ֥ תוֹכִיחֵ֑נִי וּֽבַחֲמָתְךָ֥ תְיַסְּרֵֽנִי׃
For your arrows have sunk into me, and your hand has come down on me.
כִּֽי־חִ֭צֶּיךָ נִ֣חֲתוּ בִ֑י וַתִּנְחַ֖ת עָלַ֣י יָדֶֽךָ׃
There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation; there is no health[^5] in my bones because of my sin.
אֵין־מְתֹ֣ם בִּ֭בְשָׂרִי מִפְּנֵ֣י זַעְמֶ֑ךָ אֵין־שָׁל֥וֹם בַּ֝עֲצָמַ֗י מִפְּנֵ֥י חַטָּאתִֽי׃
For my guilt has gone over my head; like a heavy burden it is too heavy for me.
כִּ֣י עֲ֭וֺנֹתַי עָבְר֣וּ רֹאשִׁ֑י כְּמַשָּׂ֥א כָ֝בֵ֗ד יִכְבְּד֥וּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
My wounds stink and fester because of my foolishness.
הִבְאִ֣ישׁוּ נָ֭מַקּוּ חַבּוּרֹתָ֑י מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י אִוַּלְתִּֽי׃
I am bent over and bowed down greatly; all day long I go about in mourning.
נַעֲוֵ֣יתִי שַׁחֹ֣תִי עַד־מְאֹ֑ד כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם קֹדֵ֥ר הִלָּֽכְתִּי׃
For my sides[^6] are filled with burning, and there is no soundness in my flesh.
כִּֽי־כְ֭סָלַי מָלְא֣וּ נִקְלֶ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין מְ֝תֹ֗ם בִּבְשָׂרִֽי׃
I am numb and badly crushed; I groan[^7] because of the turmoil of my heart.
נְפוּג֣וֹתִי וְנִדְכֵּ֣יתִי עַד־מְאֹ֑ד שָׁ֝אַ֗גְתִּי מִֽנַּהֲמַ֥ת לִבִּֽי׃
Lord, all my longing is before you; my sighing is not hidden from you.
אֲ‍ֽדנָ֗[t]י נֶגְדְּךָ֥ כָל־תַּאֲוָתִ֑י וְ֝אַנְחָתִ֗י מִמְּךָ֥ לֹא־נִסְתָּֽרָה׃
My heart pounds, my strength fails me; even the light of my eyes has gone from me.
לִבִּ֣י סְ֭חַרְחַר עֲזָבַ֣נִי כֹחִ֑י וְֽאוֹר־עֵינַ֥י גַּם־הֵ֝֗ם אֵ֣ין אִתִּֽי׃
My friends and companions stand aloof from my affliction;[^8] my neighbors stand far off.
אֹֽהֲבַ֨י ׀ וְרֵעַ֗י מִנֶּ֣גֶד נִגְעִ֣י יַעֲמֹ֑דוּ וּ֝קְרוֹבַ֗י מֵרָחֹ֥ק עָמָֽדוּ׃
Those who seek my life[^9] lay snares; those who seek my harm speak of ruin and plot deceit all day long.
וַיְנַקְשׁ֤וּ ׀ מְבַקְשֵׁ֬י נַפְשִׁ֗י וְדֹרְשֵׁ֣י רָ֭עָתִי דִּבְּר֣וּ הַוּ֑וֹת וּ֝מִרְמ֗וֹת כָּל־הַיּ֥וֹם יֶהְגּֽוּ׃
But I am like a deaf man who does not hear, like a mute man who does not open his mouth.
וַאֲנִ֣י כְ֭חֵרֵשׁ לֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֑ע וּ֝כְאִלֵּ֗ם לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־פִּֽיו׃
I have become like a man who does not hear, in whose mouth there are no arguments.
וָאֱהִ֗י כְּ֭אִישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְאֵ֥ין בְּ֝פִ֗יו תּוֹכָֽחוֹת׃
For in you, LORD, I hope; you will answer, Lord my God.
כִּֽי־לְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה הוֹחָ֑לְתִּי אַתָּ֥ה תַ֝עֲנֶ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהָֽי׃
For I said, "Do not let them gloat over me, who exalt themselves over me when my foot slips."
כִּֽי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי פֶּן־יִשְׂמְחוּ־לִ֑י בְּמ֥וֹט רַ֝גְלִ֗י עָלַ֥י הִגְדִּֽילוּ׃
For I am ready to fall, and my pain is always before me.
כִּֽי־אֲ֭נִי לְצֶ֣לַע נָכ֑וֹן וּמַכְאוֹבִ֖י נֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃
I confess my guilt; I am troubled by my sin.
כִּֽי־עֲוֺנִ֥י אַגִּ֑יד אֶ֝דְאַ֗ג מֵ֖חַטָּאתִֽי׃
My enemies are full of life and strong;[^10] many are those who hate me wrongfully.
וְֽ֭אֹיְבַי חַיִּ֣ים עָצֵ֑מוּ וְרַבּ֖וּ שֹׂנְאַ֣י שָֽׁקֶר׃
Those who repay evil for good accuse me[^11] because I pursue good.
וּמְשַׁלְּמֵ֣י רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה יִ֝שְׂטְנ֗וּנִי תַּ֣חַת *רדופי־**רָֽדְפִי־טֽוֹב׃
Do not abandon me, LORD; my God, do not be far from me.
אַל־תַּֽעַזְבֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אַל־תִּרְחַ֥ק מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
Come quickly to help me, Lord, my salvation.
ח֥וּשָׁה לְעֶזְרָתִ֑י אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י תְּשׁוּעָתִֽי׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–23 are 38:1–22 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *lehazkir*, "to cause to remember" or "to make a memorial". The psalm may have been sung with the memorial portion of an offering (Leviticus 2:2), or it may call on God to remember the one who prays. Also in the title of Psalm 70.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: This verse is almost the same as 6:2 (6:1 in most English Bibles).
n.5: Hebrew *shalom*: peace, well-being, wholeness.
n.6: Literally "my loins".
n.7: Literally "I roar".
n.8: Or "my disease". Hebrew *nega*, "a blow, a plague".
n.9: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.10: Literally "My enemies are living, they are strong".
n.11: Hebrew *yistenuni*, from the same root as *satan*, "adversary, accuser".

v: For the director. For Jeduthun.[^1] A psalm of David.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ *לידיתון **לִֽידוּת֗וּן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
I said, "I will guard my ways, so that I do not sin with my tongue; I will keep a muzzle on my mouth as long as the wicked are in my presence."
אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶֽשְׁמְרָ֣ה דְרָכַי֮ מֵחֲט֢וֹא בִלְשׁ֫וֹנִ֥י אֶשְׁמְרָ֥ה לְפִ֥י מַחְס֑וֹם בְּעֹ֖ד רָשָׁ֣ע לְנֶגְדִּֽי׃
I was silent and still; I kept quiet, even from good,[^3] and my pain grew worse.
נֶאֱלַ֣מְתִּי ד֭וּמִיָּה הֶחֱשֵׁ֣יתִי מִטּ֑וֹב וּכְאֵבִ֥י נֶעְכָּֽר׃
My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, a fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue:
חַם־לִבִּ֨י ׀ בְּקִרְבִּ֗י בַּהֲגִיגִ֥י תִבְעַר־אֵ֑שׁ דִּ֝בַּ֗רְתִּי בִּלְשֽׁוֹנִי׃
"LORD,[^4] let me know my end, and what is the measure of my days; let me know how fleeting I am.
הוֹדִ֘יעֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֨ה ׀ קִצִּ֗י וּמִדַּ֣ת יָמַ֣י מַה־הִ֑יא אֵ֝דְעָ֗ה מֶה־חָדֵ֥ל אָֽנִי׃
See, you have made my days a few handbreadths,[^5] and my lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely every human being, however firmly he stands, is only a breath.[^6] Selah.[^7]
הִנֵּ֤ה טְפָח֨וֹת ׀ נָ֘תַ֤תָּה יָמַ֗י וְחֶלְדִּ֣י כְאַ֣יִן נֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ אַ֥ךְ כָּֽל־הֶ֥בֶל כָּל־אָ֝דָ֗ם נִצָּ֥ב סֶֽלָה׃
Surely everyone goes about like a shadow;[^8] surely they are in turmoil for nothing. He heaps up wealth and does not know who will gather it.
אַךְ־בְּצֶ֤לֶם ׀ יִֽתְהַלֶּךְ־אִ֗ישׁ אַךְ־הֶ֥בֶל יֶהֱמָ֑יוּן יִ֝צְבֹּ֗ר וְֽלֹא־יֵדַ֥ע מִי־אֹסְפָֽם׃
And now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
וְעַתָּ֣ה מַה־קִוִּ֣יתִי אֲדֹנָ֑י תּ֝וֹחַלְתִּ֗י לְךָ֣ הִֽיא׃
Rescue me from all my offenses; do not make me the scorn of fools.
מִכָּל־פְּשָׁעַ֥י הַצִּילֵ֑נִי חֶרְפַּ֥ת נָ֝בָ֗ל אַל־תְּשִׂימֵֽנִי׃
I am silent; I do not open my mouth, for it is you who have done this.
נֶ֭אֱלַמְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶפְתַּח־פִּ֑י כִּ֖י אַתָּ֣ה עָשִֽׂיתָ׃
Remove your blow from me; I am worn out by the hostility of your hand.
הָסֵ֣ר מֵעָלַ֣י נִגְעֶ֑ךָ מִתִּגְרַ֥ת יָ֝דְךָ֗ אֲנִ֣י כָלִֽיתִי׃
When you discipline someone with rebukes for guilt, you consume like a moth what is dear to him. Surely every human being is only a breath. Selah.
בְּֽתוֹכָ֘ח֤וֹת עַל־עָוֺ֨ן ׀ יִסַּ֬רְתָּ אִ֗ישׁ וַתֶּ֣מֶס כָּעָ֣שׁ חֲמוּד֑וֹ אַ֤ךְ הֶ֖בֶל כָּל־אָדָ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
Hear my prayer, LORD, and listen to my cry for help; do not be silent at my tears. For I am a foreigner with you, a temporary resident,[^9] like all my ancestors.
שִֽׁמְעָ֥ה־תְפִלָּתִ֨י ׀ יְהוָ֡ה וְשַׁוְעָתִ֨י ׀ הַאֲזִינָה֮ אֶֽל־דִּמְעָתִ֗י אַֽל־תֶּחֱ֫רַ֥שׁ כִּ֤י גֵ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י עִמָּ֑ךְ תּ֝וֹשָׁ֗ב כְּכָל־אֲבוֹתָֽי׃
Look away from me, so that I may smile again, before I go away and am no more."
הָשַׁ֣ע מִמֶּ֣נִּי וְאַבְלִ֑יגָה בְּטֶ֖רֶם אֵלֵ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶֽנִּי׃

n.1: One of David's chief musicians (1 Chronicles 16:41; 25:1).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–14 are 39:1–13 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "to no avail".
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: A handbreadth was about 3 inches (7.5 cm), the width of four fingers.
n.6: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", the word used throughout Ecclesiastes ("Vapor of vapors", Ecclesiastes 1:2). Also in verses 7 and 12.
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 12.
n.8: Literally "as an image".
n.9: Hebrew *ger* and *toshav*, a foreigner living in the land and a temporary resident, without the rights of a citizen (compare Leviticus 25:23; 1 Chronicles 29:15).

v: For the director. Of David. A psalm.[^1]
לַ֝מְנַצֵּ֗חַ לְדָוִ֥ד מִזְמֽוֹר׃
I waited patiently for the LORD;[^2] he turned to me and heard my cry for help.
קַוֺּ֣ה קִוִּ֣יתִי יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥ט אֵ֝לַ֗י וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע שַׁוְעָתִֽי׃
He drew me up from the pit of destruction,[^3] out of the miry clay; he set my feet on a rock and made my steps secure.
וַיַּעֲלֵ֤נִי ׀ מִבּ֥וֹר שָׁאוֹן֮ מִטִּ֢יט הַיָּ֫וֵ֥ן וַיָּ֖קֶם עַל־סֶ֥לַע רַגְלַ֗י כּוֹנֵ֥ן אֲשֻׁרָֽי׃
He put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Many will see and fear,[^4] and will trust in the LORD.
וַיִּתֵּ֬ן בְּפִ֨י ׀ שִׁ֥יר חָדָשׁ֮ תְּהִלָּ֢ה לֵֽאלֹ֫הֵ֥ינוּ יִרְא֣וּ רַבִּ֣ים וְיִירָ֑אוּ וְ֝יִבְטְח֗וּ בַּיהוָֽה׃
Happy[^5] is the one who makes the LORD his trust, who does not turn to the proud, or to those who go astray after lies.[^6]
אַ֥שְׁ֥רֵי הַגֶּ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם יְ֭הֹוָה מִבְטַח֑וֹ וְֽלֹא־פָנָ֥ה אֶל־רְ֝הָבִ֗ים וְשָׂטֵ֥י כָזָֽב׃
Many are the wonders you have done, LORD my God, and your plans for us; no one can compare with you.[^7] If I would proclaim them and speak of them, they are too many to count.
רַבּ֤וֹת עָשִׂ֨יתָ ׀ אַתָּ֤ה ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַי֮ נִ֥פְלְאֹתֶ֥יךָ וּמַחְשְׁבֹתֶ֗יךָ אֵ֫לֵ֥ינוּ אֵ֤ין ׀ עֲרֹ֬ךְ אֵלֶ֗יךָ אַגִּ֥ידָה וַאֲדַבֵּ֑רָה עָ֝צְמ֗וּ מִסַּפֵּֽר׃
Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but you have opened my ears;[^8] burnt offering and sin offering[^9] you did not ask for.
זֶ֤בַח וּמִנְחָ֨ה ׀ לֹֽא־חָפַ֗צְתָּ אָ֭זְנַיִם כָּרִ֣יתָ לִּ֑י עוֹלָ֥ה וַ֝חֲטָאָ֗ה לֹ֣א שָׁאָֽלְתָּ׃
Then I said, "Here I am, I have come; in the scroll of the book it is written about me.[^10]
אָ֣ז אָ֭מַרְתִּי הִנֵּה־בָ֑אתִי בִּמְגִלַּת־סֵ֝֗פֶר כָּת֥וּב עָלָֽי׃
I delight to do your will, my God; your law[^11] is within my heart."[^12]
לַֽעֲשֽׂוֹת־רְצוֹנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֣י חָפָ֑צְתִּי וְ֝ת֥וֹרָתְךָ֗ בְּת֣וֹךְ מֵעָֽי׃
I have proclaimed the good news[^13] of righteousness in the great assembly. See, I do not hold back my lips, LORD, as you know.
בִּשַּׂ֤רְתִּי צֶ֨דֶק ׀ בְּקָ֘הָ֤ל רָ֗ב הִנֵּ֣ה שְׂ֭פָתַי לֹ֣א אֶכְלָ֑א יְ֝הוָ֗ה אַתָּ֥ה יָדָֽעְתָּ׃
I have not hidden your righteousness within my heart; I have spoken of your faithfulness and your salvation. I have not concealed your faithful love and your truth[^14] from the great assembly.
צִדְקָתְךָ֬ לֹא־כִסִּ֨יתִי ׀ בְּת֬וֹךְ לִבִּ֗י אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ וּתְשׁוּעָתְךָ֣ אָמָ֑רְתִּי לֹא־כִחַ֥דְתִּי חַסְדְּךָ֥ וַ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ לְקָהָ֥ל רָֽב׃
You, LORD, will not withhold your compassion from me; your faithful love and your truth will always protect me.
אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָ֗ה לֹא־תִכְלָ֣א רַחֲמֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּ֑נִּי חַסְדְּךָ֥ וַ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ תָּמִ֥יד יִצְּרֽוּנִי׃
For evils without number have surrounded me; my sins have overtaken me, and I cannot see. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart fails me.
כִּ֤י אָפְפֽוּ־עָלַ֨י ׀ רָע֡וֹת עַד־אֵ֬ין מִסְפָּ֗ר הִשִּׂיג֣וּנִי עֲ֭וֺנֹתַי וְלֹא־יָכֹ֣לְתִּי לִרְא֑וֹת עָצְמ֥וּ מִשַּֽׂעֲר֥וֹת רֹ֝אשִׁ֗י וְלִבִּ֥י עֲזָבָֽנִי׃
Be pleased, LORD, to rescue me; LORD, come quickly to help me.[^15]
רְצֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לְהַצִּילֵ֑נִי יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי חֽוּשָׁה׃
Let those who seek my life,[^16] to sweep it away, be put to shame and confounded together; let those who delight in my harm be turned back and disgraced.
יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ וְיַחְפְּר֨וּ ׀ יַחַד֮ מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י לִסְפּ֫וֹתָ֥הּ יִסֹּ֣גוּ אָ֭חוֹר וְיִכָּלְמ֑וּ חֲ֝פֵצֵ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃
Let those who say to me, "Aha! Aha!" be appalled because of their shame.
יָ֭שֹׁמּוּ עַל־עֵ֣קֶב בָּשְׁתָּ֑ם הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לִ֝֗י הֶ֘אָ֥ח ׀ הֶאָֽח׃
But let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation say always, "Great is the LORD!"
יָ֘שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְיִשְׂמְח֨וּ ׀ בְּךָ֗ כָּֽל־מְבַ֫קְשֶׁ֥יךָ יֹאמְר֣וּ תָ֭מִיד יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה אֹֽ֝הֲבֵ֗י תְּשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
As for me, I am afflicted and needy; may the Lord think of me. You are my help and my deliverer; my God, do not delay.
וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְיוֹן֮ אֲדֹנָ֢י יַחֲשָׁ֫ב לִ֥י עֶזְרָתִ֣י וּמְפַלְטִ֣י אַ֑תָּה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אַל־תְּאַחַֽר׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–18 are 40:1–17 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *I waited patiently*: literally "I waited and waited".
n.3: Literally "the pit of roaring", perhaps of rushing water, or "of desolation".
n.4: In Hebrew "see" (*yir'u*) and "fear" (*yira'u*) sound alike.
n.5: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.6: Or "to false gods". Hebrew *rehavim*, "the proud", and *satei khazav*, "those who turn aside to falsehood", may both refer to idols and those who worship them.
n.7: Or "they cannot be set out in order before you".
n.8: Literally "ears you have dug for me", that is, you have made me able to hear and obey. Hebrews 10:5–7 quotes verses 7–9 from the Septuagint, which reads "but a body you have prepared for me".
n.9: Hebrew *chata'ah*, a form of *chatta't*. Or "purification offering".
n.10: Or "it is written for me", that is, prescribed for me.
n.11: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching".
n.12: Literally "in the middle of my inner parts".
n.13: Hebrew *bissarti*, "I brought good news". In the Septuagint this is *euangelizomai*, the verb behind "gospel".
n.14: Hebrew *chesed ve'emet*: loyal, faithful love and reliability, truth (compare 25:10). Also in verse 12.
n.15: Verses 14–18 appear again, with small differences, as Psalm 70:2–6 (70:1–5 in most English Bibles).
n.16: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.

v: For the director. A psalm of David.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
Happy[^2] is the one who considers the poor; in the day of trouble the LORD[^3] will rescue him.
אַ֭שְׁרֵי מַשְׂכִּ֣יל אֶל־דָּ֑ל בְּי֥וֹם רָ֝עָ֗ה יְֽמַלְּטֵ֥הוּ יְהוָֽה׃
The LORD will protect him and keep him alive; he will be called happy in the land. Do not hand him over to the will[^4] of his enemies!
יְהוָ֤ה ׀ יִשְׁמְרֵ֣הוּ וִֽ֭יחַיֵּהוּ *יאשר **וְאֻשַּׁ֣ר בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְאַֽל־תִּ֝תְּנֵ֗הוּ בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ אֹיְבָֽיו׃
The LORD will sustain him on his sickbed; in his illness you restore him to health.[^5]
יְֽהוָ֗ה יִ֭סְעָדֶנּוּ עַל־עֶ֣רֶשׂ דְּוָ֑י כָּל־מִ֝שְׁכָּב֗וֹ הָפַ֥כְתָּ בְחָלְיֽוֹ׃
As for me, I said, "LORD, be gracious to me; heal me,[^6] for I have sinned against you."
אֲ‍ֽנִי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי יְהוָ֣ה חָנֵּ֑נִי רְפָאָ֥ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י כִּי־חָטָ֥אתִי לָֽךְ׃
My enemies speak evil of me: "When will he die, and his name perish?"
אוֹיְבַ֗י יֹאמְר֣וּ רַ֣ע לִ֑י מָתַ֥י יָ֝מ֗וּת וְאָבַ֥ד שְׁמֽוֹ׃
When one of them comes to see me, he speaks empty words, while his heart gathers up mischief; he goes out and tells it abroad.
וְאִם־בָּ֤א לִרְא֨וֹת ׀ שָׁ֤וְא יְדַבֵּ֗ר לִבּ֗וֹ יִקְבָּץ־אָ֥וֶן ל֑וֹ יֵצֵ֖א לַח֣וּץ יְדַבֵּֽר׃
All who hate me whisper together against me; they imagine the worst for me:
יַ֗חַד עָלַ֣י יִ֭תְלַחֲשׁוּ כָּל־שֹׂנְאָ֑י עָלַ֓י ׀ יַחְשְׁב֖וּ רָעָ֣ה לִֽי׃
"A deadly thing[^7] has been poured into him; now that he lies down, he will not rise again."
דְּֽבַר־בְּ֭לִיַּעַל יָצ֣וּק בּ֑וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁ֝כַ֗ב לֹא־יוֹסִ֥יף לָקֽוּם׃
Even my close friend,[^8] whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.[^9]
גַּם־אִ֤ישׁ שְׁלוֹמִ֨י ׀ אֲשֶׁר־בָּטַ֣חְתִּי ב֭וֹ אוֹכֵ֣ל לַחְמִ֑י הִגְדִּ֖יל עָלַ֣י עָקֵֽב׃
But you, LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, so that I may repay them.
וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָ֗ה חָנֵּ֥נִי וַהֲקִימֵ֑נִי וַֽאֲשַׁלְּמָ֥ה לָהֶֽם׃
By this I know that you delight in me: that my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.
בְּזֹ֣את יָ֭דַעְתִּי כִּֽי־חָפַ֣צְתָּ בִּ֑י כִּ֤י לֹֽא־יָרִ֖יעַ אֹיְבִ֣י עָלָֽי׃
As for me, you uphold me in my integrity, and set me in your presence forever.
וַאֲנִ֗י בְּ֭תֻמִּי תָּמַ֣כְתָּ בִּ֑י וַתַּצִּיבֵ֖נִי לְפָנֶ֣יךָ לְעוֹלָֽם׃
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen.[^10]
בָּ֘ר֤וּךְ יְהוָ֨ה ׀ אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵֽ֭הָעוֹלָם וְעַ֥ד הָעוֹלָ֗ם אָ֘מֵ֥ן ׀ וְאָמֵֽן׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–14 are 41:1–13 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "the soul (*nephesh*)", that is, the desire.
n.5: Literally "all his bed you have turned in his sickness".
n.6: Literally "heal my soul (*nephesh*)".
n.7: Literally "a thing of *beliyya'al*", "worthlessness", here perhaps a deadly disease or a curse (compare 18:5; 18:4 in most English Bibles).
n.8: Literally "the man of my peace".
n.9: That is, has turned against me. John 13:18 quotes this line.
n.10: This blessing closes Book 1 of the Psalms (Psalms 1–41). Each of the next three books ends in a similar way (72:18–19; 89:53; 89:52 in most English Bibles; 106:48); compare 1 Chronicles 16:36.

v: For the director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לִבְנֵי־קֹֽרַח׃
As a deer[^2] longs for streams of water, so my soul[^3] longs for you, God.[^4]
כְּאַיָּ֗ל תַּעֲרֹ֥ג עַל־אֲפִֽיקֵי־מָ֑יִם כֵּ֤ן נַפְשִׁ֨י תַעֲרֹ֖ג אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When may I come and appear before God?[^5]
צָמְאָ֬ה נַפְשִׁ֨י ׀ לֵאלֹהִים֮ לְאֵ֢ל חָֽ[m]י מָתַ֥י אָב֑וֹא וְ֝אֵרָאֶ֗ה פְּנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים׃
My tears have been my food day and night, while people say to me all day long, "Where is your God?"
הָֽיְתָה־לִּ֬י דִמְעָתִ֣י לֶ֭חֶם יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה בֶּאֱמֹ֥ר אֵלַ֥י כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

These things I remember as I pour out my soul:[^6] how I used to go along with the throng,[^7] leading them in procession[^8] to the house of God, with shouts of joy and thanksgiving, a crowd keeping festival.
אֵ֤לֶּה אֶזְכְּרָ֨ה ׀ וְאֶשְׁפְּכָ֬ה עָלַ֨י ׀ נַפְשִׁ֗י כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר ׀ בַּסָּךְ֮ אֶדַּדֵּ֗ם עַד־בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים בְּקוֹל־רִנָּ֥ה וְתוֹדָ֗ה הָמ֥וֹן חוֹגֵֽג׃
Why are you downcast, my soul? Why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God, for I will yet praise him for the saving help of his presence.[^9]
מַה־תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י ׀ נַפְשִׁי֮ וַתֶּהֱמִ֢י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ע֥וֹד אוֹדֶ֗נּוּ יְשׁוּע֥וֹת פָּנָֽיו׃
My God, my soul is downcast within me; so I remember you from the land of the Jordan and the heights of Hermon,[^10] from Mount Mizar.
אֱ‍ֽלֹהַ֗י עָלַי֮ נַפְשִׁ֢י תִשְׁתּ֫וֹחָ֥ח עַל־כֵּ֗ן אֶ֭זְכָּרְךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יַרְדֵּ֑ן וְ֝חֶרְמוֹנִ֗ים מֵהַ֥ר מִצְעָֽר׃
Deep calls to deep at the roar of your waterfalls;[^11] all your breakers and your waves have swept over me.
תְּהֽוֹם־אֶל־תְּה֣וֹם ק֭וֹרֵא לְק֣וֹל צִנּוֹרֶ֑יךָ כָּֽל־מִשְׁבָּרֶ֥יךָ וְ֝גַלֶּ֗יךָ עָלַ֥י עָבָֽרוּ׃
By day the LORD[^12] commands his faithful love,[^13] and at night his song[^14] is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
יוֹמָ֤ם ׀ יְצַוֶּ֬ה יְהוָ֨ה ׀ חַסְדּ֗וֹ וּ֖[d]בַלַּיְלָה *שירה **שִׁיר֣וֹ עִמִּ֑י תְּ֝פִלָּ֗ה לְאֵ֣ל חַיָּֽי׃
I say to God, my rock, "Why have you forgotten me? Why must I go about in mourning,[^15] oppressed by the enemy?"
אוֹמְרָ֤ה ׀ לְאֵ֥ל סַלְעִי֮ לָמָ֢ה שְׁכַ֫חְתָּ֥נִי לָֽמָּה־קֹדֵ֥ר אֵלֵ֗ךְ בְּלַ֣חַץ אוֹיֵֽב׃
As if my bones were being crushed,[^16] my adversaries taunt me, saying to me all day long, "Where is your God?"
בְּרֶ֤צַח ׀ בְּֽעַצְמוֹתַ֗י חֵרְפ֥וּנִי צוֹרְרָ֑י בְּאָמְרָ֥ם אֵלַ֥י כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
Why are you downcast, my soul? Why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God, for I will yet praise him, my saving help[^17] and my God.
מַה־תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י ׀ נַפְשִׁי֮ וּֽמַה־תֶּהֱמִ֢י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֽ͏ֵ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ע֣וֹד אוֹדֶ֑נּוּ יְשׁוּעֹ֥ת פָּ֝נַ֗י וֵֽאלֹהָֽי׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers (2 Chronicles 20:19). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–12 are 42:1–11 in most English Bibles. Psalms 42 and 43 were probably once a single psalm: they share a refrain (42:6, 12; 43:5; 42:5, 11 in most English Bibles), Psalm 43 has no title of its own, and many Hebrew manuscripts write them as one.
n.2: The noun is masculine but the verb is feminine, so perhaps "a doe".
n.3: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 3, 5, 6, 7 and 12.
n.4: Psalms 42–83 are often called the "Elohistic Psalter". In them God is mostly called *Elohim*, "God", where other psalms use his personal name, YHWH ("the LORD"). Compare Psalm 53 with Psalm 14, and Psalm 70 with 40:14–18 (40:13–17 in most English Bibles), where the same lines appear with *Elohim* in place of the LORD. This translation renders each name as it stands.
n.5: The vowel points read "appear before God", the usual phrase for coming to worship at the sanctuary (Exodus 23:15; 34:23). The same consonants can be read "see the face of God".
n.6: Literally "I remember these things, and I pour out my soul upon me", that is, in grief.
n.7: Hebrew *sakh*, found only here, so the meaning is uncertain.
n.8: Hebrew *eddaddem*, an uncertain form, perhaps "I walked slowly with them".
n.9: Literally "the salvations of his face". In verse 12 and 43:5 the refrain ends "the salvation of my face and my God". The Septuagint has that wording here too, joining the first word of verse 7, "my God", to this verse.
n.10: Literally "the Hermons", the peaks of Mount Hermon near the sources of the Jordan in the far north. *Mizar* means "small"; the mountain is unknown.
n.11: Or "channels", "torrents". The word appears elsewhere only in 2 Samuel 5:8.
n.12: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.13: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.14: The Hebrew text is written "a song" but read "his song".
n.15: Literally "dark", wearing the dark clothes of mourning.
n.16: Literally "With a shattering in my bones".
n.17: Literally "the salvation of my face".

v: Vindicate me, God,[^1] and plead my case against an unfaithful nation;[^2] rescue me from the deceitful and unjust.[^3]
שָׁפְטֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהִ֨ים ׀ וְרִ֘יבָ֤ה רִיבִ֗י מִגּ֥וֹי לֹא־חָסִ֑יד מֵ֤אִישׁ־מִרְמָ֖ה וְעַוְלָ֣ה תְפַלְּטֵֽנִי׃
For you are God my stronghold. Why have you rejected me? Why must I go about in mourning,[^4] oppressed by the enemy?
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה ׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י מָֽעוּזִּי֮ לָמָ֢ה זְנַ֫חְתָּ֥נִי לָֽמָּה־קֹדֵ֥ר אֶתְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּלַ֣חַץ אוֹיֵֽב׃
Send out your light and your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to your holy mountain, to the place where you dwell.[^5]
שְׁלַח־אוֹרְךָ֣ וַ֭אֲמִתְּךָ הֵ֣מָּה יַנְח֑וּנִי יְבִיא֥וּנִי אֶל־הַֽר־קָ֝דְשְׁךָ֗ וְאֶל־מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my joy and my delight,[^6] and I will praise you with the lyre, God, my God.
וְאָב֤וֹאָה ׀ אֶל־מִזְבַּ֬ח אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל־אֵל֮ שִׂמְחַ֢ת גִּ֫ילִ֥י וְאוֹדְךָ֥ בְכִנּ֗וֹר אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֱלֹהָֽי׃
Why are you downcast, my soul?[^7] Why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God, for I will yet praise him, my saving help[^8] and my God.
מַה־תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י ׀ נַפְשִׁי֮ וּֽמַה־תֶּהֱמִ֢י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֽ͏ֵ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ע֣וֹד אוֹדֶ֑נּוּ יְשׁוּעֹ֥ת פָּ֝נַ֗י וֵֽאלֹהָֽי׃

n.1: Psalm 43 has no title, and its refrain (verse 5) is the refrain of Psalm 42 (42:6, 12; 42:5, 11 in most English Bibles). The two were probably once a single psalm.
n.2: Hebrew *lo-chasid*, "not faithful", that is, ungodly. *Chasid* is related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.3: Literally "from a man of deceit and injustice".
n.4: Literally "dark", wearing the dark clothes of mourning.
n.5: Literally "to your dwellings".
n.6: Literally "the joy of my rejoicing".
n.7: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.8: Literally "the salvation of my face".

v: For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ לִבְנֵי־קֹ֬רַח מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
God, we have heard with our own ears; our ancestors have told us the work you did in their days, in the days of old.
אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ בְּאָזְנֵ֬ינוּ שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֥ינוּ סִפְּרוּ־לָ֑נוּ פֹּ֥עַל פָּעַ֥לְתָּ בִֽ֝ימֵיהֶ֗ם בִּ֣ימֵי קֶֽדֶם׃
With your own hand you drove out nations, but them you planted; you brought disaster on peoples, but them you set free.[^2]
אַתָּ֤ה ׀ יָדְךָ֡ גּוֹיִ֣ם ה֭וֹרַשְׁתָּ וַתִּטָּעֵ֑ם תָּרַ֥ע לְ֝אֻמִּ֗ים וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵֽם׃
For it was not by their sword that they took the land, and their own arm did not give them victory; it was your right hand and your arm and the light of your face, because you delighted in them.
כִּ֤י לֹ֤א בְחַרְבָּ֡ם יָ֥רְשׁוּ אָ֗רֶץ וּזְרוֹעָם֮ לֹא־הוֹשִׁ֢יעָ֫ה לָּ֥מוֹ כִּֽי־יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וּ֭זְרוֹעֲךָ וְא֥וֹר פָּנֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣י רְצִיתָֽם׃
You are my King, God; command victories[^3] for Jacob.
אַתָּה־ה֣וּא מַלְכִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים צַ֝וֵּ֗ה יְשׁוּע֥וֹת יַעֲקֹֽב׃
Through you we gore our adversaries; through your name we trample those who rise up against us.
בְּ֭ךָ צָרֵ֣ינוּ נְנַגֵּ֑חַ בְּ֝שִׁמְךָ֗ נָב֥וּס קָמֵֽינוּ׃
For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword does not save me.
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א בְקַשְׁתִּ֣י אֶבְטָ֑ח וְ֝חַרְבִּ֗י לֹ֣א תוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃
But you have saved us from our adversaries, and you have put those who hate us to shame.
כִּ֣י ה֭וֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ מִצָּרֵ֑ינוּ וּמְשַׂנְאֵ֥ינוּ הֱבִישֽׁוֹתָ׃
In God we have boasted all day long, and we will praise your name forever. Selah.[^4]
בֵּֽ֭אלֹהִים הִלַּלְ֣נוּ כָל־הַיּ֑וֹם וְשִׁמְךָ֓ ׀ לְעוֹלָ֖ם נוֹדֶ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃
Yet you have rejected us and humiliated us; you no longer go out with our armies.
אַף־זָ֭נַחְתָּ וַתַּכְלִימֵ֑נוּ וְלֹא־תֵ֝צֵ֗א בְּצִבְאוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
You make us turn back from the adversary, and those who hate us take plunder for themselves.
תְּשִׁיבֵ֣נוּ אָ֭חוֹר מִנִּי־צָ֑ר וּ֝מְשַׂנְאֵ֗ינוּ שָׁ֣סוּ לָֽמוֹ׃
You hand us over like sheep to be eaten, and you have scattered us among the nations.
תִּ֭תְּנֵנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן מַאֲכָ֑ל וּ֝בַגּוֹיִ֗ם זֵרִיתָֽנוּ׃
You sell your people for nothing; you make no profit from their price.
תִּמְכֹּֽר־עַמְּךָ֥ בְלֹא־ה֑וֹן וְלֹֽא־רִ֝בִּ֗יתָ בִּמְחִירֵיהֶֽם׃
You make us a disgrace to our neighbors, the scorn and mockery of those around us.
תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ חֶ֭רְפָּה לִשְׁכֵנֵ֑ינוּ לַ֥עַג וָ֝קֶ֗לֶס לִסְבִיבוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
You make us a byword among the nations; the peoples shake their heads at us.
תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ מָ֭שָׁל בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם מְנֽוֹד־רֹ֝֗אשׁ בַּל־אֻמִּֽים׃
All day long my disgrace is before me, and the shame of my face has covered me,
כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם כְּלִמָּתִ֣י נֶגְדִּ֑י וּבֹ֖שֶׁת פָּנַ֣י כִּסָּֽתְנִי׃
at the voice of the one who taunts and reviles, at the sight of the enemy and the avenger.
מִ֭קּוֹל מְחָרֵ֣ף וּמְגַדֵּ֑ף מִפְּנֵ֥י א֝וֹיֵ֗ב וּמִתְנַקֵּֽם׃
All this has come upon us, though we have not forgotten you or been false to your covenant.
כָּל־זֹ֣את בָּ֭אַתְנוּ וְלֹ֣א שְׁכַחֲנ֑וּךָ וְלֹֽא־שִׁ֝קַּ֗רְנוּ בִּבְרִיתֶֽךָ׃
Our hearts have not turned back, and our steps have not strayed from your path.
לֹא־נָס֣וֹג אָח֣וֹר לִבֵּ֑נוּ וַתֵּ֥ט אֲ֝שֻׁרֵ֗ינוּ מִנִּ֥י אָרְחֶֽךָ׃
Yet you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals, and covered us with deep darkness.[^5]
כִּ֣י דִ֭כִּיתָנוּ בִּמְק֣וֹם תַּנִּ֑ים וַתְּכַ֖ס עָלֵ֣ינוּ בְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃
If we had forgotten the name of our God, or spread out our hands to a foreign god,
אִם־שָׁ֭כַחְנוּ שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַנִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּ֝פֵּ֗ינוּ לְאֵ֣ל זָֽר׃
would not God have searched this out? For he knows the secrets of the heart.
הֲלֹ֣א אֱ֭לֹהִים יַֽחֲקָר־זֹ֑את כִּֽי־ה֥וּא יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ תַּעֲלֻמ֥וֹת לֵֽב׃
Yet for your sake we are killed all day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.[^6]
כִּֽי־עָ֭לֶיךָ הֹרַ֣גְנוּ כָל־הַיּ֑וֹם נֶ֝חְשַׁ֗בְנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן טִבְחָֽה׃
Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord? Rouse yourself! Do not reject us forever.
ע֤וּרָה ׀ לָ֖מָּה תִישַׁ֥ן ׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י הָ֝קִ֗יצָה אַל־תִּזְנַ֥ח לָנֶֽצַח׃
Why do you hide your face, and forget our affliction and our oppression?
לָֽמָּה־פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר תִּשְׁכַּ֖ח עָנְיֵ֣נוּ וְֽלַחֲצֵֽנוּ׃
For we have sunk down to the dust; our bodies cling to the ground.[^7]
כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה לֶעָפָ֣ר נַפְשֵׁ֑נוּ דָּבְקָ֖ה לָאָ֣רֶץ בִּטְנֵֽנוּ׃
Rise up and help us! Redeem us for the sake of your faithful love.[^8]
ק֭וּמָֽה עֶזְרָ֣תָה לָּ֑נוּ וּ֝פְדֵ֗נוּ לְמַ֣עַן חַסְדֶּֽךָ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–27 are 44:1–26 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *Them*: our ancestors (verse 2). *Set free*: or "let spread out", like a vine sending out its branches (compare 80:12; 80:11 in most English Bibles).
n.3: Literally "salvations".
n.4: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.5: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.6: Romans 8:36 quotes this verse.
n.7: Literally "For our soul (*nephesh*) is bowed down to the dust; our belly clings to the ground."
n.8: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.

v: For the director. According to "Lilies".[^1] Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A love song.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ עַל־שֹׁ֭שַׁנִּים לִבְנֵי־קֹ֑רַח מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל שִׁ֣יר יְדִידֹֽת׃
My heart overflows with a good theme;[^3] I speak my verses for the king;[^4] my tongue is the pen of a skillful scribe.
רָ֘חַ֤שׁ לִבִּ֨י ׀ דָּ֘בָ֤ר ט֗וֹב אֹמֵ֣ר אָ֭נִי מַעֲשַׂ֣י לְמֶ֑לֶךְ לְ֝שׁוֹנִ֗י עֵ֤ט ׀ סוֹפֵ֬ר מָהִֽיר׃
You are the most handsome of all human beings; grace has been poured on your lips; so God has blessed you forever.
יָפְיָפִ֡יתָ מִבְּנֵ֬י אָדָ֗ם ה֣וּצַק חֵ֭ן בְּשְׂפְתוֹתֶ֑יךָ עַל־כֵּ֤ן בֵּֽרַכְךָ֖ אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְעוֹלָֽם׃
Strap your sword on your thigh, mighty warrior, in your splendor and your majesty.
חֲגֽוֹר־חַרְבְּךָ֣ עַל־יָרֵ֣ךְ גִּבּ֑וֹר ה֝וֹדְךָ֗ וַהֲדָרֶֽךָ׃
In your majesty ride on to victory[^5] for the cause of truth and humility and righteousness;[^6] let your right hand teach you awesome deeds.
וַהֲדָ֬רְךָ֨ ׀ צְלַ֬ח רְכַ֗ב עַֽל־דְּבַר־אֱ֭מֶת וְעַנְוָה־צֶ֑דֶק וְתוֹרְךָ֖ נוֹרָא֣וֹת יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
Your arrows are sharp in the hearts of the king's enemies; peoples fall beneath you.[^7]
חִצֶּ֗יךָ שְׁנ֫וּנִ֥ים עַ֭מִּים תַּחְתֶּ֣יךָ יִפְּל֑וּ בְּ֝לֵ֗ב אוֹיְבֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
Your throne, God, is forever and ever;[^8] the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of justice.[^9]
כִּסְאֲךָ֣ אֱ֭לֹהִים עוֹלָ֣ם וָעֶ֑ד שֵׁ֥בֶט מִ֝ישֹׁ֗ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַלְכוּתֶֽךָ׃
You love righteousness and hate wickedness; so God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.[^10]
אָהַ֣בְתָּ צֶּדֶק֮ וַתִּשְׂנָ֫א רֶ֥שַׁע עַל־כֵּ֤ן ׀ מְשָׁחֲךָ֡ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֱ֭לֹהֶיךָ שֶׁ֥מֶן שָׂשׂ֗וֹן מֵֽחֲבֵרֶֽיךָ׃
All your robes are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia; from ivory palaces the music of strings[^11] makes you glad.
מֹר־וַאֲהָל֣וֹת קְ֭צִיעוֹת כָּל־בִּגְדֹתֶ֑יךָ מִֽן־הֵ֥יכְלֵי שֵׁ֝֗ן מִנִּ֥י שִׂמְּחֽוּךָ׃
Daughters of kings are among your honored women; at your right hand stands the queen[^12] in gold of Ophir.[^13]
בְּנ֣וֹת מְ֭לָכִים בְּיִקְּרוֹתֶ֑יךָ נִצְּבָ֥ה שֵׁגַ֥ל לִֽ֝ימִינְךָ֗ בְּכֶ֣תֶם אוֹפִֽיר׃
Listen, daughter, consider and turn your ear: forget your people and your father's house.
שִׁמְעִי־בַ֣ת וּ֭רְאִי וְהַטִּ֣י אָזְנֵ֑ךְ וְשִׁכְחִ֥י עַ֝מֵּ֗ךְ וּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיךְ׃
Then the king will desire your beauty. He is your lord, so bow down to him.
וְיִתְאָ֣ו הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יָפְיֵ֑ךְ כִּי־ה֥וּא אֲ֝דֹנַ֗יִךְ וְהִשְׁתַּֽחֲוִי־לֽוֹ׃
The daughter of Tyre[^14] comes with a gift; the richest of the people seek your favor.
וּבַֽת־צֹ֨ר ׀ בְּ֭מִנְחָה פָּנַ֥יִךְ יְחַלּ֗וּ עֲשִׁ֣ירֵי עָֽם׃
The king's daughter is all glorious within;[^15] her clothing is woven with gold.
כָּל־כְּבוּדָּ֣ה בַת־מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּנִ֑ימָה מִֽמִּשְׁבְּצ֖וֹת זָהָ֣ב לְבוּשָֽׁהּ׃
In embroidered robes she is led to the king; the young women, her companions, follow her; they are brought to you.
לִרְקָמוֹת֮ תּוּבַ֢ל לַ֫מֶּ֥לֶךְ בְּתוּל֣וֹת אַ֭חֲרֶיהָ רֵעוֹתֶ֑יהָ מ֖וּבָא֣וֹת לָֽךְ׃
They are led in with gladness and rejoicing; they enter the palace of the king.
תּ֭וּבַלְנָה בִּשְׂמָחֹ֣ת וָגִ֑יל תְּ֝בֹאֶ֗ינָה בְּהֵ֣יכַל מֶֽלֶךְ׃
Your sons will take the place of your ancestors; you will make them princes throughout the land.[^16]
תַּ֣חַת אֲ֭בֹתֶיךָ יִהְי֣וּ בָנֶ֑יךָ תְּשִׁיתֵ֥מוֹ לְ֝שָׂרִ֗ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
I will make your name remembered in every generation; so the peoples will praise you forever and ever.
אַזְכִּ֣ירָה שִׁ֭מְךָ בְּכָל־דֹּ֣ר וָדֹ֑ר עַל־כֵּ֥ן עַמִּ֥ים יְ֝הוֹדֻ֗ךָ לְעֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-shoshannim*, "according to lilies", probably the name of a tune.
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *A love song*: literally "a song of loves", perhaps "a wedding song". The psalm celebrates a king's wedding. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–18 are 45:1–17 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "a good word".
n.4: Literally "I say my works to the king".
n.5: Literally "succeed, ride". The verse begins "And your majesty", repeating the last word of verse 4.
n.6: Literally "for the word of truth, and humility of righteousness". The Hebrew is compressed.
n.7: The Hebrew order is "Your arrows are sharp, peoples fall beneath you, in the heart of the king's enemies".
n.8: The Hebrew *kis'akha elohim* most naturally means "Your throne, God", addressing the king as *elohim*, "God". No other Israelite king is called this, though compare Isaiah 9:5 (9:6 in most English Bibles), where the royal child is called "Mighty God" (*el gibbor*). Other possible readings are "Your throne is God's throne forever" (compare 1 Chronicles 29:23, "Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king") and "Your throne is like God's, forever". Verse 8 distinguishes the king from "God, your God". The Septuagint reads "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever", and Hebrews 1:8–9 quotes verses 7–8 in that form, applying them to the Son.
n.9: Or "of uprightness".
n.10: Or "so, God, your God has anointed you", continuing to address the king. Hebrew *meshachakha*, "has anointed you", from the same root as *mashiach*, "anointed one".
n.11: Hebrew *minni*, probably "strings" (compare 150:4).
n.12: Hebrew *shegal*, the king's consort.
n.13: A land famous for its fine gold (1 Kings 9:28).
n.14: That is, the people of Tyre, or perhaps a princess of Tyre.
n.15: That is, inside the palace, or in her chamber.
n.16: Or "in all the earth".

v: For the director. Of the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth.[^1] A song.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ לִבְנֵי־קֹ֑רַח עַֽל־עֲלָמ֥וֹת שִֽׁיר׃
God is our refuge and strength, a help in trouble, always ready to be found.[^3]
אֱלֹהִ֣ים לָ֭נוּ מַחֲסֶ֣ה וָעֹ֑ז עֶזְרָ֥ה בְ֝צָר֗וֹת נִמְצָ֥א מְאֹֽד׃
So we will not fear, though the earth gives way, though the mountains topple into the heart of the seas,
עַל־כֵּ֣ן לֹא־נִ֭ירָא בְּהָמִ֣יר אָ֑רֶץ וּבְמ֥וֹט הָ֝רִ֗ים בְּלֵ֣ב יַמִּֽים׃
though its waters roar and foam, and the mountains quake at its surging. Selah.[^4]
יֶהֱמ֣וּ יֶחְמְר֣וּ מֵימָ֑יו יִֽרְעֲשֽׁוּ־הָרִ֖ים בְּגַאֲוָת֣וֹ סֶֽלָה׃
There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy dwelling place of the Most High.[^5]
נָהָ֗ר פְּלָגָ֗יו יְשַׂמְּח֥וּ עִיר־אֱלֹהִ֑ים קְ֝דֹ֗שׁ מִשְׁכְּנֵ֥י עֶלְיֽוֹן׃
God is in her midst; she will not be shaken. God will help her at the break of day.[^6]
אֱלֹהִ֣ים בְּ֭קִרְבָּה בַּל־תִּמּ֑וֹט יַעְזְרֶ֥הָ אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לִפְנ֥וֹת בֹּֽקֶר׃
Nations roar, kingdoms totter; he raises his voice, and the earth melts.
הָמ֣וּ ג֭וֹיִם מָ֣טוּ מַמְלָכ֑וֹת נָתַ֥ן בְּ֝קוֹל֗וֹ תָּמ֥וּג אָֽרֶץ׃
The LORD of Armies[^7] is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.
יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֣וֹת עִמָּ֑נוּ מִשְׂגָּֽב־לָ֝נוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
Come, see the works of the LORD, the desolations[^8] he has brought on the earth.
לְֽכוּ־חֲ֭זוּ מִפְעֲל֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֖ם שַׁמּ֣וֹת בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
He makes wars cease to the end of the earth; he breaks the bow and snaps the spear; he burns the chariots[^9] with fire.
מַשְׁבִּ֥ית מִלְחָמוֹת֮ עַד־קְצֵ֢ה הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ קֶ֣שֶׁת יְ֭שַׁבֵּר וְקִצֵּ֣ץ חֲנִ֑ית עֲ֝גָל֗וֹת יִשְׂרֹ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
Be still,[^10] and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations; I will be exalted in the earth.
הַרְפּ֣וּ וּ֭דְעוּ כִּי־אָנֹכִ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים אָר֥וּם בַּ֝גּוֹיִ֗ם אָר֥וּם בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
The LORD of Armies is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah.
יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֣וֹת עִמָּ֑נוּ מִשְׂגָּֽב־לָ֝[t]נוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-alamot*, a musical term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "for soprano voices" (compare 1 Chronicles 15:20).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–12 are 46:1–11 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "a help in troubles, found very much".
n.4: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verses 8 and 12.
n.5: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God. Literally "the holy place of the dwellings of the Most High".
n.6: Literally "at the turning of the morning".
n.7: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 12.
n.8: Or "the astonishing deeds".
n.9: Hebrew *agalot*, "carts, wagons". The Septuagint reads "shields".
n.10: Or "Stop!", "Let go!"

v: For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ ׀ לִבְנֵי־קֹ֬רַח מִזְמֽוֹר׃
Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout to God with loud songs of joy.
כָּֽל־הָ֭עַמִּים תִּקְעוּ־כָ֑ף הָרִ֥יעוּ לֵ֝אלֹהִ֗ים בְּק֣וֹל רִנָּֽה׃
For the LORD,[^2] the Most High,[^3] is awesome, a great King over all the earth.
כִּֽי־יְהוָ֣ה עֶלְי֣וֹן נוֹרָ֑א מֶ֥לֶךְ גָּ֝דוֹל עַל־כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
He subdues peoples under us, and nations under our feet.
יַדְבֵּ֣ר עַמִּ֣ים תַּחְתֵּ֑ינוּ וּ֝לְאֻמִּ֗ים תַּ֣חַת רַגְלֵֽינוּ׃
He chose our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom he loves. Selah.[^4]
יִבְחַר־לָ֥נוּ אֶת־נַחֲלָתֵ֑נוּ אֶֽ[m]ת גְּא֨וֹן יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲשֶׁר־אָהֵ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of the ram's horn.[^5]
עָלָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה בְּק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃
Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises.
זַמְּר֣וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים זַמֵּ֑רוּ זַמְּר֖וּ לְמַלְכֵּ֣נוּ זַמֵּֽרוּ׃
For God is the King of all the earth; sing praises with a skillful psalm.[^6]
כִּ֤י מֶ֖לֶךְ כָּל־הָאָ֥רֶץ אֱלֹהִ֗ים זַמְּר֥וּ מַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
God reigns over the nations; God sits on his holy throne.
מָלַ֣ךְ אֱ֭לֹהִים עַל־גּוֹיִ֑ם אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים יָשַׁ֤ב ׀ עַל־כִּסֵּ֬א קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
The nobles of the peoples have gathered as the people of the God of Abraham.[^7] For the shields of the earth[^8] belong to God; he is highly exalted.
נְדִ֘יבֵ֤י עַמִּ֨ים ׀ נֶאֱסָ֗פוּ עַם֮ אֱלֹהֵ֢י אַבְרָ֫הָ֥ם כִּ֣י לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים מָֽגִנֵּי־אֶ֗רֶץ מְאֹ֣ד נַעֲלָֽה׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–10 are 47:1–9 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.4: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.5: Hebrew *shofar*.
n.6: Hebrew *maskil*, the term found in the titles of some psalms (see 42:1).
n.7: The Septuagint reads "with the God of Abraham".
n.8: That is, the rulers who protect the earth's peoples.

v: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.[^1]
שִׁ֥יר מִ֝זְמוֹר לִבְנֵי־קֹֽרַח׃
Great is the LORD,[^2] and most worthy of praise, in the city of our God, his holy mountain.
גָּ֘ד֤וֹל יְהוָ֣ה וּמְהֻלָּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד בְּעִ֥יר אֱ֝לֹהֵ֗ינוּ הַר־קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
Beautiful in its height, the joy of all the earth, is Mount Zion, the heights of Zaphon,[^3] the city of the great King.
יְפֵ֥ה נוֹף֮ מְשׂ֢וֹשׂ כָּל־הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ הַר־צִ֭יּוֹן יַרְכְּתֵ֣י צָפ֑וֹן קִ֝רְיַ֗ת מֶ֣לֶךְ רָֽב׃
God, in her citadels, has shown himself a fortress.
אֱלֹהִ֥ים בְּאַרְמְנוֹתֶ֗יהָ נוֹדַ֥ע לְמִשְׂגָּֽב׃
For see, the kings assembled; they advanced together.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה הַ֭מְּלָכִים נֽוֹעֲד֑וּ עָבְר֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃
They saw, and they were astounded; they were terrified and fled in haste.
הֵ֣מָּה רָ֭אוּ כֵּ֣ן תָּמָ֑הוּ נִבְהֲל֥וּ נֶחְפָּֽזוּ׃
Trembling seized them there, pain like a woman in labor.
רְ֭עָדָה אֲחָזָ֣תַם שָׁ֑ם חִ֝֗יל כַּיּוֹלֵֽדָה׃
With an east wind you shatter the ships of Tarshish.[^4]
בְּר֥וּחַ קָדִ֑ים תְּ֝שַׁבֵּ֗ר אֳנִיּ֥וֹת תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ׃
As we have heard, so we have seen, in the city of the LORD of Armies,[^5] in the city of our God: God will establish it forever. Selah.[^6]
כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֨עְנוּ ׀ כֵּ֤ן רָאִ֗ינוּ בְּעִיר־יְהוָ֣ה צְ֭בָאוֹת בְּעִ֣יר אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ אֱלֹ֘הִ֤ים יְכוֹנְנֶ֖הָ עַד־עוֹלָ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
We ponder your faithful love,[^7] God, within your temple.
דִּמִּ֣ינוּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ בְּ֝קֶ֗רֶב הֵיכָלֶֽךָ׃
Like your name, God, your praise reaches to the ends of the earth; your right hand is full of righteousness.
כְּשִׁמְךָ֤ אֱלֹהִ֗ים כֵּ֣ן תְּ֭הִלָּתְךָ עַל־קַצְוֵי־אֶ֑רֶץ צֶ֝֗דֶק מָלְאָ֥ה יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
Let Mount Zion rejoice; let the daughters of Judah[^8] be glad because of your judgments.
יִשְׂמַ֤ח ׀ הַר־צִיּ֗וֹן תָּ֭גֵלְנָה בְּנ֣וֹת יְהוּדָ֑ה לְ֝מַ֗עַן מִשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ׃
Walk around Zion, go all around her; count her towers.
סֹ֣בּוּ צִ֭יּוֹן וְהַקִּיפ֑וּהָ סִ֝פְר֗וּ מִגְדָּלֶֽיהָ׃
Consider well her ramparts; pass through her citadels,[^9] so that you may tell the next generation
שִׁ֤יתוּ לִבְּכֶ֨ם ׀ לְֽחֵילָ֗ה פַּסְּג֥וּ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ לְמַ֥עַן תְּ֝סַפְּר֗וּ לְד֣וֹר אַחֲרֽוֹן׃
that this is God, our God, forever and ever. He will guide us until death.[^10]
כִּ֤י זֶ֨ה ׀ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֱ֭לֹהֵינוּ עוֹלָ֣ם וָעֶ֑ד ה֖וּא יְנַהֲגֵ֣נוּ עַל־מֽוּת׃

n.1: *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–15 are 48:1–14 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "in the far north". *Tsaphon*, "north", was also the name of a mountain in Syria where Canaanite myth placed the home of the gods (compare Isaiah 14:13).
n.4: Large seagoing ships.
n.5: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.6: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.7: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.8: That is, the towns of Judah.
n.9: Hebrew *passegu*, found only here; the meaning is uncertain, perhaps "view".
n.10: Hebrew *al-mut*, "until death" or "over death". The Septuagint reads "forever". Some scholars take the words as a musical direction, like *almut labben* in the title of Psalm 9.

v: For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ ׀ לִבְנֵי־קֹ֬רַח מִזְמֽוֹר׃
Hear this, all you peoples; listen, all who live in the world,
שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֭את כָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינוּ כָּל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי חָֽלֶד׃
both low and high,[^2] rich and poor together.
גַּם־בְּנֵ֣י אָ֭דָם גַּם־בְּנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ יַ֝֗חַד עָשִׁ֥יר וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
My mouth will speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will be understanding.
פִּ֭י יְדַבֵּ֣ר חָכְמ֑וֹת וְהָג֖וּת לִבִּ֣י תְבוּנֽוֹת׃
I will turn my ear to a proverb;[^3] I will set out my riddle to the music of the lyre.
אַטֶּ֣ה לְמָשָׁ֣ל אָזְנִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֥ח בְּ֝כִנּ֗וֹר חִידָתֽ͏ִי׃
Why should I be afraid in days of trouble, when the wickedness of those who dog my steps[^4] surrounds me,
לָ֣מָּה אִ֭ירָא בִּ֣ימֵי רָ֑ע עֲוֺ֖ן עֲקֵבַ֣י יְסוּבֵּֽנִי׃
those who trust in their wealth and boast of their great riches?
הַבֹּטְחִ֥ים עַל־חֵילָ֑ם וּבְרֹ֥ב עָ֝שְׁרָ֗ם יִתְהַלָּֽלוּ׃
No one can ever ransom a brother,[^5] or pay God the price for his life.
אָ֗ח לֹא־פָדֹ֣ה יִפְדֶּ֣ה אִ֑ישׁ לֹא־יִתֵּ֖ן לֵאלֹהִ֣ים כָּפְרֽוֹ׃
For the ransom of their life[^6] is costly, and it will always fall short,[^7]
וְ֭יֵקַר פִּדְי֥וֹן נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְחָדַ֥ל לְעוֹלָֽם׃
that one should live on forever and never see the pit.[^8]
וִֽיחִי־ע֥וֹד לָנֶ֑צַח לֹ֖א יִרְאֶ֣ה הַשָּֽׁחַת׃
For one sees that the wise die; the fool and the senseless perish together, and leave their wealth to others.
כִּ֤י יִרְאֶ֨ה ׀ חֲכָ֘מִ֤ים יָמ֗וּתוּ יַ֤חַד כְּסִ֣יל וָבַ֣עַר יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וְעָזְב֖וּ לַאֲחֵרִ֣ים חֵילָֽם׃
Their inner thought is that their houses will last forever,[^9] their dwellings for all generations; they have named lands after themselves.
קִרְבָּ֤ם בָּתֵּ֨ימוֹ ׀ לְֽעוֹלָ֗ם מִ֭שְׁכְּנֹתָם לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹ֑ר קָֽרְא֥וּ בִ֝שְׁמוֹתָ֗ם עֲלֵ֣י אֲדָמֽוֹת׃
But a human being in his splendor does not endure;[^10] he is like the animals that perish.
וְאָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר בַּל־יָלִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ׃
This is the way of those who are foolishly confident, and of those after them who delight in their words.[^11] Selah.[^12]
זֶ֣ה דַ֭רְכָּם כֵּ֣סֶל לָ֑מוֹ וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֓ם ׀ בְּפִיהֶ֖ם יִרְצ֣וּ סֶֽלָה׃

Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol;[^13] death will be their shepherd. The upright will rule over them in the morning, and their form[^14] will waste away in Sheol, far from its lofty dwelling.[^15]
כַּצֹּ֤אן ׀ לִֽשְׁא֣וֹל שַׁתּוּ֮ מָ֤וֶת יִ֫רְעֵ֥ם וַיִּרְדּ֘וּ בָ֤ם יְשָׁרִ֨ים ׀ לַבֹּ֗קֶר *וצירם **וְ֭צוּרָם לְבַלּ֥וֹת שְׁא֗וֹל מִזְּבֻ֥ל לֽוֹ׃
But God will redeem my life from the power of Sheol,[^16] for he will take me.[^17] Selah.
אַךְ־אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִפְדֶּ֣ה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִֽיַּד־שְׁא֑וֹל כִּ֖י יִקָּחֵ֣נִי סֶֽלָה׃
Do not be afraid when someone grows rich, when the glory of his house increases;
אַל־תִּ֭ירָא כִּֽי־יַעֲשִׁ֣ר אִ֑ישׁ כִּֽי־יִ֝רְבֶּה כְּב֣וֹד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
for when he dies he will take nothing with him; his glory will not go down after him.
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א בְ֭מוֹתוֹ יִקַּ֣ח הַכֹּ֑ל לֹא־יֵרֵ֖ד אַחֲרָ֣יו כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃
Though in his lifetime he congratulates himself,[^18] and people praise you when you do well for yourself,
כִּֽי־נַ֭פְשׁוֹ בְּחַיָּ֣יו יְבָרֵ֑ךְ וְ֝יוֹדֻ֗ךָ כִּי־תֵיטִ֥יב לָֽךְ׃
he will go to the generation of his ancestors,[^19] who will never see the light.
תָּ֭בוֹא עַד־דּ֣וֹר אֲבוֹתָ֑יו עַד־נֵ֝֗צַח לֹ֣א יִרְאוּ־אֽוֹר׃
A human being in his splendor, without understanding, is like the animals that perish.[^20]
אָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–21 are 49:1–20 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "both sons of *adam* and sons of *ish*", two words for "man", perhaps common people and people of rank.
n.3: Hebrew *mashal*, a saying, parable or poem.
n.4: Literally "the iniquity of my heels", probably those who follow at my heels. Or "my deceivers", a word from the same root (compare Genesis 27:36).
n.5: Literally "A brother, a man surely cannot ransom".
n.6: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 16 and 19.
n.7: Literally "and it ceases forever". Or "and one must give it up forever".
n.8: Hebrew *shachat*, "pit", a name for the grave and the realm of the dead.
n.9: Literally "Their inward part: their houses forever". The Septuagint reads "Their graves are their homes forever", reading *qibram*, "their grave", for *qirbam*, "their inward part", with two letters reversed.
n.10: Literally "does not spend the night". Verse 21, the refrain, reads "without understanding" (*velo yavin*) where this verse has "does not endure" (*bal yalin*).
n.11: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "This is their way, folly is theirs, and after them with their mouth they are pleased".
n.12: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 16.
n.13: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. Also in verse 16.
n.14: The Hebrew text is written *tsiram*, perhaps "their image", but read *tsuram*, "their form".
n.15: The Hebrew of the second half of this verse is difficult. Literally "and their form is for Sheol to wear out, from a dwelling for it".
n.16: Literally "from the hand of Sheol".
n.17: The same verb is used when God "took" Enoch (Genesis 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3, 5). Compare 73:24.
n.19: Or "you will go to the generation of your ancestors", or "it (his soul) will go".

v: A psalm of Asaph.[^1] The Mighty One, God, the LORD,[^2] has spoken and summoned the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף אֵ֤ל ׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֡ים יְֽהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּ֥ר וַיִּקְרָא־אָ֑רֶץ מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֝֗מֶשׁ עַד־מְבֹאֽוֹ׃
Out of Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines out.
מִצִיּ֥וֹן מִכְלַל־יֹ֗פִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוֹפִֽיעַ׃
Our God comes, and he will not keep silent;[^3] before him is a devouring fire, and around him a raging storm.
יָ֤בֹ֥א אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽאַל־יֶ֫חֱרַ֥שׁ אֵשׁ־לְפָנָ֥יו תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּ֝סְבִיבָ֗יו נִשְׂעֲרָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
He calls to the heavens above, and to the earth, to judge his people:
יִקְרָ֣א אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם מֵעָ֑ל וְאֶל־הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ לָדִ֥ין עַמּֽוֹ׃
"Gather to me my faithful ones,[^4] who made a covenant with me by sacrifice."
אִסְפוּ־לִ֥י חֲסִידָ֑י כֹּרְתֵ֖י בְרִיתִ֣י עֲלֵי־זָֽבַח׃
The heavens proclaim his righteousness, for God himself is judge. Selah.[^5]
וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ שָׁמַ֣יִם צִדְק֑וֹ כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֓ים ׀ שֹׁפֵ֖ט ה֣וּא סֶֽלָה׃
"Listen, my people, and I will speak; Israel, I will testify against you: I am God, your God.
שִׁמְעָ֤ה עַמִּ֨י ׀ וַאֲדַבֵּ֗רָה יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל וְאָעִ֣ידָה בָּ֑ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ אָנֹֽכִי׃
It is not for your sacrifices that I rebuke you, or for your burnt offerings, which are always before me.
לֹ֣א עַל־זְ֭בָחֶיךָ אוֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ וְעוֹלֹתֶ֖יךָ לְנֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃
I will not take a bull from your house, or goats from your pens.
לֹא־אֶקַּ֣ח מִבֵּיתְךָ֣ פָ֑ר מִ֝מִּכְלְאֹתֶ֗יךָ עַתּוּדִֽים׃
For every animal of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills.
כִּי־לִ֥י כָל־חַיְתוֹ־יָ֑עַר בְּ֝הֵמ֗וֹת בְּהַרְרֵי־אָֽלֶף׃
I know every bird of the mountains, and all that moves in the field is mine.[^6]
יָ֭דַעְתִּי כָּל־ע֣וֹף הָרִ֑ים וְזִ֥יז שָׂ֝דַ֗י עִמָּדִֽי׃
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and all that fills it are mine.
אִם־אֶ֭רְעַב לֹא־אֹ֣מַר לָ֑ךְ כִּי־לִ֥י תֵ֝בֵ֗ל וּמְלֹאָֽהּ׃
Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
הַֽ֭אוֹכַל בְּשַׂ֣ר אַבִּירִ֑ים וְדַ֖ם עַתּוּדִ֣ים אֶשְׁתֶּֽה׃
Offer God a sacrifice of thanksgiving,[^7] and fulfill your vows to the Most High.[^8]
זְבַ֣ח לֵאלֹהִ֣ים תּוֹדָ֑ה וְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְעֶלְי֣וֹן נְדָרֶֽיךָ׃
Call on me in the day of trouble; I will rescue you, and you will honor me."
וּ֭קְרָאֵנִי בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה אֲ֝חַלֶּצְךָ֗ וּֽתְכַבְּדֵֽנִי׃
But to the wicked God says, "What right have you to recite my decrees, or to take my covenant on your lips?
וְלָ֤רָשָׁ֨ע ׀ אָ֘מַ֤ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים מַה־לְּ֭ךָ לְסַפֵּ֣ר חֻקָּ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֖א בְרִיתִ֣י עֲלֵי־פִֽיךָ׃
You hate discipline, and you throw my words behind you.
וְ֭אַתָּה שָׂנֵ֣אתָ מוּסָ֑ר וַתַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ דְּבָרַ֣י אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃
When you see a thief, you are pleased with him,[^9] and you throw in your lot with adulterers.
אִם־רָאִ֣יתָ גַ֭נָּב וַתִּ֣רֶץ עִמּ֑וֹ וְעִ֖ם מְנָאֲפִ֣ים חֶלְקֶֽךָ׃
You let your mouth loose for evil, and your tongue harnesses deceit.
פִּ֭יךָ שָׁלַ֣חְתָּ בְרָעָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנְךָ֗ תַּצְמִ֥יד מִרְמָֽה׃
You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your own mother's son.
These things you have done, and I kept silent; you thought that I was just like you. But I will rebuke you, and lay out the case before your eyes.
אֵ֤לֶּה עָשִׂ֨יתָ ׀ וְֽהֶחֱרַ֗שְׁתִּי דִּמִּ֗יתָ הֱֽיוֹת־אֶֽהְיֶ֥ה כָמ֑וֹךָ אוֹכִיחֲךָ֖ וְאֶֽעֶרְכָ֣ה לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃
Understand this, you who forget God, or I will tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you.
בִּֽינוּ־נָ֣א זֹ֭את שֹׁכְחֵ֣י אֱל֑וֹהַּ פֶּן־אֶ֝טְרֹ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּֽיל׃
Whoever offers a sacrifice of thanksgiving honors me; and to the one who keeps to the way,[^10] I will show the salvation of God."
זֹבֵ֥חַ תּוֹדָ֗ה יְֽכַבְּ֫דָֽ[m]נְנִי וְשָׂ֥ם דֶּ֑רֶךְ אַ֝רְאֶ֗נּוּ בְּיֵ֣שַׁע אֱלֹהִֽים׃

n.1: *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph". Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the temple singers (1 Chronicles 16:5–7; 25:1–2). Psalms 73–83 are also "of Asaph". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The Mighty One, God, the LORD*: Hebrew *El Elohim YHWH*, three names for God together, as in Joshua 22:22. It can also be read "The God of gods, the LORD".
n.3: Or "May our God come, and not keep silent".
n.4: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.5: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.6: Literally "is with me".
n.7: Hebrew *todah*: a sacrifice given in thanksgiving (Leviticus 7:12). Also in verse 23.
n.8: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.9: Or "you run with him", as the Septuagint reads.
n.10: Literally "and the one who sets a way". The meaning is uncertain.

v: For the director. A psalm of David,[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
when the prophet Nathan came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.[^2]
בְּֽבוֹא־אֵ֭לָיו נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־בָּ֝֗א אֶל־בַּת־שָֽׁבַע׃
Be gracious to me, God, according to your faithful love;[^3] according to your great compassion, blot out my transgressions.
חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱלֹהִ֣ים כְּחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ מְחֵ֣ה פְשָׁעָֽי׃
Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
*הרבה **הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי מֵעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽמֵחַטָּאתִ֥י טַהֲרֵֽנִי׃
For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.
כִּֽי־פְ֭שָׁעַי אֲנִ֣י אֵדָ֑ע וְחַטָּאתִ֖י נֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִֽיד׃
Against you, you alone, have I sinned, and done what is evil in your sight, so that you are right when you speak, and blameless when you judge.[^4]
לְךָ֤ לְבַדְּךָ֨ ׀ חָטָאתִי֮ וְהָרַ֥ע בְּעֵינֶ֗יךָ עָ֫שִׂ֥יתִי לְ֭מַעַן תִּצְדַּ֥ק בְּדָבְרֶ֗ךָ תִּזְכֶּ֥ה בְשָׁפְטֶֽךָ׃
Indeed, I was born in iniquity, and in sin my mother conceived me.
הֵן־בְּעָו֥וֹן חוֹלָ֑לְתִּי וּ֝בְחֵ֗טְא יֶֽחֱמַ֥תְנִי אִמִּֽי׃
Indeed, you desire truth in the inner being;[^5] in the hidden place you teach me wisdom.
הֵן־אֱ֭מֶת חָפַ֣צְתָּ בַטֻּח֑וֹת וּ֝בְסָתֻ֗ם חָכְמָ֥ה תוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃
Purify me from sin with hyssop,[^6] and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
תְּחַטְּאֵ֣נִי בְאֵז֣וֹב וְאֶטְהָ֑ר תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי וּמִשֶּׁ֥לֶג אַלְבִּֽין׃
Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones you have crushed rejoice.
תַּ֭שְׁמִיעֵנִי שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה תָּ֝גֵ֗לְנָה עֲצָמ֥וֹת דִּכִּֽיתָ׃
Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.
הַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נֶיךָ מֵחֲטָאָ֑י וְֽכָל־עֲוֺ֖נֹתַ֣י מְחֵֽה׃
Create in me a clean heart, God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא־לִ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ נָ֝כ֗וֹן חַדֵּ֥שׁ בְּקִרְבִּֽי׃
Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your holy spirit[^7] from me.
אַל־תַּשְׁלִיכֵ֥נִי מִלְּפָנֶ֑יךָ וְר֥וּחַ קָ֝דְשְׁךָ֗ אַל־תִּקַּ֥ח מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
הָשִׁ֣יבָה לִּ֭י שְׂשׂ֣וֹן יִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וְר֖וּחַ נְדִיבָ֣ה תִסְמְכֵֽנִי׃
Then I will teach transgressors your ways, and sinners will return to you.
אֲלַמְּדָ֣ה פֹשְׁעִ֣ים דְּרָכֶ֑יךָ וְ֝חַטָּאִ֗ים אֵלֶ֥יךָ יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃
Rescue me from bloodguilt,[^8] God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing aloud of your righteousness.
הַצִּ֘ילֵ֤נִי מִדָּמִ֨ים ׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י תְשׁוּעָתִ֑י תְּרַנֵּ֥ן לְ֝שׁוֹנִ֗י צִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃
Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
אֲ֭דֹנָי שְׂפָתַ֣י תִּפְתָּ֑ח וּ֝פִ֗י יַגִּ֥יד תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
For you do not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it; you take no pleasure in burnt offering.
כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־תַחְפֹּ֣ץ זֶ֣בַח וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה ע֝וֹלָ֗ה לֹ֣א תִרְצֶֽה׃
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, God, you will not despise.
זִֽבְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ ר֢וּחַ נִשְׁבָּ֫רָ֥ה לֵב־נִשְׁבָּ֥ר וְנִדְכֶּ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א תִבְזֶֽה׃
Do good to Zion in your favor; build up the walls of Jerusalem.
הֵיטִ֣יבָה בִ֭רְצוֹנְךָ אֶת־צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Then you will delight in right sacrifices,[^9] in burnt offerings and whole burnt offerings;[^10] then bulls will be offered on your altar.
אָ֤ז תַּחְפֹּ֣ץ זִבְחֵי־צֶ֭דֶק עוֹלָ֣ה וְכָלִ֑יל אָ֤ז יַעֲל֖וּ עַל־מִזְבַּחֲךָ֣ פָרִֽים׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verses 1–2, so verses 3–21 are 51:1–19 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *Gone in to*: had sexual relations with. The events are told in 2 Samuel 11–12.
n.3: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.4: Romans 3:4 quotes the second half of this verse from the Septuagint: "so that you may be justified in your words, and prevail when you are judged".
n.5: Hebrew *tuchot*, a rare word, perhaps "the inward parts" (compare Job 38:36).
n.6: Literally "Un-sin me", the verb used of rites of purification. Hyssop, a small bushy plant, was used to sprinkle blood or water in such rites (Leviticus 14:4–7; Numbers 19:18).
n.7: Literally "the spirit of your holiness". Compare Isaiah 63:10–11.
n.8: Literally "from bloods", that is, from the guilt of shedding blood, or perhaps from a violent death.
n.9: Literally "sacrifices of righteousness".
n.10: Hebrew *kalil*, "whole": an offering burned up completely.

v: For the director. A maskil of David,[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד׃
when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, "David has come to the house of Ahimelech."[^2]
בְּב֤וֹא ׀ דּוֹאֵ֣ג הָאֲדֹמִי֮ וַיַּגֵּ֢ד לְשָׁ֫א֥וּל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֑וֹ בָּ֥א דָ֝וִ֗ד אֶל־בֵּ֥ית אֲחִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
Why do you boast of evil, you mighty man? The faithful love of God lasts all day long.[^3]
מַה־תִּתְהַלֵּ֣ל בְּ֭רָעָה הַגִּבּ֑וֹר חֶ֥סֶד אֵ֝֗ל כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
Your tongue plots destruction like a sharpened razor, you worker of deceit.
הַ֭וּוֹת תַּחְשֹׁ֣ב לְשׁוֹנֶ֑ךָ כְּתַ֥עַר מְ֝לֻטָּ֗שׁ עֹשֵׂ֥ה רְמִיָּֽה׃
You love evil more than good, lying more than speaking righteousness. Selah.[^4]
אָהַ֣בְתָּ רָּ֣ע מִטּ֑וֹב שֶׁ֓קֶר ׀ מִדַּבֵּ֖ר צֶ֣דֶק סֶֽלָה׃
You love all words that devour, you deceitful tongue.
אָהַ֥בְתָּ כָֽל־דִּבְרֵי־בָ֗לַע לְשׁ֣וֹן מִרְמָֽה׃
But God will break you down forever; he will snatch you up and tear you from your tent; he will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah.
גַּם־אֵל֮ יִתָּצְךָ֢ לָ֫נֶ֥צַח יַחְתְּךָ֣ וְיִסָּחֲךָ֣ מֵאֹ֑הֶל וְשֵֽׁרֶשְׁךָ֨ מֵאֶ֖רֶץ חַיִּ֣ים סֶֽלָה׃
The righteous will see and fear; they will laugh at him, saying,
וְיִרְא֖וּ צַדִּיקִ֥ים וְיִירָ֗אוּ וְעָלָ֥יו יִשְׂחָֽקוּ׃
"See, this is the man who would not make God his stronghold, but trusted in his great wealth, and grew strong by his destruction."[^5]
הִנֵּ֤ה הַגֶּ֗בֶר לֹ֤א יָשִׂ֥ים אֱלֹהִ֗ים מָֽע֫וּזּ֥וֹ וַ֭יִּבְטַח בְּרֹ֣ב עָשְׁר֑וֹ יָ֝עֹ֗ז בְּהַוָּתֽוֹ׃
But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the faithful love of God forever and ever.
וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ כְּזַ֣יִת רַ֭עֲנָן בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּטַ֥חְתִּי בְחֶֽסֶד־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים עוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
I will give thanks to you forever, because you have done it. I will hope in your name, for it is good, in the presence of your faithful ones.[^6]
אוֹדְךָ֣ לְ֭עוֹלָם כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֑יתָ וַאֲקַוֶּ֥ה שִׁמְךָ֥ כִֽי־ט֝֗וֹב נֶ֣גֶד חֲסִידֶֽיךָ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verses 1–2, so verses 3–11 are 52:1–9 in most English Bibles.
n.2: The events are told in 1 Samuel 21:2–10 and 22:6–23 (21:1–9 in most English Bibles).
n.3: Literally "The faithful love (*chesed*) of God all the day". The Septuagint reads "lawlessness all the day".
n.4: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 7.
n.5: Hebrew *havvah*, "destruction", as in verse 4, or "craving".
n.6: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".

v: For the director. According to Mahalath.[^1] A maskil of David.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־מָחֲלַ֗ת מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד׃
The fool[^3] says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt; they do detestable wrong; there is no one who does good.
אָ֘מַ֤ר נָבָ֣ל בְּ֭לִבּוֹ אֵ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֑ים הִֽ֝שְׁחִ֗יתוּ וְהִֽתְעִ֥יבוּ עָ֝֗וֶל אֵ֣ין עֹֽשֵׂה־טֽוֹב׃
God looks down from heaven on human beings, to see if there is anyone who understands, anyone who seeks God.
אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים מִשָּׁמַיִם֮ הִשְׁקִ֢יף עַֽל־בְּנֵ֫י אָדָֽ[m]ם לִ֭רְאוֹת הֲיֵ֣שׁ מַשְׂכִּ֑יל דֹּ֝רֵ֗שׁ אֶת־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
They have all turned back;[^4] together they have become corrupt. There is no one who does good, not even one.[^5]
כֻּלּ֥וֹ סָג֮ יַחְדָּ֢ו נֶ֫אֱלָ֥חוּ אֵ֤ין עֹֽשֵׂה־ט֑וֹב אֵ֝֗ין גַּם־אֶחָֽד׃
Do they know nothing, the evildoers, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call on God?
הֲלֹ֥א יָדְעוּ֮ פֹּ֤עֲלֵ֫י אָ֥וֶן אֹכְלֵ֣י עַ֭מִּי אָ֣כְלוּ לֶ֑חֶם אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א קָרָֽאוּ׃
There they are, in great terror, where there was nothing to fear! For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you;[^6] you have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.[^7]
שָׁ֤ם ׀ פָּ֥חֲדוּ פַחַד֮ לֹא־הָ֢יָ֫[t]ה פָ֥חַד כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֗ים פִּ֭זַּר עַצְמ֣וֹת חֹנָ֑ךְ הֱ֝בִשֹׁ֗תָה כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים מְאָסָֽם׃
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come from Zion! When God restores the fortunes of his people,[^8] let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.
מִֽ[m]י יִתֵּ֣ן מִצִיּוֹן֮ יְשֻׁע֢וֹת יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל בְּשׁ֣וּב אֱ֭לֹהִים שְׁב֣וּת עַמּ֑וֹ יָגֵ֥ל יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב יִשְׂמַ֥ח יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-machalat*, a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps a tune, or "for sickness" (from *chalah*, "be sick"). Also in the title of Psalm 88.
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–7 are 53:1–6 in most English Bibles. Psalm 53 is almost the same as Psalm 14. It has *Elohim*, "God", where Psalm 14 has "the LORD" (see the note on 42:2), and its verse 6 differs from 14:5–6.
n.3: Hebrew *naval*, someone who is morally and spiritually senseless, not merely unintelligent.
n.4: Hebrew *sag*. Psalm 14:3 has *sar*, "turned aside".
n.5: Romans 3:10–12 quotes verses 2–4 freely (compare 14:1–3).
n.6: Literally "the bones of the one who camps against you".
n.7: Psalm 14:5–6 reads instead "There they are, in great terror, for God is with the generation of the righteous. You would frustrate the plans of the afflicted, but the LORD is their refuge."
n.8: Or "brings back his captive people".

v: For the director. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David,[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ בִּנְגִינֹ֗ת מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד׃
when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, "Is not David hiding among us?"[^2]
בְּב֣וֹא הַ֭זִּיפִים וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְשָׁא֑וּל הֲלֹ֥א דָ֝וִ֗ד מִסְתַּתֵּ֥ר עִמָּֽנוּ׃
God, save me by your name, and vindicate me by your might.
אֱ֭לֹהִים בְּשִׁמְךָ֣ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נִי וּבִגְבוּרָתְךָ֥ תְדִינֵֽנִי׃
God, hear my prayer; listen to the words of my mouth.
אֱ֭לֹהִים שְׁמַ֣ע תְּפִלָּתִ֑י הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינָה לְאִמְרֵי־פִֽי׃
For strangers[^3] have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life;[^4] they do not set God before them. Selah.[^5]
כִּ֤י זָרִ֨ים ׀ קָ֤מוּ עָלַ֗י וְֽ֭עָרִיצִים בִּקְשׁ֣וּ נַפְשִׁ֑י לֹ֤א שָׂ֨מוּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְנֶגְדָּ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
See, God is my helper; the Lord is the one who sustains my life.[^6]
הִנֵּ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים עֹזֵ֣ר לִ֑י אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י בְּֽסֹמְכֵ֥י נַפְשִֽׁי׃
He will repay with evil those who lie in wait for me.[^7] In your faithfulness, destroy them.
*ישוב **יָשִׁ֣יב הָ֭רַע לְשֹׁרְרָ֑י בַּ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ הַצְמִיתֵֽם׃
With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to you; I will give thanks to your name, LORD,[^8] for it is good.
בִּנְדָבָ֥ה אֶזְבְּחָה־לָּ֑ךְ א֤וֹדֶה שִּׁמְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה כִּי־טֽוֹב׃
For he has rescued me from every trouble, and my eye has looked in triumph on my enemies.[^9]
כִּ֣י מִכָּל־צָ֭רָה הִצִּילָ֑נִי וּ֝בְאֹיְבַ֗י רָאֲתָ֥ה עֵינִֽי׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verses 1–2, so verses 3–9 are 54:1–7 in most English Bibles.
n.2: The events are told in 1 Samuel 23:19–28 and 26:1.
n.3: Psalm 86:14, which is almost the same as this line, has "the arrogant" (*zedim*), a word that differs by one similar letter from *zarim*, "strangers".
n.4: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.5: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.6: Literally "the Lord is among those who uphold my soul (*nephesh*)".
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "Evil will return to those who lie in wait for me" but read "He will repay with evil those who lie in wait for me".
n.8: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.9: Literally "my eye has looked on my enemies".

v: For the director. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ בִּנְגִינֹ֗ת מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד׃
Listen to my prayer, God, and do not hide yourself from my plea for mercy.
הַאֲזִ֣ינָה אֱ֭לֹהִים תְּפִלָּתִ֑י וְאַל־תִּ֝תְעַלַּ֗ם מִתְּחִנָּתִֽי׃
Pay attention to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and I groan,
הַקְשִׁ֣יבָה לִּ֣י וַעֲנֵ֑נִי אָרִ֖יד בְּשִׂיחִ֣י וְאָהִֽימָה׃
at the voice of the enemy, because of the pressure of the wicked. For they bring down trouble on me, and in anger they bear a grudge against me.
מִקּ֤וֹל אוֹיֵ֗ב מִפְּנֵ֣י עָקַ֣ת רָשָׁ֑ע כִּי־יָמִ֥יטוּ עָלַ֥י אָ֝֗וֶן וּבְאַ֥ף יִשְׂטְמֽוּנִי׃
My heart writhes within me; the terrors of death have fallen on me.
לִ֭בִּי יָחִ֣יל בְּקִרְבִּ֑י וְאֵימ֥וֹת מָ֝֗וֶת נָפְל֥וּ עָלָֽי׃
Fear and trembling come upon me, and horror overwhelms me.
יִרְאָ֣ה וָ֭רַעַד יָ֣בֹא בִ֑י וַ֝תְּכַסֵּ֗נִי פַּלָּצֽוּת׃
And I say, "Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and be at rest.
וָאֹמַ֗ר מִֽי־יִתֶּן־לִּ֣י אֵ֭בֶר כַּיּוֹנָ֗ה אָע֥וּפָה וְאֶשְׁכֹּֽנָה׃
See, I would flee far away; I would lodge in the wilderness. Selah.[^2]
הִ֭נֵּה אַרְחִ֣יק נְדֹ֑ד אָלִ֖ין בַּמִּדְבָּ֣ר סֶֽלָה׃
I would hurry to find a shelter from the raging wind and the storm."
אָחִ֣ישָׁה מִפְלָ֣ט לִ֑י מֵר֖וּחַ סֹעָ֣ה מִסָּֽעַר׃
Confuse them, Lord, divide their tongues,[^3] for I see violence and strife in the city.
בַּלַּ֣ע אֲ֭דֹנָי פַּלַּ֣ג לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם כִּֽי־רָאִ֨יתִי חָמָ֖ס וְרִ֣יב בָּעִֽיר׃
Day and night they go around it on its walls; wickedness and trouble are within it.
יוֹמָ֤ם וָלַ֗יְלָה יְסוֹבְבֻ֥הָ עַל־חוֹמֹתֶ֑יהָ וְאָ֖וֶן וְעָמָ֣ל בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃
Destruction is within it; oppression and deceit never leave its square.
הַוּ֥וֹת בְּקִרְבָּ֑הּ וְֽלֹא־יָמִ֥ישׁ מֵ֝רְחֹבָ֗הּ תֹּ֣ךְ וּמִרְמָֽה׃
For it is not an enemy who taunts me, or I could bear it; it is not one who hates me who exalts himself against me, or I could hide from him.
כִּ֤י לֹֽא־אוֹיֵ֥ב יְחָֽרְפֵ֗נִי וְאֶ֫שָּׂ֥א לֹֽא־מְ֭שַׂנְאִי עָלַ֣י הִגְדִּ֑יל וְאֶסָּתֵ֥ר מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
But it is you, a man like myself,[^4] my companion and my close friend.
וְאַתָּ֣ה אֱנ֣וֹשׁ כְּעֶרְכִּ֑י אַ֝לּוּפִ֗י וּמְיֻדָּֽעִי׃
Together we used to share sweet counsel; we walked with the throng in the house of God.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַ֭חְדָּו נַמְתִּ֣יק ס֑וֹד בְּבֵ֥ית אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים נְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בְּרָֽגֶשׁ׃
Let death come on them by surprise;[^5] let them go down alive to Sheol,[^6] for evil is in their dwellings, in their midst.
*ישימות **יַשִּׁ֤י **מָ֨וֶת ׀ עָלֵ֗ימוֹ יֵרְד֣וּ שְׁא֣וֹל חַיִּ֑ים כִּֽי־רָע֖וֹת בִּמְגוּרָ֣ם בְּקִרְבָּֽם׃
As for me, I call to God, and the LORD[^7] will save me.
אֲ֭נִי אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֶקְרָ֑א וַ֝יהוָ֗ה יוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃
Evening and morning and at noon I complain and groan, and he hears my voice.
עֶ֤רֶב וָבֹ֣קֶר וְ֭צָהֳרַיִם אָשִׂ֣יחָה וְאֶהֱמֶ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹלִֽי׃
He redeems my life[^8] in safety from the battle against me, for many are against me.[^9]
פָּ֘דָ֤ה בְשָׁל֣וֹם נַ֭פְשִׁי מִקֲּרָב־לִ֑י כִּֽי־בְ֝רַבִּ֗ים הָי֥וּ עִמָּדִֽי׃
God will hear and answer them,[^10] he who is enthroned from of old. Selah. They never change their ways,[^11] and they do not fear God.
יִשְׁמַ֤ע ׀ אֵ֨ל ׀ וְֽיַעֲנֵם֮ וְיֹ֤שֵׁ֥ב קֶ֗דֶם סֶֽ[m]לָה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
He has stretched out his hands against his friends;[^12] he has violated his covenant.
שָׁלַ֣ח יָ֭דָיו בִּשְׁלֹמָ֗יו חִלֵּ֥ל בְּרִיתֽוֹ׃
