His speech is smoother than butter,[^13] but war is in his heart; his words are softer than oil, but they are drawn swords.
חָלְק֤וּ ׀ מַחְמָאֹ֣ת פִּיו֮ וּֽקֲרָב־לִ֫בּ֥וֹ רַכּ֖וּ דְבָרָ֥יו מִשֶּׁ֗מֶן וְהֵ֣מָּה פְתִחֽוֹת׃
Cast your burden[^14] on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never let the righteous be shaken.
הַשְׁלֵ֤ךְ עַל־יְהוָ֨ה ׀ יְהָבְךָ֮ וְה֢וּא יְכַ֫לְכְּלֶ֥ךָ לֹא־יִתֵּ֖ן לְעוֹלָ֥ם מ֗וֹט לַצַּדִּֽיק׃
But you, God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction;[^15] people of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. But as for me, I will trust in you.
וְאַתָּ֤ה אֱלֹהִ֨ים ׀ תּוֹרִדֵ֬ם ׀ לִבְאֵ֬ר שַׁ֗חַת אַנְשֵׁ֤י דָמִ֣ים וּ֖[d]מִרְמָה לֹא־יֶחֱצ֣וּ יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וַ֝אֲנִ֗י אֶבְטַח־בָּֽךְ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–24 are 55:1–23 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 20.
n.3: Literally "Swallow up, Lord, divide their tongue". Compare the confusing of languages at Babel (Genesis 11:7–9).
n.4: Literally "a man according to my rank", my equal.
n.5: The Hebrew text is written as one word, *yeshimot*, "Desolations be on them!", but read as two, *yashi mavet*, "Let death come deceitfully on them".
n.6: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. Compare Numbers 16:30–33.
n.7: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.8: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.9: Literally "for with many they are with me": either many are against me, or many are on my side.
n.10: That is, answer them with judgment. The same consonants can be read "humble them".
n.11: Literally "who have no changes". The Hebrew of verses 20–22 is difficult in places.
n.12: Literally "against those at peace with him".
n.13: The Hebrew is unusual: literally "the butter-words of his mouth are smooth".
n.14: Hebrew *yehav*, found only here, perhaps "what is given to you", your lot. The Septuagint reads "your care", and 1 Peter 5:7 echoes this line.
n.15: Literally "the well of the pit".

v: For the director. According to "The Silent Dove of Far-off Places".[^1] Of David. A miktam,[^2] when the Philistines seized him in Gath.[^3]
לַמְנַצֵּ֤חַ ׀ עַל־י֬וֹנַת אֵ֣לֶם רְ֭חֹקִים לְדָוִ֣ד מִכְתָּ֑ם בֶּֽאֱחֹ֨ז אֹת֖וֹ פְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים בְּגַֽת׃
Be gracious to me, God, for a mere mortal hounds me; all day long an attacker oppresses me.
חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱ֭לֹהִים כִּֽי־שְׁאָפַ֣נִי אֱנ֑וֹשׁ כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם לֹחֵ֥ם יִלְחָצֵֽנִי׃
Those who lie in wait for me hound me all day long, for many fight against me proudly.[^4]
שָׁאֲפ֣וּ שׁ֭וֹרְרַי כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם כִּֽי־רַבִּ֨ים לֹחֲמִ֖ים לִ֣י מָרֽוֹם׃
When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.
י֥וֹם אִירָ֑א אֲ֝נִ֗י אֵלֶ֥יךָ אֶבְטָֽח׃
In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
בֵּאלֹהִים֮ אֲהַלֵּ֢ל דְּבָ֫ר֥וֹ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים בָּ֭טַחְתִּי לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בָשָׂ֣ר לִֽי׃
All day long they twist my words;[^5] all their thoughts are against me for evil.
כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם דְּבָרַ֣י יְעַצֵּ֑בוּ עָלַ֖י כָּל־מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֣ם לָרָֽע׃
They gather together, they lie in hiding; they watch my steps,[^6] as they wait to take my life.[^7]
יָג֤וּרוּ ׀ *יצפינו **יִצְפּ֗וֹנוּ הֵ֭מָּה עֲקֵבַ֣י יִשְׁמֹ֑רוּ כַּ֝אֲשֶׁ֗ר קִוּ֥וּ נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Because of their wickedness, will they escape?[^8] In anger bring down the peoples, God.
עַל־אָ֥וֶן פַּלֶּט־לָ֑מוֹ בְּ֝אַ֗ף עַמִּ֤ים ׀ הוֹרֵ֬ד אֱלֹהִֽים׃
You have counted my wanderings;[^9] put my tears in your bottle.[^10] Are they not in your book?
נֹדִי֮ סָפַ֢רְתָּ֫ה אָ֥תָּה שִׂ֣ימָה דִמְעָתִ֣י בְנֹאדֶ֑ךָ הֲ֝לֹ֗א בְּסִפְרָתֶֽךָ׃
Then my enemies will turn back on the day I call. This I know: God is for me.
אָ֥֨ז יָ֘שׁ֤וּבוּ אוֹיְבַ֣י אָ֭חוֹר בְּי֣וֹם אֶקְרָ֑א זֶה־יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים לִֽי׃
In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD,[^11] whose word I praise,
בֵּֽ֭אלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּ֣ל דָּבָ֑ר בַּ֝יהוָ֗ה אֲהַלֵּ֥ל דָּבָֽר׃
in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can a human being do to me?
בֵּֽאלֹהִ֣ים בָּ֭טַחְתִּי לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה אָדָ֣ם[t] לִֽי׃
I am bound by vows to you, God;[^12] I will offer thanksgiving offerings to you.
עָלַ֣י אֱלֹהִ֣ים נְדָרֶ֑יךָ אֲשַׁלֵּ֖ם תּוֹדֹ֣ת לָֽךְ׃
For you have rescued my life from death, and my feet from stumbling,[^13] so that I may walk before God in the light of life.[^14]
כִּ֤י הִצַּ֪לְתָּ נַפְשִׁ֡י מִמָּוֶת֮ הֲלֹ֥א רַגְלַ֗י מִ֫דֶּ֥חִי לְ֭הִֽתְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים בְּ֝א֗וֹר הֽ͏ַחַיִּֽים׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-yonat elem rechoqim*, probably the name of a tune: "the dove of silence of far-off places". The same consonants can be read "the dove of the distant terebinths".
n.2: Hebrew *miktam*, a term of uncertain meaning (see the note on the title of Psalm 16).
n.3: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". The events are told in 1 Samuel 21:11–16 (21:10–15 in most English Bibles). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–14 are 56:1–13 in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *marom*, "on high": proudly, or perhaps addressed to God, "Most High".
n.5: Or "they hurt my cause".
n.6: Literally "my heels".
n.7: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verse 14.
n.8: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "On account of wickedness, deliver for them". Or "Because of their wickedness, cast them out".
n.9: Or "my lament". Hebrew *nodi*, which sounds like *nod*, "bottle", in the next line.
n.10: A skin bottle, for water, milk or wine.
n.11: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.12: Literally "Upon me, God, are your vows", the vows I made to you.
n.13: Literally "have you not rescued my feet from stumbling?"
n.14: Or "in the light of the living".

v: For the director. According to "Do Not Destroy".[^1] Of David. A miktam,[^2] when he fled from Saul, in the cave.[^3]
לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ אַל־תַּ֭שְׁחֵת לְדָוִ֣ד מִכְתָּ֑ם בְּבָרְח֥וֹ מִפְּנֵי־שָׁ֝א֗וּל בַּמְּעָרֽ͏ָה׃
Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me, for in you my soul[^4] takes refuge; in the shadow of your wings I will take refuge until the destruction passes by.
חָנֵּ֤נִי אֱלֹהִ֨ים ׀ חָנֵּ֗נִי כִּ֥י בְךָ֮ חָסָ֢יָה נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י וּבְצֵֽל־כְּנָפֶ֥יךָ אֶחְסֶ֑ה עַ֝֗ד יַעֲבֹ֥ר הַוּֽוֹת׃
I cry to God Most High,[^5] to God who fulfills his purpose for me.[^6]
אֶ֭קְרָא לֵֽאלֹהִ֣ים עֶלְי֑וֹן לָ֝אֵ֗ל גֹּמֵ֥ר עָלָֽי׃
He will send from heaven and save me; he will put to shame the one who hounds me.[^7] Selah.[^8] God will send out his faithful love[^9] and his faithfulness.
יִשְׁלַ֤ח מִשָּׁמַ֨יִם ׀ וְֽיוֹשִׁיעֵ֗נִי חֵרֵ֣ף שֹׁאֲפִ֣י סֶ֑לָה יִשְׁלַ֥ח אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים חַסְדּ֥וֹ וַאֲמִתּֽוֹ׃
My soul is in the midst of lions; I lie down among those who breathe fire,[^10] human beings whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongue is a sharp sword.
נַפְשִׁ֤י ׀ בְּת֥וֹךְ לְבָאִם֮ אֶשְׁכְּבָ֢ה לֹ֫הֲטִ֥ים בְּֽנֵי־אָדָ֗ם שִׁ֭נֵּיהֶם חֲנִ֣ית וְחִצִּ֑ים וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּֽה׃
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
ר֣וּמָה עַל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים עַ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
They set a net for my steps; my soul was bowed down. They dug a pit in my path; they have fallen into it themselves. Selah.
רֶ֤שֶׁת ׀ הֵכִ֣ינוּ לִפְעָמַי֮ כָּפַ֢ף נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י כָּר֣וּ לְפָנַ֣י שִׁיחָ֑ה נָפְל֖וּ בְתוֹכָ֣הּ סֶֽלָה׃
My heart is steadfast, God, my heart is steadfast;[^11] I will sing and make music.
נָ֘כ֤וֹן לִבִּ֣י אֱ֭לֹהִים נָכ֣וֹן לִבִּ֑י אָ֝שִׁ֗ירָה וַאֲזַמֵּֽרָה׃
Wake up, my glory![^12] Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
ע֤וּרָה כְבוֹדִ֗י ע֭וּרָ֥ה הַנֵּ֥בֶל וְכִנּ֗וֹר אָעִ֥ירָה שָּֽׁחַר׃
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, Lord; I will sing praise to you among the nations.
אוֹדְךָ֖ בָעַמִּ֥ים ׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י אֲ֝זַמֶּרְךָ֗ בַּל־אֻמִּֽים׃
For your faithful love is great, reaching to the heavens, and your faithfulness to the clouds.
כִּֽי־גָדֹ֣ל עַד־שָׁמַ֣יִם חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וְֽעַד־שְׁחָקִ֥ים אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
ר֣וּמָה עַל־שָׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים עַ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-tashchet*, "do not destroy", probably the name of a tune (compare Isaiah 65:8). Also in the titles of Psalms 58, 59 and 75.
n.2: Hebrew *miktam*, a term of uncertain meaning (see the note on the title of Psalm 16).
n.3: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". For the cave, compare 1 Samuel 22:1 and 24:4 (24:3 in most English Bibles). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–12 are 57:1–11 in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 5 and 7.
n.5: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.6: Literally "to God who completes for me". The Septuagint reads "who does good to me".
n.7: Or "when the one who hounds me taunts me".
n.8: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 7.
n.9: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verse 11.
n.10: Or "who devour".
n.11: Verses 8–12 appear again, with small differences, as 108:2–6 (108:1–5 in most English Bibles).
n.12: Hebrew *kevodi*, "my glory", perhaps meaning "my soul", the inner self (compare 16:9).

v: For the director. According to "Do Not Destroy".[^1] Of David. A miktam.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ אַל־תַּשְׁחֵ֗ת לְדָוִ֥ד מִכְתָּֽם׃
Do you indeed speak righteousness, you gods?[^3] Do you judge human beings fairly?
הַֽאֻמְנָ֗ם אֵ֣לֶם צֶ֭דֶק תְּדַבֵּר֑וּן מֵישָׁרִ֥ים תִּ֝שְׁפְּט֗וּ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָֽם׃
No, in your hearts you devise wrongs; on the earth you weigh out the violence of your hands.
אַף־בְּלֵב֮ עוֹלֹ֢ת תִּפְעָ֫ל֥וּן בָּאָ֡רֶץ חֲמַ֥ס יְ֝דֵיכֶ֗ם תְּפַלֵּֽסֽוּן׃
The wicked go astray from the womb; liars wander off from birth.[^4]
זֹ֣רוּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים מֵרָ֑חֶם תָּע֥וּ מִ֝בֶּ֗טֶן דֹּבְרֵ֥י כָזָֽב׃
Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a deaf cobra that stops up its ear,
חֲמַת־לָ֗מוֹ כִּדְמ֥וּת חֲמַת־נָחָ֑שׁ כְּמוֹ־פֶ֥תֶן חֵ֝רֵ֗שׁ יַאְטֵ֥ם אָזְנֽוֹ׃
that will not listen to the voice of charmers, or of the most skillful caster of spells.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־יִ֭שְׁמַע לְק֣וֹל מְלַחֲשִׁ֑ים חוֹבֵ֖ר חֲבָרִ֣ים מְחֻכָּֽם׃
God, break the teeth in their mouths; tear out the fangs of the young lions, LORD.[^5]
אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים הֲרָס־שִׁנֵּ֥ימוֹ בְּפִ֑ימוֹ מַלְתְּע֥וֹת כְּ֝פִירִ֗ים נְתֹ֣ץ ׀ יְהוָֽה׃
Let them vanish like water that runs away; when he aims his arrows,[^6] let them be cut off.[^7]
יִמָּאֲס֣וּ כְמוֹ־מַ֭יִם יִתְהַלְּכוּ־לָ֑מוֹ יִדְרֹ֥ךְ *חצו **חִ֝צָּ֗יו כְּמ֣וֹ יִתְמֹלָֽלוּ׃
Let them be like a snail that melts away as it goes, like a woman's stillborn child, that never sees the sun.
כְּמ֣וֹ שַׁ֭בְּלוּל תֶּ֣מֶס יַהֲלֹ֑ךְ נֵ֥פֶל אֵ֝֗שֶׁת בַּל־חָ֥זוּ שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃
Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns, whether green or burning, he will sweep them away.[^8]
בְּטֶ֤רֶם ׀ יָבִ֣ינוּ סִּֽירֹתֵיכֶ֣ם אָטָ֑ד כְּמוֹ־חַ֥י כְּמוֹ־חָ֝ר֗וֹן יִשְׂעָרֶֽנּוּ׃
The righteous will rejoice when they see vengeance done; they will bathe their feet in the blood of the wicked.
יִשְׂמַ֣ח צַ֭דִּיק כִּי־חָזָ֣ה נָקָ֑ם פְּעָמָ֥יו יִ֝רְחַ֗ץ בְּדַ֣ם הָרָשָֽׁע׃
And people will say, "Surely there is a reward[^9] for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges on the earth."[^10]
וְיֹאמַ֣ר אָ֭דָם אַךְ־פְּרִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֑יק אַ֥ךְ יֵשׁ־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים שֹׁפְטִ֥ים בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-tashchet*, "do not destroy", probably the name of a tune (see the title of Psalm 57).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". *Miktam*: a term of uncertain meaning (see the note on the title of Psalm 16). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–12 are 58:1–11 in most English Bibles.
n.3: The vowel points read *elem*, "silence": "Do you indeed speak righteousness in silence?" The same consonants can be read *elim*, "gods" or "mighty ones", the rulers addressed in this psalm (compare Psalm 82).
n.4: Literally "from the belly".
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: The Hebrew text is written "his arrow" but read "his arrows".
n.7: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "he treads his arrows as they are cut off".
n.8: The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult. Literally "Before your pots perceive the thornbush, like living, like burning, he will whirl it away".
n.9: Literally "fruit".
n.10: The verb "judges" is plural, as it sometimes is with *Elohim*, "God". Or "there are gods who judge".

v: For the director. According to "Do Not Destroy".[^1] Of David. A miktam, when Saul sent men, and they watched the house in order to kill him.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ אַל־תַּשְׁחֵת֮ לְדָוִ֢ד מִ֫כְתָּ֥ם בִּשְׁלֹ֥חַ שָׁא֑וּל וַֽיִּשְׁמְר֥וּ אֶת־הַ֝בַּ֗יִת לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃
Rescue me from my enemies, my God; protect me from those who rise up against me.
הַצִּילֵ֖נִי מֵאֹיְבַ֥י ׀ אֱלֹהָ֑י מִּֽמִתְקוֹמְמַ֥י תְּשַׂגְּבֵֽנִי׃
Rescue me from evildoers, and save me from bloodthirsty men.[^3]
הַ֭צִּילֵנִי מִפֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן וּֽמֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י דָ֝מִ֗ים הוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃
For see, they lie in wait for my life;[^4] fierce men band together against me, not for any transgression or sin of mine, LORD.[^5]
כִּ֤י הִנֵּ֪ה אָֽרְב֡וּ לְנַפְשִׁ֗י יָג֣וּרוּ עָלַ֣י עַזִ֑ים לֹא־פִשְׁעִ֖י וְלֹא־חַטָּאתִ֣י יְהוָֽה׃
For no guilt of mine they run and take up their positions. Rouse yourself to meet me, and see!
בְּֽלִי־עָ֭וֺן יְרוּצ֣וּן וְיִכּוֹנָ֑נוּ ע֖וּרָה לִקְרָאתִ֣י וּרְאֵה׃
You, LORD God of Armies,[^6] God of Israel, wake up to punish all the nations; show no mercy to any treacherous evildoers. Selah.[^7]
וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָֽה־אֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ צְבָא֡וֹת אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הָקִ֗יצָה לִפְקֹ֥ד כָּֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם אַל־תָּחֹ֨ן כָּל־בֹּ֖גְדֵי אָ֣וֶן סֶֽלָה׃
They return at evening, howling like dogs, and prowl around the city.
יָשׁ֣וּבוּ לָ֭עֶרֶב יֶהֱמ֥וּ כַכָּ֗לֶב וִיס֥וֹבְבוּ עִֽיר׃
See, they spew from their mouths; swords are on their lips, for they think, "Who will hear?"[^8]
הִנֵּ֤ה ׀ יַבִּ֘יע֤וּן בְּפִיהֶ֗ם חֲ֭רָבוֹת בְּשִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם כִּי־מִ֥י שֹׁמֵֽעַ׃
But you, LORD, laugh at them; you mock all the nations.
וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תִּשְׂחַק־לָ֑מוֹ תִּ֝לְעַ֗ג לְכָל־גּוֹיִֽם׃
Because of his strength, I will watch for you,[^9] for God is my fortress.
עֻ֭זּוֹ אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֶשְׁמֹ֑רָה כִּֽי־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים מִשְׂגַּבִּֽי׃
My faithful God[^10] will come to meet me; God will let me look in triumph on those who lie in wait for me.
אֱלֹהֵ֣י *חסדו **חַסְדִּ֣י יְקַדְּמֵ֑נִי אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים יַרְאֵ֥נִי בְשֹׁרְרָֽי׃
Do not kill them, or my people will forget; make them wander by your power, and bring them down, Lord, our shield.
אַל־תַּהַרְגֵ֤ם ׀ פֶּֽן־יִשְׁכְּח֬וּ עַמִּ֗י הֲנִיעֵ֣מוֹ בְ֭חֵילְךָ וְהוֹרִידֵ֑מוֹ מָ֖גִנֵּ֣נוּ אֲדֹנָֽי׃
For the sin of their mouths, the words of their lips, let them be caught in their pride, for the curses and the lies they speak.
חַטַּאת־פִּ֗ימוֹ דְּֽבַר־שְׂפָ֫תֵ֥ימוֹ וְיִלָּכְד֥וּ בִגְאוֹנָ֑ם וּמֵאָלָ֖ה וּמִכַּ֣חַשׁ יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃
Consume them in wrath, consume them until they are no more, so that they may know that God rules over Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah.
כַּלֵּ֥ה בְחֵמָה֮ כַּלֵּ֢ה וְֽאֵ֫ינֵ֥מוֹ וְֽיֵדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־אֱ֭לֹהִים מֹשֵׁ֣ל בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב לְאַפְסֵ֖י הָאָ֣רֶץ סֶֽלָה׃
They return at evening, howling like dogs, and prowl around the city.
וְיָשׁ֣וּבוּ לָ֭עֶרֶב יֶהֱמ֥וּ כַכָּ֗לֶב וִיס֥וֹבְבוּ עִֽיר׃
They wander about for food, and if they are not satisfied, they stay all night.[^11]
הֵ֭מָּה *ינועון **יְנִיע֣וּן לֶאֱכֹ֑ל אִם־לֹ֥א יִ֝שְׂבְּע֗וּ וַיָּלִֽינוּ׃
But I will sing of your strength; I will sing aloud of your faithful love in the morning. For you have been my fortress, a refuge in the day of my distress.
וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ אָשִׁ֣יר עֻזֶּךָ֮ וַאֲרַנֵּ֥ן לַבֹּ֗קֶר חַ֫סְדֶּ֥ךָ כִּֽי־הָיִ֣יתָ מִשְׂגָּ֣ב לִ֑י וּ֝מָנ֗וֹס בְּי֣וֹם צַר־לִֽי׃
My Strength, I will sing praises to you, for God is my fortress, my faithful God.[^12]
עֻ֭זִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֲזַמֵּ֑רָה כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י אֱלֹהֵ֥י חַסְדִּֽי׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-tashchet*, "do not destroy", probably the name of a tune (see the title of Psalm 57).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". *Miktam*: a term of uncertain meaning (see the note on the title of Psalm 16). The events are told in 1 Samuel 19:11–17. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–18 are 59:1–17 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "men of blood".
n.4: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: Hebrew *YHWH Elohim tseva'ot*. Compare "the LORD of Armies", traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 14.
n.8: Literally "for who hears?"
n.9: Literally "His strength, I will watch for you", perhaps meaning the enemy's strength. Verse 18 has "my strength", and the Septuagint reads that here: "My strength, I will watch for you".
n.10: Literally "The God of my faithful love (*chesed*)". The Hebrew text is written "The God of his faithful love" but read "The God of my faithful love".
n.11: Or "they growl", "they grumble".
n.12: Literally "the God of my faithful love (*chesed*)".

v: For the director. According to "The Lily of the Testimony".[^1] A miktam of David, for teaching,[^2]
לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ עַל־שׁוּשַׁ֣ן עֵד֑וּת מִכְתָּ֖ם לְדָוִ֣ד לְלַמֵּֽד׃
when he fought against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah,[^3] and when Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.[^4]
בְּהַצּוֹת֨וֹ ׀ אֶ֥ת אֲרַ֣ם נַהֲרַיִם֮ וְאֶת־אֲרַ֢ם צ֫וֹבָ֥ה וַיָּ֤שָׁב יוֹאָ֗ב וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־אֱד֣וֹם בְּגֵיא־מֶ֑לַח שְׁנֵ֖ים עָשָׂ֣ר אָֽלֶף׃
God, you have rejected us and broken us; you have been angry. Restore us!
אֱ֭לֹהִים זְנַחְתָּ֣נוּ פְרַצְתָּ֑נוּ אָ֝נַ֗פְתָּ תְּשׁ֣וֹבֵֽב לָֽנוּ׃
You have made the land quake; you have split it open. Heal its cracks, for it is tottering.
הִרְעַ֣שְׁתָּה אֶ֣רֶץ פְּצַמְתָּ֑הּ רְפָ֖ה שְׁבָרֶ֣יהָ כִי־מָֽטָה׃
You have made your people see hard times; you have given us wine to drink that makes us stagger.
הִרְאִ֣יתָה עַמְּךָ֣ קָשָׁ֑ה הִ֝שְׁקִיתָ֗נוּ יַ֣יִן תַּרְעֵלָֽה׃
You have set up a banner for those who fear you, for them to rally to, out of range of the bow.[^5] Selah.[^6]
נָ֘תַ֤תָּה לִּירֵאֶ֣יךָ נֵּ֭ס לְהִתְנוֹסֵ֑ס מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י קֹ֣שֶׁט סֶֽלָה׃
So that those you love may be rescued, save by your right hand, and answer me.[^7]
לְ֭מַעַן יֵחָלְצ֣וּן יְדִידֶ֑יךָ הוֹשִׁ֖יעָה יְמִֽינְךָ֣ *ועננו **וַעֲנֵֽנִי׃
God has spoken in his holiness:[^8] "I will exult; I will divide up Shechem, and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ דִּבֶּ֥ר בְּקָדְשׁ֗וֹ אֶ֫עְלֹ֥זָה אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה שְׁכֶ֑ם וְעֵ֖מֶק סֻכּ֣וֹת אֲמַדֵּֽד׃
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the helmet on my head;[^9] Judah is my scepter.[^10]
לִ֤י גִלְעָ֨ד ׀ וְלִ֬י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה וְ֭אֶפְרַיִם מָע֣וֹז רֹאשִׁ֑י יְ֝הוּדָ֗ה מְחֹֽקְקִי׃
Moab is my washbasin; on Edom I throw my sandal.[^11] Philistia, shout aloud because of me!"[^12]
מוֹאָ֤ב ׀ סִ֬יר רַחְצִ֗י עַל־אֱ֭דוֹם אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ נַעֲלִ֑י עָ֝לַ֗י פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת הִתְרֹעָֽעִֽי׃
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?[^13]
מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי עִ֣יר מָצ֑וֹר מִ֖י נָחַ֣נִי עַד־אֱדֽוֹם׃
Is it not you, God, who have rejected us? You no longer go out, God, with our armies.
הֲלֹֽא־אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ וְֽלֹא־תֵצֵ֥א אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בְּצִבְאוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
Give us help against the adversary, for human help is worthless.[^14]
הָֽבָה־לָּ֣נוּ עֶזְרָ֣ת מִצָּ֑ר וְ֝שָׁ֗וְא תְּשׁוּעַ֥ת אָדָם׃
With God we will do valiantly; he will trample our adversaries.
בֵּֽאלֹהִ֥ים נַעֲשֶׂה־חָ֑יִל וְ֝ה֗וּא יָב֥וּס צָרֵֽינוּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-shushan edut*, probably the name of a tune (compare the titles of Psalms 45, 69 and 80).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Miktam*: a term of uncertain meaning (see the note on the title of Psalm 16). *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verses 1–2, so verses 3–14 are 60:1–12 in most English Bibles.
n.3: *Aram-naharaim*, "Aram of the two rivers", was in northern Mesopotamia; *Aram-zobah* was an Aramean kingdom north of Damascus.
n.4: The events are told in 2 Samuel 8:3–14 and 1 Chronicles 18:3–13. In 2 Samuel 8:13 David strikes down eighteen thousand of Aram in the Valley of Salt (the Septuagint and the Syriac read "Edom"); in 1 Chronicles 18:12 Abishai strikes down eighteen thousand Edomites there.
n.5: Hebrew *qoshet*, probably a form of *qeshet*, "bow". Or "a banner to be raised because of the truth", taking *qoshet* as "truth", as in Aramaic.
n.6: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "answer us" but read "answer me". Verses 7–14 appear again, with small differences, as 108:7–14 (108:6–13 in most English Bibles).
n.8: Or "in his holy place".
n.9: Literally "the stronghold of my head".
n.10: Or "my ruler's staff" (compare Genesis 49:10).
n.11: Throwing a sandal on land was perhaps a sign of taking possession of it (compare Ruth 4:7).
n.12: Psalm 108:10 (108:9 in most English Bibles) has "over Philistia I shout in triumph".
n.13: Literally "Who has led me to Edom?" Psalm 108:11 (108:10 in most English Bibles) has the same words; there "fortified city" is *ir mivtsar*, here *ir matsor*.
n.14: Literally "the salvation of *adam* (humankind) is worthless".

v: For the director. With stringed instruments.[^1] Of David.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ ׀ עַֽל־נְגִינַ֬ת לְדָוִֽד׃
Hear my cry, God; listen to my prayer.
שִׁמְעָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים רִנָּתִ֑י הַ֝קְשִׁ֗יבָה תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃
From the end of the earth I call to you, when my heart grows faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.[^3]
מִקְצֵ֤ה הָאָ֨רֶץ ׀ אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֶ֭קְרָא בַּעֲטֹ֣ף לִבִּ֑י בְּצוּר־יָר֖וּם מִמֶּ֣נִּי תַנְחֵֽנִי׃
For you have been my refuge, a strong tower against the enemy.
כִּֽי־הָיִ֣יתָ מַחְסֶ֣ה לִ֑י מִגְדַּל־עֹ֝֗ז מִפְּנֵ֥י אוֹיֵֽב׃
Let me live in your tent forever; let me take refuge in the shelter of your wings. Selah.[^4]
אָג֣וּרָה בְ֭אָהָלְךָ עוֹלָמִ֑ים אֶֽחֱסֶ֨ה בְסֵ֖תֶר כְּנָפֶ֣יךָ סֶּֽלָה׃
For you, God, have heard my vows; you have given the inheritance of those who fear your name.
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים שָׁמַ֣עְתָּ לִנְדָרָ֑י נָתַ֥תָּ יְ֝רֻשַּׁ֗ת יִרְאֵ֥י שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
Add days to the days of the king; may his years be like generation after generation.
יָמִ֣ים עַל־יְמֵי־מֶ֣לֶךְ תּוֹסִ֑יף שְׁ֝נוֹתָ֗יו כְּמוֹ־דֹ֥ר וָדֹֽר׃
May he sit enthroned forever before God; appoint[^5] faithful love[^6] and truth to guard him.
יֵשֵׁ֣ב ע֖[d]וֹלָם לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים חֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת מַ֣ן יִנְצְרֻֽהוּ׃
So I will sing praise to your name forever, as I fulfill my vows day after day.
כֵּ֤ן אֲזַמְּרָ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֣ לָעַ֑ד לְֽשַׁלְּמִ֥י נְ֝דָרַ֗י י֣וֹם ׀ יֽוֹם׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-neginat*, "on a stringed instrument", a variant of *binginot*, "with stringed instruments", in the titles of Psalms 4, 6, 54 and 55.
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–9 are 61:1–8 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "On a rock too high for me, lead me". The Septuagint reads "You set me high on a rock".
n.4: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.5: Hebrew *man*, an uncertain word, perhaps a short form of *mannah*, "appoint".
n.6: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.

v: For the director. According to Jeduthun.[^1] A psalm of David.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־יְדוּת֗וּן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
Truly[^3] my soul waits in silence for God;[^4] my salvation comes from him.
אַ֣ךְ אֶל־אֱ֭לֹהִים דּֽוּמִיָּ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ יְשׁוּעָתִֽי׃
Truly he is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I will not be greatly shaken.
אַךְ־ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י לֹא־אֶמּ֥וֹט רַבָּֽה׃
How long will you all attack a man, to batter him down like a leaning wall, a tottering fence?[^5]
עַד־אָ֤נָה ׀ תְּה֥וֹתְת֣וּ עַל[c] אִישׁ֮ תְּרָצְּח֢וּ כֻ֫לְּכֶ֥ם כְּקִ֥יר נָט֑וּי גָּ֝דֵ֗ר הַדְּחוּֽיָה׃
Truly they plan to topple him from his high place; they delight in lies. With their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah.[^6]
אַ֤ךְ מִשְּׂאֵת֨וֹ ׀ יָ֥עֲצ֣וּ לְהַדִּיחַ֮ יִרְצ֢וּ כָ֫זָ֥ב בְּפִ֥יו יְבָרֵ֑כוּ וּ֝בְקִרְבָּ֗ם יְקַלְלוּ־סֶֽלָה׃
Truly, my soul, wait in silence for God, for my hope comes from him.
אַ֣ךְ לֵ֭אלֹהִים דּ֣וֹמִּי נַפְשִׁ֑י כִּי־מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ תִּקְוָתִֽי׃
Truly he is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I will not be shaken.
אַךְ־ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י לֹ֣א אֶמּֽוֹט׃
My salvation and my glory rest on God;[^7] my strong rock, my refuge, is in God.
עַל־אֱ֭לֹהִים יִשְׁעִ֣י וּכְבוֹדִ֑י צוּר־עֻזִּ֥י מַ֝חְסִ֗י בֵּֽאלֹהִֽים׃
Trust in him at all times, you people; pour out your hearts before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.
בִּטְח֘וּ ב֤וֹ בְכָל־עֵ֨ת ׀ עָ֗ם שִׁפְכֽוּ־לְפָנָ֥יו לְבַבְכֶ֑ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים מַחֲסֶה־לָּ֣נוּ סֶֽלָה׃
Truly, human beings are only a breath; people of rank are a lie.[^8] Placed on the scales, they go up; together they weigh less than a breath.
אַ֤ךְ ׀ הֶ֥בֶל בְּנֵֽי־אָדָם֮ כָּזָ֢ב בְּנֵ֫י אִ֥ישׁ בְּמֹאזְנַ֥יִם לַעֲל֑וֹת הֵ֝֗מָּה מֵהֶ֥בֶל יָֽחַד׃
Do not trust in extortion, or put empty hope in robbery; if wealth increases, do not set your heart on it.
אַל־תִּבְטְח֣וּ בְעֹשֶׁק֮ וּבְגָזֵ֢ל אַל־תֶּ֫הְבָּ֥לוּ חַ֤יִל ׀ כִּֽי־יָנ֑וּב אַל־תָּשִׁ֥יתוּ לֵֽב׃
Once God has spoken; twice I have heard this: that power belongs to God,
אַחַ֤ת ׀ דִּבֶּ֬ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים שְׁתַּֽיִם־ז֥וּ שָׁמָ֑עְתִּי כִּ֥י עֹ֝֗ז לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
and faithful love[^9] belongs to you, Lord. For you repay each person according to what he has done.[^10]
וּלְךָֽ־אֲדֹנָ֥י חָ֑סֶד כִּֽי־אַתָּ֨ה תְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּֽמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-yedutun*. Jeduthun was one of David's chief musicians (1 Chronicles 16:41–42; 25:1–6); here perhaps the name of a tune or a style of music. Compare the titles of Psalms 39 and 77.
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–13 are 62:1–12 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *akh*, "truly" or "only", which begins verses 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 10.
n.4: Literally "Truly to God my soul (*nephesh*) is silence". Also in verse 6.
n.5: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "How long will you rush upon a man? You will murder, all of you, like a leaning wall, a fence pushed in".
n.6: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 9.
n.7: Literally "On God my salvation and my glory".
n.8: Literally "the sons of *adam* are a breath, the sons of *ish* are a lie", two words for "man", perhaps common people and people of rank (compare 49:3; 49:2 in most English Bibles). *Breath*: Hebrew *hevel*, "vapor, breath", the word used throughout Ecclesiastes.
n.9: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.10: Compare Job 34:11; Proverbs 24:12; Romans 2:6.

v: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.[^1]
מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִ֑ד בִּ֝הְיוֹת֗וֹ בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר יְהוּדָֽה׃
God, you are my God; I seek you earnestly.[^2] My soul[^3] thirsts for you; my body[^4] longs for you, in a dry and weary land without water.
אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ אֵלִ֥י אַתָּ֗ה אֲ‍ֽשַׁחֲ֫רֶ֥ךָּ צָמְאָ֬ה לְךָ֨ ׀ נַפְשִׁ֗י כָּמַ֣הּ לְךָ֣ בְשָׂרִ֑י בְּאֶֽרֶץ־צִיָּ֖ה וְעָיֵ֣ף בְּלִי־מָֽיִם׃
So I have gazed on you in the sanctuary, to see your power and your glory.
כֵּ֭ן בַּקֹּ֣דֶשׁ חֲזִיתִ֑יךָ לִרְא֥וֹת עֻ֝זְּךָ֗ וּכְבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
Because your faithful love[^5] is better than life, my lips will praise you.
כִּי־ט֣וֹב חַ֭סְדְּךָ מֵֽחַיִּ֗ים שְׂפָתַ֥י יְשַׁבְּחֽוּנְךָ׃
So I will bless you as long as I live; in your name I will lift up my hands.
כֵּ֣ן אֲבָרֶכְךָ֣ בְחַיָּ֑י בְּ֝שִׁמְךָ אֶשָּׂ֥א כַפָּֽי׃
My soul will be satisfied as with the richest food,[^6] and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips.
כְּמ֤וֹ חֵ֣לֶב וָ֭דֶשֶׁן תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע נַפְשִׁ֑י וְשִׂפְתֵ֥י רְ֝נָנ֗וֹת יְהַלֶּל־פִּֽי׃
When I remember you on my bed, I meditate on you through the watches of the night.
אִם־זְכַרְתִּ֥יךָ עַל־יְצוּעָ֑י בְּ֝אַשְׁמֻר֗וֹת אֶהְגֶּה־בָּֽךְ׃
For you have been my help, and in the shadow of your wings I sing for joy.
כִּֽי־הָיִ֣יתָ עֶזְרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י וּבְצֵ֖ל כְּנָפֶ֣יךָ אֲרַנֵּֽן׃
My soul clings to you; your right hand holds me up.
דָּבְקָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֣י אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ בִּ֝֗י תָּמְכָ֥ה יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
But those who seek my life to destroy it will go down into the depths of the earth.
וְהֵ֗מָּה לְ֭שׁוֹאָה יְבַקְשׁ֣וּ נַפְשִׁ֑י יָ֝בֹ֗אוּ בְּֽתַחְתִּיּ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
They will be handed over to the power of the sword;[^7] they will become food for jackals.[^8]
יַגִּירֻ֥הוּ עַל־יְדֵי־חָ֑רֶב מְנָ֖ת שֻׁעָלִ֣ים יִהְיֽוּ׃
But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by him[^9] will boast, for the mouths of those who speak lies will be stopped.
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ֮ יִשְׂמַ֢ח בֵּאלֹ֫הִ֥ים יִ֭תְהַלֵּל כָּל־הַנִּשְׁבָּ֣ע בּ֑וֹ כִּ֥י יִ֝סָּכֵ֗ר פִּ֣י דֽוֹבְרֵי־שָֽׁקֶר׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". Compare 1 Samuel 23:14 and 2 Samuel 15:23–28. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–12 are 63:1–11 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *ashachareka*, related to *shachar*, "dawn"; so perhaps "I seek you at dawn".
n.3: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 6, 9 and 10.
n.4: Literally "my flesh".
n.5: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.6: Literally "as with fat and fatness".
n.7: Literally "They will pour him out on the hands of the sword".
n.8: Or "foxes".
n.9: By God, or perhaps by the king.

v: For the director. A psalm of David.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
Hear my voice, God, in my complaint; protect my life from the terror of the enemy.
שְׁמַע־אֱלֹהִ֣ים קוֹלִ֣י בְשִׂיחִ֑י מִפַּ֥חַד א֝וֹיֵ֗ב תִּצֹּ֥ר חַיָּֽי׃
Hide me from the secret plots of evildoers, from the scheming throng of evildoers,[^2]
תַּ֭סְתִּירֵנִי מִסּ֣וֹד מְרֵעִ֑ים מֵ֝רִגְשַׁ֗ת פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
who sharpen their tongues like swords, and aim bitter words like arrows,
אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁנְנ֣וּ כַחֶ֣רֶב לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם דָּרְכ֥וּ חִ֝צָּ֗ם דָּבָ֥ר מָֽר׃
to shoot from hiding at the blameless; suddenly they shoot at him, and they have no fear.
לִיר֣וֹת בַּמִּסְתָּרִ֣ים תָּ֑ם פִּתְאֹ֥ם יֹ֝רֻ֗הוּ וְלֹ֣א יִירָֽאוּ׃
They encourage one another in an evil plan;[^3] they talk of hiding snares; they say, "Who will see them?"
יְחַזְּקוּ־לָ֨מוֹ ׀ דָּ֘בָ֤ר רָ֗ע יְֽ֭סַפְּרוּ לִטְמ֣וֹן מוֹקְשִׁ֑ים אָ֝מְר֗וּ מִ֣י יִרְאֶה־לָּֽמוֹ׃
They devise injustices: "We have perfected a well-made plan!" For the inner thoughts and the heart of a man are deep.[^4]
יַֽחְפְּֽשׂוּ־עוֹלֹ֗ת תַּ֭מְנוּ חֵ֣פֶשׂ מְחֻפָּ֑שׂ וְקֶ֥רֶב אִ֝֗ישׁ וְלֵ֣ב עָמֹֽק׃
But God will shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly they will be wounded.
וַיֹּרֵ֗ם אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים חֵ֥ץ פִּתְא֑וֹם הָ֝י֗וּ מַכּוֹתָֽם׃
They will be brought down, with their own tongues turned against them;[^5] all who see them will shake their heads.
וַיַּכְשִׁיל֣וּהוּ עָלֵ֣ימוֹ לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם יִ֝תְנֹדֲד֗וּ כָּל־רֹ֥אֵה בָֽם׃
Then all people will fear; they will proclaim the work of God and ponder what he has done.
וַיִּֽירְא֗וּ כָּל־אָ֫דָ֥ם וַ֭יַּגִּידוּ פֹּ֥עַל אֱלֹהִ֗ים וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥הוּ הִשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃
Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD[^6] and take refuge in him; let all the upright in heart give praise.[^7]
יִשְׂמַ֬ח צַדִּ֣יק בַּ֭יהוָה וְחָ֣סָה ב֑וֹ וְ֝יִתְהַֽלְל֗וּ כָּל־יִשְׁרֵי־לֵֽב׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–11 are 64:1–10 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Two different Hebrew words, *mere'im* and *po'alei aven*, both "evildoers".
n.3: Literally "They make strong for themselves an evil word".
n.4: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "They search out injustices; we have finished a searched-out search; and the inward part of a man and the heart are deep".
n.5: Literally "They make him stumble, their tongue against them".
n.6: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.7: Or "let them glory", "boast".

v: For the director. A psalm of David. A song.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָוִ֥ד שִֽׁיר׃
Praise waits for you in silence, God, in Zion,[^2] and to you vows will be fulfilled.
לְךָ֤ דֻֽמִיָּ֬ה תְהִלָּ֓ה אֱלֹ֘הִ֥ים בְּצִיּ֑וֹן וּ֝לְךָ֗ יְשֻׁלַּם־נֶֽדֶר׃
You who hear prayer, to you all flesh will come.
שֹׁמֵ֥עַ תְּפִלָּ֑ה עָ֝דֶ֗יךָ כָּל־בָּשָׂ֥ר יָבֹֽאוּ׃
When iniquities[^3] overwhelm me, you atone for our transgressions.[^4]
דִּבְרֵ֣י עֲ֭וֺנֹת גָּ֣בְרוּ מֶ֑נִּי פְּ֝שָׁעֵ֗ינוּ אַתָּ֥ה תְכַפְּרֵֽם׃
Happy[^5] is the one you choose and bring near to live in your courts! We will be satisfied with the good things of your house, your holy temple.
אַשְׁרֵ֤י ׀ תִּֽבְחַ֣ר וּתְקָרֵב֮ יִשְׁכֹּ֢ן חֲצֵ֫רֶ֥יךָ נִ֭שְׂבְּעָה בְּט֣וּב בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ קְ֝דֹ֗שׁ הֵיכָלֶֽךָ׃
With awesome deeds you answer us in righteousness, God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas,
נ֤וֹרָא֨וֹת ׀ בְּצֶ֣דֶק תַּ֭עֲנֵנוּ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֑נוּ מִבְטָ֥ח כָּל־קַצְוֵי־אֶ֝֗רֶץ וְיָ֣ם רְחֹקִֽים׃
who sets the mountains firm by his strength, clothed with might,
מֵכִ֣ין הָרִ֣ים בְּכֹח֑וֹ נֶ֝אְזָ֗ר בִּגְבוּרָֽה׃
who stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.
מַשְׁבִּ֤יחַ ׀ שְׁא֣וֹן יַ֭מִּים שְׁא֥וֹן גַּלֵּיהֶ֗ם וַהֲמ֥וֹן לְאֻמִּֽים׃
Those who live at the ends of the earth are in awe at your signs; you make the lands of the morning and the evening shout for joy.[^6]
וַיִּ֤ירְא֨וּ ׀ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י קְ֭צָוֺת מֵאוֹתֹתֶ֑יךָ מ֤וֹצָֽאֵי־בֹ֖קֶר וָעֶ֣רֶב תַּרְנִֽין׃
You care for the land and water it; you make it very rich. The stream of God is full of water; you provide their grain, for so you have prepared the land.[^7]
פָּ֤קֽ͏ַדְתָּ הָאָ֨רֶץ וַתְּשֹׁ֪קְקֶ֡הָ רַבַּ֬ת תַּעְשְׁרֶ֗נָּה פֶּ֣לֶג אֱ֭לֹהִים מָ֣לֵא מָ֑יִם תָּכִ֥ין דְּ֝גָנָ֗ם כִּי־כֵ֥ן תְּכִינֶֽהָ׃
You drench its furrows, you level its ridges; you soften it with showers and bless its growth.
תְּלָמֶ֣יהָ רַ֭וֵּה נַחֵ֣ת גְּדוּדֶ֑יהָ בִּרְבִיבִ֥ים תְּ֝מֹגְגֶ֗נָּה צִמְחָ֥הּ תְּבָרֵֽךְ׃
You crown the year with your goodness, and your tracks[^8] overflow with abundance.
עִ֭טַּרְתָּ שְׁנַ֣ת טוֹבָתֶ֑ךָ וּ֝מַעְגָּלֶ֗יךָ יִרְעֲפ֥וּן דָּֽשֶׁן׃
The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are clothed with joy.[^9]
יִ֭רְעֲפוּ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֑ר וְ֝גִ֗יל גְּבָע֥וֹת תַּחְגֹּֽרְנָה׃
The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are covered with grain; they shout for joy, yes, they sing.
לָבְשׁ֬וּ כָרִ֨ים ׀ הַצֹּ֗אן וַעֲמָקִ֥ים יַֽעַטְפוּ־בָ֑ר יִ֝תְרוֹעֲע֗וּ אַף־יָשִֽׁירוּ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–14 are 65:1–13 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "To you silence (is) praise, God, in Zion". The Septuagint reads "Praise is fitting for you", taking the word *dumiyyah*, "silence", from a similar root.
n.3: Literally "matters of iniquities".
n.4: Or "you forgive", "you cover". Hebrew *kipper*, the verb used for making atonement.
n.5: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.6: Literally "you make the goings out of the morning and the evening shout for joy", that is, the far east and the far west.
n.7: Literally "you have prepared it".
n.8: Literally "your wagon tracks", as God's chariot passes over the land.
n.9: Literally "gird themselves with joy".

v: For the director. A song. A psalm.[^1] Shout for joy to God, all the earth!
לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ שִׁ֣יר מִזְמ֑וֹר הָרִ֥יעוּ לֵ֝אלֹהִים כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Sing praises to the glory of his name; make his praise glorious.
זַמְּר֥וּ כְבֽוֹד־שְׁמ֑וֹ שִׂ֥ימוּ כָ֝ב֗וֹד תְּהִלָּֽתוֹ׃
Say to God, "How awesome are your deeds! Because of your great power your enemies cringe before you.
אִמְר֣וּ לֵ֭אלֹהִים מַה־נּוֹרָ֣א מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ בְּרֹ֥ב עֻ֝זְּךָ֗ יְֽכַחֲשׁ֖וּ לְךָ֣ אֹיְבֶֽיךָ׃
All the earth bows down to you and sings praises to you; they sing praises to your name." Selah.[^2]
כָּל־הָאָ֤רֶץ ׀ יִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לְ֭ךָ וִֽיזַמְּרוּ־לָ֑ךְ יְזַמְּר֖וּ שִׁמְךָ֣ סֶֽלָה׃
Come and see the works of God, awesome in his deeds toward human beings.
לְכ֣וּ וּ֭רְאוּ מִפְעֲל֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֑ים נוֹרָ֥א עֲ֝לִילָ֗ה עַל־בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the river on foot. There we rejoiced in him.[^3]
הָ֤פַךְ יָ֨ם ׀ לְֽיַבָּשָׁ֗ה בַּ֭נָּהָר יַֽעַבְר֣וּ בְרָ֑גֶל שָׁ֝֗ם נִשְׂמְחָה־בּֽוֹ׃
He rules by his might forever; his eyes keep watch on the nations. Let the rebellious not exalt themselves. Selah.
מֹ֘שֵׁ֤ל בִּגְבוּרָת֨וֹ ׀ עוֹלָ֗ם עֵ֭ינָיו בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם תִּצְפֶּ֑ינָה הַסוֹרְרִ֓ים ׀ אַל־*ירימו **יָר֖וּמוּ לָ֣מוֹ סֶֽלָה׃
Bless our God, you peoples; let the sound of his praise be heard,
בָּרְכ֖וּ עַמִּ֥ים ׀ אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְ֝הַשְׁמִ֗יעוּ ק֣וֹל תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃
who has kept us among the living,[^4] and has not let our feet slip.
הַשָּׂ֣ם נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ בַּֽחַיִּ֑ים וְלֹֽא־נָתַ֖ן לַמּ֣וֹט רַגְלֵֽנוּ׃
For you have tested us, God; you have refined us as silver is refined.
כִּֽי־בְחַנְתָּ֥נוּ אֱלֹהִ֑ים צְ֝רַפְתָּ֗נוּ כִּצְרָף־כָּֽסֶף׃
You brought us into the net;[^5] you laid a heavy burden on our backs.[^6]
הֲבֵאתָ֥נוּ בַמְּצוּדָ֑ה שַׂ֖מְתָּ מוּעָקָ֣ה בְמָתְנֵֽינוּ׃
You let people ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water, but you brought us out to a place of abundance.[^7]
הִרְכַּ֥בְתָּ אֱנ֗וֹשׁ לְרֹ֫אשֵׁ֥נוּ בָּֽאנוּ־בָאֵ֥שׁ וּבַמַּ֑יִם וַ֝תּוֹצִיאֵ֗נוּ לָֽרְוָיָֽה׃
I will come into your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to you,
אָב֣וֹא בֵיתְךָ֣ בְעוֹל֑וֹת אֲשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְךָ֣ נְדָרָֽי׃
the vows my lips uttered and my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.
אֲשֶׁר־פָּצ֥וּ שְׂפָתָ֑י וְדִבֶּר־פִּ֝֗י בַּצַּר־לִֽי׃
I will offer you burnt offerings of fat animals, with the smoke of rams; I will offer bulls with goats. Selah.
עֹ֘ל֤וֹת מֵחִ֣ים אַעֲלֶה־לָּ֭ךְ עִם־קְטֹ֣רֶת אֵילִ֑ים אֶ֥עֱשֶֽׂה בָקָ֖ר עִם־עַתּוּדִ֣ים סֶֽלָה׃
Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for me.[^8]
לְכֽוּ־שִׁמְע֣וּ וַ֭אֲסַפְּרָה כָּל־יִרְאֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשָׂ֣ה לְנַפְשִֽׁי׃
I cried aloud to him with my mouth, and his praise[^9] was on my tongue.
אֵלָ֥יו פִּֽי־קָרָ֑אתִי וְ֝רוֹמַ֗ם תַּ֣חַת לְשׁוֹנִֽי׃
If I had cherished wickedness in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
אָ֭וֶן אִם־רָאִ֣יתִי בְלִבִּ֑י לֹ֖א יִשְׁמַ֣ע ׀ אֲדֹנָֽי׃
But truly God has listened; he has paid attention to the voice of my prayer.
אָ֭כֵן שָׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהִ֑ים הִ֝קְשִׁ֗יב בְּק֣וֹל תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃
Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, or his faithful love[^10] from me.
בָּר֥וּךְ אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־הֵסִ֘יר תְּפִלָּתִ֥י וְ֝חַסְדּ֗וֹ מֵאִתִּֽי׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verses 7 and 15.
n.3: Or "There let us rejoice in him". Compare the crossing of the sea (Exodus 14) and of the Jordan (Joshua 3).
n.4: Literally "who set our soul (*nephesh*) in life".
n.5: Or "into prison", "into a stronghold".
n.6: Literally "on our loins".
n.7: Literally "to saturation". The Septuagint reads "to refreshment".
n.8: Literally "for my soul (*nephesh*)".
n.9: Literally "exaltation".
n.10: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.

v: For the director. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥ח בִּנְגִינֹ֗ת מִזְמ֥וֹר שִֽׁיר׃
May God be gracious to us and bless us; may he make his face shine on us.[^2] Selah.[^3]
אֱ[t]לֹהִ֗ים יְחָנֵּ֥נוּ וִֽיבָרְכֵ֑נוּ יָ֤אֵ֥־[c]ר פָּנָ֖יו אִתָּ֣נוּ סֶֽלָה׃
May your way be known on earth, your salvation among all nations.[^4]
לָדַ֣עַת בָּאָ֣רֶץ דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ בְּכָל־גּ֝וֹיִ֗ם יְשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
Let the peoples praise you, God; let all the peoples praise you.
יוֹד֖וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים ׀ אֱלֹהִ֑ים י֝וֹד֗וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you judge the peoples with fairness, and guide the nations on earth. Selah.
יִֽשְׂמְח֥וּ וִֽירַנְּנ֗וּ לְאֻ֫מִּ֥ים כִּֽי־תִשְׁפֹּ֣ט עַמִּ֣ים מִישׁ֑וֹר וּלְאֻמִּ֓ים ׀ בָּאָ֖רֶץ תַּנְחֵ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
Let the peoples praise you, God; let all the peoples praise you.
יוֹד֖וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים ׀ אֱלֹהִ֑ים י֝וֹד֗וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃
The earth has yielded its harvest; may God, our God, bless us.
אֶ֭רֶץ נָתְנָ֣ה יְבוּלָ֑הּ יְ֝בָרְכֵ֗נוּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
May God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear him.
יְבָרְכֵ֥נוּ אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְיִֽירְא֥וּ אֹ֝ת֗וֹ כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–8 are 67:1–7 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "make his face shine with us". The verse echoes the priestly blessing in Numbers 6:24–26.
n.3: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 5.
n.4: Literally "to know on earth your way", that is, so that your way may be known.

v: For the director. Of David. A psalm. A song.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ לְדָוִ֗ד מִזְמ֥וֹר שִֽׁיר׃
Let God rise up, let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee before him.[^2]
יָק֣וּם אֱ֭לֹהִים יָפ֣וּצוּ אוֹיְבָ֑יו וְיָנ֥וּסוּ מְ֝שַׂנְאָ֗יו מִפָּנָֽיו׃
As smoke is blown away, so blow them away; as wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish before God.
כְּהִנְדֹּ֥ף עָשָׁ֗ן תִּ֫נְדֹּ֥ף כְּהִמֵּ֣ס דּ֭וֹנַג מִפְּנֵי־אֵ֑שׁ יֹאבְד֥וּ רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים מִפְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃
But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God; let them celebrate with joy.
וְֽצַדִּיקִ֗ים יִשְׂמְח֣וּ יַֽ֭עַלְצוּ לִפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִ֗ים וְיָשִׂ֥ישׂוּ בְשִׂמְחָֽה׃
Sing to God, sing praises to his name; build up a road for the one who rides through the deserts.[^3] His name is the LORD;[^4] rejoice before him.
שִׁ֤ירוּ ׀ לֵֽאלֹהִים֮ זַמְּר֢וּ שְׁ֫מ֥וֹ סֹ֡לּוּ לָרֹכֵ֣ב בָּ֭עֲרָבוֹת בְּיָ֥הּ שְׁמ֗וֹ וְעִלְז֥וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃
A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in his holy dwelling.
אֲבִ֣י יְ֭תוֹמִים וְדַיַּ֣ן אַלְמָנ֑וֹת אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בִּמְע֥וֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
God gives the lonely a home to live in; he leads prisoners out into prosperity,[^5] but the rebellious live in a parched land.
אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ מ֘וֹשִׁ֤יב יְחִידִ֨ים ׀ בַּ֗יְתָה מוֹצִ֣יא אֲ֭סִירִים בַּכּוֹשָׁר֑וֹת אַ֥ךְ ס֝וֹרֲרִ֗ים שָׁכְנ֥וּ צְחִיחָֽה׃
God, you went out before your people; you marched through the wasteland.[^6] Selah.[^7]
אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים בְּ֭צֵאתְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּצַעְדְּךָ֖ בִֽישִׁימ֣וֹן סֶֽלָה׃
The earth shook, the heavens poured down rain before God, the One of Sinai,[^8] before God, the God of Israel.
אֶ֤רֶץ רָעָ֨שָׁה ׀ אַף־שָׁמַ֣יִם נָטְפוּ֮ מִפְּנֵ֢י אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים זֶ֥ה סִינַ֑י מִפְּנֵ֥י אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
You poured out abundant rain, God; when your inheritance was weary, you restored it.
גֶּ֣שֶׁם נְ֭דָבוֹת תָּנִ֣יף אֱלֹהִ֑ים נַחֲלָתְךָ֥ וְ֝נִלְאָ֗ה אַתָּ֥ה כֽוֹנַנְתּֽ͏ָהּ׃
Your people[^9] settled in it; in your goodness, God, you provided for the afflicted.
חַיָּתְךָ֥ יָֽשְׁבוּ־בָ֑הּ תָּ֤כִ֥ין בְּטוֹבָתְךָ֖ לֶעָנִ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים׃
The Lord gives the word; the women who bring the good news are a great army:[^10]
אֲדֹנָ֥י יִתֶּן־אֹ֑מֶר הַֽ֝מְבַשְּׂר֗וֹת צָבָ֥א רָֽב׃
"The kings of armies flee, they flee!" And the woman who stays at home[^11] divides the plunder.
מַלְכֵ֣י צְ֭בָאוֹת יִדֹּד֣וּן יִדֹּד֑וּן וּנְוַת־בַּ֝֗יִת תְּחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁלָֽל׃
Though you lie down among the sheepfolds,[^12] the wings of a dove are covered with silver, its feathers with shining gold.
אִֽם־תִּשְׁכְּבוּן֮ בֵּ֢ין שְׁפַ֫תָּ֥יִם כַּנְפֵ֣י י֭וֹנָה נֶחְפָּ֣ה בַכֶּ֑סֶף וְ֝אֶבְרוֹתֶ֗יהָ בִּֽירַקְרַ֥ק חָרֽוּץ׃
When the Almighty[^13] scattered kings there, it snowed on Zalmon.[^14]
בְּפָ֘רֵ֤שׂ שַׁדַּ֓י מְלָ֘כִ֤ים בָּ֗הּ תַּשְׁלֵ֥ג בְּצַלְמֽוֹן׃
A mountain of God[^15] is the mountain of Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan.
הַר־אֱ֭לֹהִים הַר־בָּשָׁ֑ן הַ֥ר גַּ֝בְנֻנִּ֗ים הַר־בָּשָֽׁן׃
Why do you look with envy,[^16] you mountains of many peaks, at the mountain God desired for his dwelling? Yes, the LORD[^17] will dwell there forever.
לָ֤מָּה ׀ תְּֽרַצְּדוּן֮ הָרִ֢ים גַּבְנֻ֫נִּ֥ים הָהָ֗ר חָמַ֣ד אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְשִׁבְתּ֑וֹ אַף־יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִשְׁכֹּ֥ן לָנֶֽצַח׃
The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them, Sinai is in the holy place.[^18]
רֶ֤כֶב אֱלֹהִ֗ים רִבֹּתַ֣יִם אַלְפֵ֣י שִׁנְאָ֑ן אֲדֹנָ֥י בָ֝֗ם סִינַ֥י בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
You went up to the heights; you led captives away; you received gifts from people,[^19] even from the rebellious, so that the LORD God might dwell there.
עָ֘לִ֤יתָ לַמָּר֨וֹם ׀ שָׁ֘בִ֤יתָ שֶּׁ֗בִי לָקַ֣חְתָּ מַ֭תָּנוֹת בָּאָדָ֑ם וְאַ֥ף ס֝וֹרְרִ֗ים לִשְׁכֹּ֤ן ׀ יָ֬הּ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Blessed be the Lord, who day after day bears our burden,[^20] the God who is our salvation. Selah.
בָּ֤ר֣וּךְ אֲדֹנָי֮ י֤וֹם ׀ י֥וֹם יַֽעֲמָס־לָ֗נוּ הָ֘אֵ֤ל יְֽשׁוּעָתֵ֬נוּ סֶֽלָה׃
Our God is a God who saves,[^21] and to GOD the Lord belong the ways of escape from death.[^22]
הָ֤אֵ֣ל ׀ לָנוּ֮ אֵ֤ל לְֽמוֹשָׁ֫ע֥וֹת וְלֵיהוִ֥ה אֲדֹנָ֑י לַ֝מָּ֗וֶת תּוֹצָאֽוֹת׃
Surely God will crush the heads of his enemies, the hairy crown of the one who walks in his guilt.
אַךְ־אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִמְחַץ֮ רֹ֤אשׁ אֹ֫יְבָ֥יו קָדְקֹ֥ד שֵׂעָ֑ר מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בַּאֲשָׁמָֽיו׃
The Lord said, "I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
אָמַ֣ר אֲ֭דֹנָי מִבָּשָׁ֣ן אָשִׁ֑יב אָ֝שִׁ֗יב מִֽמְּצֻל֥וֹת יָֽם׃
so that your foot may crush them in blood,[^23] and the tongues of your dogs may have their share of the enemies."[^24]
לְמַ֤עַן ׀ תִּֽמְחַ֥ץ רַגְלְךָ֗ בְּ֫דָ֥ם לְשׁ֥וֹן כְּלָבֶ֑יךָ מֵאֹיְבִ֥ים מִנֵּֽהוּ׃
Your processions have been seen, God, the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.[^25]
רָא֣וּ הֲלִיכוֹתֶ֣יךָ אֱלֹהִ֑ים הֲלִ֘יכ֤וֹת אֵלִ֖י מַלְכִּ֣י בַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
The singers go in front, the musicians last, and between them young women playing tambourines.
קִדְּמ֣וּ שָׁ֭רִים אַחַ֣ר נֹגְנִ֑ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲ֝לָמ֗וֹת תּוֹפֵפֽוֹת׃
In the assemblies bless God, the LORD, you who come from the spring of Israel.[^26]
בְּֽ֭מַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכ֣וּ אֱלֹהִ֑ים יְ֝הוָ֗ה מִמְּק֥וֹר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
There is little Benjamin, leading them,[^27] the princes of Judah in their throng,[^28] the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
שָׁ֤ם בִּנְיָמִ֨ן ׀ צָעִ֡יר רֹדֵ֗ם שָׂרֵ֣י יְ֭הוּדָה רִגְמָתָ֑ם שָׂרֵ֥י זְ֝בֻל֗וּן שָׂרֵ֥י נַפְתָּלִֽי׃
Your God has commanded your strength.[^29] Show your strength, God, you who have acted for us.
צִוָּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עֻ֫זֶּ֥ךָ עוּזָּ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים ז֝֗וּ פָּעַ֥לְתָּ לָּֽנוּ׃
Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.
מֵֽ֭הֵיכָלֶךָ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם לְךָ֤ יוֹבִ֖ילוּ מְלָכִ֣ים שָֽׁי׃
Rebuke the beast among the reeds,[^30] the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, until it bows down with pieces of silver. He has scattered the peoples who delight in war.[^31]
גְּעַ֨ר חַיַּ֪ת קָנֶ֡ה עֲדַ֤ת אַבִּירִ֨ים ׀ בְּעֶגְלֵ֬י עַמִּ֗ים מִתְרַפֵּ֥ס בְּרַצֵּי־כָ֑סֶף בִּזַּ֥ר עַ֝מִּ֗ים קְרָב֥וֹת יֶחְפָּֽצוּ׃
Envoys[^32] will come from Egypt; Cush[^33] will quickly stretch out its hands to God.
יֶאֱתָ֣יוּ חַ֭שְׁמַנִּים מִנִּ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם כּ֥וּשׁ תָּרִ֥יץ יָ֝דָ֗יו לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord. Selah.
מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָ֭אָרֶץ שִׁ֣ירוּ לֵאלֹהִ֑ים זַמְּר֖וּ אֲדֹנָ֣י סֶֽלָה׃
To the one who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens! Listen, he utters his voice, a mighty voice.
לָ֭רֹכֵב בִּשְׁמֵ֣י שְׁמֵי־קֶ֑דֶם הֵ֥ן יִתֵּ֥ן בְּ֝קוֹלוֹ ק֣וֹל עֹֽז׃
Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.
תְּנ֥וּ עֹ֗ז לֵֽאלֹ֫הִ֥ים עַֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל גַּאֲוָת֑וֹ וְ֝עֻזּ֗וֹ בַּשְּׁחָקִֽים׃
You are awesome, God, from your sanctuary.[^34] The God of Israel is the one who gives strength and power to his people. Blessed be God!
נ֤וֹרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֗ים מִֽמִּקְדָּ֫שֶׁ֥יךָ אֵ֤ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ה֤וּא נֹתֵ֨ן ׀ עֹ֖ז וְתַעֲצֻמ֥וֹת לָעָ֗ם בָּר֥וּךְ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–36 are 68:1–35 in most English Bibles. This psalm is one of the most difficult in the Psalter. Many of its words are rare, some lines seem to be quotations from older poems, and the connection between its sections is often unclear. The notes mark the most uncertain lines.
n.2: Compare Numbers 10:35, the words Moses spoke whenever the ark set out.
n.3: Literally "cast up (a highway) for the one who rides in the *aravot*", the desert plains. Some take *aravot* as "clouds", comparing verse 34 and a title of the god Baal in Canaanite poetry, "rider of the clouds". The verb *sollu* may also mean "lift up (a song)".
n.4: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH, as in *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah". Also in verse 19.
n.5: Hebrew *kosharot*, found only here, perhaps "prosperity" or "singing".
n.6: Literally "God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wasteland", a sentence that continues in verse 9.
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verses 20 and 33. Verses 8–9 are close to Judges 5:4–5.
n.8: Literally "this Sinai", perhaps an old way of saying "the One of Sinai" (compare Judges 5:5).
n.9: Literally "Your living things", perhaps "your flock" or "your community".
n.10: Or "The Lord gives the word; great is the army of women who bring the news".
n.11: Or "the beauty of the house". The Hebrew of verses 13–15 is very difficult, and their connection with the context is uncertain.
n.12: Or "among the campfires", "between the saddlebags". The word is close to the one in Judges 5:16.
n.13: Hebrew *Shaddai*. The meaning of the name is uncertain.
n.14: A mountain, perhaps the one near Shechem (Judges 9:48), or one in Bashan. *Zalmon* is related to *tselem*, "shadow, darkness".
n.15: Or "A mighty mountain", as "mountains of God" can mean mighty mountains (compare 36:7; 36:6 in most English Bibles).
n.16: Hebrew *teratsedun*, found only here; the meaning is uncertain.
n.17: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.18: Literally "the Lord among them, Sinai, in holiness". Some scholars read "the Lord has come from Sinai into the holy place", with a small change to the Hebrew (compare Deuteronomy 33:2).
n.19: Literally "among *adam* (humankind)". Ephesians 4:8 quotes this verse in a form that reads "he gave gifts to people".
n.21: Literally "God is for us a God of acts of salvation".
n.22: Literally "to death the goings out". *GOD the Lord*: Hebrew *YHWH Adonai*. Next to "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.23: Literally "so that you may crush your foot in blood". The Septuagint reads "so that your foot may be dipped in blood" (compare 58:11; 58:10 in most English Bibles).
n.24: Literally "the tongue of your dogs, from the enemies its portion".
n.26: That is, you descendants of Israel.
n.28: Hebrew *rigmatam*, found only here, perhaps "their crowd".
n.29: The Septuagint reads "Command your strength, God".
n.30: Probably Egypt, pictured as a crocodile or hippopotamus among the reeds of the Nile.
n.31: The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult. Literally "...with calves of peoples, trampling himself with pieces of silver; he scattered peoples who delight in wars".
n.32: Hebrew *chashmannim*, found only here; the meaning is uncertain, perhaps "envoys", "nobles" or "bronze".
n.33: The lands on the upper Nile, south of Egypt.

v: For the director. According to "Lilies".[^1] Of David.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ ׀ עַֽל־שׁוֹשַׁנִּ֬ים לְדָוִֽד׃
Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck.[^3]
הוֹשִׁיעֵ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֤י בָ֖אוּ מַ֣יִם עַד־נָֽפֶשׁ׃
I sink in deep mire, where there is no foothold; I have come into deep waters, and the flood sweeps over me.
טָבַ֤עְתִּי ׀ בִּיוֵ֣ן מְ֭צוּלָה וְאֵ֣ין מָעֳמָ֑ד בָּ֥אתִי בְמַעֲמַקֵּי־מַ֝֗יִם וְשִׁבֹּ֥לֶת שְׁטָפָֽתְנִי׃
I am worn out with my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes grow dim as I wait for my God.
יָגַ֣עְתִּי בְקָרְאִי֮ נִחַ֢ר גְּר֫וֹנִ֥י כָּל֥וּ עֵינַ֑י מְ֝יַחֵ֗ל לֵאלֹהָֽי׃
More than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause;[^4] mighty are those who would destroy me, my enemies without reason.[^5] What I did not steal, must I now give back?
רַבּ֤וּ ׀ מִשַּׂעֲר֣וֹת רֹאשִׁי֮ שֹׂנְאַ֢י חִ֫נָּ֥ם עָצְמ֣וּ מַ֭צְמִיתַי אֹיְבַ֣י שֶׁ֑קֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־גָ֝זַ֗לְתִּי אָ֣ז אָשִֽׁיב׃
God, you know my folly; my guilty deeds are not hidden from you.
אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים אַתָּ֣ה יָ֭דַעְתָּ לְאִוַּלְתִּ֑י וְ֝אַשְׁמוֹתַ֗י מִמְּךָ֥ לֹא־נִכְחָֽדוּ׃
Do not let those who hope in you be put to shame because of me, Lord GOD of Armies;[^6] do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, God of Israel.
אַל־יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ בִ֨י ׀ קֹוֶיךָ֮ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֗ה צְבָ֫א֥וֹת אַל־יִכָּ֣לְמוּ בִ֣י מְבַקְשֶׁ֑יךָ אֱ֝לֹהֵ֗י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
For it is for your sake that I have borne insults, that shame has covered my face.
כִּֽי־עָ֭לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֣אתִי חֶרְפָּ֑ה כִּסְּתָ֖ה כְלִמָּ֣ה פָנָֽי׃
I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's sons.
מ֖[d]וּזָר הָיִ֣יתִי לְאֶחָ֑י וְ֝נָכְרִ֗י לִבְנֵ֥י אִמִּֽי׃
For zeal for your house has consumed me,[^7] and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.[^8]
כִּֽי־קִנְאַ֣ת בֵּיתְךָ֣ אֲכָלָ֑תְנִי וְחֶרְפּ֥וֹת ח֝וֹרְפֶ֗יךָ נָפְל֥וּ עָלָֽי׃
When I wept and humbled myself with fasting,[^9] it brought insults on me.
וָאֶבְכֶּ֣ה בַצּ֣וֹם נַפְשִׁ֑י וַתְּהִ֖י לַחֲרָפ֣וֹת לִֽי׃
When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them.
וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לְבוּשִׁ֣י שָׂ֑ק וָאֱהִ֖י לָהֶ֣ם לְמָשָֽׁל׃
Those who sit at the gate talk about me, and drunkards make songs about me.[^10]
יָשִׂ֣יחוּ בִ֭י יֹ֣שְׁבֵי שָׁ֑עַר וּ֝נְגִינ֗וֹת שׁוֹתֵ֥י שֵׁכָֽר׃
But as for me, my prayer is to you, LORD, at a time of favor. God, in your great faithful love,[^11] answer me with your sure salvation.[^12]
וַאֲנִ֤י תְפִלָּתִֽי־לְךָ֨ ׀ יְהוָ֡ה עֵ֤ת רָצ֗וֹן אֱלֹהִ֥ים בְּרָב־חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ עֲ֝נֵ֗נִי בֶּאֱמֶ֥ת יִשְׁעֶֽךָ׃
Rescue me from the mire, and do not let me sink; let me be rescued from those who hate me, and from the deep waters.
הַצִּילֵ֣נִי מִ֭טִּיט וְאַל־אֶטְבָּ֑עָה אִנָּצְלָ֥ה מִ֝שֹּֽׂנְאַ֗י וּמִמַּֽעֲמַקֵּי־מָֽיִם׃
Do not let the flood sweep over me, or the deep swallow me up, or the pit[^13] close its mouth over me.
אַל־תִּשְׁטְפֵ֤נִי ׀ שִׁבֹּ֣לֶת מַ֭יִם וְאַל־תִּבְלָעֵ֣נִי מְצוּלָ֑ה וְאַל־תֶּאְטַר־עָלַ֖י בְּאֵ֣ר פִּֽיהָ׃
Answer me, LORD, for your faithful love is good; in your great compassion turn to me.
עֲנֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה כִּי־ט֣וֹב חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ פְּנֵ֣ה אֵלָֽי׃
Do not hide your face from your servant, for I am in distress; answer me quickly.
וְאַל־תַּסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נֶיךָ מֵֽעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּֽי־צַר־לִ֝֗י מַהֵ֥ר עֲנֵֽנִי׃
Come near to me[^14] and redeem me; set me free because of my enemies.
קָרְבָ֣ה אֶל־נַפְשִׁ֣י גְאָלָ֑הּ לְמַ֖עַן אֹיְבַ֣י פְּדֵֽנִי׃
You know the insults I suffer, my shame and my disgrace; all my adversaries are before you.
אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֗עְתָּ חֶרְפָּתִ֣י וּ֭בָשְׁתִּי וּכְלִמָּתִ֑י נֶ֝גְדְּךָ֗ כָּל־צוֹרְרָֽי׃
Insults have broken my heart, and I am sick.[^15] I looked for sympathy, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none.
חֶרְפָּ֤ה ׀ שָֽׁבְרָ֥ה לִבִּ֗י וָֽאָ֫נ֥וּשָׁה וָאֲקַוֶּ֣ה לָנ֣וּד וָאַ֑יִן וְ֝לַמְנַחֲמִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א מָצָֽאתִי׃
They gave me poison[^16] for food, and for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink.[^17]
וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ בְּבָרוּתִ֣י רֹ֑אשׁ וְ֝לִצְמָאִ֗י יַשְׁק֥וּנִי חֹֽמֶץ׃
Let their table before them become a trap, and a snare for those at ease.[^18]
יְהִֽי־שֻׁלְחָנָ֣ם לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם לְפָ֑ח וְלִשְׁלוֹמִ֥ים לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and make their loins tremble continually.[^19]
תֶּחְשַׁ֣כְנָה עֵ֭ינֵיהֶם מֵרְא֑וֹת וּ֝מָתְנֵ֗יהֶם תָּמִ֥יד הַמְעַֽד׃
Pour out your fury on them, and let your burning anger overtake them.
שְׁפָךְ־עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם זַעְמֶ֑ךָ וַחֲר֥וֹן אַ֝פְּךָ֗ יַשִּׂיגֵֽם׃
Let their camp be desolate; let no one live in their tents.[^20]
תְּהִי־טִֽירָתָ֥ם נְשַׁמָּ֑ה בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם אַל־יְהִ֥י יֹשֵֽׁב׃
For they persecute the one you have struck, and they talk about the pain of those you have wounded.[^21]
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־הִכִּ֣יתָ רָדָ֑פוּ וְאֶל־מַכְא֖וֹב חֲלָלֶ֣יךָ יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃
Add guilt to their guilt; let them have no share in your righteousness.[^22]
תְּֽנָה־עָ֭וֺן עַל־עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְאַל־יָ֝בֹ֗אוּ בְּצִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃
Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; let them not be enrolled[^23] with the righteous.
יִ֭מָּחֽוּ מִסֵּ֣פֶר חַיִּ֑ים וְעִ֥ם צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים אַל־יִכָּתֵֽבוּ׃
But I am afflicted and in pain; let your salvation, God, set me safe on high.
וַ֭אֲנִי עָנִ֣י וְכוֹאֵ֑ב יְשׁוּעָתְךָ֖ אֱלֹהִ֣ים תְּשַׂגְּבֵֽנִי׃
I will praise the name of God with a song, and magnify him with thanksgiving.
אֲהַֽלְלָ֣ה שֵׁם־אֱלֹהִ֣ים בְּשִׁ֑יר וַאֲגַדְּלֶ֥נּוּ בְתוֹדָֽה׃
This will please the LORD more than an ox, a bull with its horns and hoofs.
וְתִיטַ֣ב לַֽ֭יהוָה מִשּׁ֥וֹר פָּ֗ר מַקְרִ֥ן מַפְרִֽיס׃
The humble will see it and be glad; you who seek God, let your hearts revive.
רָא֣וּ עֲנָוִ֣ים יִשְׂמָ֑חוּ דֹּרְשֵׁ֥י אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים וִיחִ֥י לְבַבְכֶֽ[t]ם׃
For the LORD hears the needy, and does not despise his own who are prisoners.
כִּֽי־שֹׁמֵ֣עַ אֶל־אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־אֲ֝סִירָ֗יו לֹ֣א בָזָֽה׃
Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
יְֽ֭הַלְלוּהוּ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֑רֶץ יַ֝מִּ֗ים וְֽכָל־רֹמֵ֥שׂ בָּֽם׃
For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah; they will live there and possess it.
כִּ֤י אֱלֹהִ֨ים ׀ י֘וֹשִׁ֤יעַ צִיּ֗וֹן וְ֭יִבְנֶה עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ שָׁ֝֗ם וִירֵשֽׁוּהָ׃
The descendants[^24] of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will live in it.
וְזֶ֣רַע עֲ֭בָדָיו יִנְחָל֑וּהָ וְאֹהֲבֵ֥י שְׁ֝מ֗וֹ יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-shoshannim*, "according to lilies", probably the name of a tune (see the title of Psalm 45).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–37 are 69:1–36 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *nephesh*, here "throat, neck". Elsewhere it means soul, life, self, as in verses 11 and 19.
n.4: Compare John 15:25.
n.5: Literally "my enemies of falsehood".
n.6: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.7: Quoted in John 2:17.
n.8: Quoted in Romans 15:3.
n.9: Literally "When I wept in the fasting of my soul (*nephesh*)".
n.10: Literally "and the songs of those who drink beer". *Beer*: or "fermented drink"; brewed from grain.
n.11: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verse 17.
n.12: Literally "in the faithfulness of your salvation".
n.13: Literally "the well".
n.14: Literally "to my soul (*nephesh*)".
n.15: Hebrew *va'anushah*, found only here, perhaps "I am in despair".
n.16: Hebrew *rosh*, a bitter and poisonous plant. The Septuagint reads "gall"; compare Matthew 27:34.
n.17: Compare Matthew 27:48; Mark 15:36; John 19:28–29.
n.18: Or "and for their allies". The Septuagint reads "and a retribution", and Romans 11:9–10 quotes verses 23–24 in that form.
n.19: The Septuagint reads "and bend their backs continually", the wording quoted in Romans 11:10.
n.20: Acts 1:20 applies this verse to Judas.
n.21: The Septuagint reads "and they have added to the pain of those you have wounded".
n.22: Literally "do not let them come into your righteousness".

v: For the director. Of David. To bring to remembrance.[^1]
לַ֝מְנַצֵּ֗חַ לְדָוִ֥ד לְהַזְכִּֽיר׃
God, come to rescue me;[^2] LORD,[^3] come quickly to help me!
אֱלֹהִ֥ים לְהַצִּילֵ֑נִי יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי חֽוּשָֽׁה׃
Let those who seek my life[^4] be put to shame and confounded; let those who delight in my harm be turned back and disgraced.
יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ וְיַחְפְּרוּ֮ מְבַקְשֵׁ֢י נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י יִסֹּ֣גוּ אָ֭חוֹר וְיִכָּלְמ֑וּ חֲ֝פֵצֵ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃
Let those who say, "Aha! Aha!" turn back because of their shame.[^5]
יָ֭שׁוּבוּ עַל־עֵ֣קֶב בָּשְׁתָּ֑ם הָ֝אֹמְרִ֗ים הֶ֘אָ֥ח ׀ הֶאָֽח׃
But let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation say always, "Great is God!"[^6]
יָ֘שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְיִשְׂמְח֨וּ ׀ בְּךָ֗ כָּֽל־מְבַ֫קְשֶׁ֥יךָ וְיֹאמְר֣וּ תָ֭מִיד יִגְדַּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֹ֝הֲבֵ֗י יְשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
As for me, I am afflicted and needy; God, come quickly to me! You are my help and my deliverer; LORD, do not delay.[^7]
וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְיוֹן֮ אֱלֹהִ֢ים חֽוּשָׁ֫ה־לִּ֥י עֶזְרִ֣י וּמְפַלְטִ֣י אַ֑תָּה יְ֝הוָ֗ה אַל־תְּאַחַֽר׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". *To bring to remembrance*: Hebrew *lehazkir* (see the note on the title of Psalm 38). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–6 are 70:1–5 in most English Bibles. Psalm 70 is almost the same as 40:14–18 (40:13–17 in most English Bibles). In several places it has *Elohim*, "God", where Psalm 40 has "the LORD" (see the note on 42:2), and the notes below give the other differences.
n.2: Literally "God, to rescue me". Psalm 40:14 (40:13 in most English Bibles) has "Be pleased, LORD, to rescue me".
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Psalm 40:15 (40:14 in most English Bibles) adds "together" and "to sweep it away".
n.5: Literally "turn back on the heel of their shame". Psalm 40:16 (40:15 in most English Bibles) has "Let them be appalled because of their shame", and "who say to me".
n.6: Psalm 40:17 (40:16 in most English Bibles) has "Great is the LORD!"
n.7: Psalm 40:18 (40:17 in most English Bibles) has "may the Lord think of me" for "God, come quickly to me", and "my God, do not delay" for "LORD, do not delay".

v: In you, LORD,[^1] I take refuge; let me never be put to shame.[^2]
בְּךָֽ־יְהוָ֥ה חָסִ֑יתִי אַל־אֵב֥וֹשָׁה לְעוֹלָֽם׃
In your righteousness rescue me and deliver me; turn your ear to me and save me.
בְּצִדְקָתְךָ֗ תַּצִּילֵ֥נִי וּֽתְפַלְּטֵ֑נִי הַטֵּֽה־אֵלַ֥י אָ֝זְנְךָ֗ וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃
Be a rock of refuge for me,[^3] where I can always come; you have given the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.
הֱיֵ֤ה לִ֨י ׀ לְצ֥וּר מָע֡וֹן לָב֗וֹא תָּמִ֗יד צִוִּ֥יתָ לְהוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נִי כִּֽי־סַלְעִ֖י וּמְצוּדָתִ֣י אָֽתָּה׃
My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and the ruthless.
אֱ‍ֽלֹהַ֗י פַּ֭לְּטֵנִי מִיַּ֣ד רָשָׁ֑ע מִכַּ֖ף מְעַוֵּ֣ל וְחוֹמֵץ׃
For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my trust from my youth.
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה תִקְוָתִ֑י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְ֝הוִ֗ה מִבְטַחִ֥י מִנְּעוּרָֽי׃
On you I have leaned from birth;[^4] you are the one who brought me out[^5] from my mother's womb. My praise is always of you.
עָלֶ֤יךָ ׀ נִסְמַ֬כְתִּי מִבֶּ֗טֶן מִמְּעֵ֣י אִ֭מִּי אַתָּ֣ה גוֹזִ֑י בְּךָ֖ תְהִלָּתִ֣י תָמִֽיד׃
I have become like a portent to many, but you are my strong refuge.
כְּ֭מוֹפֵת הָיִ֣יתִי לְרַבִּ֑ים וְ֝אַתָּ֗ה מַֽחֲסִי־עֹֽז׃
My mouth is filled with your praise, with your splendor all day long.
יִמָּ֣לֵא פִ֭י תְּהִלָּתֶ֑ךָ כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם תִּפְאַרְתֶּֽךָ׃
Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not abandon me when my strength fails.
אַֽל־תַּ֭שְׁלִיכֵנִי לְעֵ֣ת זִקְנָ֑ה כִּכְל֥וֹת כֹּ֝חִ֗י אֽ͏ַל־תַּעַזְבֵֽנִי׃
For my enemies speak against me; those who watch for my life[^6] plot together,
כִּֽי־אָמְר֣וּ אוֹיְבַ֣י לִ֑י וְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י נוֹעֲצ֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃
saying, "God has abandoned him; pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him."
לֵ֭אמֹר אֱלֹהִ֣ים עֲזָב֑וֹ רִֽדְפ֥וּ וְ֝תִפְשֻׂ֗וּהוּ כִּי־אֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃
God, do not be far from me; my God, hurry to help me!
אֱ֭לֹהִים אַל־תִּרְחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי *חישה **חֽוּשָׁה׃
Let my accusers[^7] be put to shame and consumed; let those who seek my harm be covered with scorn and disgrace.
יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ יִכְלוּ֮ שֹׂטְנֵ֢י נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י יַֽעֲט֣וּ חֶ֭רְפָּה וּכְלִמָּ֑ה מְ֝בַקְשֵׁ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃
But as for me, I will always hope, and I will add to all your praise.
וַ֭אֲנִי תָּמִ֣יד אֲיַחֵ֑ל וְ֝הוֹסַפְתִּ֗י עַל־כָּל־תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
My mouth will tell of your righteousness, of your salvation all day long, though I do not know their number.[^8]
פִּ֤י ׀ יְסַפֵּ֬ר צִדְקָתֶ֗ךָ כָּל־הַיּ֥וֹם תְּשׁוּעָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י לֹ֖א יָדַ֣עְתִּי סְפֹרֽוֹת׃
I will come with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD; I will make mention of your righteousness, yours alone.
אָב֗וֹא בִּ֭גְבֻרוֹת אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהִ֑[c]וה אַזְכִּ֖יר צִדְקָתְךָ֣ לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
God, you have taught me from my youth, and to this day I declare your wonderful deeds.
אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים לִמַּדְתַּ֥נִי מִנְּעוּרָ֑י וְעַד־הֵ֝֗נָּה אַגִּ֥יד נִפְלְאוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
So even to old age and gray hairs, God, do not abandon me, until I declare your strength[^9] to the next generation, your might to all who are to come.
וְגַ֤ם עַד־זִקְנָ֨ה ׀ וְשֵׂיבָה֮ אֱלֹהִ֢ים אַֽל־תַּעַ֫זְבֵ֥נִי עַד־אַגִּ֣יד זְרוֹעֲךָ֣ לְד֑וֹר לְכָל־יָ֝ב֗וֹא גְּבוּרָתֶֽךָ׃
Your righteousness, God, reaches to the heights, you who have done great things. God, who is like you?
וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ אֱלֹהִ֗ים עַד־מָ֫ר֥וֹם אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֥יתָ גְדֹל֑וֹת אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים מִ֣י כָמֽוֹךָ׃
You who have made me see[^10] many troubles and calamities will give me life again; from the depths of the earth you will bring me up again.
אֲשֶׁ֤ר *הראיתנו **הִרְאִיתַ֨נִי ׀ צָר֥וֹת רַבּ֗וֹת וְרָ֫ע֥וֹת תָּשׁ֥וּב *תחיינו **תְּחַיֵּ֑ינִי וּֽמִתְּהֹמ֥וֹת הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ תָּשׁ֥וּב תַּעֲלֵֽנִי׃
You will increase my greatness, and turn and comfort me.
תֶּ֤רֶב ׀ גְּֽדֻלָּתִ֗י וְתִסֹּ֥ב תְּֽנַחֲמֵֽנִי׃
I too will praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God; I will sing praises to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
גַּם־אֲנִ֤י ׀ אוֹדְךָ֣ בִכְלִי־נֶבֶל֮ אֲמִתְּךָ֢ אֱלֹ֫הָ֥י אֲזַמְּרָ֣ה לְךָ֣ בְכִנּ֑וֹר קְ֝ד֗וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
My lips will shout for joy when I sing praises to you, and so will my soul, which you have redeemed.
תְּרַנֵּ֣נָּ֣ה שְׂ֭פָתַי כִּ֣י אֲזַמְּרָה־לָּ֑ךְ וְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּדִֽיתָ׃
My tongue too will speak of your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm have been put to shame and disgraced.
גַּם־לְשׁוֹנִ֗י כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם תֶּהְגֶּ֣ה צִדְקָתֶ֑ךָ כִּי־בֹ֥שׁוּ כִֽי־חָ֝פְר֗וּ מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י רָעָתִֽי׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Psalm 71 has no title. Verses 1–3 are close to 31:2–4 (31:1–3 in most English Bibles).
n.3: Literally "a rock of dwelling". Psalm 31:3 (31:2 in most English Bibles) has "a rock of refuge (*ma'oz*), a house of fortresses".
n.4: Literally "from the belly".
n.5: Hebrew *gozi*, found only here; the meaning is uncertain, perhaps "the one who drew me out" or "my strength".
n.6: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 13 and 23.
n.7: Literally "the accusers of my soul (*nephesh*)". The word for "accusers" comes from the same root as *satan*, "adversary, accuser".
n.8: Or "though I do not know how to count them".
n.9: Literally "your arm".
n.10: The Hebrew text is written "us" but read "me", both here and in "will give me life again".

v: Of Solomon.[^1] God, give the king your justice,[^2] and the king's son your righteousness.
לִשְׁלֹמֹ֨ה ׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ תֵּ֑ן וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ לְבֶן־מֶֽלֶךְ׃
May he judge your people with righteousness, and your afflicted ones with justice.
יָדִ֣ין עַמְּךָ֣ בְצֶ֑דֶק וַעֲנִיֶּ֥יךָ בְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃
May the mountains bring well-being[^3] to the people, and the hills, righteousness.
יִשְׂא֤וּ הָרִ֓ים שָׁ֘ל֥וֹם לָעָ֑ם וּ֝גְבָע֗וֹת בִּצְדָקָֽה׃
May he defend the cause of the afflicted among the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט ׀ עֲ‍ֽנִיֵּי־עָ֗ם י֭וֹשִׁיעַ לִבְנֵ֣י אֶבְי֑וֹן וִ֖ידַכֵּ֣א עוֹשֵֽׁק׃
May they fear you[^4] as long as the sun endures, and as long as the moon, through all generations.
יִֽירָא֥וּךָ עִם־שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְלִפְנֵ֥י יָ֝רֵ֗חַ דּ֣וֹר דּוֹרִֽים׃
May he be like rain falling on mown grass, like showers that water the earth.
יֵ֭רֵד כְּמָטָ֣ר עַל־גֵּ֑ז כִּ֝רְבִיבִ֗ים זַרְזִ֥יף אָֽרֶץ׃
In his days may the righteous flourish,[^5] and peace abound, until the moon is no more.
יִֽפְרַח־בְּיָמָ֥יו צַדִּ֑יק וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַד־בְּלִ֥י יָרֵֽחַ׃
May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River[^6] to the ends of the earth.
וְ֭יֵרְדְּ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־יָ֑ם וּ֝מִנָּהָ֗ר עַד־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
May the desert tribes[^7] bow down before him, and his enemies lick the dust.
לְ֭פָנָיו יִכְרְע֣וּ צִיִּ֑ים וְ֝אֹיְבָ֗יו עָפָ֥ר יְלַחֵֽכוּ׃
May the kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba[^8] offer gifts.
מַלְכֵ֬י תַרְשִׁ֣ישׁ וְ֭אִיִּים מִנְחָ֣ה יָשִׁ֑יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י שְׁבָ֥א וּ֝סְבָ֗א אֶשְׁכָּ֥ר יַקְרִֽיבוּ׃
May all kings bow down to him, and all nations serve him.
וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ל֥וֹ כָל־מְלָכִ֑ים כָּל־גּוֹיִ֥ם יַֽעַבְדֽוּהוּ׃
For he rescues the needy who cry for help, and the afflicted who have no one to help them.
כִּֽי־יַ֭צִּיל אֶבְי֣וֹן מְשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וְ֝עָנִ֗י וְֽאֵין־עֹזֵ֥ר לֽוֹ׃
He has pity on the poor and the needy, and saves the lives[^9] of the needy.
יָ֭חֹס עַל־דַּ֣ל וְאֶבְי֑וֹן וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים יוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
From oppression and violence he redeems their life, and their blood is precious in his sight.
מִתּ֣וֹךְ וּ֖[d]מֵחָמָס יִגְאַ֣ל נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְיֵיקַ֖ר דָּמָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃
May he live long! May gold of Sheba be given to him; may prayer be made for him continually, and may people bless him all day long.
וִיחִ֗י וְיִתֶּן־לוֹ֮ מִזְּהַ֢ב שְׁ֫בָ֥א וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲד֣וֹ תָמִ֑יד כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם יְבָרֲכֶֽנְהֽוּ׃
May there be abundant grain[^10] in the land, waving on the tops of the mountains; may its fruit be like Lebanon, and may people flourish in the cities[^11] like the grass of the field.
יְהִ֤י פִסַּת־בַּ֨ר ׀ בָּאָרֶץ֮ בְּרֹ֢אשׁ הָ֫רִ֥ים יִרְעַ֣שׁ כַּלְּבָנ֣וֹן פִּרְי֑וֹ וְיָצִ֥יצוּ מֵ֝עִ֗יר כְּעֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
May his name endure forever; may his name increase[^12] as long as the sun shines. May all nations be blessed in him; may they call him happy.[^13]
יְהִ֤י שְׁמ֨וֹ ׀ לְֽעוֹלָ֗ם לִפְנֵי־שֶׁמֶשׁ֮ *ינין **יִנּ֢וֹן שְׁ֫מ֥וֹ וְיִתְבָּ֥רְכוּ ב֑וֹ כָּל־גּוֹיִ֥ם יְאַשְּׁרֽוּהוּ׃
Blessed be the LORD[^14] God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonderful things.
בָּר֤וּךְ ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֹשֵׂ֖ה נִפְלָא֣וֹת לְבַדּֽוֹ׃
Blessed be his glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and Amen.[^15]
וּבָר֤וּךְ ׀ שֵׁ֥ם כְּבוֹד֗וֹ לְע֫וֹלָ֥ם וְיִמָּלֵ֣א כְ֭בוֹדוֹ אֶת־כֹּ֥ל הָאָ֗רֶץ אָ֘מֵ֥ן ׀ וְאָמֵֽן׃
The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.[^16]
כָּלּ֥וּ תְפִלּ֑וֹת דָּ֝וִ֗ד בֶּן־יִשָֽׁי׃

n.1: Or "for Solomon", "about Solomon". Psalm 127 is the only other psalm with this title. In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. The psalm is a prayer for the king. Later Jewish and Christian readers also heard in it a picture of the reign of the promised Messiah.
n.2: Literally "your judgments".
n.3: Hebrew *shalom*: peace, well-being, prosperity. Also in verse 7.
n.4: The Septuagint reads "May he endure".
n.5: The Septuagint reads "may righteousness flourish".
n.6: That is, the Euphrates.
n.7: Hebrew *tsiyyim*, "desert dwellers" or "desert creatures".
n.8: Sheba was in southern Arabia; Seba was probably in Africa (compare Genesis 10:7; Isaiah 43:3).
n.9: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verse 14.
n.10: Hebrew *pissat bar*, found only here; perhaps "an abundance of grain".
n.11: Literally "may they flourish from the city".
n.12: Hebrew *yinnon*, found only here, perhaps "sprout", "increase".
n.13: Compare God's promise to Abraham in Genesis 12:3; 22:18.
n.14: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.15: Verses 18–19 are a doxology, a closing word of praise, which ends Book 2 of the Psalms (Psalms 42–72). Each of the five books ends with one (41:14; 41:13 in most English Bibles; 72:18–19; 89:53; 89:52 in most English Bibles; 106:48), and Psalm 150 closes the whole collection.
n.16: This line probably closed an earlier collection of David's prayers. Several later psalms are also titled "of David" (for example Psalms 86, 101, 103, 108–110 and 138–145).

v: A psalm of Asaph.[^1] Truly God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף אַ֤ךְ ט֖וֹב לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֱלֹהִ֗ים לְבָרֵ֥י לֵבָֽב׃
But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
וַאֲנִ֗י כִּ֭מְעַט *נטוי **נָטָ֣יוּ רַגְלָ֑י כְּ֝אַ֗יִן *שפכה **שֻׁפְּכ֥וּ אֲשֻׁרָֽי׃
For I envied the boastful, when I saw the prosperity[^2] of the wicked.
כִּֽי־קִ֭נֵּאתִי בַּֽהוֹלְלִ֑ים שְׁל֖וֹם רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֶרְאֶֽה׃
For they have no pangs until their death;[^3] their bodies are healthy and well fed.
כִּ֤י אֵ֖ין חַרְצֻבּ֥וֹת לְמוֹתָ֗ם וּבָרִ֥יא אוּלָֽם׃
They are not in trouble as others are;[^4] they are not struck as other people are.
בַּעֲמַ֣ל אֱנ֣וֹשׁ אֵינֵ֑מוֹ וְעִם־אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א יְנֻגָּֽעוּ׃
So pride is their necklace; violence covers them like a garment.
לָ֭כֵן עֲנָקַ֣תְמוֹ גַאֲוָ֑ה יַעֲטָף־שִׁ֝֗ית חָמָ֥ס לָֽמוֹ׃
Their eyes bulge from fatness;[^5] the imaginations of their hearts overflow.
יָ֭צָא מֵחֵ֣לֶב עֵינֵ֑מוֹ עָ֝בְר֗וּ מַשְׂכִּיּ֥וֹת לֵבָֽב׃
They mock and speak with malice; from on high they threaten oppression.
יָמִ֤יקוּ ׀ וִידַבְּר֣וּ בְרָ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁק מִמָּר֥וֹם יְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃
They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut through the earth.
שַׁתּ֣וּ בַשָּׁמַ֣יִם פִּיהֶ֑ם וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם תִּֽהֲלַ֥ךְ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
So his people turn here,[^6] and drink up waters in abundance.[^7]
לָכֵ֤ן ׀ *ישיב **יָשׁ֣וּב עַמּ֣וֹ הֲלֹ֑ם וּמֵ֥י מָ֝לֵ֗א יִמָּ֥צוּ לָֽמוֹ׃
And they say, "How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?"[^8]
וְֽאָמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֥ה יָדַֽע־אֵ֑ל וְיֵ֖שׁ דֵּעָ֣ה בְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃
See, these are the wicked; always at ease, they increase in wealth.
הִנֵּה־אֵ֥לֶּה רְשָׁעִ֑ים וְשַׁלְוֵ֥י ע֝וֹלָ֗ם הִשְׂגּוּ־חָֽיִל׃
Surely in vain I have kept my heart clean and washed my hands in innocence.
אַךְ־רִ֭יק זִכִּ֣יתִי לְבָבִ֑י וָאֶרְחַ֖ץ בְּנִקָּי֣וֹן כַּפָּֽי׃
For I have been struck all day long, and punished every morning.
וָאֱהִ֣י נָ֭גוּעַ כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם וְ֝תוֹכַחְתִּ֗י לַבְּקָרִֽים׃
If I had said, "I will speak like this," I would have betrayed the generation of your children.
אִם־אָ֭מַרְתִּי אֲסַפְּרָ֥ה כְמ֑וֹ הִנֵּ֤ה ד֭וֹר בָּנֶ֣יךָ בָגָֽדְתִּי׃
But when I tried to understand this, it was troublesome in my eyes,
וָֽ֭אֲחַשְּׁבָה לָדַ֣עַת זֹ֑את עָמָ֖ל *היא **ה֣וּא בְעֵינָֽי׃
until I went into the sanctuary of God;[^9] then I understood their end.
עַד־אָ֭בוֹא אֶל־מִקְדְּשֵׁי־אֵ֑ל אָ֝בִ֗ינָה לְאַחֲרִיתָֽם׃
Surely you set them on slippery ground; you make them fall into ruin.
אַ֣ךְ בַּ֭חֲלָקוֹת תָּשִׁ֣ית לָ֑מוֹ הִ֝פַּלְתָּ֗ם לְמַשּׁוּאֽוֹת׃
How suddenly they are destroyed, swept away completely by terrors!
אֵ֤יךְ הָי֣וּ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה כְרָ֑גַע סָ֥פוּ תַ֝֗מּוּ מִן־בַּלָּהֽוֹת׃
Like a dream when one awakes, Lord, when you rouse yourself,[^10] you will despise their image.[^11]
כַּחֲל֥וֹם מֵהָקִ֑יץ אֲ֝דֹנָי בָּעִ֤יר ׀ צַלְמָ֬ם תִּבְזֶֽה׃
When my heart was bitter, and I was pierced within,[^12]
כִּ֭י יִתְחַמֵּ֣ץ לְבָבִ֑י וְ֝כִלְיוֹתַ֗י אֶשְׁתּוֹנָֽן׃
I was senseless and did not understand; I was like a beast[^13] before you.
וַאֲנִי־בַ֭עַר וְלֹ֣א אֵדָ֑ע בְּ֝הֵמ֗וֹת הָיִ֥יתִי עִמָּֽךְ׃
Yet I am always with you; you hold me by my right hand.
וַאֲנִ֣י תָמִ֣יד עִמָּ֑ךְ אָ֝חַ֗זְתָּ בְּיַד־יְמִינִֽי׃
You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you will take me into glory.[^14]
בַּעֲצָתְךָ֥ תַנְחֵ֑נִי וְ֝אַחַ֗ר כָּב֥וֹד תִּקָּחֵֽנִי׃
Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth I desire besides you.[^15]
מִי־לִ֥י בַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְ֝עִמְּךָ֗ לֹא־חָפַ֥צְתִּי בָאָֽרֶץ׃
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the rock[^16] of my heart and my portion forever.
כָּלָ֥ה שְׁאֵרִ֗י וּלְבָ֫בִ֥י צוּר־לְבָבִ֥י וְחֶלְקִ֗י אֱלֹהִ֥ים לְעוֹלָֽם׃
For see, those who are far from you will perish; you destroy all who are unfaithful to you.[^17]
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה רְחֵקֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ הִ֝צְמַ֗תָּה כָּל־זוֹנֶ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
But as for me, it is good to be near God;[^18] I have made the Lord GOD[^19] my refuge, so that I may tell of all your works.
וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ קִֽרֲבַ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים לִ֫י־ט֥וֹב שַׁתִּ֤י ׀ בַּאדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֣ה מַחְסִ֑י לְ֝סַפֵּ֗ר כָּל־מַלְאֲכוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

n.1: *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). Psalms 73–83 are all "of Asaph". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. Psalm 73 begins Book 3 of the Psalms (Psalms 73–89).
n.2: Hebrew *shalom*: peace, well-being, prosperity.
n.3: Literally "there are no pangs to their death". Some scholars divide the letters differently to read *lamo tam*, "they have no pangs; their bodies are sound", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.4: Literally "In the trouble of a mortal they are not".
n.5: Literally "Their eye goes out from fat". The Septuagint reads "Their iniquity goes out from fat".
n.6: That is, perhaps, to the wicked and their way of thinking. The Hebrew text is written "So he brings back his people here" but read "So his people turn here".
n.7: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "and waters of fullness are drained by them".
n.8: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.9: Literally "the sanctuaries of God".
n.10: Or "in the city".
n.11: Or "their phantom", "their shadow".
n.12: Literally "in my kidneys". The kidneys were thought of as the seat of the emotions and the inner life.
n.13: Hebrew *behemot*, "beasts", perhaps meaning "a great beast", "a brute".
n.14: Or "and afterward you will receive me with honor", or "and lead me after glory". Compare 49:16 (49:15 in most English Bibles).
n.15: Literally "and with you I desire nothing on earth".
n.16: Literally "the rock of my heart".
n.17: Literally "everyone who goes away from you as a prostitute", a common picture of unfaithfulness to God.
n.18: Literally "the nearness of God is good for me".
n.19: *The Lord GOD*: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". God's personal name, YHWH, is written GOD in capitals after "Lord", and "the LORD" elsewhere, as in most English Bibles.

v: A maskil of Asaph.[^1] God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture?
מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף לָמָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים זָנַ֣חְתָּ לָנֶ֑צַח יֶעְשַׁ֥ן אַ֝פְּךָ֗ בְּצֹ֣אן מַרְעִיתֶֽךָ׃
Remember your congregation, which you acquired long ago, the tribe of your inheritance, which you redeemed, Mount Zion, where you have dwelt.
זְכֹ֤ר עֲדָתְךָ֨ ׀ קָ֘נִ֤יתָ קֶּ֗דֶם גָּ֭אַלְתָּ שֵׁ֣בֶט נַחֲלָתֶ֑ךָ הַר־צִ֝יּ֗וֹן זֶ֤ה ׀ שָׁכַ֬נְתָּ בּֽוֹ׃
Turn your steps[^2] to the everlasting ruins; the enemy has damaged everything in the sanctuary.
הָרִ֣ימָה פְ֭עָמֶיךָ לְמַשֻּׁא֣וֹת נֶ֑צַח כָּל־הֵרַ֖ע אוֹיֵ֣ב בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
Your adversaries have roared in the midst of your meeting place;[^3] they have set up their own signs as signs.[^4]
שָׁאֲג֣וּ צֹ֭רְרֶיךָ בְּקֶ֣רֶב מוֹעֲדֶ֑ךָ שָׂ֖מוּ אוֹתֹתָ֣ם אֹתֽוֹת׃
They looked like men raising axes in a thicket of trees.[^5]
יִ֭וָּדַע כְּמֵבִ֣יא לְמָ֑עְלָה בִּֽסֲבָךְ־עֵ֝֗ץ קַרְדֻּמּֽוֹת׃
And now all its carved work they smash with hatchet and hammers.
*ועת **וְ֭עַתָּה פִּתּוּחֶ֣יהָ יָּ֑חַד בְּכַשִּׁ֥יל וְ֝כֵֽילַפֹּ֗ת יַהֲלֹמֽוּן׃
They set your sanctuary on fire; they have desecrated the dwelling place of your name, bringing it to the ground.
שִׁלְח֣וּ בָ֭אֵשׁ מִקְדָּשֶׁ֑ךָ לָ֝אָ֗רֶץ חִלְּל֥וּ מִֽשְׁכַּן־שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
They said in their hearts, "Let us crush them completely!"[^6] They burned all the meeting places of God in the land.
אָמְר֣וּ בְ֭לִבָּם נִינָ֣ם יָ֑חַד שָׂרְפ֖וּ כָל־מוֹעֲדֵי־אֵ֣ל בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
