We do not see our signs; there is no longer any prophet, and none of us knows how long.
אֽוֹתֹתֵ֗ינוּ לֹ֥א רָ֫אִ֥ינוּ אֵֽין־ע֥וֹד נָבִ֑יא וְלֹֽא־אִ֝תָּ֗נוּ יֹדֵ֥עַ עַד־מָֽה׃
How long, God, will the adversary taunt? Will the enemy despise your name forever?
עַד־מָתַ֣י אֱ֭לֹהִים יְחָ֣רֶף צָ֑ר יְנָ֘אֵ֤ץ אוֹיֵ֖ב שִׁמְךָ֣ לָנֶֽצַח׃
Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand? Take it from the fold of your robe[^7] and destroy them!
לָ֤מָּה תָשִׁ֣יב יָ֭דְךָ וִֽימִינֶ֑ךָ מִקֶּ֖רֶב *חוקך **חֽ͏ֵיקְךָ֣ כַלֵּֽה׃
Yet God is my King from of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
וֵ֭אלֹהִים מַלְכִּ֣י מִקֶּ֑דֶם פֹּעֵ֥ל יְ֝שׁוּע֗וֹת בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
You split the sea by your strength; you broke the heads of the sea monsters[^8] on the waters.
אַתָּ֤ה פוֹרַ֣רְתָּ בְעָזְּךָ֣ יָ֑ם שִׁבַּ֖רְתָּ רָאשֵׁ֥י תַ֝נִּינִ֗ים עַל־הַמָּֽיִם׃
You crushed the heads of Leviathan;[^9] you gave him as food to the creatures of the desert.[^10]
אַתָּ֣ה רִ֭צַּצְתָּ רָאשֵׁ֣י לִוְיָתָ֑ן תִּתְּנֶ֥נּוּ מַ֝אֲכָ֗ל לְעָ֣ם לְצִיִּֽים׃
You split open springs and streams; you dried up ever-flowing rivers.
אַתָּ֣ה בָ֭קַעְתָּ מַעְיָ֣ן וָנָ֑חַל אַתָּ֥ה ה֝וֹבַ֗שְׁתָּ נַהֲר֥וֹת אֵיתָֽן׃
Yours is the day, and yours also the night; you established the moon[^11] and the sun.
לְךָ֣ י֭וֹם אַף־לְךָ֥ לָ֑יְלָה אַתָּ֥ה הֲ֝כִינ֗וֹתָ מָא֥וֹר וָשָֽׁמֶשׁ׃
You set all the boundaries of the earth; summer and winter, you made them.
אַתָּ֣ה הִ֭צַּבְתָּ כָּל־גְּבוּל֣וֹת אָ֑רֶץ קַ֥יִץ וָ֝חֹ֗רֶף אַתָּ֥ה יְצַרְתָּם׃
Remember this: the enemy taunts, LORD,[^12] and a foolish people despises your name.
זְכָר־זֹ֗את א֖[d]וֹיֵב חֵרֵ֣ף ׀ יְהוָ֑ה וְעַ֥ם נָ֝בָ֗ל נִֽאֲצ֥וּ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
Do not give the life of your dove to the wild beasts;[^13] do not forget the life of your afflicted forever.
אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן לְ֭חַיַּת נֶ֣פֶשׁ תּוֹרֶ֑ךָ חַיַּ֥ת עֲ֝נִיֶּ֗יךָ אַל־תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח לָנֶֽצַח׃
Look to the covenant, for the dark places of the land are full of the haunts of violence.
הַבֵּ֥ט לַבְּרִ֑ית כִּ֥י מָלְא֥וּ מַחֲשַׁכֵּי־אֶ֝֗רֶץ נְא֣וֹת חָמָֽס׃
Do not let the oppressed turn back in shame; let the afflicted and the needy praise your name.
אַל־יָשֹׁ֣ב דַּ֣ךְ נִכְלָ֑ם עָנִ֥י וְ֝אֶבְי֗וֹן יְֽהַלְל֥וּ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
Rise up, God, plead your own cause; remember how fools taunt you all day long.
קוּמָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים רִיבָ֣ה רִיבֶ֑ךָ זְכֹ֥ר חֶרְפָּתְךָ֥ מִנִּי־נָ֝בָ֗ל כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
Do not forget the clamor of your adversaries, the uproar of those who rise against you, which goes up continually.
אַל־תִּ֭שְׁכַּח ק֣וֹל צֹרְרֶ֑יךָ שְׁא֥וֹן קָ֝מֶ֗יךָ עֹלֶ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃

n.1: *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. The psalm mourns the destruction of the temple, probably by the Babylonians (2 Kings 25:8–10; compare Psalm 79).
n.2: Literally "Lift up your steps".
n.3: Hebrew *mo'ed*, "appointed place, meeting place", the word used in "tent of meeting".
n.4: Perhaps military standards or the emblems of their gods.
n.5: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "It is known as one who brings up axes on high in a thicket of wood".
n.6: Literally "Let us oppress them together".
n.7: Literally "from the midst of your bosom". The Hebrew text is written "your decree" (*chuqqekha*) but read "your bosom" (*cheqekha*).
n.8: Hebrew *tanninim*, great creatures of the sea (Genesis 1:21).
n.9: A many-headed sea monster, a picture of the forces of chaos (compare Job 40:25; 41:1 in most English Bibles; Isaiah 27:1).
n.10: Literally "to a people, to desert creatures".
n.11: Literally "the light".
n.12: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Or "the enemy taunts the LORD".
n.13: Literally "to the beast the soul (*nephesh*) of your turtledove". The Hebrew word *chayyat*, "beast", also means "life" or "community" in the next line.

v: For the director. According to "Do Not Destroy".[^1] A psalm of Asaph. A song.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ אַל־תַּשְׁחֵ֑ת מִזְמ֖וֹר לְאָסָ֣ף שִֽׁיר׃
We give thanks to you, God, we give thanks, and your name is near; people tell of your wonderful deeds.
ה֘וֹדִ֤ינּוּ לְּךָ֨ ׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים ה֭וֹדִינוּ וְקָר֣וֹב שְׁמֶ֑ךָ סִ֝פְּר֗וּ נִפְלְאוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
When I choose the appointed time,[^3] I myself will judge with fairness.
כִּ֭י אֶקַּ֣ח מוֹעֵ֑ד אֲ֝נִ֗י מֵישָׁרִ֥ים אֶשְׁפֹּֽט׃
When the earth and all who live in it melt away, it is I who hold its pillars firm. Selah.[^4]
נְֽמֹגִ֗ים אֶ֥רֶץ וְכָל־יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ אָנֹכִ֨י תִכַּ֖נְתִּי עַמּוּדֶ֣יהָ סֶּֽלָה׃
I said to the boastful, "Do not boast," and to the wicked, "Do not lift up your horn.[^5]
אָמַ֣רְתִּי לַֽ֭הוֹלְלִים אַל־תָּהֹ֑לּוּ וְ֝לָרְשָׁעִ֗ים אַל־תָּרִ֥ימוּ קָֽרֶן׃
Do not lift up your horn on high, or speak with an arrogant neck."[^6]
אַל־תָּרִ֣ימוּ לַמָּר֣וֹם קַרְנְכֶ֑ם תְּדַבְּר֖וּ בְצַוָּ֣אר עָתָֽק׃
For not from the east or from the west, and not from the wilderness, comes lifting up.[^7]
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א מִ֭מּוֹצָא וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֑ב וְ֝לֹ֗א מִמִּדְבַּ֥ר הָרִֽים׃
For God is the judge; he puts down one and lifts up another.
כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים שֹׁפֵ֑ט זֶ֥ה יַ֝שְׁפִּ֗יל וְזֶ֣ה יָרִֽים׃
For in the hand of the LORD[^8] there is a cup, with foaming wine, richly mixed; he pours from it, and all the wicked of the earth must drain it to the dregs and drink.
כִּ֤י כ֪וֹס בְּֽיַד־יְהוָ֡ה וְיַ֤יִן חָמַ֨ר ׀ מָ֥לֵא מֶסֶךְ֮ וַיַּגֵּ֢ר מִ֫זֶּ֥ה אַךְ־שְׁ֭מָרֶיהָ יִמְצ֣וּ יִשְׁתּ֑וּ כֹּ֝֗ל רִשְׁעֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
But as for me, I will declare it forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
וַ֭אֲנִי אַגִּ֣יד לְעֹלָ֑ם אֲ֝זַמְּרָ֗ה לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃
All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be lifted up.[^9]
וְכָל־קַרְנֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֲגַדֵּ֑עַ תְּ֝רוֹמַ֗מְנָה קַֽרְנ֥וֹת צַדִּֽ֥[c]יק׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-tashchet*, "do not destroy", probably the name of a tune (see the title of Psalm 57).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–11 are 75:1–10 in most English Bibles.
n.3: God speaks in verses 3–6, or perhaps only in verses 3–4.
n.4: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.5: The horn of an animal is a picture of strength and pride. Also in verses 6 and 11.
n.6: Literally "with a neck of arrogance". The Septuagint reads "speak injustice against God".
n.7: Hebrew *harim*, "lifting up", as in verses 5–6 and 8. Or "and not from the wilderness of the mountains".
n.8: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.9: The speaker may be God, as in verses 3–6, or the psalmist.

v: For the director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ בִּנְגִינֹ֑ת מִזְמ֖וֹר לְאָסָ֣ף שִֽׁיר׃
God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
נוֹדָ֣ע בִּֽיהוּדָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים בְּ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל גָּד֥וֹל שְׁמֽוֹ׃
His tent[^2] is in Salem,[^3] his dwelling place in Zion.
וַיְהִ֣י בְשָׁלֵ֣ם סֻכּ֑וֹ וּמְע֖וֹנָת֣וֹ בְצִיּֽוֹן׃
There he broke the flaming arrows of the bow,[^4] the shield, the sword and the weapons of war.[^5] Selah.[^6]
שָׁ֭מָּה שִׁבַּ֣ר רִשְׁפֵי־קָ֑שֶׁת מָגֵ֬ן וְחֶ֖רֶב וּמִלְחָמָ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃
You are radiant, majestic, more than the mountains of prey.[^7]
נָ֭אוֹר אַתָּ֥ה אַדִּ֗יר מֵֽהַרְרֵי־טָֽרֶף׃
The stouthearted have been plundered; they have sunk into their sleep; none of the warriors could lift their hands.[^8]
אֶשְׁתּוֹלְל֨וּ ׀ אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֭ב נָמ֣וּ שְׁנָתָ֑ם וְלֹא־מָצְא֖וּ כָל־אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֣יִל יְדֵיהֶֽם׃
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse lay stunned.[^9]
מִ֭גַּעֲרָ֣תְךָ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב נִ֝רְדָּ֗ם וְרֶ֣כֶב וָסֽוּס׃
You, you are awesome! Who can stand before you once your anger is roused?
אַתָּ֤ה ׀ נ֥וֹרָא אַ֗תָּה וּמִֽי־יַעֲמֹ֥ד לְפָנֶ֗יךָ מֵאָ֥ז אַפֶּֽךָ׃
From heaven you pronounced judgment; the earth feared and was still,
מִ֭שָּׁמַיִם הִשְׁמַ֣עְתָּ דִּ֑ין אֶ֖רֶץ יָֽרְאָ֣ה וְשָׁקָֽטָה׃
when God rose up to judge, to save all the humble of the earth. Selah.
בְּקוּם־לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט אֱלֹהִ֑ים לְהוֹשִׁ֖יעַ כָּל־עַנְוֵי־אֶ֣רֶץ סֶֽלָה׃
Surely human wrath will praise you; with the remnant of wrath you will clothe yourself.[^10]
כִּֽי־חֲמַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם תּוֹדֶ֑ךָּ שְׁאֵרִ֖ית חֵמֹ֣ת תַּחְגֹּֽר׃
Make vows to the LORD[^11] your God, and fulfill them; let all around him bring gifts to the one who is to be feared.
נִֽדֲר֣וּ וְשַׁלְּמוּ֮ לַיהוָ֢ה אֱ‍ֽלֹהֵ֫יכֶ֥ם כָּל־סְבִיבָ֑יו יוֹבִ֥ילוּ שַׁ֝֗י לַמּוֹרָֽא׃
He cuts short the spirit of princes; he is feared by the kings of the earth.
יִ֭בְצֹר ר֣וּחַ נְגִידִ֑ים נ֝וֹרָ֗א לְמַלְכֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–13 are 76:1–12 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Or "his shelter", "his lair", as of a lion.
n.3: Another name for Jerusalem (compare Genesis 14:18).
n.4: Literally "the flames of the bow".
n.5: Literally "and war".
n.6: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 10.
n.7: The Septuagint reads "from the everlasting mountains".
n.8: Literally "did not find their hands".
n.9: Literally "fell into a deep sleep".
n.10: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "the remnant of wraths you will gird on". Or "the survivors of wrath will keep your festivals".
n.11: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.

v: For the director. According to Jeduthun.[^1] Of Asaph. A psalm.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־*ידיתון **יְדוּת֗וּן לְאָסָ֥ף מִזְמֽוֹר׃
My voice goes up to God, and I cry out; my voice goes up to God, and he will listen to me.[^3]
קוֹלִ֣י אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאֶצְעָ֑קָה קוֹלִ֥י אֶל־אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים וְהַאֲזִ֥ין אֵלָֽי׃
In the day of my trouble I seek the Lord; at night my hand is stretched out without growing weary;[^4] my soul[^5] refuses to be comforted.
בְּי֥וֹם צָרָתִי֮ אֲדֹנָ֢י דָּ֫רָ֥שְׁתִּי יָדִ֤י ׀ לַ֣יְלָה נִ֭גְּרָה וְלֹ֣א תָפ֑וּג מֵאֲנָ֖ה הִנָּחֵ֣ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃
I remember God, and I groan; I meditate, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.[^6]
אֶזְכְּרָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאֶֽהֱמָיָ֑ה אָשִׂ֓יחָה ׀ וְתִתְעַטֵּ֖ף רוּחִ֣י סֶֽלָה׃
You hold my eyelids open;[^7] I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
אָ֭חַזְתָּ שְׁמֻר֣וֹת עֵינָ֑י נִ֝פְעַ֗מְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אֲדַבֵּֽר׃
I think about the days of old, the years long past.
חִשַּׁ֣בְתִּי יָמִ֣ים מִקֶּ֑דֶם שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת עוֹלָמִֽים׃
I remember my song in the night; I meditate in my heart, and my spirit searches:
אֶֽזְכְּרָ֥ה נְגִינָתִ֗י בַּ֫לָּ֥יְלָה עִם־לְבָבִ֥י אָשִׂ֑יחָה וַיְחַפֵּ֥שׂ רוּחִֽי׃
"Will the Lord reject forever? Will he never again show favor?
הַֽ֭לְעוֹלָמִים יִזְנַ֥ח ׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י וְלֹֽא־יֹסִ֖יף לִרְצ֣וֹת עֽוֹד׃
Has his faithful love[^8] ceased forever? Has his promise[^9] come to an end for all generations?
הֶאָפֵ֣ס לָנֶ֣צַח חַסְדּ֑וֹ גָּ֥מַר אֹ֝֗מֶר לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃
Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he in anger shut up his compassion?" Selah.
הֲשָׁכַ֣ח חַנּ֣וֹת אֵ֑ל אִם־קָפַ֥ץ בְּ֝אַ֗ף רַחֲמָ֥יו סֶֽלָה׃
Then I said, "This is my grief: that the right hand of the Most High has changed."[^10]
וָ֭אֹמַר חַלּ֣וֹתִי הִ֑יא שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת יְמִ֣ין עֶלְיֽוֹן׃
I will remember[^11] the deeds of the LORD;[^12] yes, I will remember your wonders of old.
*אזכיר **אֶזְכּ֥וֹר מַֽעַלְלֵי־יָ֑הּ כִּֽי־אֶזְכְּרָ֖ה מִקֶּ֣דֶם פִּלְאֶֽךָ׃
I will meditate on all your work, and ponder your mighty deeds.
וְהָגִ֥יתִי בְכָל־פָּעֳלֶ֑ךָ וּֽבַעֲלִ֖ילוֹתֶ֣יךָ אָשִֽׂיחָה׃
God, your way is in holiness.[^13] What god is great like God?
אֱ֭לֹהִים בַּקֹּ֣דֶשׁ דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ מִי־אֵ֥ל גָּ֝ד֗וֹל כֵּֽאלֹהִֽים׃
You are the God who works wonders; you have made known your strength among the peoples.
אַתָּ֣ה הָ֭אֵל עֹ֣שֵׂה פֶ֑לֶא הוֹדַ֖עְתָּ בָעַמִּ֣ים עֻזֶּֽךָ׃
With your arm you redeemed your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
גָּאַ֣לְתָּ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּנֵי־יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְיוֹסֵ֣ף סֶֽלָה׃
The waters saw you, God, the waters saw you and writhed; the depths too trembled.
רָ֘א֤וּךָ מַּ֨יִם ׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים רָא֣וּךָ מַּ֣יִם יָחִ֑ילוּ אַ֝֗ף יִרְגְּז֥וּ תְהֹמֽוֹת׃
The clouds poured down water; the skies thundered;[^14] your arrows flashed back and forth.
זֹ֤רְמוּ מַ֨יִם ׀ עָב֗וֹת ק֭וֹל נָתְנ֣וּ שְׁחָקִ֑ים אַף־חֲ֝צָצֶ֗יךָ יִתְהַלָּֽכוּ׃
The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind;[^15] lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.
ק֤וֹל רַעַמְךָ֨ ׀ בַּגַּלְגַּ֗ל הֵאִ֣ירוּ בְרָקִ֣ים תֵּבֵ֑ל רָגְזָ֖ה וַתִּרְעַ֣שׁ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Your way was through the sea, your path[^16] through the mighty waters, yet your footprints were not seen.
בַּיָּ֤ם דַּרְכֶּ֗ךָ *ושביליך **וּֽ֭שְׁבִֽילְךָ בְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝עִקְּבוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א נֹדָֽעוּ׃
You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
נָחִ֣יתָ כַצֹּ֣אן עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּֽיַד־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-yedutun*. Jeduthun was one of David's chief musicians (see the note on the title of Psalm 62).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–21 are 77:1–20 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "My voice to God, and I cry out; my voice to God, and listen to me".
n.4: Literally "my hand at night was poured out and did not grow numb", that is, stretched out in prayer.
n.5: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.6: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verses 10 and 16.
n.7: Literally "You have held the guards of my eyes".
n.8: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.9: Literally "word".
n.10: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "My sickness, it is the changing of the right hand of the Most High". *Shenot*, "changing", can also mean "years": "the years of the right hand of the Most High". *Most High*: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "I will make mention of" but read "I will remember".
n.12: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH, as in *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah".
n.13: Or "in the holy place".
n.14: Literally "gave a voice".
n.15: Hebrew *galgal*, "wheel" or "whirlwind".
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "your paths" but read "your path".

v: A maskil of Asaph.[^1] Listen, my people, to my instruction;[^2] turn your ears to the words of my mouth.
מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף הַאֲזִ֣ינָה עַ֭מִּי תּוֹרָתִ֑י הַטּ֥וּ אָ֝זְנְכֶ֗ם לְאִמְרֵי פִֽי׃
I will open my mouth in a parable;[^3] I will pour out riddles from of old,[^4]
אֶפְתְּחָ֣ה בְמָשָׁ֣ל פִּ֑י אַבִּ֥יעָה חִ֝יד֗וֹת מִנִּי־קֶֽדֶם׃
things that we have heard and known, that our ancestors have told us.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁ֭מַעְנוּ וַנֵּדָעֵ֑ם וַ֝אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ סִפְּרוּ־לָֽנוּ׃
We will not hide them from their children; we will tell the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the LORD,[^5] his might, and the wonders he has done.
לֹ֤א נְכַחֵ֨ד ׀ מִבְּנֵיהֶ֗ם לְד֥וֹר אַחֲר֗וֹן מְֽ֭סַפְּרִים תְּהִלּ֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וֶעֱזוּז֥וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָֽׂה׃
He established a statute[^6] in Jacob, and set a law in Israel, which he commanded our ancestors to make known to their children,
וַיָּ֤קֶם עֵד֨וּת ׀ בְּֽיַעֲקֹ֗ב וְתוֹרָה֮ שָׂ֤ם בְּיִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִ֭וָּה אֶת־אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ לְ֝הוֹדִיעָ֗ם לִבְנֵיהֶֽם׃
so that the next generation might know them, the children yet to be born, and they in turn would rise up and tell their children,
לְמַ֤עַן יֵדְע֨וּ ׀ דּ֣וֹר אַ֭חֲרוֹן בָּנִ֣ים יִוָּלֵ֑דוּ יָ֝קֻ֗מוּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לִבְנֵיהֶֽם׃
so that they would put their confidence in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commands,
וְיָשִׂ֥ימוּ בֵֽאלֹהִ֗ים כִּ֫סְלָ֥ם וְלֹ֣א יִ֭שְׁכְּחוּ מַֽעַלְלֵי אֵ֑ל וּמִצְוֺתָ֥יו יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃
and so that they would not be like their ancestors, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not steadfast, whose spirit was not faithful to God.
וְלֹ֤א יִהְי֨וּ ׀ כַּאֲבוֹתָ֗ם דּוֹר֮ סוֹרֵ֢ר וּמֹ֫רֶ֥ה דּ֭וֹר לֹא־הֵכִ֣ין לִבּ֑וֹ וְלֹא־נֶאֶמְנָ֖ה אֶת־אֵ֣ל רוּחֽוֹ׃
The Ephraimites, armed with bows,[^7] turned back on the day of battle.
בְּֽנֵי־אֶפְרַ֗יִם נוֹשְׁקֵ֥י רוֹמֵי־קָ֑שֶׁת הָ֝פְכ֗וּ בְּי֣וֹם קְרָֽב׃
They did not keep God's covenant, and they refused to walk in his law.
לֹ֣א שָׁ֭מְרוּ בְּרִ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּ֝בְתוֹרָת֗וֹ מֵאֲנ֥וּ לָלֶֽכֶת׃
They forgot what he had done, the wonders he had shown them.
וַיִּשְׁכְּח֥וּ עֲלִילוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶרְאָֽם׃
In the sight of their ancestors he did wonders in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.[^8]
נֶ֣גֶד אֲ֭בוֹתָם עָ֣שָׂה פֶ֑לֶא בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מִצְרַ֣יִם שְׂדֵה־צֹֽעַן׃
He split the sea and led them through; he made the waters stand up like a heap.[^9]
בָּ֣קַע יָ֭ם וַיַּֽעֲבִירֵ֑ם וַֽיַּצֶּב־מַ֥יִם כְּמוֹ־נֵ[c]ד׃
He led them with the cloud by day, and all night long with the light of fire.
וַיַּנְחֵ֣ם בֶּעָנָ֣ן יוֹמָ֑ם וְכָל־הַ֝לַּ֗יְלָה בְּא֣וֹר אֵֽשׁ׃
He split rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink as abundant as the great deep.[^10]
יְבַקַּ֣ע צֻ֭רִים בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַ֝יַּ֗שְׁקְ כִּתְהֹמ֥וֹת רַבָּֽה׃
He brought streams out of the rock, and made water flow down like rivers.
וַיּוֹצִ֣א נוֹזְלִ֣ים מִסָּ֑לַע וַיּ֖וֹרֶד כַּנְּהָר֣וֹת מָֽיִם׃
But they went on sinning against him, rebelling against the Most High[^11] in the desert.
וַיּוֹסִ֣יפוּ ע֖[d]וֹד לַחֲטֹא־ל֑וֹ לַֽמְר֥וֹת עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן בַּצִּיָּֽה׃
They put God to the test in their hearts, demanding food for their craving.[^12]
וַיְנַסּוּ־אֵ֥ל בִּלְבָבָ֑ם לִֽשְׁאָל־אֹ֥כֶל לְנַפְשָֽׁם׃
They spoke against God; they said, "Can God spread a table in the wilderness?
וַֽיְדַבְּר֗וּ בֵּֽאלֹ֫הִ֥ים אָ֭מְרוּ הֲי֣וּכַל אֵ֑ל לַעֲרֹ֥ךְ שֻׁ֝לְחָ֗ן בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
True, he struck the rock, and water gushed out, and streams overflowed. But can he also give bread, or provide meat for his people?"
הֵ֤ן הִכָּה־צ֨וּר ׀ וַיָּז֣וּבוּ מַיִם֮ וּנְחָלִ֢ים יִ֫שְׁטֹ֥פוּ הֲגַם־לֶ֭חֶם י֣וּכַל תֵּ֑ת אִם־יָכִ֖ין שְׁאֵ֣ר לְעַמּֽוֹ׃
So when the LORD heard, he was furious; a fire was kindled against Jacob, and his anger rose against Israel,[^13]
לָכֵ֤ן ׀ שָׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֗ה וַֽיִּתְעַבָּ֥ר וְ֭אֵשׁ נִשְּׂקָ֣ה בְיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְגַם־אַ֝֗ף עָלָ֥ה בְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
because they did not believe in God, or trust in his salvation.
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א הֶ֭אֱמִינוּ בֵּאלֹהִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א בָ֝טְח֗וּ בִּֽישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃
Yet he commanded the skies above, and opened the doors of heaven;
וַיְצַ֣ו שְׁחָקִ֣ים מִמָּ֑עַל וְדַלְתֵ֖י שָׁמַ֣יִם פָּתָֽח׃
he rained down manna on them to eat, and gave them the grain of heaven.[^14]
וַיַּמְטֵ֬ר עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם מָ֣ן לֶאֱכֹ֑ל וּדְגַן־שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם נָ֣תַן לָֽמוֹ׃
Each of them ate the bread of the mighty;[^15] he sent them food in abundance.
לֶ֣חֶם אַ֭בִּירִים אָ֣כַל אִ֑ישׁ צֵידָ֬ה שָׁלַ֖ח לָהֶ֣ם לָשֹֽׂבַע׃
He let loose the east wind in the heavens, and by his power he drove out the south wind.
יַסַּ֣ע קָ֭דִים בַּשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיְנַהֵ֖ג בְּעֻזּ֣וֹ תֵימָֽן׃
He rained meat on them like dust, winged birds like the sand of the seas.
וַיַּמְטֵ֬ר עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּעָפָ֣ר שְׁאֵ֑ר וּֽכְח֥וֹל יַ֝מִּ֗ים ע֣וֹף כָּנָֽף׃
He let them fall in the middle of their camp, all around their dwellings.[^16]
וַ֭יַּפֵּל בְּקֶ֣רֶב מַחֲנֵ֑הוּ סָ֝בִ֗יב לְמִשְׁכְּנֹתָֽיו׃
So they ate and were well filled, for he gave them what they craved.
וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׂבְּע֣וּ מְאֹ֑ד וְ֝תַֽאֲוָתָ֗ם יָבִ֥א לָהֶֽם׃
But before they had turned from their craving, while the food was still in their mouths,
לֹא־זָ֥רוּ מִתַּאֲוָתָ֑ם ע֝֗וֹד אָכְלָ֥ם בְּפִיהֶֽם׃
the anger of God rose against them; he killed the strongest of them,[^17] and struck down the young men of Israel.[^18]
וְאַ֤ף אֱלֹהִ֨ים ׀ עָ֘לָ֤ה בָהֶ֗ם וַֽ֭יַּהֲרֹג בְּמִשְׁמַנֵּיהֶ֑ם וּבַחוּרֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הִכְרִֽיעַ׃
In spite of all this, they went on sinning; they did not believe in his wonders.
בְּכָל־זֹ֥את חָֽטְאוּ־ע֑וֹד וְלֹֽא־הֶ֝אֱמִ֗ינוּ בְּנִפְלְאוֹתָֽיו׃
So he made their days vanish like a breath,[^19] and their years in sudden terror.
וַיְכַל־בַּהֶ֥בֶל יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וּ֝שְׁנוֹתָ֗ם בַּבֶּהָלָֽה׃
Whenever he killed some of them, the rest would seek him; they would turn and look eagerly for God.
אִם־הֲרָגָ֥ם וּדְרָשׁ֑וּהוּ וְ֝שָׁ֗בוּ וְשִֽׁחֲרוּ־אֵֽל׃
They remembered that God was their rock, God Most High their redeemer.
וַֽ֭יִּזְכְּרוּ כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֣ים צוּרָ֑ם וְאֵ֥ל עֶ֝לְיוֹן גֹּאֲלָֽם׃
But they flattered him with their mouths, and lied to him with their tongues.
וַיְפַתּ֥וּהוּ בְּפִיהֶ֑ם וּ֝בִלְשׁוֹנָ֗ם יְכַזְּבוּ־לֽוֹ׃
Their hearts were not steadfast toward him; they were not faithful to his covenant.
וְ֭לִבָּם לֹא־נָכ֣וֹן עִמּ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א נֶ֝אֶמְנ֗וּ בִּבְרִיתֽוֹ׃
Yet he, being compassionate, forgave[^20] their iniquity and did not destroy them; again and again he held back his anger, and did not stir up all his wrath.
וְה֤וּא רַח֨וּם ׀ יְכַפֵּ֥ר עָוֺן֮ וְֽלֹא־יַ֫שְׁחִ֥ית וְ֭הִרְבָּה לְהָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָ֝עִיר כָּל־חֲמָתֽוֹ׃
He remembered that they were only flesh, a breath of wind[^21] that passes and does not return.
וַ֭יִּזְכֹּר כִּי־בָשָׂ֣ר הֵ֑מָּה ר֥וּחַ ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ וְלֹ֣א יָשֽׁוּב׃
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness, and grieved him in the wasteland!
כַּ֭מָּה יַמְר֣וּהוּ בַמִּדְבָּ֑ר יַ֝עֲצִיב֗וּהוּ בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן׃
Again and again they put God to the test, and provoked[^22] the Holy One of Israel.
וַיָּשׁ֣וּבוּ וַיְנַסּ֣וּ אֵ֑ל וּקְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הִתְווּ׃
They did not remember his power,[^23] the day when he redeemed them from the adversary,
לֹא־זָכְר֥וּ אֶת־יָד֑וֹ י֝֗וֹם אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־פָּדָ֥ם מִנִּי־צָֽר׃
when he displayed his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the region of Zoan.[^24]
אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם בְּ֭מִצְרַיִם אֹֽתוֹתָ֑יו וּ֝מוֹפְתָ֗יו בִּשְׂדֵה־צֹֽעַן׃
He turned their rivers[^25] into blood, so that they could not drink from their streams.
וַיַּהֲפֹ֣ךְ לְ֭דָם יְאֹרֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝נֹזְלֵיהֶ֗ם בַּל־יִשְׁתָּיֽוּן׃
He sent swarms of flies among them, which devoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them.
יְשַׁלַּ֬ח בָּהֶ֣ם עָ֭רֹב וַיֹּאכְלֵ֑ם וּ֝צְפַרְדֵּ֗עַ וַתַּשְׁחִיתֵֽם׃
He gave their crops to the grasshopper, and the fruit of their labor to the locust.
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לֶחָסִ֣יל יְבוּלָ֑ם וִֽ֝יגִיעָ֗ם לָאַרְבֶּֽה׃
He killed their vines with hail, and their sycamore-fig trees with frost.[^26]
יַהֲרֹ֣ג בַּבָּרָ֣ד גַּפְנָ֑ם וְ֝שִׁקְמוֹתָ֗ם בַּֽחֲנָמַֽל׃
He gave over their cattle to the hail, and their livestock to bolts of lightning.
וַיַּסְגֵּ֣ר לַבָּרָ֣ד בְּעִירָ֑ם וּ֝מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם לָרְשָׁפִֽים׃
He let loose on them his burning anger, fury, indignation and distress, a band of destroying angels.[^27]
יְשַׁלַּח־בָּ֨ם ׀ חֲר֬וֹן אַפּ֗וֹ עֶבְרָ֣ה וָזַ֣עַם וְצָרָ֑ה מִ֝שְׁלַ֗חַת מַלְאֲכֵ֥י רָעִֽים׃
He cleared a path for his anger; he did not spare them from death, but gave their lives[^28] over to the plague.
יְפַלֵּ֥ס נָתִ֗יב לְאַ֫פּ֥וֹ לֹא־חָשַׂ֣ךְ מִמָּ֣וֶת נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְ֝חַיָּתָ֗ם לַדֶּ֥בֶר הִסְגִּֽיר׃
He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.[^29]
וַיַּ֣ךְ כָּל־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם רֵאשִׁ֥ית א֝וֹנִ֗ים בְּאָהֳלֵי־חָֽם׃
Then he led out his people like sheep, and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
וַיַּסַּ֣ע כַּצֹּ֣אן עַמּ֑וֹ וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֥ם כַּ֝עֵ֗דֶר בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
He led them in safety, so that they were not afraid; but the sea covered their enemies.
וַיַּנְחֵ֣ם לָ֭בֶטַח וְלֹ֣א פָחָ֑דוּ וְאֶת־א֝וֹיְבֵיהֶ֗ם כִּסָּ֥ה הַיָּֽם׃
He brought them to his holy land,[^30] to this mountain that his right hand had won.
וַ֭יְבִיאֵם אֶל־גְּב֣וּל קָדְשׁ֑וֹ הַר־זֶ֝֗ה קָנְתָ֥ה יְמִינֽוֹ׃
He drove out nations before them, and allotted their land as an inheritance by measuring line;[^31] he settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
וַיְגָ֤רֶשׁ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֨ם ׀ גּוֹיִ֗ם וַֽ֭יַּפִּילֵם בְּחֶ֣בֶל נַחֲלָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ן בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Yet they tested God Most High and rebelled against him, and did not keep his statutes.
וַיְנַסּ֣וּ וַ֭יַּמְרוּ אֶת־אֱלֹהִ֣ים עֶלְי֑וֹן וְ֝עֵדוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א שָׁמָֽרוּ׃
They turned away and were treacherous like their ancestors; they twisted like a faulty bow.[^32]
וַיִּסֹּ֣גוּ וַֽ֭יִּבְגְּדוּ כַּאֲבוֹתָ֑ם נֶ֝הְפְּכ֗וּ כְּקֶ֣שֶׁת רְמִיָּֽה׃
They provoked him to anger with their high places, and made him jealous with their carved images.
וַיַּכְעִיס֥וּהוּ בְּבָמוֹתָ֑ם וּ֝בִפְסִילֵיהֶ֗ם יַקְנִיאֽוּהוּ׃
When God heard, he was furious, and he utterly rejected Israel.
שָׁמַ֣ע אֱ֭לֹהִים וַֽיִּתְעַבָּ֑ר וַיִּמְאַ֥ס מְ֝אֹ֗ד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
He abandoned the tabernacle at Shiloh, the tent where he had dwelt among human beings.[^33]
He gave up his strength to captivity, his splendor into the hand of the adversary.[^34]
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לַשְּׁבִ֣י עֻזּ֑וֹ וְֽתִפְאַרְתּ֥וֹ בְיַד־צָֽר׃
He handed his people over to the sword, and he was furious with his inheritance.
וַיַּסְגֵּ֣ר לַחֶ֣רֶב עַמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְנַחֲלָת֗וֹ הִתְעַבָּֽר׃
Fire consumed their young men, and their young women had no wedding songs.[^35]
בַּחוּרָ֥יו אָֽכְלָה־אֵ֑שׁ וּ֝בְתוּלֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א הוּלָּֽלוּ׃
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows could not weep.
כֹּ֭הֲנָיו בַּחֶ֣רֶב נָפָ֑לוּ וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה׃
Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior shouting because of wine.[^36]
וַיִּקַ֖ץ כְּיָשֵׁ֥ן ׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י כְּ֝גִבּ֗וֹר מִתְרוֹנֵ֥ן מִיָּֽיִן׃
He beat back his adversaries;[^37] he put them to everlasting shame.
וַיַּךְ־צָרָ֥יו אָח֑וֹר חֶרְפַּ֥ת ע֝וֹלָ֗ם נָ֣תַן לָֽמוֹ׃
He rejected the tent of Joseph, and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim;
וַ֭יִּמְאַס בְּאֹ֣הֶל יוֹסֵ֑ף וּֽבְשֵׁ֥בֶט אֶ֝פְרַ֗יִם לֹ֣א בָחָֽר׃
but he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loves.
וַ֭יִּבְחַר אֶת־שֵׁ֣בֶט יְהוּדָ֑ה אֶֽת־הַ֥ר צִ֝יּ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהֵֽב׃
He built his sanctuary like the heights,[^38] like the earth, which he founded forever.
וַיִּ֣בֶן כְּמוֹ־רָ֭מִים מִקְדָּשׁ֑וֹ כְּ֝אֶ֗רֶץ יְסָדָ֥הּ לְעוֹלָֽם׃
He chose David his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds;
וַ֭יִּבְחַר בְּדָוִ֣ד עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַ֝יִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ מִֽמִּכְלְאֹ֥ת צֹֽאן׃
from following the nursing ewes he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people, Israel his inheritance.
מֵאַחַ֥ר עָל֗וֹת הֱבִ֫יא֥וֹ לִ֭רְעוֹת בְּיַעֲקֹ֣ב עַמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃
He shepherded them with integrity of heart,[^39] and guided them with skillful hands.
וַ֭יִּרְעֵם כְּתֹ֣ם לְבָב֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנ֖וֹת כַּפָּ֣יו יַנְחֵֽם׃

n.1: *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. The psalm retells Israel's history from the exodus to the choice of David and Zion, as a warning to each new generation.
n.2: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching".
n.3: Hebrew *mashal*, a saying, parable or poem.
n.4: Matthew 13:35 quotes this verse.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: Hebrew *edut*, traditionally "testimony": the solemn terms of the covenant. Also in verse 56, in the plural.
n.7: Literally "equipped shooters of the bow". The event is not known.
n.8: Literally "the field of Zoan". Zoan was a city in the eastern Nile delta (Numbers 13:22).
n.9: Compare Exodus 14:21–22; 15:8.
n.10: Literally "like the great deeps". Compare Exodus 17:6; Numbers 20:11.
n.11: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God. Also in verses 35 and 56.
n.12: Literally "for their soul (*nephesh*)", that is, their appetite.
n.13: Verses 18–31 recall Exodus 16 and Numbers 11.
n.14: John 6:31 quotes this verse.
n.15: Hebrew *abbirim*, "mighty ones". The Septuagint reads "the bread of angels".
n.16: Literally "his camp... his dwellings": Israel's.
n.17: Literally "among their fat ones".
n.20: Or "atoned for", "covered". Hebrew *kipper*, the verb used for making atonement.
n.22: Or "pained". The meaning of the Hebrew *hitvu* is uncertain.
n.24: Verses 44–51 recall the plagues of Egypt (Exodus 7–12), not all of them, and not in the same order.
n.25: Hebrew *ye'orim*, the Nile and its channels.
n.26: Hebrew *chanamal*, found only here, perhaps "frost" or "hailstones".
n.27: Literally "a sending of messengers of evils".
n.28: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. The second line can also be read "but gave their animals over to the plague".
n.29: Ham was the ancestor of the Egyptians (Genesis 10:6).
n.30: Literally "to the territory of his holiness".
n.31: Literally "and made them fall by a line as an inheritance".
n.32: Literally "a bow of deceit", one that does not shoot straight.
n.34: That is, the ark of the covenant, captured by the Philistines (1 Samuel 4:21–22).
n.36: Or "like a warrior overcome by wine". The meaning of *mitronen* is uncertain.
n.37: Or "He struck his adversaries from behind".
n.38: Literally "like high places", perhaps the heavens.
n.39: Literally "according to the blamelessness of his heart".

v: A psalm of Asaph.[^1] God, the nations have come into your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a heap of ruins.[^2]
מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֡ים בָּ֤אוּ גוֹיִ֨ם ׀ בְּֽנַחֲלָתֶ֗ךָ טִ֭מְּאוּ אֶת־הֵיכַ֣ל קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ שָׂ֖מוּ אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֣͏ִם לְעִיִּֽים׃
They have given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of the sky, the flesh of your faithful ones[^3] to the wild animals of the earth.
נָֽתְנ֡וּ אֶת־נִבְלַ֬ת עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ מַ֭אֲכָל לְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בְּשַׂ֥ר חֲ֝סִידֶ֗יךָ לְחַיְתוֹ־אָֽרֶץ׃
They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury them.[^4]
שָׁפְכ֬וּ דָמָ֨ם ׀ כַּמַּ֗יִם סְֽבִ֘יב֤וֹת יְֽרוּשָׁלִָ֗ם וְאֵ֣ין קוֹבֵֽר׃
We have become a disgrace to our neighbors, the scorn and mockery of those around us.
הָיִ֣ינוּ חֶ֭רְפָּה לִשְׁכֵנֵ֑ינוּ לַ֥עַג וָ֝קֶ֗לֶס לִסְבִיבוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
How long, LORD?[^5] Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy[^6] burn like fire?
עַד־מָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תֶּאֱנַ֣ף לָנֶ֑צַח תִּ֭[t]בְעַ֥ר כְּמוֹ־אֵ֝֗שׁ קִנְאָתֶֽךָ׃
Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the kingdoms that do not call on your name.
שְׁפֹ֤ךְ חֲמָתְךָ֗ אֶֽל־הַגּוֹיִם֮ אֲשֶׁ֢ר לֹא־יְדָ֫ע֥וּךָ וְעַ֥ל מַמְלָכ֑וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּ֝שִׁמְךָ֗ לֹ֣א קָרָֽאוּ׃
For they have devoured Jacob,[^7] and laid waste his homeland.[^8]
כִּ֭י אָכַ֣ל אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְֽאֶת־נָוֵ֥הוּ הֵשַֽׁמּוּ׃
Do not hold against us the iniquities of former times;[^9] let your compassion come quickly to meet us, for we have been brought very low.
אַֽל־תִּזְכָּר־לָנוּ֮ עֲוֺנֹ֢ת רִאשֹׁ֫נִ֥ים מַ֭הֵר יְקַדְּמ֣וּנוּ רַחֲמֶ֑יךָ כִּ֖י דַלּ֣וֹנוּ מְאֹֽד׃
Help us, God of our salvation, for the sake of the glory of your name; rescue us and atone for our sins,[^10] for the sake of your name.
עָזְרֵ֤נוּ ׀ אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י יִשְׁעֵ֗נוּ עַל־דְּבַ֥ר כְּבֽוֹד־שְׁמֶ֑ךָ וְהַצִּילֵ֥נוּ וְכַפֵּ֥ר עַל־חַ֝טֹּאתֵ֗ינוּ לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?" Before our eyes, let it be known among the nations that you avenge the blood of your servants that has been poured out.[^11]
לָ֤מָּה ׀ יֹאמְר֣וּ הַגּוֹיִם֮ אַיֵּ֢ה אֱ‍ֽלֹהֵ֫יהֶ֥ם יִוָּדַ֣ע *בגיים **בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם לְעֵינֵ֑ינוּ נִ֝קְמַ֗ת דַּֽם־עֲבָדֶ֥יךָ הַשָּׁפֽוּךְ׃
Let the groaning of the prisoner come before you; by the greatness of your arm, preserve[^12] those condemned to die.[^13]
תָּ֤ב֣וֹא לְפָנֶיךָ֮ אֶנְקַ֢ת אָ֫סִ֥יר כְּגֹ֥דֶל זְרוֹעֲךָ֑ ה֝וֹתֵ֗ר בְּנֵ֣י תְמוּתָֽה׃
Pay back our neighbors sevenfold into their laps[^14] for the taunts with which they have taunted you, Lord.
וְהָ֘שֵׁ֤ב לִשְׁכֵנֵ֣ינוּ שִׁ֭בְעָתַיִם אֶל־חֵיקָ֑ם חֶרְפָּ֘תָ֤ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר חֵרְפ֣וּךָ אֲדֹֽ[c]נָי׃
Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever; from generation to generation we will tell of your praise.
וַאֲנַ֤חְנוּ עַמְּךָ֨ ׀ וְצֹ֥אן מַרְעִיתֶךָ֮ נ֤וֹדֶ֥ה לְּךָ֗ לְע֫וֹלָ֥ם לְדֹ֥ר וָדֹ֑ר נְ֝סַפֵּ֗ר תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃

n.1: *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. The psalm mourns the plundering of Jerusalem and its temple, probably by the Babylonians (2 Kings 25:8–10; compare Psalm 74).
n.2: Compare Micah 3:12 and Jeremiah 26:18.
n.3: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.4: 1 Maccabees 7:17 quotes verses 2–3.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: Or "zeal".
n.7: The verb is singular in the Hebrew, "he has devoured", that is, the enemy. Verses 6–7 are nearly the same as Jeremiah 10:25.
n.8: Or "his pasture", "his dwelling place".
n.9: Literally "the iniquities of the first ones": either our own former sins, or the sins of our ancestors.
n.10: Or "cover our sins", "forgive our sins". Hebrew *kapper*, the verb used for making atonement.
n.11: Literally "Let the avenging of the poured-out blood of your servants be known among the nations before our eyes."
n.12: Literally "leave over", that is, keep alive.
n.13: Literally "the sons of death".
n.14: Literally "into their bosom", the fold of a garment above the belt, where things were carried.

v: For the director. According to "Lilies".[^1] A testimony[^2] of Asaph. A psalm.[^3]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ אֶל־שֹׁשַׁנִּ֑ים עֵד֖וּת לְאָסָ֣ף מִזְמֽוֹר׃
Shepherd of Israel, listen, you who lead Joseph like a flock! You who are enthroned on the cherubim,[^4] shine out!
רֹ֘עֵ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל ׀ הַאֲזִ֗ינָה נֹהֵ֣ג כַּצֹּ֣אן יוֹסֵ֑ף יֹשֵׁ֖ב הַכְּרוּבִ֣ים הוֹפִֽיעָה׃
Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up your might, and come to save us.
לִפְנֵ֤י אֶפְרַ֨יִם ׀ וּבִנְיָ֘מִ֤ן וּמְנַשֶּׁ֗ה עוֹרְרָ֥ה אֶת־גְּבֽוּרָתֶ֑ךָ וּלְכָ֖ה לִישֻׁעָ֣תָה לָּֽנוּ׃
God, restore us;[^5] let your face shine, and we will be saved.[^6]
אֱלֹהִ֥ים הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נוּ וְהָאֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעָה׃
LORD God of Armies,[^7] how long will you smolder with anger[^8] against the prayer of your people?
יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֑וֹת עַד־מָתַ֥י עָ֝שַׁ֗נְתָּ בִּתְפִלַּ֥ת עַמֶּֽךָ׃
You have fed them the bread of tears, and made them drink tears by the measure.[^9]
הֶ֭אֱכַלְתָּם לֶ֣חֶם דִּמְעָ֑ה וַ֝תַּשְׁקֵ֗מוֹ בִּדְמָע֥וֹת שָׁלִֽישׁ׃
You make us an object of strife for our neighbors, and our enemies laugh among themselves.[^10]
תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ מָ֭דוֹן לִשְׁכֵנֵ֑ינוּ וְ֝אֹיְבֵ֗ינוּ יִלְעֲגוּ־לָֽמוֹ׃
God of Armies, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֣וֹת הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נוּ וְהָאֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעָה׃
You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.
גֶּ֭פֶן מִמִּצְרַ֣יִם תַּסִּ֑יעַ תְּגָרֵ֥שׁ גּ֝וֹיִ֗ם וַתִּטָּעֶֽהָ׃
You cleared the ground before it; it took deep root and filled the land.
פִּנִּ֥יתָ לְפָנֶ֑יהָ וַתַּשְׁרֵ֥שׁ שָׁ֝רָשֶׁ֗יהָ וַתְּמַלֵּא־אָֽרֶץ׃
The mountains were covered with its shade, and the mighty cedars[^11] with its branches.
כָּסּ֣וּ הָרִ֣ים צִלָּ֑הּ וַ֝עֲנָפֶ֗יהָ אַֽרְזֵי־אֵֽל׃
It sent out its boughs to the Sea, and its shoots to the River.[^12]
תְּשַׁלַּ֣ח קְצִירֶ֣הָ עַד־יָ֑ם וְאֶל־נָ֝הָ֗ר יֽוֹנְקוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
Why have you broken down its walls, so that all who pass along the road pluck its fruit?
לָ֭מָּה פָּרַ֣צְתָּ גְדֵרֶ֑יהָ וְ֝אָר֗וּהָ כָּל־עֹ֥בְרֵי דָֽרֶךְ׃
The boar from the forest[^13] ravages it, and all that moves in the field feeds on it.
יְכַרְסְמֶ֣נָּֽה חֲזִ֣יר מִיָּ֑עַ[7]ר וְזִ֖יז שָׂדַ֣י יִרְעֶֽנָּה׃
God of Armies, turn back, please! Look down from heaven and see; take care of this vine,
אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָאוֹת֮ שֽׁ֫וּב־נָ֥א הַבֵּ֣ט מִשָּׁמַ֣יִם וּרְאֵ֑ה וּ֝פְקֹ֗ד גֶּ֣פֶן זֹֽאת׃
the stock[^14] that your right hand planted, and the son[^15] you made strong for yourself.
וְ֭כַנָּה אֲשֶׁר־נָטְעָ֣ה יְמִינֶ֑ךָ וְעַל־בֵּ֝֗ן אִמַּ֥צְתָּה לָּֽךְ׃
It is burned with fire; it is cut down. At the rebuke of your face they perish.
שְׂרֻפָ֣ה בָאֵ֣שׁ כְּסוּחָ֑ה מִגַּעֲרַ֖ת פָּנֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃
Let your hand be on the man of your right hand,[^16] on the son of man[^17] you made strong for yourself.
תְּֽהִי־יָ֭דְךָ עַל־אִ֣ישׁ יְמִינֶ֑ךָ עַל־בֶּן־אָ֝דָ֗ם אִמַּ֥צְתָּ לָּֽךְ׃
Then we will not turn away from you; give us life, and we will call on your name.
וְלֹא־נָס֥וֹג מִמֶּ֑ךָּ תְּ֝חַיֵּ֗נוּ וּבְשִׁמְךָ֥ נִקְרָֽא׃
LORD God of Armies, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְבָא֣וֹת הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נוּ הָאֵ֥ר פָּ֝נֶ֗יךָ וְנִוָּשֵֽׁעָה׃

n.1: Hebrew *el-shoshannim*, "according to lilies", probably the name of a tune (compare the titles of Psalms 45 and 69).
n.2: Hebrew *edut*, "testimony", perhaps part of the name of the tune, "Lilies of the Testimony" (compare the title of Psalm 60).
n.3: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–20 are 80:1–19 in most English Bibles.
n.4: Or "above the cherubim". Hebrew *keruvim*: winged heavenly beings. Two gold cherubim stood on the cover of the ark (Exodus 25:18–22).
n.5: Or "bring us back". The refrain comes again, growing longer each time, in verses 8 and 20.
n.6: *Let your face shine*: compare the priestly blessing in Numbers 6:25.
n.7: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD God of Armies*: Hebrew *YHWH Elohim tseva'ot*. Compare "the LORD of Armies", traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Verse 20 has the same title, and verses 8 and 15 have *Elohim tseva'ot*, "God of Armies".
n.8: Literally "will you smoke".
n.9: Hebrew *shalish*, "a third", a measure of uncertain size, probably large.
n.10: Literally "mock for themselves". The Septuagint reads "mock us".
n.11: Literally "the cedars of God", that is, the tallest cedars.
n.12: The Mediterranean Sea and the river Euphrates, the ideal limits of the land (compare Exodus 23:31).
n.13: In the Hebrew text the letter *ayin* of *miya'ar*, "from the forest", is written raised above the line, a scribal mark. According to Jewish tradition it marks the middle letter of the book of Psalms.
n.14: Hebrew *kannah*, found only here, probably "stock" or "root". Some take it as a verb, "protect".
n.15: Hebrew *ben*, "son", here also a branch of the vine (compare Genesis 49:22, where Joseph is a fruitful *ben*). The Septuagint reads "the son of man", as in verse 18.
n.16: Probably the king, or Israel as a whole. *Man of your right hand* may play on the name Benjamin, "son of the right hand" (verse 3).
n.17: Hebrew *ben adam*, "son of man", a human being.

v: For the director. According to the Gittith.[^1] Of Asaph.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ ׀ עַֽל־הַגִּתִּ֬ית לְאָסָֽף׃
Sing for joy to God our strength; shout aloud to the God of Jacob.
הַ֭רְנִינוּ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים עוּזֵּ֑נוּ הָ֝רִ֗יעוּ לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃
Raise a song and sound the tambourine, the sweet lyre with the harp.
שְֽׂאוּ־זִ֭מְרָה וּתְנוּ־תֹ֑ף כִּנּ֖וֹר נָעִ֣ים עִם־נָֽבֶל׃
Blow the ram's horn[^3] at the new moon, at the full moon,[^4] on the day of our festival.
תִּקְע֣וּ בַחֹ֣דֶשׁ שׁוֹפָ֑ר בַּ֝כֵּ֗סֶה לְי֣וֹם חַגֵּֽנוּ׃
For this is a decree for Israel, a ruling of the God of Jacob.
כִּ֤י חֹ֣ק לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ה֑וּא מִ֝שְׁפָּ֗ט לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃
He made it a statute[^5] in Joseph[^6] when he went out against the land of Egypt.[^7] I heard a voice I did not know:[^8]
עֵד֤וּת ׀ בִּֽיה֘וֹסֵ֤ף שָׂמ֗וֹ בְּ֭צֵאתוֹ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם שְׂפַ֖ת לֹא־יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
"I removed the burden from his shoulder; his hands were set free from the basket.[^9]
הֲסִיר֣וֹתִי מִסֵּ֣בֶל שִׁכְמ֑וֹ כַּ֝פָּ֗יו מִדּ֥וּד תַּעֲבֹֽרְנָה׃
In distress you called, and I rescued you; I answered you from the hiding place of the thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah.[^10] Selah.[^11]
בַּצָּרָ֥ה קָרָ֗אתָ וָאֲחַ֫לְּצֶ֥ךָּ אֶ֭עֶנְךָ בְּסֵ֣תֶר רַ֑עַם אֶבְחָֽנְךָ֨ עַל־מֵ֖י מְרִיבָ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃
Hear, my people, and I will warn you; Israel, if only you would listen to me!
שְׁמַ֣ע עַ֭מִּי וְאָעִ֣ידָה בָּ֑ךְ יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל אִם־תִּֽשְׁמַֽע־לִֽי׃
There shall be no strange god among you; you shall not bow down to a foreign god.
לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה בְ֭ךָ אֵ֣ל זָ֑ר וְלֹ֥א תִ֝שְׁתַּחֲוֶ֗ה לְאֵ֣ל נֵכָֽר׃
I am the LORD[^12] your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.[^13] Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
אָנֹכִ֨י ׀ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ הַֽ֭מַּעַלְךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הַרְחֶב־פִּ֝֗יךָ וַאֲמַּלְאֵֽהוּ׃
But my people did not listen to my voice, and Israel would have none of me.
וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֣ע עַמִּ֣י לְקוֹלִ֑י וְ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹא־אָ֥בָה לִֽי׃
So I let them go their way in the stubbornness of their hearts, to follow their own plans.
וָֽ֭אֲשַׁלְּחֵהוּ בִּשְׁרִיר֣וּת לִבָּ֑ם יֵ֝לְכ֗וּ בְּֽמוֹעֲצוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
If only my people would listen to me, if only Israel would walk in my ways!
ל֗וּ עַ֭מִּי שֹׁמֵ֣עַֽ לִ֑י יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל בִּדְרָכַ֥י יְהַלֵּֽכוּ׃
I would soon subdue their enemies, and turn my hand against their adversaries.
כִּ֭מְעַט אוֹיְבֵיהֶ֣ם אַכְנִ֑יעַ וְעַ֥ל צָ֝רֵיהֶ֗ם אָשִׁ֥יב יָדִֽי׃
Those who hate the LORD would come cringing to him,[^14] and their time would last forever.[^15]
מְשַׂנְאֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה יְכַֽחֲשׁוּ־ל֑וֹ וִיהִ֖י עִתָּ֣ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃
But he would feed you[^16] with the finest of the wheat, and with honey from the rock I would satisfy you."[^17]
וֽ͏ַ֭יַּאֲכִילֵהוּ מֵחֵ֣לֶב חִטָּ֑ה וּ֝מִצּ֗וּר דְּבַ֣שׁ אַשְׂבִּיעֶֽךָ׃

n.1: Hebrew *gittit*, a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps an instrument or tune from Gath, or a song for the winepress (*gat*). Also in the titles of Psalms 8 and 84.
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–17 are 81:1–16 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *shofar*.
n.4: Hebrew *keseh*, probably the full moon, when the festivals of Passover and of Booths began (Leviticus 23:5–6, 34).
n.5: Hebrew *edut*, traditionally "testimony": the solemn terms of the covenant.
n.6: Here spelled *Yehoseph*, a longer form of the name Joseph, standing for the people of Israel.
n.7: Or "when he went out over the land of Egypt". *He* may be God, who went out against Egypt (Exodus 11:4), or Joseph, who went out over Egypt as its governor (Genesis 41:45). The Septuagint reads "when he went out of the land of Egypt".
n.8: Literally "A lip I did not know I heard." The speaker hears God's words, which follow in verses 7–17. Or "where I heard a language I did not know", that is, in Egypt.
n.9: The baskets used for carrying clay and bricks in Egypt (compare Exodus 1:14).
n.10: *Meribah* means "quarreling". The events are told in Exodus 17:1–7 and Numbers 20:1–13.
n.11: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.12: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.13: Verses 10–11 echo the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2–3; Deuteronomy 5:6–7).
n.14: Or "would pretend to obey him".
n.15: Literally "and their time would be forever", perhaps their time of punishment.
n.16: Literally "he would feed him". The Hebrew moves between "he" and "I", and between "him" and "you".
n.17: Compare Deuteronomy 32:13–14.

v: A psalm of Asaph.[^1] God takes his stand in the divine council;[^2] in the midst of the gods[^3] he gives judgment:
מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ף אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים נִצָּ֥ב בַּעֲדַת־אֵ֑ל בְּקֶ֖רֶב אֱלֹהִ֣ים יִשְׁפֹּֽט׃
"How long will you judge unjustly, and show favor to the wicked?[^4] Selah.[^5]
עַד־מָתַ֥י תִּשְׁפְּטוּ־עָ֑וֶל וּפְנֵ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים תִּשְׂאוּ־סֶֽלָה׃
Give justice to the poor and the fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and the destitute.
שִׁפְטוּ־דַ֥ל וְיָת֑וֹם עָנִ֖י וָרָ֣שׁ הַצְדִּֽיקוּ׃
Rescue the poor and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
פַּלְּטוּ־דַ֥ל וְאֶבְי֑וֹן מִיַּ֖ד רְשָׁעִ֣ים הַצִּֽילוּ׃
They do not know, and they do not understand; they walk about in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken.[^6]
לֹ֤א יָֽדְע֨וּ ׀ וְלֹ֥א יָבִ֗ינוּ בַּחֲשֵׁכָ֥ה יִתְהַלָּ֑כוּ יִ֝מּ֗וֹטוּ כָּל־מ֥וֹסְדֵי אָֽרֶץ׃
"I said, 'You are gods;[^7] you are all sons of the Most High.'[^8]
אֲ‍ֽנִי־אָ֭מַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִ֣ים אַתֶּ֑ם וּבְנֵ֖י עֶלְי֣וֹן כֻּלְּכֶֽם׃
But you will die like human beings,[^9] and fall like any of the princes."
אָ֭כֵן כְּאָדָ֣ם תְּמוּת֑וּן וּכְאַחַ֖ד הַשָּׂרִ֣ים תִּפֹּֽלוּ׃
Rise up, God, judge the earth, for all the nations are your inheritance.[^10]
קוּמָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים שָׁפְטָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה תִ֝נְחַ֗ל בְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

n.1: *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "in the assembly of El", or "in the assembly of God". *El* is a word for God, and in the myths of Canaan it was also the name of the chief god, who presided over an assembly of gods. Here God (*Elohim*) stands in judgment in his own heavenly council (compare 89:6–8; 89:5–7 in most English Bibles; 1 Kings 22:19; Job 1:6).
n.3: Hebrew *elohim*, the same word as "God" at the start of the verse. Here it means the members of God's council, heavenly beings who were given rule over the nations (compare Deuteronomy 32:8, as read in the Septuagint and a Dead Sea Scroll). Many Jewish and Christian interpreters have understood these "gods" as human rulers or judges, who judge in God's name (compare Exodus 21:6; 22:7–8; 22:8–9 in most English Bibles, where *ha-elohim*, "God", may mean the judges).
n.4: Literally "lift up the faces of the wicked", that is, show them partiality.
n.5: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.6: Verse 5 may be God's words about the gods of the council, or the psalmist's own comment. Their injustice shakes the order of the world.
n.7: Hebrew *elohim*, as in verse 1. Jesus quotes this line in John 10:34, arguing from it that Scripture calls "gods" those "to whom the word of God came" (John 10:35).
n.8: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.9: Literally "like *adam*": like humankind, or "like Adam".
n.10: Or "for you will take possession of all the nations".

v: A song. A psalm of Asaph.[^1]
שִׁ֖יר מִזְמ֣וֹר לְאָסָֽף׃
God, do not keep silent; do not be quiet, and do not be still, God.
אֱלֹהִ֥ים אַל־דֳּמִי־לָ֑ךְ אַל־תֶּחֱרַ֖שׁ וְאַל־תִּשְׁקֹ֣ט אֵֽל׃
For look, your enemies are in an uproar; those who hate you have raised their heads.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה א֭וֹיְבֶיךָ יֶהֱמָי֑וּן וּ֝מְשַׂנְאֶ֗יךָ נָ֣שְׂאוּ רֹֽאשׁ׃
Against your people they make crafty plans; they conspire against those you shelter.[^2]
עַֽל־עַ֭מְּךָ יַעֲרִ֣ימוּ ס֑וֹד וְ֝יִתְיָעֲצ֗וּ עַל־צְפוּנֶֽיךָ׃
They say, "Come, let us wipe them out as a nation, so that the name of Israel will be remembered no more."
אָמְר֗וּ לְ֭כוּ וְנַכְחִידֵ֣ם מִגּ֑וֹי וְלֹֽא־יִזָּכֵ֖ר שֵֽׁם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עֽוֹד׃
For they conspire with one mind;[^3] against you they make a covenant:
כִּ֤י נוֹעֲצ֣וּ לֵ֣ב יַחְדָּ֑ו עָ֝לֶ֗יךָ בְּרִ֣ית יִכְרֹֽתוּ׃
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,[^4]
אָהֳלֵ֣י אֱ֭דוֹם וְיִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֗ים מוֹאָ֥ב וְהַגְרֽ͏ִים׃
Gebal[^5] and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the people of Tyre.
גְּבָ֣ל וְ֭עַמּוֹן וַעֲמָלֵ֑ק פְּ֝לֶ֗שֶׁת עִם־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי צֽוֹר׃
Assyria too has joined them; they have become the strong arm of the descendants of Lot.[^6] Selah.[^7]
גַּם־אַ֭שּׁוּר נִלְוָ֣ה עִמָּ֑ם הָ֤י֥וּ זְר֖וֹעַ לִבְנֵי־ל֣וֹט סֶֽלָה׃
Do to them as you did to Midian,[^8] as to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River,[^9]
עֲשֵֽׂה־לָהֶ֥ם כְּמִדְיָ֑ן כְּֽסִֽיסְרָ֥א כְ֝יָבִ֗ין בְּנַ֣חַל קִישֽׁוֹן׃
who were destroyed at En-dor,[^10] who became dung for the ground.
נִשְׁמְד֥וּ בְֽעֵין־דֹּ֑אר הָ֥יוּ דֹ֝֗מֶן לָאֲדָמָֽה׃
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,[^11]
שִׁיתֵ֣מוֹ נְ֭דִיבֵמוֹ כְּעֹרֵ֣ב וְכִזְאֵ֑ב וּֽכְזֶ֥בַח וּ֝כְצַלְמֻנָּ֗ע כָּל־נְסִיכֵֽמוֹ׃
who said, "Let us take possession for ourselves of the pastures of God."[^12]
אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָ֭מְרוּ נִ֣ירֲשָׁה לָּ֑נוּ אֵ֝֗ת נְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִֽים׃
My God, make them like whirling dust,[^13] like chaff before the wind.
אֱ‍ֽלֹהַ֗י שִׁיתֵ֥מוֹ כַגַּלְגַּ֑ל כְּ֝קַ֗שׁ לִפְנֵי־רֽוּחַ׃
As fire burns a forest, and as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
כְּאֵ֥שׁ תִּבְעַר־יָ֑עַר וּ֝כְלֶהָבָ֗ה תְּלַהֵ֥ט הָרִֽים׃
so pursue them with your tempest, and terrify them with your storm.
כֵּ֭ן תִּרְדְּפֵ֣ם בְּסַעֲרֶ֑ךָ וּבְסוּפָתְךָ֥ תְבַהֲלֵֽם׃
Fill their faces with shame, so that they will seek your name, LORD.[^14]
מַלֵּ֣א פְנֵיהֶ֣ם קָל֑וֹן וִֽיבַקְשׁ֖וּ שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָֽה׃
Let them be put to shame and terrified forever; let them be disgraced and perish.
יֵבֹ֖שׁוּ וְיִבָּהֲל֥וּ עֲדֵי־עַ֗ד וְֽיַחְפְּר֥וּ וְיֹאבֵֽדוּ׃
Let them know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High[^15] over all the earth.
וְֽיֵדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֬ה שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה לְבַדֶּ֑ךָ עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן עַל־כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

n.1: *Of Asaph*: or "for Asaph", a Levite who led the temple singers (see the note on 50:1). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–19 are 83:1–18 in most English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "against your hidden ones", those whom God keeps hidden and safe (compare 27:5).
n.3: Literally "with heart together".
n.4: A people living east of Gilead (1 Chronicles 5:10, 19–20).
n.5: Probably the Phoenician city of Gebal, later called Byblos (compare Joshua 13:5). Some think instead of a region south of the Dead Sea, near Edom.
n.6: Literally "they have become an arm to the sons of Lot", that is, Moab and Ammon (Genesis 19:36–38).
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.8: The victory of Gideon over Midian is told in Judges 7–8.
n.9: The victory over Sisera and Jabin is told in Judges 4–5. Hebrew *nachal*, a stream or wadi.
n.10: En-dor is not named in Judges 4–5. It lay near Mount Tabor and the plain where the battle was fought (compare Joshua 17:11).
n.11: The leaders of Midian (Judges 7:25; 8:21).
n.12: That is, the land that belongs to God.
n.13: Hebrew *galgal*, "wheel", perhaps the dry heads of wild plants that the wind rolls along like wheels (compare Isaiah 17:13).
n.14: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.15: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.

v: For the director. According to the Gittith.[^1] Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.[^2]
לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־הַגִּתִּ֑ית לִבְנֵי־קֹ֥רַח מִזְמֽוֹר׃
How lovely is your dwelling place,[^3] LORD of Armies!
מַה־יְּדִיד֥וֹת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֶ֗יךָ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
My soul[^4] longs, it even faints for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.
נִכְסְפָ֬ה וְגַם־כָּלְתָ֨ה ׀ נַפְשִׁי֮ לְחַצְר֢וֹת יְ[t]ה֫וָ֥ה לִבִּ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֑י יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ אֶ֣ל אֵֽל־חָֽי׃
Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, at your altars, LORD of Armies, my King and my God.
גַּם־צִפּ֨וֹר ׀ מָ֪צְאָה בַ֡יִת וּדְר֤וֹר ׀ קֵ֥ן לָהּ֮ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֢תָה אֶפְרֹ֫חֶ֥יהָ אֶֽת־מִ֭זְבְּחוֹתֶיךָ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מַ֝לְכִּ֗י וֵאלֹהָֽי׃
Happy[^5] are those who live in your house; they will praise you continually.[^6] Selah.[^7]
אַ֭שְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י בֵיתֶ֑ךָ ע֝֗וֹד יְֽהַלְל֥וּךָ סֶּֽלָה׃
Happy are those whose strength is in you, whose hearts are set on the highways.[^8]
אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם עֽוֹז־ל֥וֹ בָ֑ךְ מְ֝סִלּ֗וֹת בִּלְבָבָֽם׃
As they pass through the Valley of Baca,[^9] they make it a place of springs; the early rain also covers it with blessings.[^10]
עֹבְרֵ֤י ׀ בְּעֵ֣מֶק הַ֭בָּכָא מַעְיָ֣ן יְשִׁית֑וּהוּ גַּם־בְּ֝רָכ֗וֹת יַעְטֶ֥ה מוֹרֶֽה׃
They go from strength to strength; each one appears before God in Zion.[^11]
יֵ֭לְכוּ מֵחַ֣יִל אֶל־חָ֑יִל יֵרָאֶ֖ה אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים בְּצִיּֽוֹן׃
LORD God of Armies, hear my prayer; listen, God of Jacob. Selah.
יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְ֭בָאוֹת שִׁמְעָ֣ה תְפִלָּתִ֑י הַאֲזִ֨ינָה אֱלֹהֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
Look on our shield, God;[^12] look on the face of your anointed.[^13]
מָ֭גִנֵּנוּ רְאֵ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְ֝הַבֵּ֗ט פְּנֵ֣י מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃
For a day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere.[^14] I would rather stand at the threshold[^15] of the house of my God than live in the tents of wickedness.
כִּ֤י טֽוֹב־י֥וֹם בַּחֲצֵרֶ֗יךָ מֵ֫אָ֥לֶף בָּחַ֗רְתִּי הִ֭סְתּוֹפֵף בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהַ֑י מִ֝דּ֗וּר בְּאָהֳלֵי־רֶֽשַׁע׃
For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory. He does not hold back any good thing from those who walk blamelessly.
כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ ׀ וּמָגֵן֮ יְהוָ֢ה אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים חֵ֣ן וְ֭כָבוֹד יִתֵּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֥א יִמְנַע־ט֝֗וֹב לַֽהֹלְכִ֥ים בְּתָמִֽים׃
LORD of Armies, happy is the one who trusts in you.
יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֑וֹת אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י אָ֝דָ֗ם בֹּטֵ֥חַ בָּֽךְ׃

n.1: Hebrew *gittit*, a term of uncertain meaning (see the note on the title of Psalm 8).
n.2: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–13 are 84:1–12 in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "your dwellings". *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verses 4 and 13, and in verse 9, where the Hebrew is *YHWH Elohim tseva'ot*, "the LORD God of Armies".
n.4: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.5: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed" (see the note on 1:1). Also in verses 6 and 13.
n.6: Literally "they will still praise you".
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 9.
n.8: Literally "highways are in their heart", that is, the roads of pilgrimage to Zion.
n.9: Hebrew *ha-bakha*, perhaps a kind of balsam tree that grows in dry places (compare 2 Samuel 5:23–24), or "weeping" (from *bakhah*, "weep"). The valley is unknown.
n.10: Hebrew *berakhot*. The same consonants can be read *berekhot*, "pools".
n.11: The Septuagint reads "the God of gods will be seen in Zion", taking *el*, "to", as *El*, "God". For "appear before God", compare 42:3 (42:2 in most English Bibles).
n.12: Or "God, our shield, look". *Our shield* may be the king, who is also "your anointed".
n.13: Hebrew *meshichekha*, "your anointed one", from *mashiach*: the king, anointed with oil.
n.14: Literally "than a thousand".
n.15: Hebrew *histofef*, from *saf*, "threshold": to wait at the threshold, or to serve as a doorkeeper.

v: For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ ׀ לִבְנֵי־קֹ֬רַח מִזְמֽוֹר׃
LORD,[^2] you have shown favor to your land; you have restored the fortunes of Jacob.[^3]
רָצִ֣יתָ יְהוָ֣ה אַרְצֶ֑ךָ שַׁ֝֗בְתָּ *שבות **שְׁבִ֣ית יַעֲקֹֽב׃
You have forgiven[^4] the iniquity of your people; you have covered all their sin. Selah.[^5]
נָ֭שָׂאתָ עֲוֺ֣ן עַמֶּ֑ךָ כִּסִּ֖יתָ כָל־חַטָּאתָ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
You have withdrawn all your fury; you have turned from your burning anger.
אָסַ֥פְתָּ כָל־עֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ הֱ֝שִׁיב֗וֹתָ מֵחֲר֥וֹן אַפֶּֽךָ׃
Restore us,[^6] God of our salvation, and put an end to your displeasure toward us.
שׁ֭וּבֵנוּ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֑נוּ וְהָפֵ֖ר כַּֽעַסְךָ֣ עִמָּֽנוּ׃
Will you be angry with us forever? Will you drag out your anger to all generations?
הַלְעוֹלָ֥ם תֶּֽאֱנַף־בָּ֑נוּ תִּמְשֹׁ֥ךְ אַ֝פְּךָ֗ לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃
Will you not give us life again, so that your people may rejoice in you?
הֽ͏ֲלֹא־אַ֭תָּה תָּשׁ֣וּב תְּחַיֵּ֑נוּ וְ֝עַמְּךָ֗ יִשְׂמְחוּ־בָֽךְ׃
Show us your faithful love,[^7] LORD, and grant us your salvation.
הַרְאֵ֣נוּ יְהוָ֣ה חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝יֶשְׁעֲךָ֗ תִּתֶּן־לָֽנוּ׃
Let me hear what God, the LORD, will say, for he will speak peace to his people, to his faithful ones;[^8] but let them not turn back to folly.[^9]
אֶשְׁמְעָ֗ה מַה־יְדַבֵּר֮ הָאֵ֢ל ׀ יְה֫וָ֥ה כִּ֤י ׀ יְדַבֵּ֬ר שָׁל֗וֹם אֶל־עַמּ֥וֹ וְאֶל־חֲסִידָ֑יו וְֽאַל־יָשׁ֥וּבוּ לְכִסְלָֽה׃
Surely his salvation is near to those who fear him, so that glory may dwell in our land.
אַ֤ךְ ׀ קָר֣וֹב לִירֵאָ֣יו יִשְׁע֑וֹ לִשְׁכֹּ֖ן כָּב֣וֹד בְּאַרְצֵֽנוּ׃
Faithful love and faithfulness[^10] have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.
חֶֽסֶד־וֶאֱמֶ֥ת נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ צֶ֖דֶק וְשָׁל֣וֹם נָשָֽׁקוּ׃
Faithfulness springs up from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
אֱ֭מֶת מֵאֶ֣רֶץ תִּצְמָ֑ח וְ֝צֶ֗דֶק מִשָּׁמַ֥יִם נִשְׁקָֽף׃
The LORD will indeed give what is good, and our land will yield its harvest.
גַּם־יְ֭הוָה יִתֵּ֣ן הַטּ֑וֹב וְ֝אַרְצֵ֗נוּ תִּתֵּ֥ן יְבוּלָֽהּ׃
Righteousness will go before him, and make a path for his steps.[^11]
צֶ֭דֶק לְפָנָ֣יו יְהַלֵּ֑ךְ וְיָשֵׂ֖ם לְדֶ֣רֶךְ פְּעָמָֽיו׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–14 are 85:1–13 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "you have brought back the captives of Jacob".
n.4: Literally "lifted", that is, taken away.
n.5: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.6: Or "Return to us". Literally "Turn us back".
n.7: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verse 11.
n.8: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.9: The Septuagint reads "and to those who turn their hearts to him".
n.10: Hebrew *chesed* and *emet*, the pair in God's description of himself in Exodus 34:6. *Emet* means firmness, reliability, truth. Also in verse 12.
n.11: Literally "and will set his steps for a way". Or "and will set us on the way of his steps".

v: A prayer of David.[^1] Turn your ear, LORD,[^2] and answer me, for I am afflicted and needy.
תְּפִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥ד הַטֵּֽה־יְהוָ֣ה אָזְנְךָ֣ עֲנֵ֑נִי כִּֽי־עָנִ֖י וְאֶבְי֣וֹן אָֽנִי׃
Guard my life,[^3] for I am faithful;[^4] you are my God; save your servant, who trusts in you.
שָֽׁמְרָ֣ה נַפְשִׁי֮ כִּֽי־חָסִ֢יד אָ֥נִי הוֹשַׁ֣ע עַ֭בְדְּךָ אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֑י הַבּוֹטֵ֥חַ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
Be gracious to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
חָנֵּ֥נִי אֲדֹנָ֑י כִּ֥י אֵלֶ֥יךָ אֶ֝קְרָ֗א כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
Make your servant's soul glad, for to you, Lord, I lift up my soul.
שַׂ֭מֵּחַ נֶ֣פֶשׁ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י אֵלֶ֥יךָ אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י נַפְשִׁ֥י אֶשָּֽׂא׃
For you, Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in faithful love[^5] to all who call on you.
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה אֲ֭דֹנָי ט֣וֹב וְסַלָּ֑ח וְרַב־חֶ֝֗סֶד לְכָל־קֹרְאֶֽיךָ׃
Listen, LORD, to my prayer, and pay attention to the sound of my pleas for mercy.
הַאֲזִ֣ינָה יְ֭הוָה תְּפִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝הַקְשִׁ֗יבָה בְּק֣וֹל תַּחֲנוּנוֹתָֽי׃
In the day of my trouble I call on you, for you will answer me.
בְּי֣וֹם צָ֭רָתִ֥י אֶקְרָאֶ֗ךָּ כִּ֣י תַעֲנֵֽנִי׃
There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, and there are no works like yours.
אֵין־כָּמ֖וֹךָ בָאֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ אֲדֹנָ֗י וְאֵ֣ין כְּֽמַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ׃
All the nations you have made will come and bow down before you, Lord, and they will glorify your name.
כָּל־גּוֹיִ֤ם ׀ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ יָב֤וֹאוּ ׀ וְיִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֲדֹנָ֑י וִ֖יכַבְּד֣וּ לִשְׁמֶֽךָ׃
For you are great, and you do wonders; you alone are God.
כִּֽי־גָד֣וֹל אַ֭תָּה וְעֹשֵׂ֣ה נִפְלָא֑וֹת אַתָּ֖ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
Teach me your way, LORD, so that I may walk in your truth; give me an undivided heart[^6] to fear your name.
ה֘וֹרֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֨ה ׀ דַּרְכֶּ֗ךָ אֲהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּאֲמִתֶּ֑ךָ יַחֵ֥ד לְ֝בָבִ֗י לְיִרְאָ֥ה שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
I will give thanks to you, Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever.
אוֹדְךָ֤ ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י אֱ֭לֹהַי בְּכָל־לְבָבִ֑י וַאֲכַבְּדָ֖ה שִׁמְךָ֣ לְעוֹלָֽם׃
For your faithful love toward me is great; you have rescued my life from the depths of Sheol.[^7]
כִּֽי־חַ֭סְדְּךָ גָּד֣וֹל עָלָ֑י וְהִצַּ֥לְתָּ נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּחְתִּיּֽ͏ָה׃
God, the arrogant have risen against me, and a band of ruthless men seeks my life; they do not set you before them.[^8]
אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ זֵ֘דִ֤ים קָֽמוּ־עָלַ֗י וַעֲדַ֣ת עָ֭רִיצִים בִּקְשׁ֣וּ נַפְשִׁ֑י וְלֹ֖א שָׂמ֣וּךָ לְנֶגְדָּֽם׃
But you, Lord, are a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in faithful love and faithfulness.[^9]
וְאַתָּ֣ה אֲ֭דֹנָי אֵל־רַח֣וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃
Turn to me and be gracious to me; give your strength to your servant, and save the son of your female servant.[^10]
פְּנֵ֥ה אֵלַ֗י וְחָ֫נֵּ֥נִי תְּנָֽה־עֻזְּךָ֥ לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝הוֹשִׁ֗יעָה לְבֶן־אֲמָתֶֽךָ׃
Show me a sign of your goodness,[^11] so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame, for you, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
עֲשֵֽׂה־עִמִּ֥י א֗וֹת לְט֫וֹבָ֥ה וְיִרְא֣וּ שֹׂנְאַ֣י וְיֵבֹ֑שׁוּ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה עֲזַרְתַּ֥נִי וְנִחַמְתָּֽנִי׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". It is the only psalm in Book 3 (Psalms 73–89) with David's name in its title. In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. Many of its lines echo other psalms and Exodus 34:6.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 4, 13 and 14.
n.4: Hebrew *chasid*, "faithful one", related to *chesed*, "faithful love". Or "devoted to you".
n.5: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verses 13 and 15.
n.6: Literally "unite my heart". The Septuagint reads "let my heart rejoice", taking the same consonants from another verb.
n.7: Literally "from lowest Sheol". Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.8: This verse is almost the same as 54:5 (54:3 in most English Bibles), which has "strangers" where this verse has "the arrogant".
n.9: These words repeat God's description of himself in Exodus 34:6 (compare 103:8; 145:8).
n.10: That is, a servant born in the household, and so bound to it for life (compare 116:16).
n.11: Literally "Do with me a sign for good".

v: Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.[^1] The city he founded stands on the holy mountains.[^2]
לִבְנֵי־קֹ֖[d]רַח מִזְמ֣וֹר שִׁ֑יר יְ֝סוּדָת֗וֹ בְּהַרְרֵי־קֹֽדֶשׁ׃
The LORD[^3] loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
אֹהֵ֣ב יְ֭הוָה שַׁעֲרֵ֣י צִיּ֑וֹן מִ֝כֹּ֗ל מִשְׁכְּנ֥וֹת יַעֲקֹֽב׃
Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God. Selah.[^4]
נִ֭כְבָּדוֹת מְדֻבָּ֣ר בָּ֑ךְ עִ֖יר הָאֱלֹהִ֣ים סֶֽלָה׃
I will record Rahab[^5] and Babylon among those who know me; look, Philistia and Tyre, with Cush:[^6] "This one was born there."[^7]
אַזְכִּ֤יר ׀ רַ֥הַב וּבָבֶ֗ל לְֽיֹ֫דְעָ֥י הִנֵּ֤ה פְלֶ֣שֶׁת וְצ֣וֹר עִם־כּ֑וּשׁ זֶ֝֗ה יֻלַּד־שָֽׁם׃
And of Zion it will be said, "Each one and every one[^8] was born in her," and the Most High[^9] himself will establish her.
וּֽלֲצִיּ֨וֹן ׀ יֵאָמַ֗ר אִ֣ישׁ וְ֭אִישׁ יֻלַּד־בָּ֑הּ וְה֖וּא יְכוֹנְנֶ֣הָ עֶלְיֽוֹן׃
The LORD will record, as he registers the peoples,[^10] "This one was born there." Selah.
יְֽהוָ֗ה יִ֭סְפֹּר בִּכְת֣וֹב עַמִּ֑ים זֶ֖ה יֻלַּד־שָׁ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
Singers and dancers alike say,[^11] "All my springs are in you."
וְשָׁרִ֥ים כְּחֹלְלִ֑ים כָּֽל־מַעְיָנַ֥י בָּֽךְ׃

n.1: *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "His foundation is on the holy mountains", that is, Zion, the city God founded.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 6.
n.5: Hebrew *Rahav*, a poetic name for Egypt (Isaiah 30:7), taken from the name of a sea monster (89:11; 89:10 in most English Bibles; Job 26:12). It is not the Rahab of Joshua 2, whose name is spelled differently in Hebrew.
n.6: The land on the upper Nile, south of Egypt.
n.7: That is, people of these nations will be counted as born in Zion, as its own citizens.
n.8: Literally "a man and a man".
n.9: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.10: Literally "in the writing of the peoples", that is, in the register of citizens.
n.11: Literally "And singers like dancers: all my springs are in you." The Hebrew is very brief, and "say" is supplied. *Dancers*: or "flute players". *Springs*: sources of life and blessing.

v: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the director. According to Mahalath Leannoth.[^1] A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.[^2]
שִׁ֥יר מִזְמ֗וֹר לִבְנֵ֫י קֹ֥רַח לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ עַל־מָחֲלַ֣ת לְעַנּ֑וֹת מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְהֵימָ֥ן הָאֶזְרָחִֽי׃
LORD,[^3] God of my salvation, by day I cry out, and by night, before you.[^4]
יְ֭הוָה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יְשׁוּעָתִ֑י יוֹם־צָעַ֖קְתִּי בַלַּ֣יְלָה נֶגְדֶּֽךָ׃
Let my prayer come before you; turn your ear to my cry.
תָּב֣וֹא לְ֭פָנֶיךָ תְּפִלָּתִ֑י הַטֵּֽה־אָ֝זְנְךָ֗ לְרִנָּתִֽי׃
For my soul[^5] is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.[^6]
כִּֽי־שָֽׂבְעָ֣ה בְרָע֣וֹת נַפְשִׁ֑י וְ֝חַיַּ֗י לִשְׁא֥וֹל הִגִּֽיעוּ׃
I am counted among those who go down to the pit; I have become like a man without strength,[^7]
נֶ֭חְשַׁבְתִּי עִם־י֣וֹרְדֵי ב֑וֹר הָ֝יִ֗יתִי כְּגֶ֣בֶר אֵֽין־אֱיָֽל׃
left alone[^8] among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more, for they are cut off from your hand.
בַּמֵּתִ֗ים חָ֫פְשִׁ֥י כְּמ֤וֹ חֲלָלִ֨ים ׀ שֹׁ֥כְבֵי קֶ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹ֣א זְכַרְתָּ֣ם ע֑וֹד וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה מִיָּדְךָ֥ נִגְזָֽרוּ׃
You have put me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.
שַׁ֭תַּנִי בְּב֣וֹר תַּחְתִּיּ֑וֹת בְּ֝מַחֲשַׁכִּ֗ים בִּמְצֹלֽוֹת׃
Your wrath lies heavy on me, and you have afflicted me with all your breakers. Selah.[^9]
עָ֭לַי סָמְכָ֣ה חֲמָתֶ֑ךָ וְכָל־מִ֝שְׁבָּרֶ֗יךָ עִנִּ֥יתָ סֶּֽלָה׃
You have taken my friends far from me; you have made me a horror to them. I am shut in, and I cannot get out.
הִרְחַ֥קְתָּ מְיֻדָּעַ֗י מִ֫מֶּ֥נִּי שַׁתַּ֣נִי תוֹעֵב֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ כָּ֝לֻ֗א וְלֹ֣א אֵצֵֽא׃
My eye grows dim from affliction. I call on you, LORD, every day; I spread out my hands to you.
עֵינִ֥י דָאֲבָ֗ה מִנִּ֫י עֹ֥נִי קְרָאתִ֣יךָ יְהוָ֣ה בְּכָל־י֑וֹם שִׁטַּ֖חְתִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ כַפָּֽי׃
Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the shades[^10] rise up to praise you? Selah.
הֲלַמֵּתִ֥ים תַּעֲשֶׂה־פֶּ֑לֶא אִם־רְ֝פָאִ֗ים יָק֤וּמוּ ׀ יוֹד֬וּךָ סֶּֽלָה׃
Is your faithful love[^11] told in the grave, your faithfulness in Abaddon?[^12]
הַיְסֻפַּ֣ר בַּקֶּ֣בֶר חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ בָּאֲבַדּֽוֹן׃
Are your wonders known in the darkness, or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?[^13]
הֲיִוָּדַ֣ע בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ פִּלְאֶ֑ךָ וְ֝צִדְקָ[t]תְךָ֗ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ נְשִׁיָּֽה׃
But I cry to you for help, LORD; in the morning my prayer comes before you.
וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְהוָ֣ה שִׁוַּ֑עְתִּי וּ֝בַבֹּ֗קֶר תְּֽפִלָּתִ֥י תְקַדְּמֶֽךָּ׃
Why, LORD, do you reject my soul? Why do you hide your face from me?
לָמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תִּזְנַ֣ח נַפְשִׁ֑י תַּסְתִּ֖יר פָּנֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
I have been afflicted and close to death from my youth; I bear your terrors; I am helpless.[^14]
עָ֘נִ֤י אֲנִ֣י וְגֹוֵ֣עַ מִנֹּ֑עַר נָשָׂ֖אתִי אֵמֶ֣יךָ אָפֽוּנָה׃
Your burning anger has swept over me; your terrors have destroyed me.
עָ֭לַי עָבְר֣וּ חֲרוֹנֶ֑יךָ בִּ֝עוּתֶ֗יךָ צִמְּתוּתֻֽנִי׃
They surround me like water all day long; they close in on me together.
סַבּ֣וּנִי כַ֭מַּיִם כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם הִקִּ֖יפוּ עָלַ֣י יָֽחַד׃
You have taken lover and friend far from me; darkness is my only companion.[^15]
הִרְחַ֣קְתָּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי אֹהֵ֣ב וָרֵ֑עַ מְֽיֻדָּעַ֥י מַחְשָֽׁךְ׃

n.1: Hebrew *al-machalat le'annot*. *Machalat* is a term of uncertain meaning (see the note on the title of Psalm 53). *Le'annot* may mean "for singing", "for responsive singing", or "for affliction".
n.2: *Of the sons of Korah*: or "for the sons of Korah", a family of Levites who served as temple singers. *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of Heman*: or "for Heman". A wise man named Heman is mentioned in 1 Kings 5:11 (4:31 in most English Bibles), and Heman was also one of David's chief musicians (1 Chronicles 15:17, 19; 25:1). *Ezrahite* probably means a descendant of Zerah (1 Chronicles 2:6). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–19 are 88:1–18 in most English Bibles.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "the day I cried out in the night before you". The Hebrew is unusual.
n.5: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verse 15.
n.6: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.7: Hebrew *eyal*, a word found only here, probably "strength".
n.8: Literally "free", perhaps meaning released from life, or abandoned.
n.9: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verse 11.
n.10: Hebrew *repha'im*, the spirits of the dead (compare Isaiah 14:9).
n.11: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.12: Hebrew *Abaddon*, "Destruction", a name for the realm of the dead (Job 26:6; Proverbs 15:11).
n.13: That is, the realm of the dead, where the dead are forgotten and forget.
n.14: Hebrew *afunah*, a word found only here; the meaning is uncertain, perhaps "I am in despair" or "I am numb".
n.15: Literally "my friends are darkness", or "my friends are in darkness". The psalm ends without any word of hope.

v: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.[^1]
מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְאֵיתָ֥ן הָֽאֶזְרָחִֽי׃
I will sing of the faithful love[^2] of the LORD[^3] forever; with my mouth I will make your faithfulness[^4] known to all generations.
חַֽסְדֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה עוֹלָ֣ם אָשִׁ֑ירָה לְדֹ֥ר וָדֹ֓ר ׀ אוֹדִ֖יעַ אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ בְּפִֽי׃
For I said, "Faithful love will be built up forever; in the heavens you will establish your faithfulness."[^5]
כִּֽי־אָמַ֗רְתִּי ע֭וֹלָם חֶ֣סֶד יִבָּנֶ֑ה שָׁמַ֓יִם ׀ תָּכִ֖ן אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ בָהֶֽם׃
I have made a covenant with my chosen one;[^6] I have sworn to David my servant:
כָּרַ֣תִּֽי בְ֭רִית לִבְחִירִ֑י נִ֝שְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי לְדָוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃
"I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations." Selah.[^7]
עַד־ע֭וֹלָם אָכִ֣ין זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וּבָנִ֨יתִי לְדֹר־וָד֖וֹר כִּסְאֲךָ֣ סֶֽלָה׃
The heavens praise your wonders, LORD, and your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.[^8]
וְי֘וֹד֤וּ שָׁמַ֣יִם פִּלְאֲךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה אַף־אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ בִּקְהַ֥ל קְדֹשִֽׁים׃
For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the sons of the gods[^9] is like the LORD,
כִּ֤י מִ֣י בַ֭שַּׁחַק יַעֲרֹ֣ךְ לַיהוָ֑ה יִדְמֶ֥ה לַ֝יהוָ֗ה בִּבְנֵ֥י אֵלִים׃
a God greatly feared in the council of the holy ones, and awesome above all who are around him?
אֵ֣ל נַ֭עֲרָץ בְּסוֹד־קְדֹשִׁ֣ים רַבָּ֑ה וְ֝נוֹרָ֗א עַל־כָּל־סְבִיבָֽיו׃
LORD God of Armies,[^10] who is like you? You are mighty, LORD,[^11] and your faithfulness surrounds you.
יְהוָ֤ה ׀ אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י צְבָא֗וֹת מִֽי־כָֽמ֖וֹךָ חֲסִ֥ין ׀ יָ֑הּ וֶ֝אֱמ֥וּנָתְךָ֗ סְבִיבוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
You rule the raging of the sea; when its waves rise, you calm them.
אַתָּ֣ה מ֖[d]וֹשֵׁל בְּגֵא֣וּת הַיָּ֑ם בְּשׂ֥וֹא גַ֝לָּ֗יו אַתָּ֥ה תְשַׁבְּחֵֽם׃
You crushed Rahab[^12] like one who is slain; with your strong arm you scattered your enemies.
אַתָּ֤ה דִכִּ֣אתָ כֶחָלָ֣ל רָ֑הַב בִּזְר֥וֹעַ עֻ֝זְּךָ֗ פִּזַּ֥רְתָּ אוֹיְבֶֽיךָ׃
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours as well; the world and all that fills it, you founded them.
לְךָ֣ שָׁ֭מַיִם אַף־לְךָ֥ אָ֑רֶץ תֵּבֵ֥ל וּ֝מְלֹאָ֗הּ אַתָּ֥ה יְסַדְתָּֽם׃
The north and the south,[^13] you created them; Tabor and Hermon[^14] sing for joy at your name.
צָפ֣וֹן וְ֭יָמִין אַתָּ֣ה בְרָאתָ֑ם תָּב֥וֹר וְ֝חֶרְמ֗וֹן בְּשִׁמְךָ֥ יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃
Yours is an arm with might; your hand is strong, your right hand is raised high.
לְךָ֣ זְ֭רוֹעַ עִם־גְּבוּרָ֑ה תָּעֹ֥ז יָ֝דְךָ֗ תָּר֥וּם יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; faithful love and faithfulness[^15] go before you.
צֶ֣דֶק וּ֭מִשְׁפָּט מְכ֣וֹן כִּסְאֶ֑ךָ חֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת יְֽקַדְּמ֥וּ פָנֶֽיךָ׃
Happy[^16] are the people who know the festal shout,[^17] who walk, LORD, in the light of your face.
אַשְׁרֵ֣י הָ֭עָם יוֹדְעֵ֣י תְרוּעָ֑ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה בְּֽאוֹר־פָּנֶ֥יךָ יְהַלֵּכֽוּן׃
In your name they rejoice all day long, and in your righteousness they are lifted up.
בְּ֭שִׁמְךָ יְגִיל֣וּן כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם וּבְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ יָרֽוּמוּ׃
For you are the glory of their strength, and by your favor our horn[^18] is lifted high.[^19]
כִּֽי־תִפְאֶ֣רֶת עֻזָּ֣מוֹ אָ֑תָּה וּ֝בִרְצֹנְךָ֗ *תרים **תָּר֥וּם קַרְנֵֽנוּ׃
For our shield belongs to the LORD, and our king to the Holy One of Israel.[^20]
כִּ֣י לַֽ֭יהוָה מָֽגִנֵּ֑נוּ וְלִקְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מַלְכֵּֽנוּ׃
Once you spoke in a vision to your faithful ones,[^21] and said, "I have given help to a mighty man; I have raised up one chosen from the people.[^22]
אָ֤ז דִּבַּ֥רְתָּֽ־בְחָז֡וֹן לַֽחֲסִידֶ֗יךָ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁוִּ֣יתִי עֵ֭זֶר עַל־גִּבּ֑וֹר הֲרִימ֖וֹתִי בָח֣וּר מֵעָֽם׃
I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.[^23]
מָ֭צָאתִי דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֑י בְּשֶׁ֖מֶן קָדְשִׁ֣י מְשַׁחְתִּֽיו׃
My hand will be with him to support him; my arm also will strengthen him.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָ֭דִי תִּכּ֣וֹן עִמּ֑וֹ אַף־זְרוֹעִ֥י תְאַמְּצֶֽנּוּ׃
No enemy will get the better of him;[^24] no wicked man[^25] will humble him.
לֹֽא־יַשִּׁ֣א אוֹיֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ וּבֶן־עַ֝וְלָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְעַנֶּֽנּוּ׃
I will crush his adversaries before him, and strike down those who hate him.
וְכַתּוֹתִ֣י מִפָּנָ֣יו צָרָ֑יו וּמְשַׂנְאָ֥יו אֶגּֽוֹף׃
My faithfulness and my faithful love will be with him, and through my name his horn will be lifted high.
וֶֽאֶֽמוּנָתִ֣י וְחַסְדִּ֣י עִמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בִשְׁמִ֗י תָּר֥וּם קַרְנֽוֹ׃
I will set his hand on the sea, and his right hand on the rivers.[^26]
וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י בַיָּ֣ם יָד֑וֹ וּֽבַנְּהָר֥וֹת יְמִינֽוֹ׃
He will call to me, 'You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation.'
ה֣וּא יִ֭קְרָאֵנִי אָ֣בִי אָ֑תָּה אֵ֝לִ֗י וְצ֣וּר יְשׁוּעָתִֽי׃
I will also make him my firstborn,[^27] the highest[^28] of the kings of the earth.
אַף־אָ֭נִי בְּכ֣וֹר אֶתְּנֵ֑הוּ עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן לְמַלְכֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
I will keep my faithful love for him forever, and my covenant with him will stand firm.
לְ֭עוֹלָ֗[c]ם *אשמור־**אֶשְׁמָר־ל֣וֹ חַסְדִּ֑י וּ֝בְרִיתִ֗י נֶאֱמֶ֥נֶת לֽוֹ׃
I will establish his offspring forever, and his throne as long as the heavens endure.[^29]
וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י לָעַ֣ד זַרְע֑וֹ וְ֝כִסְא֗וֹ כִּימֵ֥י שָׁמָֽיִם׃
If his sons forsake my law, and do not walk in my rulings,
אִם־יַֽעַזְב֣וּ בָ֭נָיו תּוֹרָתִ֑י וּ֝בְמִשְׁפָּטַ֗י לֹ֣א יֵלֵכֽוּן׃
if they violate my decrees, and do not keep my commands,
אִם־חֻקֹּתַ֥י יְחַלֵּ֑לוּ וּ֝מִצְוֺתַ֗י לֹ֣א יִשְׁמֹֽרוּ׃
then I will punish their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with blows.[^30]
וּפָקַדְתִּ֣י בְשֵׁ֣בֶט פִּשְׁעָ֑ם וּבִנְגָעִ֥ים עֲוֺנָֽם׃
But I will not take my faithful love away from him, or be false to my faithfulness.
וְ֭חַסְדִּי לֹֽא־אָפִ֣יר מֵֽעִמּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־אֲ֝שַׁקֵּ֗ר בֶּאֱמוּנָתִֽי׃
I will not violate my covenant, or change what my lips have spoken.
לֹא־אֲחַלֵּ֥ל בְּרִיתִ֑י וּמוֹצָ֥א שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י לֹ֣א אֲשַׁנֶּֽה׃
Once for all I have sworn by my holiness; I will not lie to David.
אַ֭חַת נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתִּי בְקָדְשִׁ֑י אִֽם־לְדָוִ֥ד אֲכַזֵּֽב׃
His offspring will endure forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me.
זַ֭רְעוֹ לְעוֹלָ֣ם יִהְיֶ֑ה וְכִסְא֖וֹ כַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ נֶגְדִּֽי׃
Like the moon it will be established forever, a faithful witness in the skies."[^31] Selah.
כְּ֭יָרֵחַ יִכּ֣וֹן עוֹלָ֑ם וְעֵ֥ד בַּ֝שַּׁ֗חַק נֶאֱמָ֥ן סֶֽלָה׃
But you have rejected and spurned him; you are furious with your anointed.[^32]
וְאַתָּ֣ה זָ֭נַחְתָּ וַתִּמְאָ֑ס הִ֝תְעַבַּ֗רְתָּ עִם־מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃
You have renounced the covenant with your servant; you have defiled his crown in the dust.[^33]
נֵ֭אַרְתָּה בְּרִ֣ית עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ חִלַּ֖לְתָּ לָאָ֣רֶץ נִזְרֽוֹ׃
You have broken down all his walls; you have made his strongholds a ruin.
פָּרַ֥צְתָּ כָל־גְּדֵרֹתָ֑יו שַׂ֖מְתָּ מִבְצָרָ֣יו מְחִתָּה׃
All who pass along the road plunder him; he has become a disgrace to his neighbors.
שַׁ֭סֻּהוּ כָּל־עֹ֣בְרֵי דָ֑רֶךְ הָיָ֥ה חֶ֝רְפָּ֗ה לִשְׁכֵֽנָיו׃
You have raised the right hand of his adversaries; you have made all his enemies rejoice.
הֲ֭רִימוֹתָ יְמִ֣ין צָרָ֑יו הִ֝שְׂמַ֗חְתָּ כָּל־אוֹיְבָֽיו׃
You have also turned back the edge[^34] of his sword, and you have not made him stand in battle.
אַף־תָּ֭שִׁיב צ֣וּר חַרְבּ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א הֲ֝קֵימֹת֗וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
You have put an end to his splendor,[^35] and hurled his throne to the ground.
הִשְׁבַּ֥תָּ מִטְּהָר֑וֹ וְ֝כִסְא֗וֹ לָאָ֥רֶץ מִגַּֽרְתָּה׃
You have cut short the days of his youth; you have covered him with shame. Selah.
הִ֭קְצַרְתָּ יְמֵ֣י עֲלוּמָ֑יו הֶֽעֱטִ֨יתָ עָלָ֖יו בּוּשָׁ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃
How long, LORD? Will you hide yourself forever? Will your wrath burn like fire?
עַד־מָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תִּסָּתֵ֣ר לָנֶ֑צַח תִּבְעַ֖ר כְּמוֹ־אֵ֣שׁ חֲמָתֶֽךָ׃
Remember how short my life is![^36] For what futility you have created all humankind!
זְכָר־אֲנִ֥י מֶה־חָ֑לֶד עַל־מַה־שָּׁ֝֗וְא בָּרָ֥אתָ כָל־בְּנֵי־אָדָֽם׃
Who can live and never see death? Who can rescue his life[^37] from the power of Sheol?[^38] Selah.
מִ֤י גֶ֣בֶר יִֽ֭חְיֶה וְלֹ֣א יִרְאֶה־מָּ֑וֶת יְמַלֵּ֨ט נַפְשׁ֖וֹ מִיַּד־שְׁא֣וֹל סֶֽלָה׃
Lord, where are your former acts of faithful love, which you swore to David in your faithfulness?
אַיֵּ֤ה ׀ חֲסָדֶ֖יךָ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֥ים ׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתָּ לְ֝דָוִ֗ד בֶּאֱמוּנָתֶֽךָ׃
Remember, Lord, how your servants are taunted, how I carry in my heart the insults of all the many peoples,[^39]
זְכֹ֣ר אֲ֭דֹנָי חֶרְפַּ֣ת עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ שְׂאֵתִ֥י בְ֝חֵיקִ֗י כָּל־רַבִּ֥ים עַמִּֽים׃
with which your enemies have taunted, LORD, with which they have taunted the footsteps of your anointed.[^40]
אֲשֶׁ֤ר חֵרְפ֖וּ אוֹיְבֶ֥יךָ ׀ יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חֵ֝רְפ֗וּ עִקְּב֥וֹת מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃
Blessed be the LORD forever. Amen and Amen.[^41]
בָּר֖וּךְ יְהוָ֥ה לְ֝עוֹלָ֗ם אָ֘מֵ֥ן ׀ וְאָמֵֽן׃

n.1: *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of Ethan*: or "for Ethan". A wise man named Ethan the Ezrahite is mentioned in 1 Kings 5:11 (4:31 in most English Bibles), and Ethan was also one of David's chief musicians (1 Chronicles 15:17, 19). *Ezrahite* probably means a descendant of Zerah (1 Chronicles 2:6). In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–53 are 89:1–52 in most English Bibles. The psalm celebrates God's covenant with David (verses 4–5 and 20–38; compare 2 Samuel 7:8–16) and then laments that God seems to have abandoned it, for the king of David's line has been defeated and shamed (verses 39–52).
n.2: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Here and in verse 50 it is plural, "acts of faithful love". Also in verses 3, 15, 25, 29 and 34.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *emunah*: firmness, reliability, faithfulness. Also in verses 3, 6, 9, 25, 34 and 50. *Chesed* and *emunah* each appear seven times in the psalm.
n.5: The Septuagint reads "For you said".
n.6: God speaks in verses 4–5, summing up the promise that is given in full in verses 20–38.
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verses 38, 46 and 49.
n.8: The heavenly beings who serve in God's court, as in verse 8.
n.9: Literally "sons of gods" (Hebrew *bene elim*): heavenly beings who serve in God's court (compare 29:1; Job 1:6).
n.10: Hebrew *YHWH Elohei tseva'ot*. Compare "the LORD of Armies", traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.11: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH. *Mighty*: Hebrew *chasin*, found only here.
n.12: Hebrew *Rahav*, a sea monster, a picture of the chaos that God subdued (Job 26:12; Isaiah 51:9), and also a poetic name for Egypt (87:4).
n.13: Literally "the right", since the south lies on the right hand of one who faces east.
n.14: Two mountains in the north of Israel.
n.15: Hebrew *chesed* and *emet*, the pair in God's description of himself in Exodus 34:6. *Emet* means firmness, reliability, truth.
n.16: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
