n.17: Hebrew *teru'ah*, the shout or trumpet blast of worship and festival (compare Leviticus 23:24; Numbers 10:5).
n.18: A symbol of strength, like the horns of a wild ox. Also in verse 25.
n.19: The Hebrew text is written "you lift high our horn" but read "our horn is lifted high".
n.20: That is, the king, "our shield", belongs to God. Or "For the LORD is our shield, the Holy One of Israel is our king".
n.21: Hebrew *chasidim*, "faithful ones", related to *chesed*, "faithful love". The vision is probably the one given to Nathan the prophet (2 Samuel 7:4–17).
n.22: Or "I have exalted a young man from the people".
n.23: Hebrew *meshachtiv*, from the same root as *mashiach*, "anointed one". Acts 13:22 echoes the first half of this verse, together with 1 Samuel 13:14.
n.25: Literally "a son of injustice". Compare 2 Samuel 7:10.
n.26: Perhaps the Mediterranean Sea and the river Euphrates with its streams (compare 72:8; 80:12; 80:11 in most English Bibles). The king's rule mirrors God's rule over the sea (verse 10).
n.27: Compare 2 Samuel 7:14 and Exodus 4:22, where Israel is God's firstborn son.
n.28: Hebrew *elyon*, the word used as a title of God, "the Most High". Revelation 1:5 echoes this verse and verse 38, calling Jesus "the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth".
n.29: Literally "as the days of the heavens".
n.31: Literally "and a witness in the skies is faithful": the moon, or God himself.
n.32: Hebrew *meshichekha*, "your anointed one", from *mashiach*: the king of David's line, anointed with oil. Also in verse 52. Later Jewish and Christian readers also heard in this psalm the hope of the promised Messiah, the son of David.
n.33: Literally "you have profaned his crown to the ground".
n.35: Hebrew *mittehar*, an unusual form, probably "from his brightness". Or "his purity".
n.36: Literally "Remember: I, what is a lifetime!" The Hebrew is difficult.
n.38: Literally "from the hand of Sheol". Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.39: Literally "my carrying in my bosom all of many peoples". The Hebrew is difficult, and "the insults of" is supplied from the context.
n.40: *Footsteps*: that is, every step he takes, wherever he goes. Later Jewish tradition used the phrase "the footsteps of the Messiah" for the troubled time before his coming.
n.41: This blessing closes Book 3 of the Psalms (Psalms 73–89). Books 1, 2 and 4 end in a similar way (41:14; 41:13 in most English Bibles; 72:18–19; 106:48), and Psalm 150 closes the whole collection.

v: A prayer of Moses, the man of God.[^1] Lord, you have been our dwelling place[^2] in every generation.
תְּפִלָּה֮ לְמֹשֶׁ֢ה אִֽישׁ־הָאֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים אֲ‍ֽדֹנָ֗י מָע֣וֹן אַ֭תָּה הָיִ֥יתָ לָּ֗נוּ בְּדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃
Before the mountains were born, before you brought forth the earth and the world,[^3] from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
בְּטֶ֤רֶם ׀ הָ֘רִ֤ים יֻלָּ֗דוּ וַתְּח֣וֹלֵֽל אֶ֣רֶץ וְתֵבֵ֑ל וּֽמֵעוֹלָ֥ם עַד־ע֝וֹלָ֗ם אַתָּ֥ה אֵֽל׃
You turn human beings back to dust,[^4] and say, "Return, children of humankind."[^5]
תָּשֵׁ֣ב אֱ֭נוֹשׁ עַד־דַּכָּ֑א וַ֝תֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וּבוּ בְנֵי־אָדָֽם׃
For a thousand years in your sight are like yesterday when it has passed, like a watch in the night.[^6]
כִּ֤י אֶ֪לֶף שָׁנִ֡ים בְּֽעֵינֶ֗יךָ כְּי֣וֹם אֶ֭תְמוֹל כִּ֣י יַעֲבֹ֑ר וְאַשְׁמוּרָ֥ה בַלָּֽיְלָה׃
You sweep them away; they are like a sleep.[^7] In the morning they are like grass that springs up;
זְ֭רַמְתָּם שֵׁנָ֣ה יִהְי֑וּ בַּ֝בֹּ֗קֶר כֶּחָצִ֥יר יַחֲלֹֽף׃
in the morning it flourishes and springs up; by evening it withers and dries up.
בַּ֭בֹּקֶר יָצִ֣יץ וְחָלָ֑ף לָ֝עֶ֗רֶב יְמוֹלֵ֥ל וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃
For we are consumed by your anger, and by your wrath we are terrified.
כִּֽי־כָלִ֥ינוּ בְאַפֶּ֑ךָ וּֽבַחֲמָתְךָ֥ נִבְהָֽלְנוּ׃
You have set our iniquities before you, our secret sins in the light of your face.
*שת **שַׁתָּ֣ה עֲוֺנֹתֵ֣ינוּ לְנֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ עֲ֝לֻמֵ֗נוּ לִמְא֥וֹר פָּנֶֽיךָ׃
For all our days pass away under your fury; we finish our years like a sigh.[^8]
כִּ֣י כָל־יָ֭מֵינוּ פָּנ֣וּ בְעֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּלִּ֖ינוּ שָׁנֵ֣ינוּ כְמוֹ־הֶֽגֶה׃
The days of our years are seventy years, or eighty if we are strong;[^9] yet the best of them[^10] is toil and trouble, for they are soon gone, and we fly away.
יְמֵֽי־שְׁנוֹתֵ֨ינוּ בָהֶ֥ם שִׁבְעִ֪ים שָׁנָ֡ה וְאִ֤ם בִּגְבוּרֹ֨ת ׀ שְׁמ֘וֹנִ֤ים שָׁנָ֗ה וְ֭רָהְבָּם עָמָ֣ל וָאָ֑וֶן כִּי־גָ֥ז חִ֝֗ישׁ וַנָּעֻֽפָה׃
Who knows the power of your anger? Your wrath is as great as the fear that is due to you.[^11]
מִֽי־י֭וֹדֵעַ עֹ֣ז אַפֶּ֑ךָ וּ֝כְיִרְאָתְךָ֗ עֶבְרָתֶֽךָ׃
So teach us to count our days, so that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
לִמְנ֣וֹת יָ֭מֵינוּ כֵּ֣ן הוֹדַ֑ע וְ֝נָבִ֗א לְבַ֣ב חָכְמָֽה׃
Turn back, LORD![^12] How long? Have compassion on your servants.[^13]
שׁוּבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה עַד־מָתָ֑י וְ֝הִנָּחֵ֗ם עַל־עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃
Satisfy us in the morning with your faithful love,[^14] so that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
שַׂבְּעֵ֣נוּ בַבֹּ֣קֶר חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וּֽנְרַנְּנָ֥ה וְ֝נִשְׂמְחָ֗ה בְּכָל־יָמֵֽינוּ׃
Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
שַׂ֭מְּחֵנוּ כִּימ֣וֹת עִנִּיתָ֑נוּ שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת רָאִ֥ינוּ רָעָֽה׃
Let your work be seen by your servants, and your splendor by their children.
יֵרָאֶ֣ה אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ פָעֳלֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲדָרְךָ֗ עַל־בְּנֵיהֶֽם׃
May the favor[^15] of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.
וִיהִ֤י ׀ נֹ֤עַם אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עָ֫לֵ֥ינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָ֭דֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָ֥ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דֵ֗ינוּ כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ׃

n.1: *Of Moses*: or "for Moses". Moses is called "the man of God" also in Deuteronomy 33:1. This is the only psalm with Moses' name in its title. Psalm 90 begins Book 4 of the Psalms (Psalms 90–106). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *ma'on*, "dwelling, refuge". The Septuagint reads "refuge".
n.3: Literally "before you writhed in labor with the earth and the world", an image of giving birth. Or "before the earth and the world were brought forth".
n.4: Hebrew *dakka*, "what is crushed", that is, dust (compare Genesis 3:19).
n.5: Literally "sons of *adam*". *Return* may mean "return to dust", or "turn back" to God.
n.6: One of the three parts into which the night was divided. 2 Peter 3:8 echoes this verse.
n.7: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "You flood them away; they become sleep".
n.8: Or "a murmur", "a breath".
n.9: Literally "or if with strength, eighty years".
n.10: Literally "their pride".
n.11: Literally "and according to your fear, your wrath".
n.12: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.13: Or "Relent concerning your servants". Moses uses the same words, "turn" and "relent", when he prays for the people in Exodus 32:12.
n.14: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.15: Hebrew *no'am*, "pleasantness, kindness, beauty".

v: Whoever lives in the shelter of the Most High[^1] will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.[^2]
יֹ֭שֵׁב בְּסֵ֣תֶר עֶלְי֑וֹן בְּצֵ֥ל שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יִתְלוֹנָֽן׃
I will say to the LORD,[^3] "My refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust."
אֹמַ֗ר לַֽ֭יהוָה מַחְסִ֣י וּמְצוּדָתִ֑י אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אֶבְטַח־בּֽוֹ׃
For he will rescue you from the snare of the fowler, and from the deadly plague.[^4]
כִּ֤י ה֣וּא יַ֭צִּֽילְךָ מִפַּ֥ח יָק֗וּשׁ מִדֶּ֥בֶר הַוּֽוֹת׃
He will cover you with his feathers, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is a shield and a wall.[^5]
בְּאֶבְרָת֨וֹ ׀ יָ֣סֶךְ לָ֭ךְ וְתַֽחַת־כְּנָפָ֣יו תֶּחְסֶ֑ה צִנָּ֖ה וְֽסֹחֵרָ֣ה אֲמִתּֽוֹ׃
You will not fear the terror of the night, or the arrow that flies by day,
לֹא־תִ֭ירָא מִפַּ֣חַד לָ֑יְלָה מֵ֝חֵ֗ץ יָע֥וּף יוֹמָֽם׃
or the plague that stalks in the darkness, or the destruction that lays waste at noon.[^6]
מִ֭דֶּבֶר בָּאֹ֣פֶל יַהֲלֹ֑ךְ מִ֝קֶּ֗טֶב יָשׁ֥וּד צָהֳרָֽיִם׃
A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you.
יִפֹּ֤ל מִצִּדְּךָ֨ ׀ אֶ֗לֶף וּרְבָבָ֥ה מִימִינֶ֑ךָ אֵ֝לֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א יִגָּֽשׁ׃
You will only look with your eyes and see the punishment of the wicked.
רַ֭ק בְּעֵינֶ֣יךָ תַבִּ֑יט וְשִׁלֻּמַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים תִּרְאֶֽה׃
For you, LORD, are my refuge! You have made the Most High your dwelling place;[^7]
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה מַחְסִ֑י עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן שַׂ֣מְתָּ מְעוֹנֶֽךָ׃
no harm will befall you, and no plague will come near your tent.
לֹֽא־תְאֻנֶּ֣ה אֵלֶ֣יךָ רָעָ֑ה וְ֝נֶ֗גַע לֹא־יִקְרַ֥ב בְּאָהֳלֶֽךָ׃
For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
כִּ֣י מַ֭לְאָכָיו יְצַוֶּה־לָּ֑ךְ לִ֝שְׁמָרְךָ֗ בְּכָל־דְּרָכֶֽיךָ׃
They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.[^8]
עַל־כַּפַּ֥יִם יִשָּׂא֑וּנְךָ פֶּן־תִּגֹּ֖ף בָּאֶ֣בֶן רַגְלֶֽךָ׃
You will tread on the lion and the cobra; you will trample the young lion and the serpent.[^9]
עַל־שַׁ֣חַל וָפֶ֣תֶן תִּדְרֹ֑ךְ תִּרְמֹ֖ס כְּפִ֣יר וְתַנִּֽין׃
Because he holds fast to me in love,[^10] I will rescue him; I will set him safe on high, because he knows my name.
כִּ֤י בִ֣י חָ֭שַׁק וַאֲפַלְּטֵ֑הוּ אֲ֝שַׂגְּבֵ֗הוּ כִּֽי־יָדַ֥ע שְׁמִֽי׃
He will call on me, and I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him and honor him.
יִקְרָאֵ֨נִי ׀ וְֽאֶעֱנֵ֗הוּ עִמּֽוֹ־אָנֹכִ֥י בְצָרָ֑ה אֲ֝חַלְּצֵ֗הוּ וַֽאֲכַבְּדֵֽהוּ׃
With long life I will satisfy him, and show him my salvation.
אֹ֣רֶךְ יָ֭מִים אַשְׂבִּיעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אַרְאֵ֗הוּ בִּֽישׁוּעָתִֽי׃

n.1: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God. Also in verse 9. Psalm 91 has no title in the Hebrew. The Septuagint gives it the title "A song of praise, of David".
n.2: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "from the plague of destruction". The same consonants can be read *davar*, "word", for *dever*, "plague", as the Septuagint did: "from a troubling word".
n.5: Hebrew *socherah*, found only here, perhaps a wall around a city, or a kind of shield. *Faithfulness*: Hebrew *emet*, firmness, reliability, truth.
n.6: Hebrew *qetev*, "destruction" or "pestilence". The Septuagint reads "the demon of noonday".
n.7: Literally "For you, LORD, my refuge; the Most High you have made your dwelling." The speaker changes suddenly: the first line repeats the words of the one who trusts (verse 2), and the second speaks to him again. Or "Because you have made the LORD, my refuge, the Most High, your dwelling place".
n.8: In Matthew 4:6 and Luke 4:10–11 the devil quotes verses 11–12 to Jesus.
n.9: Hebrew *tannin*, a serpent or sea monster.
n.10: Hebrew *chashaq*, "be attached to, set one's love on". God speaks in verses 14–16.

v: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.[^1]
מִזְמ֥וֹר שִׁ֗יר לְי֣וֹם הַשַׁבָּֽת׃
It is good to give thanks to the LORD,[^2] and to sing praise to your name, Most High,[^3]
ט֗וֹב לְהֹד֥וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה וּלְזַמֵּ֖ר לְשִׁמְךָ֣ עֶלְיֽוֹן׃
to declare your faithful love[^4] in the morning, and your faithfulness by night,
לְהַגִּ֣יד בַּבֹּ֣קֶר חַסְֽדֶּ֑ךָ וֶ֝אֱמֽוּנָתְךָ֗ בַּלֵּילֽוֹת׃
on the ten-stringed instrument and on the harp, to the melody[^5] of the lyre.
עֲ‍ֽלֵי־עָ֭שׂוֹר וַעֲלֵי־נָ֑בֶל עֲלֵ֖י הִגָּי֣וֹן בְּכִנּֽוֹר׃
For you have made me glad, LORD, by what you have done; I sing for joy at the works of your hands.
כִּ֤י שִׂמַּחְתַּ֣נִי יְהוָ֣ה בְּפָעֳלֶ֑ךָ בְּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖י יָדֶ֣יךָ אֲרַנֵּֽן׃
How great are your works, LORD! How very deep are your thoughts!
מַה־גָּדְל֣וּ מַעֲשֶׂ֣יךָ יְהוָ֑ה מְ֝אֹ֗ד עָמְק֥וּ מַחְשְׁבֹתֶֽיךָ׃
The senseless man does not know, and the fool does not understand this:
אִֽישׁ־בַּ֭עַר לֹ֣א יֵדָ֑ע וּ֝כְסִ֗יל לֹא־יָבִ֥ין אֶת־זֹֽאת׃
though the wicked sprout like grass, and all evildoers flourish, they will be destroyed forever.
בִּפְרֹ֤חַ רְשָׁעִ֨ים ׀ כְּמ֥וֹ עֵ֗שֶׂב וַ֭יָּצִיצוּ כָּל־פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן לְהִשָּֽׁמְדָ֥ם עֲדֵי־עַֽד׃
But you, LORD, are on high forever.
וְאַתָּ֥ה מָר֗וֹם לְעֹלָ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
For look, your enemies, LORD, for look, your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.
כִּ֤י הִנֵּ֪ה אֹיְבֶ֡יךָ יְֽהוָ֗ה כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה אֹיְבֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ יִ֝תְפָּרְד֗וּ כָּל־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
But you have raised my horn like that of the wild ox;[^6] I am anointed with fresh oil.[^7]
וַתָּ֣רֶם כִּרְאֵ֣ים קַרְנִ֑י בַּ֝לֹּתִ֗י בְּשֶׁ֣מֶן רַעֲנָֽן׃
My eyes have looked in triumph on those who lie in wait for me; my ears have heard the downfall of the evildoers who rise against me.[^8]
וַתַּבֵּ֥ט עֵינִ֗י בְּשׁ֫וּרָ֥י בַּקָּמִ֖ים עָלַ֥י מְרֵעִ֗ים תִּשְׁמַ֥עְנָה אָזְנָֽי׃
The righteous will flourish like the palm tree, and grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon.
צַ֭דִּיק כַּתָּמָ֣ר יִפְרָ֑ח כְּאֶ֖רֶז בַּלְּבָנ֣וֹן יִשְׂגֶּֽה׃
Planted in the house of the LORD, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
שְׁ֭תוּלִים בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בְּחַצְר֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣ינוּ יַפְרִֽיחוּ׃
They will still bear fruit in old age; they will stay full of sap and green,
ע֭וֹד יְנוּב֣וּן בְּשֵׂיבָ֑ה דְּשֵׁנִ֖ים וְרַֽעֲנַנִּ֣ים יִהְיֽוּ׃
to declare that the LORD is upright; he is my rock, and there is no injustice in him.
לְ֭הַגִּיד כִּֽי־יָשָׁ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה צ֝וּרִ֗י וְֽלֹא־*עלתה **עַוְלָ֥תָה בּֽוֹ׃

n.1: This is the only psalm whose title names the Sabbath. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–16 are 92:1–15 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.4: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.5: Hebrew *higgayon*, "a murmuring sound", perhaps the resounding music of the lyre. Compare 9:17 (9:16 in most English Bibles), where it is a musical term.
n.6: A symbol of strength. Hebrew *re'em*, the wild ox.
n.7: Hebrew *balloti*, of uncertain meaning, probably "I am anointed" or "you have poured over me". The Septuagint reads "my old age with rich oil", taking the same consonants from another verb.
n.8: Literally "My eye has looked on those who watch me; of those who rise against me, evildoers, my ears hear."

v: The LORD[^1] reigns;[^2] he is clothed with majesty. The LORD is clothed; he has wrapped himself in strength. The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.[^3]
יְהוָ֣ה מָלָךְ֮ גֵּא֢וּת לָ֫בֵ֥שׁ לָבֵ֣שׁ יְ֭הוָה עֹ֣ז הִתְאַזָּ֑ר אַף־תִּכּ֥וֹן תֵּ֝בֵ֗ל בַּל־תִּמּֽוֹט׃
Your throne was established long ago; you are from everlasting.
נָכ֣וֹן כִּסְאֲךָ֣ מֵאָ֑ז מֵ֖עוֹלָ֣ם אָֽתָּה׃
The floods have lifted up, LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their pounding waves.[^4]
נָשְׂא֤וּ נְהָר֨וֹת ׀ יְֽהוָ֗ה נָשְׂא֣וּ נְהָר֣וֹת קוֹלָ֑ם יִשְׂא֖וּ נְהָר֣וֹת דָּכְיָֽם׃
Mightier than the sound of many waters, mightier than the breakers of the sea, is the LORD, mighty on high.
מִקֹּל֨וֹת ׀ מַ֤יִם רַבִּ֗ים אַדִּירִ֣ים מִשְׁבְּרֵי־יָ֑ם אַדִּ֖יר בַּמָּר֣וֹם יְהוָֽה׃
Your statutes[^5] are very trustworthy; holiness befits your house, LORD, for all time to come.[^6]
עֵֽדֹתֶ֨יךָ ׀ נֶאֶמְנ֬וּ מְאֹ֗ד לְבֵיתְךָ֥ נַאֲוָה־קֹ֑דֶשׁ יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְאֹ֣רֶךְ יָמִֽים׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 93 has no title in the Hebrew. The Septuagint gives it one: "For the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was settled. A song of praise, of David."
n.2: Or "The LORD has become king", "The LORD is king". Hebrew *YHWH malakh*. Psalms 93 and 95–99 are often called the "The LORD is king" psalms, or the enthronement psalms. They celebrate the LORD's rule as king over the whole world and its peoples (93:1; 95:3; 96:10; 97:1; 98:6; 99:1; compare 47:9; 47:8 in most English Bibles).
n.3: The same words are in 96:10 and 1 Chronicles 16:30.
n.4: Hebrew *dokhyam*, found only here, "their pounding" or "their crashing". *Floods*: Hebrew *neharot*, "rivers", here the great waters that stand for the forces of chaos which God rules (compare 89:10; 89:9 in most English Bibles).
n.5: Hebrew *edot*, traditionally "testimonies": the solemn terms of the covenant.
n.6: Literally "for length of days".

v: God of vengeance,[^1] LORD,[^2] God of vengeance, shine out!
אֵל־נְקָמ֥וֹת יְהוָ֑ה אֵ֖ל נְקָמ֣וֹת הוֹפִֽיעַ[t]׃
Rise up, Judge of the earth; pay back to the proud what they deserve.
הִ֭נָּשֵׂא שֹׁפֵ֣ט הָאָ֑רֶץ הָשֵׁ֥ב גְּ֝מ֗וּל עַל־גֵּאִֽים׃
How long will the wicked, LORD, how long will the wicked exult?
עַד־מָתַ֖י רְשָׁעִ֥ים ׀ יְהוָ֑ה עַד־מָ֝תַ֗י רְשָׁעִ֥ים יַעֲלֹֽזוּ׃
They pour out arrogant words; all the evildoers boast.
יַבִּ֣יעוּ יְדַבְּר֣וּ עָתָ֑ק יִֽ֝תְאַמְּר֗וּ כָּל־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
They crush your people, LORD, and afflict your inheritance.
עַמְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה יְדַכְּא֑וּ וְֽנַחֲלָתְךָ֥ יְעַנּֽוּ׃
They kill the widow and the foreigner, and murder the fatherless.
אַ֭לְמָנָה וְגֵ֣ר יַהֲרֹ֑גוּ וִ֖יתוֹמִ֣ים יְרַצֵּֽחוּ׃
They say, "The LORD[^3] does not see; the God of Jacob pays no attention."
וַ֭יֹּ֣אמְרוּ לֹ֣א יִרְאֶה־יָּ֑הּ וְלֹא־יָ֝בִ֗ין אֱלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃
Understand, you senseless among the people! You fools, when will you be wise?
בִּ֭ינוּ בֹּעֲרִ֣ים בָּעָ֑ם וּ֝כְסִילִ֗ים מָתַ֥י תַּשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃
He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see?
הֲנֹ֣טַֽע אֹ֭זֶן הֲלֹ֣א יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִֽם־יֹ֥צֵֽר עַ֝֗יִן הֲלֹ֣א יַבִּֽיט׃
He who disciplines the nations, does he not punish, he who teaches humankind knowledge?[^4]
הֲיֹסֵ֣ר גּ֭וֹיִם הֲלֹ֣א יוֹכִ֑יחַ הַֽמְלַמֵּ֖ד אָדָ֣ם דָּֽעַת׃
The LORD knows the thoughts of humankind, that they are only a breath.[^5]
יְֽהוָ֗ה יֹ֭דֵעַ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת אָדָ֑ם כִּי־הֵ֥מָּה הָֽבֶל׃
Happy[^6] is the one you discipline, LORD, and whom you teach from your law,
אַשְׁרֵ֤י ׀ הַגֶּ֣בֶר אֲשֶׁר־תְּיַסְּרֶ֣נּוּ יָּ֑הּ וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ תְלַמְּדֶֽנּוּ׃
to give him rest from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
לְהַשְׁקִ֣יט ל֭וֹ מִ֣ימֵי רָ֑ע עַ֤ד יִכָּרֶ֖ה לָרָשָׁ֣ע שָֽׁחַת׃
For the LORD will not abandon his people; he will not forsake his inheritance.
כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־יִטֹּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ וְ֝נַחֲלָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א יַעֲזֹֽב׃
For justice will again be righteous,[^7] and all the upright in heart will follow it.
כִּֽי־עַד־צֶ֭דֶק יָשׁ֣וּב מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְ֝אַחֲרָ֗יו כָּל־יִשְׁרֵי־לֵֽב׃
Who will rise up for me against evildoers? Who will take a stand for me against evildoers?
מִֽי־יָק֣וּם לִ֭י עִם־מְרֵעִ֑ים מִֽי־יִתְיַצֵּ֥ב לִ֝י עִם־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
If the LORD had not been my help, my soul[^8] would soon have lived in the land of silence.[^9]
לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה עֶזְרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י כִּמְעַ֓ט ׀ שָֽׁכְנָ֖ה דוּמָ֣ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃
When I said, "My foot is slipping," your faithful love,[^10] LORD, held me up.
אִם־אָ֭מַרְתִּי מָ֣טָה רַגְלִ֑י חַסְדְּךָ֥ יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִסְעָדֵֽנִי׃
When my anxious thoughts multiply within me, your comforts delight my soul.
בְּרֹ֣ב שַׂרְעַפַּ֣י בְּקִרְבִּ֑י תַּ֝נְחוּמֶ֗יךָ יְֽשַׁעַשְׁע֥וּ נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Can a throne of destruction be allied with you, one that frames trouble by decree?[^11]
הַֽ֭יְחָבְרְךָ כִּסֵּ֣א הַוּ֑וֹת יֹצֵ֖ר עָמָ֣ל עֲלֵי־חֹֽק׃
They band together against the life of the righteous, and condemn the innocent to death.[^12]
יָ֭גוֹדּוּ עַל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ צַדִּ֑יק וְדָ֖ם נָקִ֣י יַרְשִֽׁיעוּ׃
But the LORD has become my stronghold, and my God the rock of my refuge.
וַיְהִ֬י יְהוָ֣ה לִ֣י לְמִשְׂגָּ֑ב וֵ֝אלֹהַ֗י לְצ֣וּר מַחְסִֽי׃
He will turn their own iniquity back on them, and destroy them for their wickedness; the LORD our God will destroy them.
וַיָּ֤שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֨ם ׀ אֶת־אוֹנָ֗ם וּבְרָעָתָ֥ם יַצְמִיתֵ֑ם יַ֝צְמִיתֵ֗ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

n.1: Literally "God of vengeances", the God who punishes wrong and sets it right. Psalm 94 has no title in the Hebrew. The Septuagint gives it one: "A psalm of David, for the fourth day of the week."
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH. Also in verse 12.
n.4: The Hebrew breaks off, leaving the question unfinished: literally "he who teaches humankind knowledge".
n.5: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", something without substance (compare Ecclesiastes 1:2). 1 Corinthians 3:20 quotes this verse, with "the wise" in place of "humankind".
n.6: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.7: Literally "For judgment will return to righteousness".
n.8: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 19 and 21.
n.9: Hebrew *dumah*, "silence", a name for the realm of the dead (compare 115:17).
n.10: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.11: Or "by law". Hebrew *choq*, "decree". *A throne of destruction*: unjust rulers.
n.12: Literally "and condemn innocent blood".

v: Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD;[^1] let us shout aloud to the rock of our salvation.
לְ֭כוּ נְרַנְּנָ֣ה לַיהוָ֑ה נָ֝רִ֗יעָה לְצ֣וּר יִשְׁעֵֽנוּ׃
Let us come before him with thanksgiving; let us shout aloud to him with songs of praise.
נְקַדְּמָ֣ה פָנָ֣יו בְּתוֹדָ֑ה בִּ֝זְמִר֗וֹת נָרִ֥יעַֽ לֽוֹ׃
For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.[^2]
כִּ֤י אֵ֣ל גָּד֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה וּמֶ֥לֶךְ גָּ֝ד֗וֹל עַל־כָּל־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
In his hand are the depths of the earth, and the peaks[^3] of the mountains are his.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ֭יָדוֹ מֶחְקְרֵי־אָ֑רֶץ וְתוֹעֲפ֖וֹת הָרִ֣ים לֽוֹ׃
The sea is his, for he made it, and his hands formed the dry land.
אֲשֶׁר־ל֣וֹ הַ֭יָּם וְה֣וּא עָשָׂ֑הוּ וְ֝יַבֶּ֗שֶׁת יָדָ֥יו יָצָֽרוּ׃
Come, let us bow down and worship; let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.
בֹּ֭אוּ נִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֣ה וְנִכְרָ֑עָה נִ֝בְרְכָ֗ה לִֽפְנֵי־יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֵֽׂנוּ׃
For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, the sheep of his hand. Today, if only you would listen to his voice:[^4]
כִּ֘י ה֤וּא אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וַאֲנַ֤חְנוּ עַ֣ם מַ֭רְעִיתוֹ וְצֹ֣אן יָד֑וֹ הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אִֽם־בְּקֹל֥וֹ תִשְׁמָֽעוּ׃
"Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,[^5]
אַל־תַּקְשׁ֣וּ לְ֭בַבְכֶם כִּמְרִיבָ֑ה כְּי֥וֹם מַ֝סָּ֗ה בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
when your ancestors tested me; they put me to the test, though they had seen what I had done.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִ֭סּוּנִי אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם בְּ֝חָנ֗וּנִי גַּם־רָא֥וּ פָעֳלֽ͏ִי׃
For forty years I loathed that generation, and I said, 'They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they do not know my ways.'
אַרְבָּ֘עִ֤ים שָׁנָ֨ה ׀ אָ֘ק֤וּט בְּד֗וֹר וָאֹמַ֗ר עַ֤ם תֹּעֵ֣י לֵבָ֣ב הֵ֑ם וְ֝הֵ֗ם לֹא־יָדְע֥וּ דְרָכָֽי׃
So I swore in my anger, 'They shall never enter my rest.'"[^6]
אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי בְאַפִּ֑י אִם־יְ֝בֹא֗וּן אֶל־מְנוּחָתִֽי׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 95 has no title in the Hebrew. The Septuagint gives it the title "A song of praise, of David", and Hebrews 4:7 speaks of these words as spoken "through David".
n.2: Psalm 95 is one of the "The LORD is king" psalms (see the note on 93:1).
n.3: Hebrew *to'afot*, a rare word, perhaps "heights" or "summits".
n.4: Hebrews 3:7–11 quotes verses 7–11 from the Septuagint, and returns to them in 3:15 and 4:3–7. From verse 8 on, God speaks.
n.5: *Meribah* means "quarreling" and *Massah* "testing". The events are told in Exodus 17:1–7 and Numbers 20:1–13. The Septuagint, quoted in Hebrews 3:8, translates the names: "as in the rebellion, as on the day of testing in the wilderness".
n.6: Literally "If they enter my rest", the form of an oath meaning "they will certainly not enter". *My rest*: the land God promised to give his people (compare Numbers 14:21–23; Deuteronomy 12:9).

v: Sing to the LORD[^1] a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.[^2]
שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ שִׁ֥ירוּ לַ֝יהוָ֗ה כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Sing to the LORD, bless his name; proclaim his salvation day after day.
שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה בָּרֲכ֣וּ שְׁמ֑וֹ בַּשְּׂר֥וּ מִיּֽוֹם־לְ֝י֗וֹם יְשׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃
Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all the peoples.
סַפְּר֣וּ בַגּוֹיִ֣ם כְּבוֹד֑וֹ בְּכָל־הָֽ֝עַמִּ֗ים נִפְלְאוֹתָֽיו׃
For the LORD is great and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
כִּ֥י גָ֘ד֤וֹל יְהוָ֣ה וּמְהֻלָּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד נוֹרָ֥א ה֝֗וּא עַל־כָּל־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
For all the gods of the peoples are idols,[^3] but the LORD made the heavens.
כִּ֤י ׀ כָּל־אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָעַמִּ֣ים אֱלִילִ֑ים וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם עָשָֽׂה׃
Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.[^4]
הוֹד־וְהָדָ֥ר לְפָנָ֑יו עֹ֥ז וְ֝תִפְאֶ֗רֶת בְּמִקְדָּשֽׁוֹ׃
Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת עַמִּ֑ים הָב֥וּ לַ֝יהוָ֗ה כָּב֥וֹד וָעֹֽז׃
Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name;[^5] bring an offering and come into his courts.[^6]
הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה כְּב֣וֹד שְׁמ֑וֹ שְׂאֽוּ־מִ֝נְחָ֗ה וּבֹ֥אוּ לְחַצְרוֹתָֽיו׃
Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness;[^7] tremble before him, all the earth.
הִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה בְּהַדְרַת־קֹ֑דֶשׁ חִ֥ילוּ מִ֝פָּנָ֗יו כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Say among the nations, "The LORD reigns![^8] The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved. He will judge the peoples with fairness."
אִמְר֤וּ בַגּוֹיִ֨ם ׀ יְה֘וָ֤ה מָלָ֗ךְ אַף־תִּכּ֣וֹן תֵּ֭בֵל בַּל־תִּמּ֑וֹט יָדִ֥ין עַ֝מִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
יִשְׂמְח֣וּ הַ֭שָּׁמַיִם וְתָגֵ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ יִֽרְעַ֥ם הַ֝יָּ֗ם וּמְלֹאֽוֹ׃
let the fields exult, and everything in them. Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy
יַעֲלֹ֣ז שָׂ֭דַי וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־בּ֑וֹ אָ֥ז יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ כָּל־עֲצֵי־יָֽעַר׃
before the LORD, for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with his faithfulness.[^9]
לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָ֨ה ׀ כִּ֬י בָ֗א כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֢ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ יִשְׁפֹּֽט־תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בֶּאֱמוּנָתֽוֹ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 96 has no title in the Hebrew. The Septuagint gives it one: "When the house was being built after the captivity. A song of David."
n.2: Most of this psalm appears also in 1 Chronicles 16:23–33, in the song of thanksgiving sung when David brought the ark to Jerusalem, with some differences in wording and order. The notes give the main differences. For *a new song*, compare 33:3 and 98:1. 1 Chronicles 16:23 has only "Sing to the LORD, all the earth", and then the second half of verse 2.
n.3: Hebrew *elilim*, "worthless things", which sounds like *elohim*, "gods".
n.4: 1 Chronicles 16:27 has "strength and joy are in his place".
n.5: Literally "the glory of his name". Verses 7–9 are close to 29:1–2.
n.6: 1 Chronicles 16:29 has "come before him".
n.7: Or "in holy attire".
n.8: Or "The LORD has become king!" (see the note on 93:1). In 1 Chronicles 16:31 these words come after the first half of verse 11, and the rest of this verse is not there, except for the line "The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved" (1 Chronicles 16:30).
n.9: Hebrew *emunah*: firmness, reliability, faithfulness. 1 Chronicles 16:33 ends at "for he comes to judge the earth". Verse 13 is almost the same as 98:9.

v: The LORD[^1] reigns![^2] Let the earth rejoice; let the many coastlands[^3] be glad.
יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ תָּגֵ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ יִ֝שְׂמְח֗וּ אִיִּ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃
Clouds and thick darkness surround him;[^4] righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
עָנָ֣ן וַעֲרָפֶ֣ל סְבִיבָ֑יו צֶ֥דֶק וּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט מְכ֣וֹן כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
Fire goes before him and burns up his adversaries all around.
אֵ֭שׁ לְפָנָ֣יו תֵּלֵ֑ךְ וּתְלַהֵ֖ט סָבִ֣יב צָרָֽיו׃
His lightnings light up the world; the earth sees and trembles.
הֵאִ֣ירוּ בְרָקָ֣יו תֵּבֵ֑ל רָאֲתָ֖ה וַתָּחֵ֣ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
הָרִ֗ים כַּדּוֹנַ֗ג נָ֭מַסּוּ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה מִ֝לִּפְנֵ֗י אֲד֣וֹן כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
The heavens proclaim his righteousness, and all the peoples see his glory.
הִגִּ֣ידוּ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם צִדְק֑וֹ וְרָא֖וּ כָל־הָעַמִּ֣ים כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃
All who serve carved images are put to shame, those who boast in idols.[^5] Bow down to him, all you gods![^6]
יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ ׀ כָּל־עֹ֬בְדֵי פֶ֗סֶל הַמִּֽתְהַלְלִ֥ים בָּאֱלִילִ֑ים הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ל֝וֹ כָּל־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Zion hears and rejoices, and the daughters of Judah[^7] exult because of your judgments, LORD.
שָׁמְעָ֬ה וַתִּשְׂמַ֨ח ׀ צִיּ֗וֹן וַ֭תָּגֵלְנָה בְּנ֣וֹת יְהוּדָ֑ה לְמַ֖עַן מִשְׁפָּטֶ֣יךָ יְהוָֽה׃
For you, LORD, are the Most High[^8] over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods.
כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָ֗ה עֶלְי֥וֹן עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ מְאֹ֥ד נַ֝עֲלֵ֗יתָ עַל־כָּל־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
You who love the LORD, hate evil! He guards the lives[^9] of his faithful ones;[^10] he rescues them from the hand of the wicked.
אֹהֲבֵ֥י יְהוָ֗ה שִׂנְא֫וּ רָ֥ע שֹׁ֭מֵר נַפְשׁ֣וֹת חֲסִידָ֑יו מִיַּ֥ד רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יַצִּילֵֽם׃
Light is sown[^11] for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.
א֖וֹר זָרֻ֣עַ לַצַּדִּ֑יק וּֽלְיִשְׁרֵי־לֵ֥ב שִׂמְחָֽה׃
Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous, and give thanks to his holy name.[^12]
שִׂמְח֣וּ צַ֭דִּיקִים בַּֽיהוָ֑ה וְ֝הוֹד֗וּ לְזֵ֣כֶר קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 97 has no title in the Hebrew.
n.2: Or "The LORD has become king!" (see the note on 93:1).
n.3: Or "islands", the distant lands across the sea.
n.4: Compare God's coming at Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:16–18; Deuteronomy 4:11).
n.5: Hebrew *elilim*, "worthless things", which sounds like *elohim*, "gods".
n.6: Hebrew *elohim*. The Septuagint reads "all his angels". Hebrews 1:6 quotes similar words, "Let all God's angels worship him", from the Septuagint of Deuteronomy 32:43 or of this verse.
n.7: That is, the towns of Judah. Compare 48:12 (48:11 in most English Bibles).
n.8: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.9: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Here it is plural.
n.10: Hebrew *chasidim*, "faithful ones", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.11: The Septuagint reads "Light has dawned", from a word that differs by one letter (*zarach* for *zarua*).
n.12: Literally "to the remembrance of his holiness".

v: A psalm.[^1] Sing to the LORD[^2] a new song, for he has done wonders; his right hand and his holy arm have won him victory.[^3]
מִזְמ֡וֹר שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה ׀ שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ כִּֽי־נִפְלָא֣וֹת עָשָׂ֑ה הוֹשִֽׁיעָה־לּ֥וֹ יְ֝מִינ֗וֹ וּזְר֥וֹעַ קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
The LORD has made his salvation known; in the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness.[^4]
הוֹדִ֣יעַ יְ֭הוָה יְשׁוּעָת֑וֹ לְעֵינֵ֥י הַ֝גּוֹיִ֗ם גִּלָּ֥ה צִדְקָתֽוֹ׃
He has remembered his faithful love[^5] and his faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
זָ֘כַ֤ר חַסְדּ֨וֹ ׀ וֶֽאֱֽמוּנָתוֹ֮ לְבֵ֢ית יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל רָא֥וּ כָל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ אֵ֝֗ת יְשׁוּעַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
Shout aloud to the LORD, all the earth; break out in songs of joy and sing praises.
הָרִ֣יעוּ לַֽ֭יהוָה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ פִּצְח֖וּ וְרַנְּנ֣וּ וְזַמֵּֽרוּ׃
Sing praises to the LORD with the lyre, with the lyre and the sound of song.
זַמְּר֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה בְּכִנּ֑וֹר בְּ֝כִנּ֗וֹר וְק֣וֹל זִמְרָֽה׃
With trumpets and the sound of the ram's horn,[^6] shout aloud before the King, the LORD.[^7]
בַּ֭חֲצֹ֣צְרוֹת וְק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָ֑ר הָ֝רִ֗יעוּ לִפְנֵ֤י ׀ הַמֶּ֬לֶךְ יְהוָֽה׃
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it, the world and those who live in it.
יִרְעַ֣ם הַ֭יָּם וּמְלֹא֑וֹ תֵּ֝בֵ֗ל וְיֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃
Let the rivers clap their hands; let the mountains sing for joy together
נְהָר֥וֹת יִמְחֲאוּ־כָ֑ף יַ֝֗חַד הָרִ֥ים יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃
before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with fairness.[^8]
לִֽפְֽנֵי־יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֢ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ יִשְׁפֹּֽט־תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃

n.1: In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "have saved for him".
n.4: Or "his vindication", his justice that sets things right.
n.5: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.6: Hebrew *shofar*. The trumpets (*chatsotserot*) were made of hammered silver (Numbers 10:2).
n.7: Psalm 98 is one of the "The LORD is king" psalms (see the note on 93:1).
n.8: Verse 9 is almost the same as 96:13.

v: The LORD[^1] reigns![^2] Let the peoples tremble! He is enthroned on the cherubim;[^3] let the earth quake!
יְהוָ֣ה מָ֭לָךְ יִרְגְּז֣וּ עַמִּ֑ים יֹשֵׁ֥ב כְּ֝רוּבִ֗ים תָּנ֥וּט הָאָֽרֶץ׃
The LORD is great in Zion; he is exalted above all the peoples.
יְ֭הוָה בְּצִיּ֣וֹן גָּד֑וֹל וְרָ֥ם ה֝֗וּא עַל־כָּל־הָֽעַמִּֽים׃
Let them praise your great and awesome name. Holy is he![^4]
יוֹד֣וּ שִׁ֭מְךָ גָּד֥וֹל וְנוֹרָ֗א קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא׃
The King in his might loves justice.[^5] You have established fairness; you have done justice and righteousness in Jacob.
וְעֹ֥ז מֶלֶךְ֮ מִשְׁפָּ֢ט אָ֫הֵ֥ב אַ֭תָּה כּוֹנַ֣נְתָּ מֵישָׁרִ֑ים מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה בְּיַעֲקֹ֤ב ׀ אַתָּ֬ה עָשִֽׂיתָ׃
Exalt the LORD our God, and bow down at his footstool.[^6] Holy is he!
רֽוֹמְמ֡וּ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְֽ֭הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַהֲדֹ֥ם רַגְלָ֗יו קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא׃
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel among those who called on his name.[^7] They called to the LORD, and he answered them.
מֹ֘שֶׁ֤ה וְאַהֲרֹ֨ן ׀ בְּֽכֹהֲנָ֗יו וּ֖[d]שְׁמוּאֵל בְּקֹרְאֵ֣י שְׁמ֑וֹ קֹרִ֥אים אֶל־יְ֝הוָ֗ה וְה֣וּא יַעֲנֵֽם׃
He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud;[^8] they kept his statutes[^9] and the decree he gave them.
בְּעַמּ֣וּד עָ֭נָן יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם שָׁמְר֥וּ עֵ֝דֹתָ֗יו וְחֹ֣ק נָֽתַן־לָֽמוֹ׃
LORD our God, you answered them; you were a God who forgave them, yet you punished their misdeeds.[^10]
יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵינוּ֮ אַתָּ֢ה עֲנִ֫יתָ֥ם אֵ֣ל נֹ֭שֵׂא הָיִ֣יתָ לָהֶ֑ם וְ֝נֹקֵ֗ם עַל־עֲלִילוֹתָֽם׃
Exalt the LORD our God, and bow down at his holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.
רֽוֹמְמ֡וּ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְ֭הִֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַ֣ר קָדְשׁ֑וֹ כִּֽי־קָ֝ד֗וֹשׁ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 99 has no title in the Hebrew.
n.2: Or "The LORD has become king!" (see the note on 93:1). Psalm 99 is the last of the "The LORD is king" psalms.
n.3: Or "above the cherubim". Hebrew *keruvim*: winged heavenly beings. Two gold cherubim stood on the cover of the ark (Exodus 25:18–22).
n.4: This refrain comes again in verse 5, and in a longer form at the end of verse 9 (compare Isaiah 6:3).
n.5: Literally "And the strength of a king loves justice." Or "Mighty King, who loves justice, you have established fairness".
n.6: The ark, or the temple where it stood (compare 132:7; 1 Chronicles 28:2).
n.7: Aaron was the first high priest. Moses also served as a priest when the priesthood was set up (Exodus 24:4–8; Leviticus 8), and Samuel offered sacrifices (1 Samuel 7:9). All three were known for interceding for the people (Exodus 32:11–14; Numbers 17:11–13; 16:46–48 in most English Bibles; 1 Samuel 7:5–9; compare Jeremiah 15:1).
n.8: Compare Exodus 33:9 and Numbers 12:5.
n.9: Hebrew *edot*, traditionally "testimonies": the solemn terms of the covenant.
n.10: Or "and you avenged the wrongs done to them". *A God who forgave*: literally "a God who lifts", the word used for forgiving in Exodus 34:7.

v: A psalm for thanksgiving.[^1] Shout aloud to the LORD,[^2] all the earth!
מִזְמ֥וֹר לְתוֹדָ֑ה הָרִ֥יעוּ לַ֝יהוָ֗ה כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Serve the LORD with gladness; come before him with songs of joy.
עִבְד֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּשִׂמְחָ֑ה בֹּ֥אוּ לְ֝פָנָ֗יו בִּרְנָנָֽה׃
Know that the LORD is God. It is he who made us, and we are his;[^3] we are his people, the sheep of his pasture.
דְּע֗וּ כִּֽי־יְהוָה֮ ה֤וּא אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים הֽוּא־עָ֭שָׂנוּ *ולא **וְל֣וֹ אֲנַ֑חְנוּ עַ֝מּ֗וֹ וְצֹ֣אן מַרְעִיתֽוֹ׃
Enter his gates with thanksgiving, and his courts with praise; give thanks to him, bless his name.
בֹּ֤אוּ שְׁעָרָ֨יו ׀ בְּתוֹדָ֗ה חֲצֵרֹתָ֥יו בִּתְהִלָּ֑ה הֽוֹדוּ־ל֝֗וֹ בָּרֲכ֥וּ שְׁמֽוֹ׃
For the LORD is good; his faithful love[^4] endures forever, and his faithfulness to all generations.
כִּי־ט֣וֹב יְ֭הֹוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְעַד־דֹּ֥ר וָ֝דֹ֗ר אֱמוּנָֽתוֹ׃

n.1: Or "for the thank offering". Hebrew *todah*, "thanksgiving", also a sacrifice given in thanksgiving (Leviticus 7:12; compare 50:14). Also in verse 4. In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: The Hebrew text is written "and not we ourselves" but read "and we are his". The two words sound the same.
n.4: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. *His faithful love endures forever* is a refrain of praise found often in the Psalms and elsewhere (106:1; 107:1; 118:1; 136; 1 Chronicles 16:34).

v: Of David. A psalm.[^1] I will sing of faithful love[^2] and justice; to you, LORD,[^3] I will sing praise.
לְדָוִ֗ד מִ֫זְמ֥וֹר חֶֽסֶד־וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט אָשִׁ֑ירָה לְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֲזַמֵּֽרָה׃
I will pay attention to the blameless way.[^4] When will you come to me? I will walk with integrity of heart within my house.
אַשְׂכִּ֤ילָה ׀ בְּדֶ֬רֶךְ תָּמִ֗ים מָ֭תַי תָּב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑י אֶתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בְּתָם־לְ֝בָבִ֗י בְּקֶ֣רֶב בֵּיתִֽי׃
I will not set anything worthless[^5] before my eyes. I hate the deeds of those who turn aside;[^6] they will not cling to me.
לֹֽא־אָשִׁ֨ית ׀ לְנֶ֥גֶד עֵינַ֗י דְּֽבַר־בְּלִ֫יָּ֥עַל עֲשֹֽׂה־סֵטִ֥ים שָׂנֵ֑אתִי לֹ֖א יִדְבַּ֣ק בִּֽי׃
A crooked heart will be far from me; I will have nothing to do with evil.[^7]
לֵבָ֣ב עִ֭קֵּשׁ יָס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נִּי רָ֝֗ע לֹ֣א אֵדָֽע׃
Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will silence;[^8] whoever has haughty eyes and a proud heart, him I will not tolerate.
*מלושני **מְלָשְׁנִ֬י בַסֵּ֨תֶר ׀ רֵעֵהוּ֮ אוֹת֢וֹ אַ֫צְמִ֥ית גְּֽבַהּ־עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַ֣ב לֵבָ֑ב אֹ֝ת֗וֹ לֹ֣א אוּכָֽל׃
My eyes will be on the faithful in the land, so that they may live with me; whoever walks in the blameless way will serve me.
עֵינַ֤י ׀ בְּנֶֽאֶמְנֵי־אֶרֶץ֮ לָשֶׁ֢בֶת עִמָּ֫דִ֥י הֹ֭לֵךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ תָּמִ֑ים ה֝֗וּא יְשָׁרְתֵֽנִי׃
No one who practices deceit will live in my house; no one who tells lies will stand firm in my sight.
לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֨ב ׀ בְּקֶ֥רֶב בֵּיתִי֮ עֹשֵׂ֢ה רְמִ֫יָּ֥ה דֹּבֵ֥ר שְׁקָרִ֑ים לֹֽא־יִ֝כּ֗וֹן לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינָֽי׃
Morning by morning[^9] I will silence all the wicked in the land, cutting off all evildoers from the city of the LORD.
לַבְּקָרִ֗ים אַצְמִ֥ית כָּל־רִשְׁעֵי־אָ֑רֶץ לְהַכְרִ֥ית מֵֽעִיר־יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. The speaker is a king, who promises to rule justly.
n.2: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Or "I will act wisely in the blameless way".
n.5: Literally "a thing of *beliyya'al*", "worthlessness".
n.6: Hebrew *setim*, a rare word, "those who swerve", or "faithlessness".
n.7: Literally "evil I will not know".
n.8: Or "destroy". Also in verse 8.
n.9: The king heard cases and gave judgment in the morning (compare 2 Samuel 15:2; Jeremiah 21:12).

v: A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his complaint before the LORD.[^1]
תְּ֭פִלָּה לְעָנִ֣י כִֽי־יַעֲטֹ֑ף וְלִפְנֵ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ שִׂיחֽוֹ׃
LORD, hear my prayer; let my cry for help come to you.
יְ֭הוָה שִׁמְעָ֣ה תְפִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝שַׁוְעָתִ֗י אֵלֶ֥יךָ תָבֽוֹא׃
Do not hide your face from me in the day of my distress; turn your ear to me; in the day I call, answer me quickly.
אַל־תַּסְתֵּ֬ר פָּנֶ֨יךָ ׀ מִמֶּנִּי֮ בְּי֢וֹם צַ֫ר לִ֥י הַטֵּֽה־אֵלַ֥י אָזְנֶ֑ךָ בְּי֥וֹם אֶ֝קְרָ֗א מַהֵ֥ר עֲנֵֽנִי׃
For my days vanish like smoke, and my bones burn like a hearth.
כִּֽי־כָל֣וּ בְעָשָׁ֣ן יָמָ֑י וְ֝עַצְמוֹתַ֗י כְּמוֹ־קֵ֥ד נִחָֽרוּ׃
My heart is struck down like grass and has withered; I even forget to eat my bread.
הוּכָּֽה־כָ֭עֵשֶׂב וַיִּבַ֣שׁ לִבִּ֑י כִּֽי־שָׁ֝כַ֗חְתִּי מֵאֲכֹ֥ל לַחְמִֽי׃
Because of my loud groaning, my bones cling to my flesh.[^2]
מִקּ֥וֹל אַנְחָתִ֑י דָּבְקָ֥ה עַ֝צְמִ֗י לִבְשָׂרִֽי׃
I am like a pelican in the wilderness;[^3] I have become like a little owl among the ruins.
דָּ֭מִיתִי לִקְאַ֣ת מִדְבָּ֑ר הָ֝יִ֗יתִי כְּכ֣וֹס חֳרָבֽוֹת׃
I lie awake; I have become like a lonely bird on a roof.
שָׁקַ֥דְתִּי וָאֶֽהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝צִפּ֗וֹר בּוֹדֵ֥ד עַל־גָּֽג׃
All day long my enemies taunt me; those who mock me use my name as a curse.[^4]
כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם חֵרְפ֣וּנִי אוֹיְבָ֑י מְ֝הוֹלָלַ֗י בִּ֣י נִשְׁבָּֽעוּ׃
For I eat ashes like bread, and mix my drink with tears,
כִּי־אֵ֭פֶר כַּלֶּ֣חֶם אָכָ֑לְתִּי וְ֝שִׁקֻּוַ֗י בִּבְכִ֥י מָסָֽכְתִּי׃
because of your indignation and your anger, for you have lifted me up and thrown me away.
מִפְּנֵֽי־זַֽעַמְךָ֥ וְקִצְפֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י נְ֝שָׂאתַ֗נִי וַתַּשְׁלִיכֵֽנִי׃
My days are like a lengthening shadow;[^5] I wither away like grass.
יָ֭מַי כְּצֵ֣ל נָט֑וּי וַ֝אֲנִ֗י כָּעֵ֥שֶׂב אִיבָֽשׁ׃
But you, LORD, sit enthroned forever, and your name endures[^6] through all generations.
וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֑ב וְ֝זִכְרְךָ֗ לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃
You will rise up and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to be gracious to her; the appointed time has come.
אַתָּ֣ה תָ֭קוּם תְּרַחֵ֣ם צִיּ֑וֹן כִּי־עֵ֥ת לְ֝חֶֽנְנָ֗הּ כִּי־בָ֥א מוֹעֵֽד׃
For your servants hold her stones dear, and have pity on her dust.
כִּֽי־רָצ֣וּ עֲ֭בָדֶיךָ אֶת־אֲבָנֶ֑יהָ וְֽאֶת־עֲפָרָ֥הּ יְחֹנֵֽנוּ׃
The nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth your glory.
וְיִֽירְא֣וּ ג֭וֹיִם אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ אֶת־כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
For the LORD will build up Zion; he will appear in his glory.[^7]
כִּֽי־בָנָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה צִיּ֑וֹן נִ֝רְאָ֗ה בִּכְבוֹדֽוֹ׃
He will turn to the prayer of the destitute,[^8] and will not despise their prayer.
פָּ֭נָה אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֣ת הָעַרְעָ֑ר וְלֹֽא־בָ֝זָ֗ה אֶת־תְּפִלָּתָֽם׃
Let this be written down for a generation to come, so that a people yet to be created may praise the LORD:[^9]
תִּכָּ֣תֶב זֹ֭את לְד֣וֹר אַחֲר֑וֹן וְעַ֥ם נִ֝בְרָ֗א יְהַלֶּל־יָֽהּ׃
that he looked down from his holy height; from heaven the LORD gazed on the earth,
כִּֽי־הִ֭שְׁקִיף מִמְּר֣וֹם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ יְ֝הוָ֗ה מִשָּׁמַ֤יִם ׀ אֶל־אֶ֬רֶץ הִבִּֽיט׃
to hear the groaning of the prisoner, to set free those condemned to die,[^10]
לִ֭שְׁמֹעַ אֶנְקַ֣ת אָסִ֑יר לְ֝פַתֵּ֗חַ בְּנֵ֣י תְמוּתָֽה׃
so that the name of the LORD may be declared in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem,
לְסַפֵּ֣ר בְּ֭צִיּוֹן שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וּ֝תְהִלָּת֗וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
when the peoples gather together, and the kingdoms, to serve the LORD.
בְּהִקָּבֵ֣ץ עַמִּ֣ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וּ֝מַמְלָכ֗וֹת לַעֲבֹ֥ד אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
He has broken my strength[^11] on the way; he has cut short my days.
עִנָּ֖ה בַדֶּ֥רֶךְ *כחו **כֹּחִ֗י קִצַּ֥ר יָמָֽי׃
I say, "My God, do not take me away in the middle of my days, you whose years go on through all generations.
אֹמַ֗ר אֵלִ֗י אַֽל־תַּ֭עֲלֵנִי בַּחֲצִ֣י יָמָ֑י בְּד֖וֹר דּוֹרִ֣ים שְׁנוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
Long ago you laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.[^12]
לְ֭פָנִים הָאָ֣רֶץ יָסַ֑דְתָּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ שָׁמָֽיִם׃
They will perish, but you will remain; they will all wear out like a garment. You will change them like clothing, and they will pass away.
הֵ֤מָּה ׀ יֹאבֵדוּ֮ וְאַתָּ֢ה תַ֫עֲמֹ֥ד וְ֭כֻלָּם כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֑וּ כַּלְּב֖וּשׁ תַּחֲלִיפֵ֣ם וְֽיַחֲלֹֽפוּ׃
But you are the same,[^13] and your years will have no end.
וְאַתָּה־ה֑וּא וּ֝שְׁנוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א יִתָּֽמּוּ׃
The children of your servants will live secure, and their offspring will be established before you."
בְּנֵֽי־עֲבָדֶ֥יךָ יִשְׁכּ֑וֹנוּ וְ֝זַרְעָ֗ם לְפָנֶ֥יךָ יִכּֽוֹן׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. This is the only psalm title that describes the one who prays, rather than naming a person. *Complaint*: or "lament". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–29 are 102:1–28 in most English Bibles.
n.2: That is, I am nothing but skin and bones.
n.3: Hebrew *qa'at*, an unclean bird (Leviticus 11:18), perhaps a pelican or a kind of owl. *Little owl*: Hebrew *kos* (Leviticus 11:17).
n.4: Literally "swear by me", using my fate in their curses (compare Jeremiah 29:22).
n.5: Literally "a shadow stretched out", as shadows grow long when the day is ending.
n.6: Literally "your remembrance", the name by which you are remembered and called on.
n.7: The verbs in verses 17–18 are in the past tense in Hebrew, speaking of what God will do as though it were already done.
n.8: Hebrew *ar'ar*, "stripped, bare", perhaps also a shrub of the desert (compare Jeremiah 17:6).
n.9: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH.
n.10: Literally "the sons of death". Compare 79:11.
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "his strength" but read "my strength". The Septuagint reads the same consonants differently: "He answered him in the way of his strength: Tell me the shortness of my days."
n.12: Hebrews 1:10–12 quotes verses 26–28 from the Septuagint, which begins "You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth", and applies them to the Son.
n.13: Literally "you are he" (compare Isaiah 41:4; 43:10).

v: Of David.[^1] Bless the LORD,[^2] my soul,[^3] and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
לְדָוִ֨ד ׀ בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְכָל־קְ֝רָבַ֗י אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
Bless the LORD, my soul, and do not forget all his benefits:
בָּרְכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְאַל־תִּ֝שְׁכְּחִ֗י כָּל־גְּמוּלָֽיו׃
he forgives all your iniquity; he heals all your diseases;
הַסֹּלֵ֥חַ לְכָל־עֲוֺנֵ֑כִי הָ֝רֹפֵ֗א לְכָל־תַּחֲלֻאָֽיְכִי׃
he redeems your life from the pit; he crowns you with faithful love[^4] and compassion;
הַגּוֹאֵ֣ל מִשַּׁ֣חַת חַיָּ֑יְכִי הַֽ֝מְעַטְּרֵ֗כִי חֶ֣סֶד וְרַחֲמִֽים׃
he satisfies you with good things as long as you live,[^5] so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's.[^6]
הַמַּשְׂבִּ֣יעַ בַּטּ֣וֹב עֶדְיֵ֑ךְ תִּתְחַדֵּ֖שׁ כַּנֶּ֣שֶׁר נְעוּרָֽיְכִי׃
The LORD does what is right,[^7] and brings justice for all who are oppressed.
עֹשֵׂ֣ה צְדָק֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וּ֝מִשְׁפָּטִ֗ים לְכָל־עֲשׁוּקִֽים׃
He made known his ways to Moses, his deeds to the people of Israel.[^8]
יוֹדִ֣יעַ דְּרָכָ֣יו לְמֹשֶׁ֑ה לִבְנֵ֥י יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל עֲלִילֽוֹתָיו׃
The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in faithful love.[^9]
רַח֣וּם וְחַנּ֣וּן יְהוָ֑ה אֶ֖רֶךְ אַפַּ֣יִם וְרַב־חָֽסֶד׃
He will not always accuse, nor will he keep his anger forever.
לֹֽא־לָנֶ֥צַח יָרִ֑יב וְלֹ֖א לְעוֹלָ֣ם יִטּֽוֹר׃
He has not dealt with us according to our sins, or repaid us according to our iniquities.
לֹ֣א כַ֭חֲטָאֵינוּ עָ֣שָׂה לָ֑נוּ וְלֹ֥א כַ֝עֲוֺנֹתֵ֗ינוּ גָּמַ֥ל עָלֵֽינוּ׃
For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his faithful love toward those who fear him.
כִּ֤י כִגְבֹ֣הַּ שָׁ֭מַיִם עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ גָּבַ֥ר חַ֝סְדּ֗וֹ עַל־יְרֵאָֽיו׃
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.
כִּרְחֹ֣ק מִ֭זְרָח מִֽמַּֽעֲרָ֑ב הִֽרְחִ֥יק מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ אֶת־פְּשָׁעֵֽינוּ׃
As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him.
כְּרַחֵ֣ם אָ֭ב עַל־בָּנִ֑ים רִחַ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה עַל־יְרֵאָֽיו׃
For he knows how we are formed;[^10] he remembers that we are dust.
כִּי־ה֭וּא יָדַ֣ע יִצְרֵ֑נוּ זָ֝כ֗וּר כִּי־עָפָ֥ר אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃
As for human beings, their days are like grass; they flourish like a flower of the field;
אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כֶּחָצִ֣יר יָמָ֑יו כְּצִ֥יץ הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה כֵּ֣ן יָצִֽיץ׃
when the wind passes over it, it is gone, and its place knows it no more.
כִּ֤י ר֣וּחַ עָֽבְרָה־בּ֣וֹ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְלֹא־יַכִּירֶ֖נּוּ ע֣וֹד מְקוֹמֽוֹ׃
But the faithful love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness to their children's children,
וְחֶ֤סֶד יְהוָ֨ה ׀ מֵעוֹלָ֣ם וְעַד־ע֖[d]וֹלָם עַל־יְרֵאָ֑יו וְ֝צִדְקָת֗וֹ לִבְנֵ֥י בָנִֽים׃
to those who keep his covenant and remember to do his precepts.
לְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י בְרִית֑וֹ וּלְזֹכְרֵ֥י פִ֝קֻּדָ֗יו לַעֲשׂוֹתָֽם׃
The LORD has established his throne in the heavens, and his kingdom rules over all.
יְֽהוָ֗ה בַּ֭שָּׁמַיִם הֵכִ֣ין כִּסְא֑וֹ וּ֝מַלְכוּת֗וֹ בַּכֹּ֥ל מָשָֽׁלָה׃
Bless the LORD, you his angels, you mighty ones who carry out his word, who obey the voice of his word.
בָּרֲכ֥וּ יְהוָ֗ה מַלְאָ֫כָ֥יו גִּבֹּ֣רֵי כֹ֭חַ עֹשֵׂ֣י דְבָר֑וֹ לִ֝שְׁמֹ֗עַ בְּק֣וֹל דְּבָרֽוֹ׃
Bless the LORD, all his armies,[^11] you his servants who do his will.
בָּרֲכ֣וּ יְ֭הוָה כָּל־צְבָאָ֑יו מְ֝שָׁרְתָ֗יו עֹשֵׂ֥י רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃
Bless the LORD, all his works, in all places where he rules. Bless the LORD, my soul.
בָּרֲכ֤וּ יְהוָ֨ה ׀ כָּֽל־מַעֲשָׂ֗יו בְּכָל־מְקֹמ֥וֹת מֶמְשַׁלְתּ֑וֹ בָּרֲכִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 2 and 22. The psalmist speaks to himself.
n.4: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verses 8, 11 and 17.
n.5: Hebrew *edyekh*, "your ornament", a word of uncertain meaning here, perhaps "your years" or "your life". The Septuagint reads "your desire".
n.6: Hebrew *nesher*, the eagle or the vulture (compare Isaiah 40:31).
n.7: Literally "The LORD does righteous acts".
n.8: Compare Moses' prayer in Exodus 33:13, "show me your ways".
n.9: These words echo God's description of himself in Exodus 34:6 (compare 86:15; 145:8).
n.10: Literally "our form", from the verb used in Genesis 2:7, where God forms the man from the dust.
n.11: Hebrew *tseva'av*, "his armies", the heavenly hosts (compare "the LORD of Armies", 24:10).

v: Bless the LORD,[^1] my soul![^2] LORD my God, you are very great; you are clothed with splendor and majesty.[^3]
בָּרֲכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י אֶת־יְה֫וָ֥ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהַי גָּדַ֣לְתָּ מְּאֹ֑ד ה֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר לָבָֽשְׁתָּ׃
He wraps himself in light as in a robe; he stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain.[^4]
עֹֽטֶה־א֭וֹר כַּשַּׂלְמָ֑ה נוֹטֶ֥ה שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם כַּיְרִיעָֽה׃
He lays the beams of his upper rooms on the waters;[^5] he makes the clouds his chariot; he rides on the wings of the wind.
הַ֥מְקָרֶֽה בַמַּ֗יִם עֲ‍ֽלִיּ֫וֹתָ֥יו הַשָּׂם־עָבִ֥ים רְכוּב֑וֹ הַֽ֝מְהַלֵּ֗ךְ עַל־כַּנְפֵי־רֽוּחַ׃
He makes the winds his messengers, flames of fire his servants.[^6]
עֹשֶׂ֣ה מַלְאָכָ֣יו רוּח֑וֹת מְ֝שָׁרְתָ֗יו אֵ֣שׁ לֹהֵֽט׃
He set the earth on its foundations, so that it will never be moved.
יָֽסַד־אֶ֭רֶץ עַל־מְכוֹנֶ֑יהָ בַּל־תִּ֝מּ֗וֹט עוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
You covered it with the deep[^7] as with a garment; the waters stood above the mountains.
תְּ֭הוֹם כַּלְּב֣וּשׁ כִּסִּית֑וֹ עַל־הָ֝רִ֗ים יַ֖עַמְדוּ־מָֽיִם׃
At your rebuke they fled; at the sound of your thunder they hurried away.
מִן־גַּעֲרָ֣תְךָ֣ יְנוּס֑וּן מִן־ק֥וֹל רַֽ֝עַמְךָ֗ יֵחָפֵזֽוּן׃
They went up the mountains; they went down into the valleys,[^8] to the place you appointed for them.
יַעֲל֣וּ הָ֭רִים יֵרְד֣וּ בְקָע֑וֹת אֶל־מְ֝ק֗וֹם זֶ֤ה ׀ יָסַ֬דְתָּ לָהֶֽם׃
You set a boundary they may not pass, so that they will not return to cover the earth.[^9]
גְּֽבוּל־שַׂ֭מְתָּ בַּל־יֽ͏ַעֲבֹר֑וּן בַּל־יְ֝שׁוּב֗וּן לְכַסּ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
He makes springs gush out into the valleys; they flow between the hills.
הַֽמְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ מַ֭עְיָנִים בַּנְּחָלִ֑ים בֵּ֥ין הָ֝רִ֗ים יְהַלֵּכֽוּן׃
They give drink to every wild animal; the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
יַ֭שְׁקוּ כָּל־חַיְת֣וֹ שָׂדָ֑י יִשְׁבְּר֖וּ פְרָאִ֣ים צְמָאָֽם׃
Beside them the birds of the sky have their homes; they sing among the branches.
עֲ֭לֵיהֶם עוֹף־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יִשְׁכּ֑וֹן מִבֵּ֥ין עֳ֝פָאיִ֗ם יִתְּנוּ־קֽוֹל׃
He waters the mountains from his upper rooms; the earth is satisfied with the fruit of your works.
מַשְׁקֶ֣ה הָ֭רִים מֵעֲלִיּוֹתָ֑יו מִפְּרִ֥י מַ֝עֲשֶׂ֗יךָ תִּשְׂבַּ֥ע הָאָֽרֶץ׃
He makes grass grow for the cattle, and plants for people to cultivate,[^10] to bring forth food[^11] from the earth,
מַצְמִ֤יחַ חָצִ֨יר ׀ לַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וְ֭עֵשֶׂב לַעֲבֹדַ֣ת הָאָדָ֑ם לְה֥וֹצִיא לֶ֝֗חֶם מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
and wine to gladden the human heart, oil to make faces shine, and bread to strengthen the human heart.
וְיַ֤יִן ׀ יְשַׂמַּ֬ח לְֽבַב־אֱנ֗וֹשׁ לְהַצְהִ֣יל פָּנִ֣ים מִשָּׁ֑מֶן וְ֝לֶ֗חֶם לְֽבַב־אֱנ֥וֹשׁ יִסְעָֽד׃
The trees of the LORD drink their fill, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted,
יִ֭שְׂבְּעוּ עֲצֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אַֽרְזֵ֥י לְ֝בָנ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָטָֽע׃
where the birds build their nests; the stork has her home in the junipers.
אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֭ם צִפֳּרִ֣ים יְקַנֵּ֑נוּ חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה בְּרוֹשִׁ֥ים בֵּיתָֽהּ׃
The high mountains are for the wild goats; the crags are a refuge for the rock badgers.[^12]
הָרִ֣ים הַ֭גְּבֹהִים לַיְּעֵלִ֑ים סְ֝לָעִ֗ים מַחְסֶ֥ה לַֽשְׁפַנִּֽים׃
He made the moon to mark the seasons;[^13] the sun knows when to set.
עָשָׂ֣ה יָ֭רֵחַ לְמוֹעֲדִ֑ים שֶׁ֝֗מֶשׁ יָדַ֥ע מְבוֹאֽוֹ׃
You bring darkness, and it is night, when all the animals of the forest creep about.
תָּֽשֶׁת־חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וִ֣יהִי לָ֑יְלָה בּֽוֹ־תִ֝רְמֹ֗שׂ כָּל־חַיְתוֹ־יָֽעַר׃
The young lions roar for their prey, seeking their food from God.
הַ֭כְּפִירִים שֹׁאֲגִ֣ים לַטָּ֑רֶף וּלְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מֵאֵ֣ל אָכְלָֽם׃
When the sun rises, they withdraw and lie down in their dens.
תִּזְרַ֣ח הַ֭שֶּׁמֶשׁ יֵאָסֵפ֑וּן וְאֶל־מְ֝עוֹנֹתָ֗ם יִרְבָּצֽוּן׃
People go out to their work, and to their labor until evening.
יֵצֵ֣א אָדָ֣ם לְפָעֳל֑וֹ וְֽלַעֲבֹ֖דָת֣וֹ עֲדֵי־עָֽרֶב׃
How many are your works, LORD! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
מָֽה־רַבּ֬וּ מַעֲשֶׂ֨יךָ ׀ יְֽהוָ֗ה כֻּ֭לָּם בְּחָכְמָ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ מָלְאָ֥ה הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ קִנְיָנֶֽךָ׃
There is the sea, great and wide,[^14] teeming with creatures beyond number, living things both small and great.
זֶ֤ה ׀ הַיָּ֥ם גָּדוֹל֮ וּרְחַ֢ב יָ֫דָ֥יִם שָֽׁם־רֶ֭מֶשׂ וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר חַיּ֥וֹת קְ֝טַנּ֗וֹת עִם־גְּדֹלֽוֹת׃
There the ships go to and fro, and Leviathan,[^15] which you formed to play in it.[^16]
שָׁ֭ם אֳנִיּ֣וֹת יְהַלֵּכ֑וּן לִ֝וְיָתָ֗ן זֶֽה־יָצַ֥רְתָּ לְשַֽׂחֶק־בּֽוֹ׃
All of them look to you to give them their food at the right time.
כֻּ֭לָּם אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְשַׂבֵּר֑וּן לָתֵ֖ת אָכְלָ֣ם בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃
When you give it to them, they gather it up; when you open your hand, they are filled with good things.
תִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם יִלְקֹט֑וּן תִּפְתַּ֥ח יָֽ֝דְךָ֗ יִשְׂבְּע֥וּן טֽוֹב׃
When you hide your face, they are terrified; when you take away their breath, they die and return to their dust.[^17]
תַּסְתִּ֥יר פָּנֶיךָ֮ יִֽבָּהֵ֫ל֥וּן תֹּסֵ֣ף ר֭וּחָם יִגְוָע֑וּן וְֽאֶל־עֲפָרָ֥ם יְשׁוּֽבוּ֥ן׃[t]
When you send out your Spirit,[^18] they are created, and you renew the face of the ground.
תְּשַׁלַּ֣ח ר֭וּחֲךָ יִבָּרֵא֑וּן וּ֝תְחַדֵּ֗שׁ פְּנֵ֣י אֲדָמָֽה׃
May the glory of the LORD endure forever; may the LORD rejoice in his works,
יְהִ֤י כְב֣וֹד יְהוָ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֑ם יִשְׂמַ֖ח יְהוָ֣ה בְּמַעֲשָֽׂיו׃
he who looks at the earth, and it trembles, who touches the mountains, and they smoke.
הַמַּבִּ֣יט לָ֭אָרֶץ וַתִּרְעָ֑ד יִגַּ֖ע בֶּהָרִ֣ים וְֽיֶעֱשָֽׁנוּ׃
I will sing to the LORD as long as I live; I will sing praise to my God while I have being.
אָשִׁ֣ירָה לַיהוָ֣ה בְּחַיָּ֑י אֲזַמְּרָ֖ה לֵאלֹהַ֣י בְּעוֹדִֽי׃
May my meditation be pleasing to him; I rejoice in the LORD.
יֶעֱרַ֣ב עָלָ֣יו שִׂיחִ֑י אָ֝נֹכִ֗י אֶשְׂמַ֥ח בַּיהוָֽה׃
Let sinners vanish from the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless the LORD, my soul! Praise the LORD![^19]
יִתַּ֤מּוּ חַטָּאִ֨ים ׀ מִן־הָאָ֡רֶץ וּרְשָׁעִ֤ים ׀ ע֤וֹד אֵינָ֗ם בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verse 35. Psalm 104 has no title in the Hebrew. The Septuagint gives it the title "Of David". Like Psalm 103, it begins and ends with "Bless the LORD, my soul".
n.3: Psalm 104 praises God as the maker and keeper of the world. It follows roughly the order of the creation account in Genesis 1: light and the heavens (verses 2–4), the earth and the waters (5–9), springs, plants and animals (10–18), the moon and the sun (19–23), and the sea and its creatures (25–26). Many scholars compare it with the Egyptian *Great Hymn to the Aten*, which has some similar images (compare especially verses 20–30). The psalm moves between speaking to God ("you") and speaking about him ("he").
n.4: Hebrew *yeri'ah*, the word used for the curtains of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:1).
n.5: The waters above the sky (Genesis 1:7).
n.6: Or "He makes his messengers winds, and his servants flaming fire." Hebrew *mal'akh* means "messenger" or "angel", and *ruach* "wind" or "spirit". Hebrews 1:7 quotes this verse from the Septuagint in the second sense: "He makes his angels winds, and his servants flames of fire."
n.7: Hebrew *tehom*, the deep waters of Genesis 1:2.
n.8: Or "The mountains rose; the valleys sank down".
n.9: Compare Job 38:8–11; Jeremiah 5:22.
n.10: Literally "for the work of humankind", or "for humankind to use".
n.11: Hebrew *lechem*, "bread", also food in general, as in verse 15.
n.12: Hebrew *shephannim*, the rock hyrax, a small animal that lives among rocks (Leviticus 11:5; Proverbs 30:26).
n.13: Hebrew *mo'adim*, "appointed times", including the festivals (compare Genesis 1:14).
n.14: Literally "wide of hands", stretching out on every side.
n.15: A great sea creature, pictured elsewhere as a monster of chaos (74:14; Job 3:8; 40:25; 41:1 in most English Bibles; Isaiah 27:1). Here it is one of the creatures God has made.
n.16: Or "to play with".
n.17: Compare Genesis 3:19.
n.18: Or "your breath". Hebrew *ruach* means spirit, wind or breath; in verse 29 it is "their breath" (*rucham*).
n.19: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. This is the first time the call appears in the Psalms. The Septuagint places it at the start of Psalm 105 instead.

v: Give thanks to the LORD;[^1] call on his name. Make known his deeds among the peoples.[^2]
הוֹד֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה קִרְא֣וּ בִשְׁמ֑וֹ הוֹדִ֥יעוּ בָ֝עַמִּ֗ים עֲלִילוֹתָֽיו׃
Sing to him, sing praises to him; tell of all his wonders.
שִֽׁירוּ־ל֭וֹ זַמְּרוּ־ל֑וֹ שִׂ֝֗יחוּ בְּכָל־נִפְלְאוֹתָֽיו׃
Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
הִֽ֭תְהַלְלוּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ יִ֝שְׂמַ֗ח לֵ֤ב ׀ מְבַקְשֵׁ֬י יְהוָֽה׃
Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his face[^3] always.
דִּרְשׁ֣וּ יְהוָ֣ה וְעֻזּ֑וֹ בַּקְּשׁ֖וּ פָנָ֣יו תָּמִֽיד׃
Remember the wonders he has done, his miracles and the judgments he has spoken,[^4]
זִכְר֗וּ נִפְלְאוֹתָ֥יו אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֑ה מֹ֝פְתָ֗יו וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי־פִֽיו׃
you offspring of Abraham his servant,[^5] children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
זֶ֭רַע אַבְרָהָ֣ם עַבְדּ֑וֹ בְּנֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב בְּחִירָֽיו׃
He is the LORD our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
ה֭וּא יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ בְּכָל־הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ מִשְׁפָּטָֽיו׃
He remembers his covenant forever,[^6] the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
זָכַ֣ר לְעוֹלָ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ דָּבָ֥ר צִ֝וָּ֗ה לְאֶ֣לֶף דּֽוֹר׃
the covenant he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּ֭רַת אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם וּשְׁב֖וּעָת֣וֹ לְיִשְׂחָֽק׃
He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree, to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
וַיַּֽעֲמִידֶ֣הָ לְיַעֲקֹ֣ב לְחֹ֑ק לְ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָֽם׃
saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance."[^7]
לֵאמֹ֗ר לְךָ֗ אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־אֶֽרֶץ־כְּנָ֑עַן חֶ֝֗בֶל נַחֲלַתְכֶֽם׃
When they were few in number,[^8] very few, and foreigners in the land,
בִּֽ֭הְיוֹתָם מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֑ר כִּ֝מְעַ֗ט וְגָרִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃
they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
וַֽ֭יִּתְהַלְּכוּ מִגּ֣וֹי אֶל־גּ֑וֹי מִ֝מַּמְלָכָ֗ה אֶל־עַ֥ם אַחֵֽר׃
He allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their account:
לֹֽא־הִנִּ֣יחַ אָדָ֣ם לְעָשְׁקָ֑ם וַיּ֖וֹכַח עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם מְלָכִֽים׃
"Do not touch my anointed ones;[^9] do not harm my prophets."
אַֽל־תִּגְּע֥וּ בִמְשִׁיחָ֑י וְ֝לִנְבִיאַי אַל־תָּרֵֽעוּ׃
He called down a famine on the land; he broke every staff of bread.[^10]
וַיִּקְרָ֣א רָ֭עָב עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כָּֽל־מַטֵּה־לֶ֥חֶם שָׁבָֽר׃
He sent a man ahead of them, Joseph, who was sold as a slave.
שָׁלַ֣ח לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם אִ֑ישׁ לְ֝עֶ֗בֶד נִמְכַּ֥ר יוֹסֵֽף׃
They hurt his foot[^11] with shackles; his neck[^12] was put in iron,
עִנּ֣וּ בַכֶּ֣בֶל *רגליו **רַגְל֑וֹ בַּ֝רְזֶ֗ל בָּ֣אָה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
until the time that his word came true; the word of the LORD tested him.[^13]
עַד־עֵ֥ת בֹּֽא־דְבָר֑וֹ אִמְרַ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה צְרָפָֽתְהוּ׃
The king sent and released him; the ruler of peoples set him free.
שָׁ֣לַח מֶ֭לֶךְ וַיַּתִּירֵ֑הוּ מֹשֵׁ֥ל עַ֝מִּ֗ים וַֽיְפַתְּחֵֽהוּ׃
He made him lord of his household, and ruler over all his possessions,
שָׂמ֣וֹ אָד֣וֹן לְבֵית֑וֹ וּ֝מֹשֵׁ֗ל בְּכָל־קִנְיָנֽוֹ׃
to bind his princes as he pleased,[^14] and to teach his elders wisdom.
לֶאְסֹ֣ר שָׂרָ֣יו בְּנַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּזְקֵנָ֥יו יְחַכֵּֽם׃
Then Israel came to Egypt; Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.[^15]
וַיָּבֹ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מִצְרָ֑יִם וְ֝יַעֲקֹ֗ב גָּ֣ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־חָֽם׃
The LORD made his people very fruitful, and made them stronger than their adversaries.
וַיֶּ֣פֶר אֶת־עַמּ֣וֹ מְאֹ֑ד וַ֝יַּֽעֲצִמֵהוּ מִצָּרָֽיו׃
He turned their hearts to hate his people, to deal craftily with his servants.
הָפַ֣ךְ לִ֭בָּם לִשְׂנֹ֣א עַמּ֑וֹ לְ֝הִתְנַכֵּ֗ל בַּעֲבָדָֽיו׃
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
שָׁ֭לַח מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֑וֹ אַ֝הֲרֹ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽחַר־בּֽוֹ׃
They performed his signs among them,[^16] and wonders in the land of Ham.
שָֽׂמוּ־בָ֭ם דִּבְרֵ֣י אֹתוֹתָ֑יו וּ֝מֹפְתִ֗ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חָֽם׃
He sent darkness and made it dark, and they did not rebel against his word.[^17]
שָׁ֣לַֽח חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וַיַּחְשִׁ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־מָ֝ר֗וּ אֶת־*דברוו **דְּבָרֽוֹ׃
He turned their waters into blood, and killed their fish.
הָפַ֣ךְ אֶת־מֵימֵיהֶ֣ם לְדָ֑ם וַ֝יָּ֗מֶת אֶת־דְּגָתָֽם׃
Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings.
שָׁרַ֣ץ אַרְצָ֣ם צְפַרְדְּעִ֑ים בְּ֝חַדְרֵ֗י מַלְכֵיהֶֽם׃
He spoke, and there came swarms of flies,[^18] and gnats throughout their country.
אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א עָרֹ֑ב כִּ֝נִּ֗ים בְּכָל־גְּבוּלָֽם׃
He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire throughout their land.
נָתַ֣ן גִּשְׁמֵיהֶ֣ם בָּרָ֑ד אֵ֖שׁ לֶהָב֣וֹת בְּאַרְצָֽם׃
He struck down their vines and their fig trees, and shattered the trees of their country.
וַיַּ֣ךְ גַּ֭פְנָם וּתְאֵנָתָ֑ם וַ֝יְשַׁבֵּ֗ר עֵ֣ץ גְּבוּלָֽם׃
He spoke, and the locusts came, and young locusts without number.
אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א אַרְבֶּ֑ה וְ֝יֶ֗לֶק וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃
They devoured all the plants in their land, and devoured the fruit of their ground.
וַיֹּ֣אכַל כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב בְּאַרְצָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗אכַל פְּרִ֣י אַדְמָתָֽם׃
He struck down all the firstborn in their land, the first fruit of all their strength.[^19]
וַיַּ֣ךְ כָּל־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּאַרְצָ֑ם רֵ֝אשִׁ֗ית לְכָל־אוֹנָֽם׃
He brought them out with silver and gold, and among his tribes no one stumbled.
וַֽ֭יּוֹצִיאֵם בְּכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֑ב וְאֵ֖ין בִּשְׁבָטָ֣יו כּוֹשֵֽׁל׃
Egypt was glad when they left, for dread of them had fallen on the Egyptians.
שָׂמַ֣ח מִצְרַ֣יִם בְּצֵאתָ֑ם כִּֽי־נָפַ֖ל פַּחְדָּ֣ם עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
He spread out a cloud as a covering, and fire to give light by night.
פָּרַ֣שׂ עָנָ֣ן לְמָסָ֑ךְ וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לְהָאִ֥יר לָֽיְלָה׃
They asked,[^20] and he brought quail, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven.[^21]
שָׁאַ֣ל[t] וַיָּבֵ֣א שְׂלָ֑ו וְלֶ֥חֶם שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם יַשְׂבִּיעֵֽם׃
He opened the rock, and water gushed out; it flowed through the desert like a river.
פָּ֣תַח צ֭וּר וַיָּז֣וּבוּ מָ֑יִם הָ֝לְכ֗וּ בַּצִּיּ֥וֹת נָהָֽר׃
For he remembered his holy word to Abraham his servant.[^22]
כִּֽי־זָ֭כַר אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר קָדְשׁ֑וֹ אֶֽת־אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדּֽוֹ׃
He brought out his people with joy, his chosen ones with shouts of joy.
וַיּוֹצִ֣א עַמּ֣וֹ בְשָׂשׂ֑וֹן בְּ֝רִנָּ֗ה אֶת־בְּחִירָֽיו׃
He gave them the lands of the nations, and they took possession of what the peoples had toiled for,
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם אַרְצ֣וֹת גּוֹיִ֑ם וַעֲמַ֖ל לְאֻמִּ֣ים יִירָֽשׁוּ׃
so that they would keep his decrees and observe his laws. Praise the LORD![^23]
בַּעֲב֤וּר ׀ יִשְׁמְר֣וּ חֻ֭קָּיו וְתוֹרֹתָ֥יו יִנְצֹ֗רוּ הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 105 has no title in the Hebrew.
n.2: Verses 1–15 appear also in 1 Chronicles 16:8–22, in the song of thanksgiving sung when David brought the ark to Jerusalem, with small differences. The psalm then retells the story of Israel from Abraham to the entry into the land, as the keeping of God's promise to Abraham (verses 8–11, 42).
n.3: Or "his presence".
n.4: Literally "the judgments of his mouth".
n.5: 1 Chronicles 16:13 has "Israel his servant".
n.6: 1 Chronicles 16:15 has "Remember his covenant forever".
n.7: Literally "the cord of your inheritance", the measuring line used to mark out a share of land.
n.8: 1 Chronicles 16:19 has "When you were few in number".
n.9: Hebrew *meshichai*, "my anointed ones", from *mashiach*. Here it refers to the patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
n.10: That is, the supply of food that people depend on, as one leans on a staff. The story of Joseph that follows is told in Genesis 37–50.
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "his feet" but read "his foot".
n.12: Hebrew *nephesh*, here perhaps "neck" or "throat" (compare 69:2; 69:1 in most English Bibles), or "he himself".
n.13: *His word* may be Joseph's word, his reading of the dreams (Genesis 40–41), or God's word. *Tested*: or "refined", as metal is refined.
n.14: Literally "by his *nephesh*". The Septuagint reads "to instruct his princes", from a verb that differs by one letter.
n.15: That is, Egypt (compare Genesis 10:6, where Ham is the ancestor of Egypt).
n.16: Literally "They set among them the words of his signs". The plagues in verses 28–36 follow the account of Exodus 7–12, but in a different order, and without the plagues on livestock and of boils.
n.17: The Hebrew text is written "his words" but read "his word". *They* are probably Moses and Aaron. The Septuagint reads "and they rebelled against his words", without "not".
n.18: Hebrew *arov*, "swarm" or "mixture" (see Exodus 8:17; 8:21 in most English Bibles). *Gnats*: Hebrew *kinnim* (Exodus 8:12–14; 8:16–18 in most English Bibles).
n.20: Literally "He asked", that is, the people. The events are told in Exodus 16 and Numbers 11:31–34.

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Give thanks to the LORD,[^2] for he is good; his faithful love[^3] endures forever.
הַֽלְלְויָ֨הּ[c] ׀ הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Who can tell of the mighty deeds of the LORD, or proclaim all his praise?
מִ֗י יְ֭מַלֵּל גְּבוּר֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה יַ֝שְׁמִ֗יעַ כָּל־תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃
Happy[^4] are those who keep justice, who do what is right at all times.
אַ֭שְׁרֵי שֹׁמְרֵ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֑ט עֹשֵׂ֖ה צְדָקָ֣ה בְכָל־עֵֽת׃
Remember me, LORD, when you show favor to your people; come to me[^5] with your salvation,
זָכְרֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה בִּרְצ֣וֹן עַמֶּ֑ךָ פָּ֝קְדֵ֗נִי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
so that I may see the prosperity of your chosen ones, rejoice in the joy of your nation, and glory together with your inheritance.
לִרְא֤וֹת ׀ בְּט֘וֹבַ֤ת בְּחִירֶ֗יךָ לִ֭שְׂמֹחַ בְּשִׂמְחַ֣ת גּוֹיֶ֑ךָ לְ֝הִתְהַלֵּ֗ל עִם־נַחֲלָתֶֽךָ׃
We have sinned, as our ancestors did;[^6] we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.
חָטָ֥אנוּ עִם־אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ הֶעֱוִ֥ינוּ הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ׃
Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand your wonders; they did not remember your many acts of faithful love, but they rebelled by the sea, at the Red Sea.[^7]
אֲב֘וֹתֵ֤ינוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם ׀ לֹא־הִשְׂכִּ֬ילוּ נִפְלְאוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א זָ֭כְרוּ אֶת־רֹ֣ב חֲסָדֶ֑יךָ וַיַּמְר֖וּ עַל־יָ֣ם בְּיַם־סֽוּף׃
Yet he saved them for the sake of his name, to make his might known.
וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמ֑וֹ לְ֝הוֹדִ֗יעַ אֶת־גְּבוּרָתֽוֹ׃
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up; he led them through the depths as through a desert.
וַיִּגְעַ֣ר בְּיַם־ס֭וּף וֽ͏ַיֶּחֱרָ֑ב וַיּוֹלִיכֵ֥ם בַּ֝תְּהֹמ֗וֹת כַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
He saved them from the hand of those who hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם מִיַּ֣ד שׂוֹנֵ֑א וַ֝יִּגְאָלֵ֗ם מִיַּ֥ד אוֹיֵֽב׃
The waters covered their adversaries; not one of them was left.
וַיְכַסּוּ־מַ֥יִם צָרֵיהֶ֑ם אֶחָ֥ד מֵ֝הֶ֗ם לֹ֣א נוֹתָֽר׃
Then they believed his words; they sang his praise.[^8]
וַיַּאֲמִ֥ינוּ בִדְבָרָ֑יו יָ֝שִׁ֗ירוּ תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃
But they soon forgot what he had done; they did not wait for his counsel.
מִֽ֭הֲרוּ שָׁכְח֣וּ מַעֲשָׂ֑יו לֹֽא־חִ֝כּ֗וּ לַעֲצָתֽוֹ׃
They gave in to their craving in the wilderness, and put God to the test in the desert.
וַיִּתְאַוּ֣וּ תַ֭אֲוָה בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיְנַסּוּ־אֵ֝֗ל בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן׃
He gave them what they asked for, but sent a wasting disease among them.[^9]
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם שֶׁאֱלָתָ֑ם וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח רָז֣וֹן בְּנַפְשָֽׁם׃
In the camp they grew jealous of Moses, and of Aaron, the holy one of the LORD.
וַיְקַנְא֣וּ לְ֭מֹשֶׁה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה לְ֝אַהֲרֹ֗ן קְד֣וֹשׁ יְהוָֽה׃
The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
תִּפְתַּח־אֶ֭רֶץ וַתִּבְלַ֣ע דָּתָ֑ן וַ֝תְּכַ֗ס עַל־עֲדַ֥ת אֲבִירָֽם׃
Fire blazed among their company; flames burned up the wicked.[^10]
וַתִּבְעַר־אֵ֥שׁ בַּעֲדָתָ֑ם לֶ֝הָבָ֗ה תְּלַהֵ֥ט רְשָׁעִֽים׃
They made a calf at Horeb and bowed down to a cast image.
יַעֲשׂוּ־עֵ֥גֶל בְּחֹרֵ֑ב וַ֝יִּשְׁתַּחֲו֗וּ לְמַסֵּכָֽה׃
They exchanged their Glory[^11] for the image of an ox that eats grass.
וַיָּמִ֥ירוּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדָ֑ם בְּתַבְנִ֥ית שׁ֝֗וֹר אֹכֵ֥ל עֵֽשֶׂב׃
They forgot God their Savior, who had done great things in Egypt,
שָׁ֭כְחוּ אֵ֣ל מוֹשִׁיעָ֑ם עֹשֶׂ֖ה גְדֹל֣וֹת בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃
wonders in the land of Ham,[^12] awesome deeds by the Red Sea.
נִ֭פְלָאוֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חָ֑ם נ֝וֹרָא֗וֹת עַל־יַם־סֽוּף׃
So he said he would destroy them, had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn his wrath away from destroying them.[^13]
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְֽהַשְׁמִ֫ידָ֥ם לוּלֵ֡י מֹ֘שֶׁ֤ה בְחִיר֗וֹ עָמַ֣ד בַּפֶּ֣רֶץ לְפָנָ֑יו לְהָשִׁ֥יב חֲ֝מָת֗וֹ מֵֽהַשְׁחִֽית׃
Then they despised the pleasant land; they did not believe his word.
וַֽ֭יִּמְאֲסוּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֶמְדָּ֑ה לֹֽא־הֶ֝אֱמִ֗ינוּ לִדְבָרֽוֹ׃
They grumbled in their tents; they did not listen to the voice of the LORD.[^14]
וַיֵּרָגְנ֥וּ בְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָֽה׃
So he raised his hand against them,[^15] to make them fall in the wilderness,
וַיִשָּׂ֣א יָד֣וֹ לָהֶ֑ם לְהַפִּ֥יל א֝וֹתָ֗ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
to make their offspring fall among the nations, and to scatter them through the lands.
וּלְהַפִּ֣יל זַ֭רְעָם בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וּ֝לְזָרוֹתָ֗ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
They joined in the worship of the Baal of Peor, and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.[^16]
וַ֭יִּצָּ֣מְדוּ לְבַ֣עַל פְּע֑וֹר וַ֝יֹּאכְל֗וּ זִבְחֵ֥י מֵתִֽים׃
They provoked him to anger with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
וַ֭יַּכְעִיסוּ בְּמַ֥עַלְלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתִּפְרָץ־בָּ֝֗ם מַגֵּפָֽה׃
Then Phinehas stood up and intervened,[^17] and the plague was stopped.
וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד פִּֽ֭ינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּ֑ל וַ֝תֵּעָצַ֗ר הַמַּגֵּפָֽה׃
That was credited to him as righteousness,[^18] from generation to generation forever.
וַתֵּחָ֣שֶׁב ל֭וֹ לִצְדָקָ֑ה לְדֹ֥ר וָ֝דֹ֗ר עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
They angered him at the waters of Meribah, and it went badly for Moses because of them;
וַ֭יַּקְצִיפוּ עַל־מֵ֥י מְרִיבָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥רַע לְ֝מֹשֶׁ֗ה בַּעֲבוּרָֽם׃
for they rebelled against his spirit,[^19] and he spoke rashly with his lips.[^20]
כִּֽי־הִמְר֥וּ אֶת־רוּח֑וֹ וַ֝יְבַטֵּ֗א בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃
They did not destroy the peoples, as the LORD had told them to,
לֹֽא־הִ֭שְׁמִידוּ אֶת־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה לָהֶֽם׃
but they mixed with the nations and learned their ways.
וַיִּתְעָרְב֥וּ בַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽ֝יִּלְמְד֗וּ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃
They served their idols, which became a snare to them.
וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֑ם וַיִּהְי֖וּ לָהֶ֣ם לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃
They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.[^21]
וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ אֶת־בְּ֭נֵיהֶם וְאֶת־בְּנֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם לַשֵּֽׁדִים׃
They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the land was defiled with blood.
וַיִּ֥שְׁפְּכ֨[t]וּ דָ֪ם נָקִ֡י דַּם־בְּנֵ֘יהֶ֤ם וּֽבְנוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר זִ֭בְּחוּ לַעֲצַבֵּ֣י כְנָ֑עַן וַתֶּחֱנַ֥ף הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ בַּדָּמִֽים׃
They made themselves unclean by what they did, and prostituted themselves by their deeds.[^22]
וַיִּטְמְא֥וּ בְמַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּזְנ֗וּ בְּמַ֥עַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃
So the anger of the LORD burned against his people, and he abhorred his inheritance.
וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֣ף יְהוָ֣ה בְּעַמּ֑וֹ וַ֝יְתָעֵ֗ב אֶת־נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃
He handed them over to the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם בְּיַד־גּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽיִּמְשְׁל֥וּ בָ֝הֶ֗ם שֹׂנְאֵיהֶֽם׃
Their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought low under their power.
וַיִּלְחָצ֥וּם אוֹיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּכָּנְע֗וּ תַּ֣חַת יָדָֽם׃
Many times he rescued them, but they kept rebelling in their plans, and they sank down in their iniquity.
פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֗וֹת יַצִּ֫ילֵ֥ם וְ֭הֵמָּה יַמְר֣וּ בַעֲצָתָ֑ם וַ֝יָּמֹ֗כּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָֽם׃
Yet he looked on their distress when he heard their cry.
וַ֭יַּרְא בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת־רִנָּתָֽם׃
For their sake he remembered his covenant, and relented according to his many acts of faithful love.[^23]
וַיִּזְכֹּ֣ר לָהֶ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ וַ֝יִּנָּחֵ֗ם כְּרֹ֣ב *חסדו **חֲסָדָֽיו׃
He caused them to be pitied by all who held them captive.
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אוֹתָ֣ם לְרַחֲמִ֑ים לִ֝פְנֵ֗י כָּל־שׁוֹבֵיהֶֽם׃
Save us, LORD our God, and gather us from among the nations, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.[^24]
הוֹשִׁיעֵ֨נוּ ׀ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְקַבְּצֵנוּ֮ מִֽן־הַגּ֫וֹיִ֥ם לְ֭הֹדוֹת לְשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ לְ֝הִשְׁתַּבֵּ֗חַ בִּתְהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, "Amen!" Praise the LORD![^25]
בָּ֤רֽ[t]וּךְ־יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֪י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל מִן־הָ֤עוֹלָ֨ם ׀ וְעַ֬ד הָעוֹלָ֗ם וְאָמַ֖ר כָּל־הָעָ֥ם אָמֵ֗ן הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah" (see the note on 104:35). Also in verse 48. Psalm 106 has no other title.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. The rest of this verse is the same as 1 Chronicles 16:34 (compare 100:5; 107:1; 118:1; 136:1).
n.3: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verses 7 and 45, where it is plural, "acts of faithful love".
n.4: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.5: Literally "visit me".
n.6: Literally "with our ancestors". The psalm goes on to retell Israel's history as a history of rebellion and of God's mercy, from the exodus to the exile.
n.7: Hebrew *yam suf*, literally "Sea of Reeds", traditionally "the Red Sea". Also in verses 9 and 22. For the rebellion at the sea, see Exodus 14:10–12.
n.8: Compare Exodus 14:31–15:21.
n.9: Literally "and sent leanness into their soul (*nephesh*)". The events of verses 14–15 are told in Numbers 11:4–34.
n.10: The rebellion of Dathan and Abiram and the others is told in Numbers 16 (compare Deuteronomy 11:6).
n.11: That is, God, the glory of Israel (compare Jeremiah 2:11; Romans 1:23). Jewish scribal tradition lists this verse among the places where the scribes are said to have changed a word out of reverence, reading "their glory" for an original "my glory". The story of the calf is told in Exodus 32.
n.12: That is, Egypt (see 105:23).
n.13: Like a soldier standing in a gap in a broken wall. See Exodus 32:9–14.
n.14: The events of verses 24–27 are told in Numbers 13–14.
n.15: The gesture of swearing an oath (compare Numbers 14:28–30; Ezekiel 20:23).
n.16: Literally "sacrifices of the dead": either offerings to lifeless gods (compare Numbers 25:2), or offerings made for the dead. The events of verses 28–31 are told in Numbers 25:1–13.
n.17: Hebrew *vayefallel*, "and he intervened", or "and he carried out judgment" (compare Numbers 25:7–8).
n.18: The same words are used of Abraham in Genesis 15:6.
n.19: That is, God's Spirit (compare Isaiah 63:10), or Moses' own spirit.
n.20: The events are told in Numbers 20:2–13. *Meribah* means "quarreling".
n.21: Hebrew *shedim*, a word found elsewhere only in Deuteronomy 32:17.
n.22: A picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to God, as of a wife to her husband (compare Hosea 2; Ezekiel 16).
n.23: The Hebrew text is written "his faithful love" but read "his acts of faithful love".
n.24: Verses 47–48 are close to 1 Chronicles 16:35–36, where verse 35 begins "Say, 'Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us and rescue us from the nations…'"
n.25: 1 Chronicles 16:36 has "Then all the people said, 'Amen!' and praised the LORD." The blessing in this verse closes Book 4 of the Psalms (Psalms 90–106). Books 1, 2 and 3 end in a similar way (41:14; 41:13 in most English Bibles; 72:18–19; 89:53; 89:52 in most English Bibles), and Psalm 150 closes the whole collection.

v: Give thanks to the LORD,[^1] for he is good; his faithful love[^2] endures forever.
הֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, those he redeemed from the hand of the adversary,
יֹ֭אמְרוּ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר גְּ֝אָלָ֗ם מִיַּד־צָֽר׃
and gathered from the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the sea.[^3]
וּֽמֵאֲרָצ֗וֹת קִ֫בְּצָ֥ם מִמִּזְרָ֥ח וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֑ב מִצָּפ֥וֹן וּמִיָּֽם׃
Some wandered in the wilderness, in the desert wastes;[^4] they found no way to a city to live in.
תָּע֣וּ בַ֭מִּדְבָּר בִּישִׁימ֣וֹן דָּ֑רֶךְ עִ֥יר מ֝וֹשָׁ֗ב לֹ֣א מָצָֽאוּ׃
They were hungry and thirsty; their soul[^5] fainted within them.
רְעֵבִ֥ים גַּם־צְמֵאִ֑ים נַ֝פְשָׁ֗ם בָּהֶ֥ם תִּתְעַטָּֽף׃
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he rescued them from their distress.[^6]
וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֽוּקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יַצִּילֵֽם׃
He led them by a straight road, to go to a city to live in.
וַ֭יּֽ͏ַדְרִיכֵם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יְשָׁרָ֑ה לָ֝לֶ֗כֶת אֶל־עִ֥יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.[^7]
יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
For he satisfies the thirsty soul, and fills the hungry soul with good things.
כִּי־הִ֭שְׂבִּיעַ נֶ֣פֶשׁ שֹׁקֵקָ֑ה וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ רְ֝עֵבָה מִלֵּא־טֽוֹב׃
Some sat in darkness and deep darkness,[^8] prisoners in misery and in iron,
יֹ֭שְׁבֵי חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָ֑וֶת אֲסִירֵ֖י עֳנִ֣י וּבַרְזֶֽל׃
because they had rebelled against the words of God, and spurned the counsel of the Most High.[^9]
כִּֽי־הִמְר֥וּ אִמְרֵי־אֵ֑ל וַעֲצַ֖ת עֶלְי֣וֹן נָאָֽצוּ׃
So he humbled their hearts with hard labor; they stumbled, and there was no one to help.
וַיַּכְנַ֣ע בֶּעָמָ֣ל לִבָּ֑ם כָּ֝שְׁל֗וּ וְאֵ֣ין עֹזֵֽר׃
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֻֽקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃
He brought them out of darkness and deep darkness, and snapped their chains.
יֽ֭וֹצִיאֵם מֵחֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָ֑וֶת וּמוֹסְר֖וֹתֵיהֶ֣ם יְנַתֵּֽק׃
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
For he shatters the doors of bronze, and cuts through the bars of iron.[^10]
כִּֽי־שִׁ֭בַּר דַּלְת֣וֹת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וּבְרִיחֵ֖י בַרְזֶ֣ל גִּדֵּֽעַ׃
Some were fools because of their rebellious ways,[^11] and suffered affliction because of their iniquities.
אֱ֭וִלִים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ פִּשְׁעָ֑ם וּֽ֝מֵעֲוֺ֥נֹתֵיהֶ֗ם[t] יִתְעַנּֽוּ׃
They loathed all food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
כָּל־אֹ֭כֶל תְּתַעֵ֣ב נַפְשָׁ֑ם וַ֝יַּגִּ֗יעוּ עַד־שַׁ֥עֲרֵי מָֽוֶת׃
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֻֽקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃
He sent out his word and healed them, and rescued them from their graves.[^12]
יִשְׁלַ֣ח דְּ֭בָרוֹ וְיִרְפָּאֵ֑ם וִֽ֝ימַלֵּ֗ט מִשְּׁחִיתוֹתָֽם׃ [8]׆
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃ [8]׆
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving,[^13] and tell of his deeds with songs of joy.
וְ֭יִזְבְּחוּ זִבְחֵ֣י תוֹדָ֑ה וִֽיסַפְּר֖וּ מַעֲשָׂ֣יו בְּרִנָּֽה׃ [8]׆
